title: shiny application breaks with release 1.8.1
description:
We have an older shiny app, [statnetWeb](https://github.com/statnet/statnetWeb) that broke between releases 1.8.0 and 1.8.1.   

The page rendering no longer works properly for a page that uses direct calls to `conditionalPanel()` and `uiOutput()`, and since your [1.8.1 release notes](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/releases/tag/v1.8.1) explicitly state these have changed behavior that might break apps that call them directly, I'm thinking this might be our problem.

I'm not sure how to create a self-contained reprex for this, and I'm not an expert in coding shiny apps.  But I can show the problem.

Desired behavior can be observed currently on the app hosted on the shiny server:  https://statnet.shinyapps.io/statnetWeb/

Select the "Data" tab up at the top, and work through the options.  It will look like this:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f15f97cc-0664-4e0c-992a-bff0d507a286)


1. The screen updates interactively with different input options as you choose a "File type" -- compare "built-in network" to any of the other choices.  
2. Once you choose a built-in network, the network is loaded and the summaries appear on the right tab, and you can continue working with it.

Using shiny 1.8.1, and running the app locally, this is what the "Data" page looks like now -- note the difference with the hosted app:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/799de75d-97d3-45f0-82c9-4fbaab3e5f8e)

1. Nothing changes interactively now with the File type selection
2. It doesn't load the data when you "Choose a network"

The code for this page of the app is found [here](https://github.com/statnet/statnetWeb/blob/4f90fdc471a4c6d19acb325e615e2a4a03b4fdf7/inst/shiny/statnetWeb/ui.R#L152-L474)

It calls `conditionalPanel()` directly and repeatedly.  

I've isolated the shiny release change as the cause by reinstalling shiny 1.8.0 from the CRAN archive and running that version locally.  The behavior of 1.8.0 matches the desired behavior, as seen on the hosted app.

Hopefully this is enough to identify what the issue is, and whether there's a simple fix for our code to update to shiny 1.8.1.

TIA!  Shiny is awesome :)

title: ExtendedTasks: how to kill a task?
description:
Thanks ExtendedTasks implementation, it has a promissing future!

As of shiny 1.8.1.1, the methods available for ExtendedTasks are:

         • ‘ExtendedTask$new()’

         • ‘ExtendedTask$invoke()’

         • ‘ExtendedTask$status()’

         • ‘ExtendedTask$result()’

It would be quite useful to have a `ExtendedTask$Kill()` method that would kill the respective process associated with the task. Such method would better handle cases of expensive tasks where user decides to change inputs half-way. Such actions would create multiple processes running expensive tasks, which is something we want to avoid.

Concept:

```r
ExtendedTask$kill() # kill all previous task
ExtendedTask$invoke() #start a new task based on new input
```

title: `req()`/`isTruthy()` can give suprising results for matrices (with `NA`s)
description:
Some might consider this surprising behavior:

```r
m <- matrix(c(NA, "b", "c", NA), 2, 2)
#>     [,1] [,2]
#> [1,] NA   "c" 
#> [2,] "b"  NA 
shiny::isTruthy(m)
#> FALSE
```

The reason `m` is falsy is that `stats::na.omit()` returns a 0 row matrix:

```r
x <- stats::na.omit(m)
str(x)
#> chr[0 , 1:2] 
#> - attr(*, "na.action")= 'omit' num [1:2] 1 2
nzchar(x)
#> logical(0)
```

I suppose this might be expected if you truly want to discard all rows with any `NA`, but that may not always be the case. It would probably make sense for `req()`/`isTruthy()` to gain a `na.action = na.omit` argument to customize the handling of `NA`s

title: Password managers try to autofill selectInput
description:
### System details

Browser Versions:
 - Chrome: 125.0.6422.113
 - Firefox: 124.0.2

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 4.4.0 (2024-04-24)
Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin20
Running under: macOS Sonoma 14.5

Matrix products: default
BLAS:   /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-arm64/Resources/lib/libRblas.0.dylib
LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.4-arm64/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib;  LAPACK version 3.12.0

locale:
[1] en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/C/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8

time zone: Europe/London
tzcode source: internal

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices datasets  utils     methods   base

other attached packages:
[1] shiny_1.8.1.1

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] digest_0.6.35     later_1.3.2       R6_2.5.1          httpuv_1.6.15
 [5] fastmap_1.2.0     magrittr_2.0.3    htmltools_0.5.8.1 lifecycle_1.0.4
 [9] promises_1.3.0    cli_3.6.2         xtable_1.8-4      renv_1.0.7
[13] compiler_4.4.0    tools_4.4.0       mime_0.12         Rcpp_1.0.12
[17] rlang_1.1.3
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  # this is the input the password manager recognises as a password field
  selectInput("1", "test", choices = list(a=1, b=2))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

I noticed on new shiny apps my team created, our password manager software (Keeper) started recognising `selectInput` as a password field. The password manager then generates a popup to prompting to create a new password, creating an annoying experience for users. I have tested with LastPass, which does not recognise the input field or cause any issues.

With some testing, this behaviour was found in shiny versions 1.8.0 through to the current version (1.8.1.1 at the time of writing). Rolling back to version 1.7.5.1 stops this behaviour. Digging a bit deeper, I found this is due to a `autocomplete="new-password"` attribute in the HTML input element; whereas this tag is `autocomplete="off"` in older versions. 

**Input element generated using shiny version 1.8.1.1:**

```html
<input type="text" autocomplete="new-password" autofill="no" tabindex="" id="1-selectized" role="combobox" aria-expanded="false" haspopup="listbox" aria-owns="0bxb7sopar" style="width: 4px;">
```

**Input element generated using shiny version 1.7.5.1:**

```html
<input type="text" autocomplete="off" tabindex="" id="1-selectized" role="combobox" aria-expanded="false" haspopup="listbox" aria-owns="8l4sn3d8vj" style="width: 4px;">
```

This appears to be due to the upgrade of the selectize.js shiny dependency from v0.12.4 to v0.15.2 in [shiny version 1.8.0](https://rstudio.github.io/shiny/news/index.html#shiny-180).

## Work around

This problem can be solved by replacing `selectInput` with `selectizeInput` and using the `autofill_disable` plugin:

```R
selectizeInput(
    "1",
    "test",
    choices = list(a=1, b=2),
    options = list(
        plugins=list('autofill_disable')
    )
)
```

title: Documentation: selectizeInput doesn't explain what selectize.js means
description:
The argument `selectize` says "Whether to use selectize.js or not". Most shiny users probably don't know that selectize.js is a javascript dropdown library, and that argument is a mystery to them.

Similarly, I've seen many intermediate shiny users being completely unaware of the difference between `selectInput()` and `selectizeInput()`. It would be good to explain that difference.

title: Documentation: clarify how to use plugins in selectizeInput()
description:
The [blog post](https://shiny.posit.co/blog/posts/shiny-r-1.8.0/) for shiny 1.8.0 release had a section about selectizeInput's upgrade and plugins. It shows an example of using `options = list(plugins = "remove_button")`. However, by just looking at the documentation for `selectizeInput()`, it would be very difficult to know that plugins are available and how to use them. The `options` argument docs simply refer to https://selectize.dev/docs/usage for possible options, but has no examples.

Because of extensive prior experience I do know how to read selectize's documentation, and how to translate that to shiny's selectizeInput. But for anyone who isn't already familiar with it, I would argue it's almost impossible to realize that they can use plugins and how to do so (without Googling). It's also very hard for them to know how to use other options. I recommend adding examples of using `options` in the docs.

title: Documentation: devmode docs need some improvement
description:
Since devmode is continuing to get new features, it might be worthwhile to make sure it's easy to understand so that its usage isn't suffered.

1. The documentation for devmode opens with:

    ```
    Developer Mode enables a number of [options()](https://rdrr.io/r/base/options.html) to make a developer's life easier, like enabling 
    non-minified JS and printing messages about deprecated functions and options.
    ```

    This does not tell me what are all the options that get set with devmode. I could not find anywhere a clearly defined list of options that are affected by devmode.

2. It might be obvious, but I think it's important to still note that devmode should only be used while developing/testing and not in production

3. I assume that the vast majority of shiny users and devmode users are creating shiny apps rather than creating shiny packages. The majority of the documentation page for devmode is dealing with functions and concepts that are only relevant for package authors. This adds a lot of noise and clutter for shiny developers who are just trying to understand how they can use devmode. As a shiny app developer, when I look at the list of functions on that page, it's a lot to take in and can cause me to give up.

4. The documentation was for the `verbose` parameter is "Logical value which should be set to TRUE display" - it's missing a word

5. The explanation for the `devmode()` function is: "Function to set two options to enable/disable Shiny Developer Mode and Developer messages". I found this confusing. I thought this is referring to the two options mentioned at the top of the docs - minifying JS and printing messages. The part that's confusing is that it mentions "two options" - that's getting into the detail of what the function is literally doing, but it's ambiguous because setting the devmode option causes other options to get enabled. Therefore, I think that language should be avoided, and it should just say "Enable/disable Shiny Developer Mode and Developer messages"

6. There's a lot of inconsistent terminology used for the messaging. "Shiny Developer messages", "Developer Mode message", "Developer messages". Choose one way to call it and stick with it to make it clear that it's talking about the same thing in all these instances.

7. I find it unintuitive that calling `devmode()` does not give deterministic results. Calling `devmode()` in a new session causes devmode to turn on. If I then call `devmode(F)`, it turns devmode off - all this makes sense. But if I then call `devmode()` again, it doesn't turn it back on. This is the part that is strange. I understand it's because it's looking at the existing option, but that's exactly what I find strange. Calling `in_devmode()` should look at the existing option, it's weird to me that the `devmode()` argument is using the option that it sets as its default.

8.  The docs for `?shinyOptions` say this about devmode:

    ```
    shiny.devmode (defaults to NULL)
        Option to enable Shiny Developer Mode. When set, different default getOption(key) values will be returned.
    ```
    
    It looks like the option is a boolean, and most other shiny options that are booleans have a default of either TRUE or FALSE. Is there a reason why this is defaulting to NULL rather than FALSE, like all other options? Also, the sentence "different default getOption(key) values will be returned" is an awkward unclear sentence.

title: Documentation clarification: is `page_fluid()` now the default recommendation over `fluidPage()`?
description:
For many years the default convention for writing a simple shiny app was `ui <- fluidPage(...)`. I've noticed that in the official docs for layout now mention `page_fluid()` and don't mention `fluidPage()` https://shiny.posit.co/r/articles/build/layout-guide/

I thought that perhaps this means `fluidPage()` is being phased out, so I looked at the function documentation for it and there is no mention there. It seems that any new shiny user will learn to use `page_fluid()`, but as an old shiny user, it's confusing whether I should also be moving to it or not.

Documentation should clarify this.

observeEvent does not trigger to changes in reactiveValues
description:
Taking an example from this post https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68707709/observeevent-not-reacting-to-changes-in-reactivevalues 

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("x", "x", 5),
  numericInput("y", "y", 10)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  test_vals <- reactiveValues(
    x = reactive(input$x),
    y = reactive(input$y)
  )
 
  observeEvent(test_vals, {
    print("test_vals changed")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The message is printed in the console only once when the app is launched but nothing happens when the value changes. 

In this case I know the issue will be fixed if I use `observeEvent(c(input$x, input$y), {...})` but this is very simplistic example and my actualy example is much more complicated. My goal is to make `observeEvent` (or `observe`) trigger based on the changes in `reactiveValues`. 

I have searched the internet quite extensively along with Github issue but could not find this topic being discussed.

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("select", "Select", choices = c("A", "B", "C"),selected = c("A", "B"), multiple = TRUE),
  actionButton("clear", "Clear")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$clear, {
    updateSelectInput(session, "select", selected = NULL)
    print(glue("click {input$clear}"))
    cat("selectInput value: ")
    print(input$select)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Updating reactive value on a timer results on JS error
description:
Introduced by #4039. This app now produces a JS error: `Shiny server has sent a progress message for number, but the output is in an unexpected state of: idle`.

Seems it's expected that a progress message can be sent to move output status from Idle to Invalidated (i.e., skip the value stage)

```r
library(shiny)

devmode()

ui <- fluidPage(uiOutput("number"))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
    output$number <- renderUI({ val() })
    val <- reactiveVal(0)
    observe({
        invalidateLater(3000)
        val(runif(1))
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

    handle_json(input$sect)
  })

    }) %...>% {

I created a small reprex based on my application. I use nested future_promises (because I have a progress bar and this way I can set it properly which I could not, using one future_promise only). ```
You can check it using this line:

```
After the first future_promise is resolved, it works fine. After the second and third, it throws the error above.

Second issue is related to a reactive function:
```
Warning: Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext: Operation not allowed without an active reactive context.
• You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive consumer.
```
You can check it using this line:
```
session$userData$result <- calculate_result()
```
After the first future_promise is resolved, it works fine. After the second and third, it throws the error above.

Thanks in advance for your help.

title: Set outputOtions at assignment
description:
Currently this works (in this order):

```r
output$some_ui<- renderUI({ ... })

outputOptions(output, "some_ui", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
```

And this also works:

```r
observe(outputOptions(output, "some_ui", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE))

output$some_ui<- renderUI({ ... })
```

In both cases, the assignment and the setting of options need to happen in different places (also `outputOptions()` looks like a loose side effect).

## Proposal 

This could become:

```r
output$some_ui<- renderUI({ ... }) |>
  setOutputOption(suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
```

Which seems inline with recent additions such as `bindEvent()` and `bindCache()`.

Or could be:

```r
output$some_ui<- renderUI({ ... }, outputOptions = list(suspendWhenHidden = FALSE))
```

title: With Bootstrap 5, `uiOutput()` doesn't dim in opacity when recalculating
description:
Starting with #3957, `uiOutput()` (and `conditionalPanel()`) containers started getting `display: contents;`. Turns out this is problematic for the `.recalculating { opacity: 0.3; }`  that shiny adds to output containers. Consider the following example which now fails to dim in opacity when recalculating (since the output container div is now `display: contents;`, `opacity` no longer applies):

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_fixed(
  actionButton("btn", "Press me"),
  uiOutput("foo")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  output$foo <- renderUI({
    input$btn
    Sys.sleep(3)
    span(paste("Number of clicks:", input$btn))
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
library(shiny)
# Using shiny bookmarking, freezing any input that is part of the bookmark results in an error
# but does not appear to break restoration
shinyApp(
  ui = function(request) {
    fluidPage(
      selectizeInput("dynamic_parent", "Dynamic Parent", choices = c('mtcars', 'airquality', 'warpbreaks'), multiple = FALSE),
      selectizeInput("dynamic_child", "Dynamic Child", choices = NULL, multiple = FALSE),
      verbatimTextOutput("output")
    )
  },
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    # Automatically bookmark every time an input changes
    observe({
      reactiveValuesToList(input)
      session$doBookmark()
    })
    # Update the query string
    onBookmarked(updateQueryString)
    # Dynamically created inputs must be restored
    onRestored(function(state) {
      updateSelectizeInput(session, "dynamic_child", selected = state$input$dynamic_child)
    })
    # Update the dynamic child based on the dynamic parent
    observe({
      if (!input$dynamic_parent == "") {
        updateSelectizeInput(session, "dynamic_child", choices = names(get(input$dynamic_parent)))
        freezeReactiveValue(input, "dynamic_child")
      }
    })
    # Output
    output$output <- renderText({paste0(names(reactiveValuesToList(input)),' = ',reactiveValuesToList(input), collapse = ", ")})
  },
  enableBookmarking = "url"
)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

Freezing an input that is also bookmarked generates an error: "Error bookmarking state:". The bookmarking state appears to load correctly despite this error message, and it isn't clear from the bookmarking documentation that freezing an input should create an issue. While freezing is not necessary in this example application, this error is preventing me from rolling out bookmarking in a more complicated application that does require `freezeReactiveValue` on inputs that would also be bookmarked.

title: Update ionRangeSlider to use CSS variables in a Bootstrap 5 context
description:
ionRangeSlider's sass still uses color functions that result in realized colors -- as opposed to CSS variables -- once compiled.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/e2b7f9113866a2f0a98b0cac240320116c5ff56a/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/scss/shiny.scss#L39-L46

We should either:

1. Update `ionRangeSlider/scss/shiny.scss` to avoid these color calculations.
2. Add `ionRangeSlider/scss/bootstrap5.scss` to avoid these color calculations in BS5, renaming the current `shiny.scss` to `bootstrap4.scss`.

title: In TS code, convert `Shiny` from `interface` to `class`
description:
Some issues we currently have with the `Shiny` interface in our Typescript code:
- Some function types end up being circular if you Cmd-click on them, like `shinyUnbindAll`.
- Some of the methods on the `Shiny` object appear only after initialization, like `setInputValue`, `bindAll`, `user`, and so some authors might wait for those methods to be available, which is weird. https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/e2b7f9113866a2f0a98b0cac240320116c5ff56a/srcts/src/shiny/initedMethods.ts#L11-L22
- It's just weird to have a `Shiny` interface and a `FullShinyDef` type.
- It's strange that we initialize `window.Shiny` as an empty object, but we say that it is a `Shiny` object. https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/e2b7f9113866a2f0a98b0cac240320116c5ff56a/srcts/src/window/libraries.ts#L3-L10

Proposed solution (with help from @schloerke):
- Change `Shiny` from an interface to a class, and make sure it has all methods from the beginning.
- Add an `init()` method to that class.
- If some of the methods are called before `init()`, then throw an error, with information on how to fix the problem.
- Add `initPromise()` method, which returns a promise that resolves at the end of `init()`. Then code that needs to wait for Shiny to be ready can just wait for that.
- Add an `onInit()` method, which lets you register a callback to be invoked when the `initPromise()` resolves.

Shiny server not supporting http range requests. This disables seekbars for locally (www folder) hosted media files.
description:
Shiny does not return HTTP range requests for files hosted in the "www" folder.  The MWE below demonstrates the issue. In setting up this example, save the "sample-mp4-file.mp4" file [(download here](https://jsoncompare.org/LearningContainer/SampleFiles/Video/MP4/sample-mp4-file.mp4)) into the "www" subdirectory of the folder hosting the app.R file. You'll notice the seeker is disabled for the locally hosted mp4 file. This issue doesn't apply to files < 1MB, which might explain why others have not provided compelling examples. This file is 10MB, so Chrome will require a response of 206 from the allow HTTP range inquiry.

```
library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

    # Application title
    titlePanel("Streaming Video Issue"),
    
    h1("Externally Hosted File"),
    tags$iframe(src = "https://jsoncompare.org/LearningContainer/SampleFiles/Video/MP4/sample-mp4-file.mp4", 
                type = "video/mp4",
                width = "600px",
                height = "333px"),
    
    h1("Locally Hosted File"),    
    tags$iframe(src = "sample-mp4-file.mp4", 
                type = "video/mp4",
                width = "600px",
                height = "333px")
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {

}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Others have posted about this issue without resolution. See [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71958281/r-shiny-embedded-video-works-but-wont-fast-forward-skip-time](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71958281/r-shiny-embedded-video-works-but-wont-fast-forward-skip-time). It may be helpful to read this article on HTTP range requests: [https://www.zeng.dev/post/2023-http-range-and-play-mp4-in-browser/](https://www.zeng.dev/post/2023-http-range-and-play-mp4-in-browser/l)

title: Error in init.ts when using library(jsTreeR)
description:
I've already raised the issue [here](https://github.com/stla/jsTreeR/issues/23), however, I'm not sure if in this case `shiny` or `jsTreeR` needs to make a move.

When running the following app using the latest CRAN version of `library(jsTreeR)` (2.5.0) **after resizing** the browser window this error can be seen in the browser console:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/36849480/67d5093b-5987-495f-86fd-50698a91c3bc)

Example app:

```
library(jsTreeR)
library(shiny)

nodes <- list(
  list(
    text = "Fruits",
    type = "fruit",
    children = list(
      list(
        text = "Apple",
        type = "fruit",
        data = list(
          quantity = 20
        )
      ),
      list(
        text = "Banana",
        type = "fruit",
        data = list(
          quantity = 31
        )
      ),
      list(
        text = "Grapes",
        type = "fruit",
        data = list(
          quantity = 34
        )
      )
    ),
    state = list(
      opened = TRUE
    )
  )
)

grid <- list(
  columns = list(
    list(
      width = 200,
      header = "Product"
    ),
    list(
      width = 150,
      value = "quantity",
      header = "Quantity"
    )
  )
)

ui <-   fluidPage(
  titlePanel("jsTree grid"),
  jstreeOutput("jstree")
)

server <-   function(input, output, session){
  output$jstree <- renderJstree(jstree(nodes, search = TRUE, grid = grid))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This is only the case when `jstree` is provided with the grid parameter (table wrapped around the tree).

@stla [identified ](https://github.com/stla/jsTreeR/issues/23#issuecomment-1938935935) that the class `shiny-bound-output` is assigned to the `jstree-grid-wrapper` div which causes the issue and that removing it prevents the issue.

I'm wondering whether removing the class only is "combating symptoms" and if this should be addressed in shiny (similar to [this](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2956)).

title: How to use `Shiny.bindAll` for a DT table?
description:
In order to use a Shiny widget in a DT table with **shiny** `< 1.8`, we used the following options:
```r
  options = list(
    preDrawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node()); }'),
    drawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node()); }')
  ))
```
That doesn't work anymore. This is probably due to the [breaking change](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/news/news.html) in **shiny** `1.8.0`. I tried to play with `async/await` without success. What should we do?

Here is an example:

```r
library(shiny)
library(DT)

dat <- data.frame(
  select = as.character(selectInput("id", label = NULL, choices = c("A", "B")))
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  br(),
  DTOutput("dtable")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  output$dtable <- renderDT({
    dat
  },
  rownames = FALSE,
  escape = FALSE,
  options = list(
    preDrawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node()); }'),
    drawCallback = JS('function() { Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node()); }')
  ))

  observe({
    print(input$id)
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```

title: v1.8.0: Unable to highlight multiple selected values at once in selectInput/selectizeInput
description: Up until v1.7.5.1, it was possible to highlight multiple selected values in a selectInput/selectizeInput by using shift + click or ctrl + click and remove them all at once, e.g.: ```R library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( selectInput( inputId = "letters", label = "Letters", choices = LETTERS, selected = LETTERS, multiple = TRUE ) ) server <- function(input, output) { } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` In v1.8.0, only one can be selected at a time: This is with R 4.3.1 on Windows 10 and happens both in the RStudio viewer and on Chrome.

```R
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel(tag("u", "Test"), "Test"),
  selectizeInput(
    inputId = "selectID",
    label = "Select id type",
    choices = c("Numeric", "Letters"),
    selected = "Numeric",
    multiple = FALSE
  ),
  selectizeInput(
    inputId = "library",
    label = "Select libraries",
    choices = as.character(seq(5)),
    selected = 1,
    multiple = TRUE
  ),
  h3("And now!?"),
  br(),
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  observeEvent(input$selectID, {
    if (input$selectID == "Numeric") {
      choices <- as.character(seq(5))
    } else {
      choices <- LETTERS[1:5]
    }
    updateSelectizeInput(
      inputId = "library",
      choices = choices,
      selected = choices[1],
      server = TRUE
    )

  },
               ignoreNULL = TRUE, ignoreInit = FALSE)
  session$onSessionEnded(function() { stopApp() })
}
print(shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(launch.browser = TRUE)))
```

### Describe the problem in detail
A new bug in 1.8.0, I can verify that this does not happen in 1.7.4, which I had before I updated today.  

When you have a box (library) with selectable numbers 1,2,3,4,5 and another box (selectID) that defines id type of box (library) (numeric is default or character: i.e. changes the selection in (library) to A,B,C,D,E.

title: shiny.autoreload does not work when runApp is given shinyApp result or a list
description:
### Description

Hi! Today I have noticed that running an application with `shinyApp`, i.e. relying on its print, does not enable autoreload.

See Reproduction and Cause below.

### Reproduction
Use the following `app.R`:
```R
options(shiny.port = 8080, shiny.autoreload = TRUE)

shiny::shinyApp(
  "Hello world!",
  function(input, output, session) {}
)
```

1. Run app with `Rscript app.R` (or just interactively). Notice that autoreload **is not working**.
2. Run app with `Rscript -e shiny::runApp("app.R")`. Notice that auroreload **is working**.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/38053499/79bfcb63-a496-4d6c-a006-011f356a14e7

### Cause
I went down the rabbit hole to find a root cause of this, and here are my findings.

`shinyApp` is printed by [`print.shiny.appobj`][] that calls `runApp`:
```r
print.shiny.appobj <- function(x, ...) {
  runApp(x)
}
```

Our object created with `shinyApp` (of class `shiny.appobj`) eventually, within `runApp`, [gets passed to `as.shiny.appobj`][]:
```r
appParts <- as.shiny.appobj(appDir)
```

`appDir`, according to [its documentation][] supports three different classes of objects: characters (directories and file names), a list, and `shiny.appobj`. [The implementations of `as.shiny.appobj`][] are as follows:

```r
as.shiny.appobj.shiny.appobj <- function(x) {
  x
}

as.shiny.appobj.list <- function(x) {
  shinyApp(ui = x$ui, server = x$server)
}

as.shiny.appobj.character <- function(x) {
  if (identical(tolower(tools::file_ext(x)), "r"))
    shinyAppFile(x)
  else
    shinyAppDir(x)
}
```

Taking a look where `initAutoReloadMonitor`, the function responsible for watching files, is being called leads us to two places: [`shinyAppDir_serverR`][] and [`shinyAppDir_appR`][]. Checking references of these two functions we see that:
- `shinyAppFile` calls `shinyAppDir_appR`
- `shinyAppDir` calls either of these

This leads to a conclusion that only `as.shiny.appobj.character` spawns file watcher. Therefore, passing either a list or result of `shinyApp` makes the autoreload functionality not work.

[`print.shiny.appobj`]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v1.8.0/R/shinyapp.R#L552-L554
[gets passed to `as.shiny.appobj`]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v1.8.0/R/runapp.R#L127
[its documentation]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v1.8.0/R/runapp.R#L12-L21
[The implementations of `as.shiny.appobj`]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b8923e9497778b3dfba54c8a054590f88e96998f/R/shinyapp.R#L524-L541
[`shinyAppDir_serverR`]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v1.8.0/R/shinyapp.R#L242
[`shinyAppDir_appR`]: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/v1.8.0/R/shinyapp.R#L466

### Summary
I see a point in having it this way as `shinyApp` and its `print` are likely to be used within interactive sessions, and then tying a directory to that feels clunky. However, given that autoreload is an opt-in feature, then I think it would be safe to run watcher on `getwd()` directory - just like `runApp()` does by default. With that in mind I think it might be a bug to have these inconsistent (that's quite confusing!).

At the very least, I think this warrants a mention in the documentation as I haven't seen it documented anywhere between `shinyOptions`, `shinyApp`, and `runApp` - a venture into source code made me discover the findings described above.

title: Shiny is not releasing memory
description:
Hello,

We have detected that shiny app is not releasing memory when the user session ends, which we believe is a similar problem to this bug https://github.com/rstudio/plumber/issues/938 that we have posted.

We understand that in this case the problem is that R memory usage is growing because some objects are not released in a specific case.

We have tried to solve the problem by adding a gc() in the session$onSessionEnded, however it has not generated the expected result as we obtained with the postserialize in the plumber apis. We are not experts on how shiny destroys reactive objects, but we believe that this is where the problem lies because we assume that onSessionEnded happens after shiny destroys the objects.

We do not know if there is another way to implement gc() so that the memory is freed when the user session ends

Reading previous bugs we have found this bug https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1253 which we understand is similar

This problem has an impact when you always have a process active. This becomes relevant when you have the apps in a productive environment with high demand (hosted in posit connect for example).

Regards,

title: Should check for overlapping input and output binding IDs, and only enable error console in local development
description:
We merged #3946 so that apps with `insertUI` would no longer be broken with the dev version of Shiny, but we should also do the following:

- Check for cases where an input binding and an output binding have the same ID (currently we special case this and allow it).
- Only enable the error console when developing locally.
    - I think in R, it would be sufficient to check for `interactive()`. I'm not sure this will works in environments like VS Code, so we'll want to test there as well.

title: Client error console issue with dynamic bslib accordions
description:
I'm opening this here to triage, this is most likely another variant of #3944, or it could be another issue entirely.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Run [306-accordion-add-remove](https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/blob/fix-snaps-2023-11-28/inst/apps/306-accordion-add-remove/app.R) from shinycoreci
2. Remove one letter from the "Displayed sections" panel, e.g. remove `B`.
3. Add the removed panel back.
4. Click the checkbox "Allow multiple panels to be open" to deselect the setting.
5. Observe the client error console: _The following ID was repeated: "acc": 2 inputs_

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/5420529/5a978112-3c84-4df4-befc-03feb7ac6959

What's interesting is that adding the panel calls `accordion_panel_insert()`. Without this (e.g. if you skip step 3) the client error isn't displayed. Moreover, this error isn't shown when the `accordion_panel_insert()` happens, it's shown when `input$multiple` is toggled (step 4), which calls `renderUI()` to create an entirely new `accordion(id = "acc")`.

Also, if you repeat steps 2 and 3 `n` times before toggling `input$multiple`, the client error will report `n + 1` repeated `"acc"` input IDs.

title: Client error console and inserted/removed UI elements
description:
With #3931, when dynamically adding UI to a running app, it seems that the matching IDs checks run on the entire app and flag stable input/output elements as duplicated.

The following app ([shinycoreci: 111-insert-ui](https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/blob/main/inst/apps/111-insert-ui/)) reproduces the problem:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton('insertBtn', 'Insert'),
  actionButton('removeBtn', 'Remove'),
  tags$div(id = 'placeholder') #<< ui elements will be added here
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  ## keep track of elements inserted and not yet removed
  inserted <- c()

  observeEvent(input$insertBtn, {
    count <- input$insertBtn
    # give the inserted element a unique id so we can remove it later
    id <- paste0('txt', count)
    
    # push a new element in to the app
    insertUI(
      selector = '#placeholder',
      ui = tags$div(
        tags$p(paste('Element number', count)),
        id = id
      )
    )
    inserted <<- c(inserted, id)
  })

  observeEvent(input$removeBtn, {
    # pop last inserted element out of the app
    removeUI(
      selector = paste0('#', inserted[length(inserted)])
    )
    # and remove it from the list of inserted elements
    inserted <<- inserted[-length(inserted)]
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```

## With client error console


https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/5420529/3655c873-ec1e-4115-b5f9-3adf129fd7ee

## shiny 1.8.0

title: Client error console prevents apps with matching input and output IDs
description:
#3931 adds a check for matching input IDs that match output IDs, which was previously allowed. The following app runs with shiny 1.8.0 and will break in the 1.8.0.9000 because of the duplicate `caption` ID, which is used once for an input and once for an output.

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("caption", "Caption", "Data Summary"),
  textOutput("caption")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$caption <- renderText(input$caption)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

![The following ID was repeated: "caption": 1 input and 1 output](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/5420529/f4a2b7bf-2c5a-450c-8d46-9ee0ea21afc4)

This example is extracted from [shinycoreci: 003-reactivity](https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/blob/main/inst/apps/003-reactivity/app.R).

We may want to reduce the severity of the message to a warning in the case of `1 input and 1 output`, or we may want to remove this particular check altogether.

Personally, I think it's important that we continue to support overlapping IDs in input and outputs, e.g. `input$caption` and `output$caption`.

  responsive = FALSE,
  titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),
  fixedRow(
    column(12,
           wellPanel(
             fixedRow(
             column(4,
                    sliderInput(inputId = "a",
                                label = "slider 1",
                                min = 1,
                                max = 10,
                                value = 3)),
             column(4,
                    sliderInput(inputId = "b",
                                label = "slider 2",
                                min = 1,
                                max = 10,
                                value = 5)),
             column(4,
                    checkboxGroupInput(inputId = "c",
                                       label = "checkbox 1",
                                       choices = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
                                       selected = "a"))
           ))
           )
  )

)

server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
The shiny application layout guide (https://shiny.posit.co/r/articles/build/layout-guide/) describes the argument responsive = FALSE passed to fixedPage() as a way to turn off responsive boostrap features. This argument however doesn't work to turn off responsive bootstrap features. When the window in the example shiny app code above becomes smaller than 768px the wellPanel() is resized stacking the widgets. I didn't see anything about the responsive argument in the docs. Is this an issue with the function or does it need to be updated another way?

title: Pass a reason to onSessionEnded
description:
I currently already use session$token and onSessionEnded to track when a user starts a session and leaves a session and thus how many users are currently using an application. (Useful for knowing if it is safe to restart an application or if I am going to interrupt a user doing work!). However, aside from looking at the output log, I am having issues finding a way to detect why a session has ended (more specifically, if the session has ended with an error).

Using the likes of rlang::last_error is too global - if one session ends with an error, rlang::last_error will be set for all future sessions as well. Less interested if an output has produced an error which has been captured and returned to the user, more interested in an error which causes the session to crash/end prematurely.

Another alternative which could be useful would be to have an onSessionError handler.

In short: can the reason a session has ended (e.g. user disconnect or error) be accessible or passed through to onSessionEnded?

title: Slider does not fit in container `div` when `ticks=FALSE`

### System details

Browser Version: Not Applicable

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```

 [1] digest_0.6.33    later_1.3.1      R6_2.5.1         httpuv_1.6.11    fastmap_1.1.1    magrittr_2.0.3   cachem_1.0.8     memoise_2.0.1    htmltools_0.5.5  lifecycle_1.0.3  promises_1.2.0.1 cli_3.6.1        xtable_1.8-4     sass_0.4.6      
[15] jquerylib_0.1.4  compiler_4.3.1   tools_4.3.1      bslib_0.5.0      mime_0.12        ellipsis_0.3.2   Rcpp_1.0.11      rlang_1.1.1      jsonlite_1.8.7
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R

ui <- function(req){    
    shiny::textOutput("restored")    
}

server <- function(input, output, session){

    restored <- shiny::reactiveVal("NO")

    shiny::onRestore(function(state){
        restored("YES")
    })    
    
    output[["restored"]] <- shiny::renderText({paste("Went through onRestored", restored())})    
}

shiny::shinyApp(
    ui=ui,
    server = server,
    enableBookmarking = "url"
)
```

Open this application with `127.0.0.1:1234/` and `127.0.0.1:1234/?a`. In the first case it does not go through the onRestore function, as expected. But in the second it does go through the onRestore even when there is no bookmark, unexpected.

### Describe the problem in detail

According to the documentation is not clear when onRestore is called. https://shiny.posit.co/r/reference/shiny/0.14/onbookmark

In none of the cases in the example section is there a bookmark, usually identified by `_inputs_`, `state_id` and others.

It should be documented that any query string will trigger the `onRestore/d` functions. This becomes relevant when used in combination with, for example, `AzureAuth`, to authenticate an app https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/AzureAuth/vignettes/shiny.html

In that case the redirected url contains a `code` query parameter used to retrieve a token. In those cases the onRestore is called and can produce bugs as state does not contain the expected values, is empty.

Thanks!

title: Issue with dynamic UI in 1.7.5 (runs fine in 1.7.4)
description:
I started a discussion at the link below and @GShotwell suggested I post an issue:

https://discord.com/channels/1109483223987277844/1154545900211937340

The issue seems to be caused by a change in how dynamic UI elements are processed in 1.7.5.1 compared to 1.7.4. The issue occurs in every component where there are column names from a dataset are used to populate a dropdown after switching from one dataset to another (e.g., diamonds to titanic)

Steps to reproduce: 

1. Install radiant.model or radiant `install.packages("radiant")`
2. Start radiant from the Addins dropdown in Studio or using `radiant::radiant()`
3. Use shiny 1.7.5
4. Follow the steps in the (unlisted) video: https://youtu.be/RFQeFDKtk3c

To see what happens in 1.7.4.1 and all prior versions of shiny that I have used see below.

1. Install shiny 1.7.4.1: `remotes::install_version("shiny", "1.7.4.1")`
2. Follow the steps in the video above or view the (unlisted) video here: https://youtu.be/_7fOJemmtsw

As you can see in the first video, an error comes up in the JS console. There is only one `ui_reg_rvar`, a dynamic input that depends on the available data set, but somehow when a dataset is changed the JS code sees both the old one and refuses to create the new/updated one. Since most other inputs in _Model > Linear regression_ depend `ui_reg_rvar` being available, those don't render either. 

This is not just an issue with one component in Radiat. In every component that depends on a selected data to provide values for a dropdown, the same `duplicate binding for ID ...` error occurs.

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/2998956/8efca125-ad43-4ef9-b132-7d6023ecd2fb)

Is there way to turn off the new dynamic processing approach in shiny 1.7.5? That would be quickest way forward with students starting classes next week.

Thanks,

Vincent

title: observe + bindEvent generates an error when the code is long
selectize dropdown isn't dismiss-able after multiple `updateSelectInput()` calls
description:
Introduced by #3875. To reprex, run this app and notice how, after selecting items in the 1st dropdown, the dropdown doesn't go away when clicking elsewhere on the page:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  div(
    style = "display:flex",
    selectizeInput("foo", NULL, letters, multiple = TRUE),
    selectizeInput("bar", NULL, letters, multiple = TRUE)
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  observe({
    updateSelectizeInput(inputId = "foo", choices = letters[1:5])
    updateSelectizeInput(inputId = "bar", choices = letters[6:10])
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
``` 


Here are some really odd things to note about the conditions under which the reprex occurs:

1. More than one input/update is necessary.
2. Only the 1st dropdown is problematic.
3. The order of the updates matters. That is, if you update `"bar"` first, the problem disappears?!

description:
This report follows 
* https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/2514

I am opening another issue in shiny repo directly so that we can track on both side until we know what / where to adapt.

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/assets/6791940/118af49e-39b4-458a-a197-89bf8aa38dca)

This creates

output: ioslides_presentation
runtime: shiny

This R Markdown presentation is made interactive using Shiny. The viewers of the presentation can change the assumptions underlying what's presented and see the results immediately. 

To learn more, see [Interactive Documents](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html).

## Interactive Plot

```{r eruptions}

  sliderInput("bw_adjust", label = "Bandwidth adjustment:",
              min = 0.2, max = 2, value = 1, step = 0.2)
)

renderPlot({
  hist(faithful$eruptions, probability = TRUE, breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks),
       xlab = "Duration (minutes)", main = "Geyser eruption duration")
  
  dens <- density(faithful$eruptions, adjust = input$bw_adjust)
  lines(dens, col = "blue")
})
```

## Bullets

- Bullet 1
- Bullet 2
- Bullet 3

## R Output

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```
````

This is the commit that cause the issue from a git bisect: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/a06354040717de6a29644461bd6ed4665816f734

It is the build a the new shiny.js version as part of

* https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3666

Change is in NEWS as the following

> Closed https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/789: Dynamic UI is now rendered asynchronously, thanks in part to the newly exported Shiny.renderDependenciesAsync(), Shiny.renderHtmlAsync(), and Shiny.renderContentAsync(). Importantly, this means <script> tags are now loaded asynchronously (the old way used XMLHttpRequest, which is synchronous). In addition, Shiny now manages a queue of async tasks (exposed via Shiny.shinyapp.taskQueue) so that order of execution is preserved. (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3666)

Not sure what are the implication of that change for ioslides format. Maybe there is a conflict with the format dependencies. 

More details in 
* https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/2514

title: Regression in `updateSelectizeInput()` introduced by v0.15.2
Consider changes to eslint and prettier rules
description:
There were a few suggestions for eslint/prettier config changes brought up in https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/787 that would be nice to consider as a team. Here are some points for discussion. (Note I'm only wanting to open the door to a team conversation so these are all just conversation starters.)

1. eslint and prettier sometimes have different ideas about how indentation should be. I had to add `eslint-disable-next-line indent` (i.e. disable one of the linters) or they would each fail to approve the other's choice.

   @wch suggested we remove this eslint rule: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b054e45402ee31f1e58cb6e1d1f51f76f98a0aca/.eslintrc.yml#L33-L36

2. Another suggested eslint change proposed that we adjust `no-unused-vars` and turn off `no-empty-function` rules, see https://github.com/wch/shinycomponent/blob/2fd89b3c49991341d3d8368c673f6ff2f2ebbf35/js/.eslintrc#L15-L16

   ```json
   "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": ["warn", { "args": "none" }],
   "@typescript-eslint/no-empty-function": "off",
   ```

3. I'd also like to review the file naming conventions to allow `-` in file names, which I think is set by this rule https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b054e45402ee31f1e58cb6e1d1f51f76f98a0aca/.eslintrc.yml#L55-L57

4. Is it possible to require return types on functions except when the type is `void`? I think that requirement comes from somewhere in these rules. https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b054e45402ee31f1e58cb6e1d1f51f76f98a0aca/.eslintrc.yml#L24-L29

5. Do private methods have to start with leading underscore? https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b054e45402ee31f1e58cb6e1d1f51f76f98a0aca/.eslintrc.yml#L79-L82

title: Inform user that files in `R/` are being sourced
description:
I've been working in an app where I use code in `global.R` to source scripts in `R/`. I wanted to try deploying my app, and I wanted to make sure the logic of the app would run on the server before I tried configuring my deployed app to read from SQL.

To make testing easier, I overloaded some functions in `R/` in my `global.R` script like so:

``` r
# -- R/read_stuff.R -- #
read_stuff <- function() DBI::dbReadTable(connect_to_sql(), DBI::Id(schema = "foo", table = "bar"))
```

``` r
# -- global.R -- #
purrr::walk(list.files("R", full.names = TRUE), source)

# Temporary overloading to test deployment
read_stuff <- function() readr::read_csv("stuff.csv")
```

This seemed straightforward enough, but reloading my app, I found it was still using `read_stuff()` as defined in `R/read_stuff.R`. After some lengthy brow furrowing, I remembered that this is because `runApp()` not only sources `global.R`, `server.R` and `ui.R`, but also all R scripts in `R/` - `read_stuff()` was being defined *a third time* on app startup!

This feels to me like a prime example of 'spooky action'. The in-progress [Tidy design principles](https://design.tidyverse.org/spooky-action.html#how-can-i-remediate-spooky-actions) recommends remediating spooky action by advertising what's happening to the user. I'd therefore suggest that `runApp()` informs the user about which files it's sourcing. It may also be worth adding an additional argument like `appFiles` to give the user more obvious control. 

NB, `?runApp()` currently doesn't document that files in `R/` are automatically loaded. I had to go to the [online documentation](https://design.tidyverse.org/spooky-action.html#how-can-i-remediate-spooky-actions) for more info.

title: v1.7.5: How to know if an HTML element is a shiny input immediately when it appears in DOM? This was possible until 1.7.5
description:
In {shinyjs}, many functions try to infer whether an HTML element is a shiny input or not. This is necessary so that when a function is performed on an ID, if that ID corresponds to a shiny input then {shinyjs} will automatically know to move up the DOM tree to the container for the input (for example, if I want to hide an input that corresponds to a selectize input, hiding the ID itself will not achieve much, but hiding the `shiny-input-container` will).

The way {shinyjs} infers whether an element is an input or not is by checking if it contains the class `shiny-bound-input`. 

{shinyjs} also works on dynamically created elements, and for that to work, there is a mutation observer that checks if newly added elements are shiny inputs.

In shiny version 1.7.5, this mechanism broke. I haven't tested all inputs, but at least with select inputs, the `shiny-bound-input` class does not exist when the `<select>` element is added to the DOM dynamically. I don't see any other placeholder classes instead either. The class only appears after the selectizeJS renders the input. This is causing bugs https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/issues/270

This might have happened as a side effect of shiny using a different dynamic UI system. Is this specific change explicitly required for the new system, or could the `shiny-bound-input` class come back on initialization? If it cannot come back, can there be another class added to every input even before it gets fully renedered by its javascript?

title: `renderPlot()` does not work with `bindEvent()`
description:
### Problem description When I bind `renderPlot()` to a trigger button using `bindEvent()`, the `renderPlot()` expression is only ran once (on the first click). Subsequent clicks on the button have no effect ie. plot is not re-rendered. ### Reprex ```R library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( actionButton(inputId = "trigger", label = "Plot"), plotOutput("myPlot") ) server <- function(input, output, session) { output$myPlot <- renderPlot({ cols <- sample(names(iris)[1:4], size = 2, replace = FALSE) cat("`renderPlot()` expr executed.\n") plot( iris[, cols], col = iris[["Species"]], pch = 19 ) }) |> bindEvent(input$trigger) # initialize button click counter: counter <- reactiveVal(0L) observeEvent(input$trigger, { counter(counter() + 1) # print number of button clicks: cat("Clicks: ", counter(), "\n") }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` Might this be a possible bug or am I missing something? ### More details 1. The same reprex above will work as expected if I put the `renderPlot()` inside `observeEvent()`.
Show/hide the reprex using observeEvent() ```R library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( actionButton(inputId = "trigger", label = "Plot"), plotOutput("myPlot") ) server <- function(input, output, session) { # initialize button click counter: counter <- reactiveVal(0L) observeEvent(input$trigger, { counter(counter() + 1) # print number of button clicks: cat("Clicks: ", counter(), "\n") output$myPlot <- renderPlot({ cols <- sample(names(iris)[1:4], size = 2, replace = FALSE) cat("`renderPlot()` expr executed.\n") plot( iris[, cols], col = iris[["Species"]], pch = 19 ) }) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ```
2. For comparison purposes, `renderTable()` works fine with `bindEvent()`, with the table output changing each time the button is clicked.
Show/hide renderTable() reprex ```R library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( actionButton(inputId = "trigger", label = "Trigger"), tableOutput(outputId = "tbl") ) server <- function(input, output, session) { output$tbl <- renderTable({ cols <- sample(x = names(iris)[1:4], size = 2, replace = FALSE) cat("`renderTable()` expr executed.\n") iris[, cols] |> head() }) |> bindEvent(input$trigger) # initialize button click counter: counter <- reactiveVal(0L) observeEvent(input$trigger, { counter(counter() + 1) # print number of button clicks: cat("Clicks: ", counter(), "\n") }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ```

title: Support HTML for the `update` methods that have a `label` arg
description:
Hi Shiny devs,
It would be awesome if the `update` methods allowed HTML for the `label` arg similar to the UI component call. This currently errors if a `shiny.tag` is passed to `label` on the `update` method. Wrapping the tag with `htmltools::doRenderTags`, the `update` method escapes the HTML and shows it as is (shown in this example):
```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  shiny::sliderInput(
    "slider",
    label = tags$span("Some HTML"),
    min = 0,
    max = 100,
    value = 55,
    step = 1,
    inline = TRUE
  ),
  actionButton(
    "update",
    "Update the label"
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  observeEvent(input$update, {
    shiny::updateSliderInput(
      inputId = "slider",
      label = htmltools::doRenderTags(tags$p("Some mo HTML"))
    )
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: NavbarPage could use a sticky-top and sticky-bottom position argument
description:
In the documentation for navbarPage, there is a note as follows:
`Note that using "fixed-top" or "fixed-bottom" will cause the navbar to overlay your body content, unless you add padding, e.g.: \code{tags$style(type="text/css", "body {padding-top: 70px;}`
I've been reworking the CSS for an app, and instead of adding padding I've made the navbar stick to the top while still occupying space so that the other elements behave as expected, using 
`position: -webkit-sticky;
  position: sticky;
top: 0;`
for the nav element.

This would eliminate the need to pad the element by default. Wouldn't this make a default that is more in line with user expectations? Or at least provide useful extra options for the `position` parameter in navbarPage?
Thanks for your hard work.

title: Use `npm` and `yarn` scripts for managing all bundled dev dependencies
description:
Currently, several update scripts in `tools/` will download a bundled dependency (i.e. a dependency that is ultimately included in the shiny R package) from GitHub. We should instead declare these dependencies as dev dependencies and use yarn/npm to provision the correct version.

From https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3788:

> Another approach, which may actually be a bit better, is to:
> 
> * Keep these entries in packages.json
> * Get rid of scripts like `tools/updateStrftime.R`
> * Update the TS build scripts so that they copy the JS files (like strftime-min.js) from node_modules/ to inst/www/shared/, apply patches if needed, and update the version files in the R/ directory.

This does mean we would reverse #3788 and add these packages back into `package.json`, but we should also then avoid downloading deps directly from GitHub, esp. if we use a build script via `yarn` to replace the update scripts in `tools/`.

title: R-devel raises warnings on package load, because of `as.numeric_version()`
description:
I just got an email from CRAN:

*****

A recent PR (<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=18548>) showed
that whereas version inputs to numeric_version() and package_version()
were always documented to be "suitable character vectors" (or numeric
vesion objects), the implementation also accepted numeric inputs via
as.character() coercion, the results of which however are (at least
currently) dependent on the setting of the OutDec option.  Given that
numeric input is certainly error-prone, imagine

```
  as.numeric_version(1.20)
  as.numeric_version(1.5-1)
```

R Core has decided it would be best to gradually phase out such inputs.

Thus, With c84610 R-devel now *warns* about such inputs, which will
typically not show in the check results (but immediately giving errors
would cause too much disruption).

Now in shiny, you have

```
  register_upgrade_message("htmlwidgets", 1.5)
```

in your .onLoad() in globals.R, which should really be

```
  register_upgrade_message("htmlwidgets", "1.5")
```

Can you please fix asap?  (This causes warnings whenever the shiny
namespace is loaded ...)

```R
library(shiny)

  actionButton("btn_one", "Button 1"),
  actionButton("btn_two", "Button 2"),
  textOutput("text1"),
  textOutput("text2"),
  textOutput("text3")

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  observeEvent(input$btn_one, ignoreInit = F, {
    output$text1 <- renderText("Button 1 was clicked")
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$btn_two, ignoreInit = F, {
    output$text2 <- renderText("Button 2 was clicked")
  })

  })

```

See the minimal example above. When listening for more than one input, the observeEvent triggers although none of the inputs changed. title: Improve `selectInput()` docs for `NULL` handling when `multiple = TRUE` and `selected = NULL`
description:
I had the exact same issue as outlined in this SO post: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61333206/detecting-a-selectinput-value-change-to-null-in-r-shiny

I feel as though the default behavior here, when multiple = TRUE in a selectInput, needs to be observing and handling NULLs better and more explicitly, especially if _selected_ also equals NULL.

I just find it very opaque that the change from 1 selection to NULL is not being registered as a change by observers unless they have been explicitly set to have ignoreNULL set to TRUE--it means many forms of validation will fail silently currently, as checks for NULL won't even occur if they are inside the observers....

I know that to some this "bug" is a "feature," but I think a warning() might at least be justified to give some flag to folks that this is the default behavior.

title: Destroy reactive domain and all its observers
description:
By briefly skimming through the source code it seems that all observers/reactives within a module are registered to a scoped reactive domain (see https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/1b7709411beeb345af54d159c0af6528fd542525/R/modules.R#L190-L198) so that they can automatically be deactivated once the reactive domain itself is destroyed. Is that something that happens automatically? I doubt so because servers do not need to return anything to stay active (they do not go out of scope).

Is there a way to trigger the destruction of that scoped reactive domain, or at least list all observers attached to it to call `$destroy()` on each of them explicitly??

Related:
  - https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2374
  - https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2281

title: Floating Label Inputs
description:
It seems common for input fields (text, numeric, etc.) to have "floating" labels, where the label is either inside the input box itself and "floats" out of the way when users input a value. Bootstrap, at least v5, has a version of this built in. I've been able to use this in shiny but only with hackery. It would be nice to create these inputs directly and I'm happy to help out.

I'm not sure if this is the right place to bring up such a feature since Shiny seems to have to support old versions of bootstrap where this isn't possible by default. But it seems at least worth bringing up since the style is so common.

title: Calling `el.trigger("hidden")` in JavaScript doesn't work on elements that are being animated to be hidden
description:
Originally reported in https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/issues/266

When an element is being hidden from the DOM, a `trigger("hidden")` javacript call needs to be made on that element, to notify shiny to not render it anymore. The classic way to hide an element is using the `.hide()` method. However, it seems like elements that are being hidden using animation javascript do not properly get hidden in the reactive graph.  Example:

```r
library(shiny)

jscode <- "
Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('hide', function(m) { $('#out').fadeOut(); $('#out').trigger('hidden'); });
Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('show', function(m) { $('#out').fadeIn(); $('#out').trigger('shown'); });
"

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script(HTML(jscode)),
  actionButton("hide", "hide"),
  actionButton("show", "show"),
  numericInput("num", "num", 5),
  textOutput("out")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$out <- renderText({
    print("rendering")
    input$num
  })
  observeEvent(input$hide, session$sendCustomMessage('hide', list()))
  observeEvent(input$show, session$sendCustomMessage('show', list()))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

In this code, an element is being hidden using jquery's `fadeOut()`. You can see that despite triggering the `hidden` event, the output still gets rendered. A similar thing happens when using `slideUp()` instead of `fadeOut()`.

It seems that if you make the animation very fast, for example using `fadeOut(5)` (5 milliseconds), then the trigger does hold.

I noticed that if I add a callback function to the animation `fadeOut(500, function() { $(this).trigger('hidden'); })` then it does work correctly. Because of this, my theory is that when `hidden` is triggered, shiny looks at the element, and only acts if the element has `display:none`.

title: [Feature request] Allow runApp() to use port value to produce the app URL
description:
## Problem

I've got an older Shiny app that is launched via following command:
```
shiny::runApp('my_app_location', port = 4476)
```
This used to produce a URL looking like this: https://rstudio.io/p/4476/. This had an advantage of being static - it did not change when I restarted a session and was always dependent on the value of the port.

Recently I attempted to upgrade this Shiny app to the latest version of the library. However I am facing a problem where the URL does not use the port value anymore. Instead an 8-character alphanumerical code is produced, looking like this: https://rstudio.io/p/dec57e8d/. Unfortunately this code is not static anymore, but instead changes everytime the session is restarted, and that does not suit my purposes.

## Feature request

I am requesting to consider bringing back the ability to use the original behavior as described above. 

Based on what I was able to understand from the `runApp()` source code, the current behavior is caused by [this line of code](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/main/R/runapp.R#L144). _(I might be wrong though, please keep in mind that I am a simple R user, not a developer)_

My idea is to have a new parameter added to the `runApp()` function, called e.g. `useStaticAppToken` (with default value equal to `FALSE`) which would then be reflected later in the code like this:
```
if (isTRUE(useStaticAppToken)) {
  shinyOptions(appToken = port)
} else {
  shinyOptions(appToken = createUniqueId(8))
}
```

However, I am not sure if this would really solve my problem, and if this wouldn't pose some deeper implications in the codebase. 

Thanks a lot in advance!

title: Navbar isn't accessible - accessibility broken on moving from bootstrap to shiny because invalid HTML generated
description:
Hi, I have noticed a problem with the accessibility of navbars (specifically, the ability to navigate using only a keyboard and no mouse) created by `navbarPage` in shiny apps. As a minimal example consider the `app.R` ```r library(shiny) # Define UI for application that draws a histogram ui <- navbarPage("App Title", tabPanel("Plot"), tabPanel("Summary"), tabPanel("Table") ) # Define server logic required to draw a histogram server <- function(input, output) { } # Run the application shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server) ``` which produces the html ```html
App Title
  • Plot
  • Summary
  • Table
``` When using the Tab button to navigate through the nav bar you are initially able to tab through each tab in order and select any one. However, once a tab has previously been selected this is no longer available when tabbing through the navbar. The reason for this is that when a tab is selected the `class="active"` tag is added to the corresponding `
  • ` element, as in the Plot tab in the example html above. You can see this in the bootstrap docs [here](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.0/components/navbar/#nav) . When the tab is then navigated away from the "active" class is removed. For the shiny app this leaves just `
  • ` , rather than returning it to `
  • `, as it was before. This is now invalid html and the item is skipped when tabbing through the navbar from now on. This doesn't happen in bootstrap because all \
  • items also have the "nav-item" class, so they are left as `
  • ` afterwards. In shiny, however, this class is removed at [line 430 in bootstrap.R](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62bb21d5b6eb34a5701f849c78a04ff5efd5b46d/R/bootstrap.R#LL430C1-L430C1). This has the effect that invalid html is being created, and accessibility is broken. The same happens with items in dropdowns within the navbar. Would you please be able to fix this problem by including a different class for all these elements, even if you don't want the nav-item class to be included?

title: Add hooks around dynamic UI lifecycle
description:
## Background

We often need to run a small amount of initialization code for custom components, e.g. in bslib for sidebars, cards and accordions. In a static context, we could, in theory, just use `$(document).ready()` and initialize everything once on page load.

In Shiny, though, we need to support dynamically inserted UI, where the elements appear on the page either via `uiOutput()` or `insertUI()` after the initial startup. While our immediate use case is initialization, we could also imagine having a similar need to run clean up code when UI elements are removed with `removeUI()` or replaced via a new `uiOutput()` update.

Both `uiOutput()` and `insertUI()` (in R) result in client-side calls to [`renderContentAsync()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62bb21d5b6eb34a5701f849c78a04ff5efd5b46d/srcts/src/shiny/render.ts#L38). While this function kicks off a lot of related work to handle html dependencies and other nuances, the key step of adding the new HTML to the DOM is performed by [`renderHTML()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62bb21d5b6eb34a5701f849c78a04ff5efd5b46d/srcts/src/shiny/singletons.ts#L16). That insertion step is sandwiched between output unbinding (if replacing) and input/output binding post-insertion. 

## Other use cases

* In a recent issue, a user described a situation where they know that the UI insertion step will take some time to complete and they'd like to be informed when that work is complete.
    
   https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3348#issuecomment-958814151
    

## Proposal

My proposal is to trigger events for two key steps in the `renderHtml()` process:

1. When an element is going to be removed, we emit `shiny:render.willremove` on the children of the element whose inner HTML will change.

2. After the content is inserted, we emit `shiny:render.inserted` on the content that was added.

3. As an optional third event, we could emit `shiny:render.complete` from `renderContentAsync()` after the input/output binding occurs.

Adding the first two events requires a small change in `renderHtml()`. Currently, it receives `html` [as a string](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62bb21d5b6eb34a5701f849c78a04ff5efd5b46d/srcts/src/shiny/singletons.ts#L17) that's processed by `processHtml()` where it's [returned as a string of HTML](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62bb21d5b6eb34a5701f849c78a04ff5efd5b46d/srcts/src/shiny/singletons.ts#L80) having caught singletons and items destined for `<head>`.

The change would be to update `processHtml()` to instead use jQuery to convert the `html` string to HTMLElements using `html: $(val)`, knowing that we'll use jQuery for insertion in `renderHtml()`.

```js
// instead of this
const processed = processHtml(html);

// we need to do this
const processed = processHtml(html);
processed.html = $(processed.html);
```

This way, `processed.html` will contain references to the elements themselves. Later when we call, e.g. 

```js
$(el).before(processed.html);
```

jQuery will here returns a reference to `el` and we'd have to go find the added elements ourselves. When `processed.html` refers to the DOM elements, after insertion we can call

```js
processed.html.trigger('shiny:render.inserted')
```

and anyone who needs to know about the inserted UI can listen for the `shiny:render.inserted` event.

```js
$(document).on('shiny:render.inserted', function(ev) {
  const inserted = ev.target
  // process inserted elements
})
```

The event-based method naturally solves the problem of wanting to limit the initialization to specific components

```js
$(document).on('shiny:render.inserted', '.my-component', function(ev) {
  // only process newly-inserted UI with .my-component class
})
```

Update: this is actually less useful than I first thought. Because `.my-component` can be anywhere within the inserted UI, you can't expect a filter like this to work. Instead you'd have to `$(ev.target).find('.my-component')`. I still think it's reasonable to include the `shiny:render.inserted` event, but in practice `shiny:render.complete` would probably be most used.

The final `shiny:render.complete` event could be helpful. E.g. in the case of the linked issue above where the user would like to know when a `renderUI()` step is fully complete, this event could be helpful. To emit from the inserted elements we'd have to pass the DOM references back up to `renderContentAsync()`, but that seems reasonably straight-forward.

## Alternative

I gave some thought to another process where the JavaScript author would need to register callbacks to be executed at various steps in the html-insertion lifecycle. An advantage of this approach is that you could do more work on the HTML prior to insertion, rather than just after insertion. 

In the end, I think it would be a more complicated system to set up and the advantage would be small. It would also be a Shiny-focused solution. In the above approach, component authors can write one "on load" function that can be used to in both `DOMContentLoaded` and `shiny:render.inserted` events.

## Questions

Most of my questions are around naming. Here are some other things I've thought of:

* Use `shiny:renderhtml` as the prefix. This is more verbose but also more specific, where `shiny:render` might be confused with many other actions in Shiny.
  * `shiny:renderhtml.willremove`
  * `shiny:renderhtml.inserted`
  * `shiny:renderhtml.complete`

* Use names that might be associated with other common frameworks, e.g.
  * `shiny:render.willUnmount` (but I think this sounds more like unbind + remove than just remove)
  * `shiny:render.mounted`
  * `shiny:render.complete`

* Camel case (`shiny:renderHtml`, `shiny:render.willRemove`) or all lowercase (`shiny:renderhtml`, `shiny:render.willremove`)?

* Event name pattern: I like `{namespace}:{event}.{type}` but all of our other events are `shiny:{event}`. E.g. we don't differentiate between input/output `bound` events, but it's something we could consider doing with `shiny:bound.input` or `shiny:bound.output`.

title: tags$head() doesn't work in Rmarkdown
description:
In regular shiny apps, using `tags$head()` will result in the contents going into the `<head>` tag. For example:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(tags$style("body { background: red; }"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The resulting page has the style tag in the head.  But in Rmd documents, `tags$head()` seems to not do anything, and the contents get treated as text. Example:

````r
---
runtime: shiny
---

```{r}
tags$head(tags$style("body { background: red; }"))
```
````

That does not result in anything useful.

If instead of `tags$head()` I use any shiny tag such as `tagList()` or `div()`, then the contents do get inserted into the document, but at that spot instead of the `<head>` tag.

Is there a technical reason why `tags$head()` can't work in Rmd, or is this simply a bug?

title: Add option to remove aria-live attribute in textOutput
description:
Since 921650f, `textOutput` and similar functions have automatically been augmented with `aria-live="polite"`. I think this is a good default but I haven't been able to find any obvious way to override it. Take this toy app: ``` r ui = basicPage( tags$p( "Some text." ), tags$p( "Your random number is ", textOutput("random", container = tags$span), `aria-live` = "polite", `aria-atomic` = "true" ), tags$p( "Some more text." ) ) server = function(input, output, session) { output$random <- renderText({ invalidateLater(as.integer(10000), session) rnorm(1) }) } ``` Because `textOutput` automatically has `aria-live="polite"` added to it, the HTML markup for the middle paragraph looks like: ``` html

Your random number is -0.2228559

``` It seems like, with VoiceOver on a Mac at least, the inner `aria-live="polite"` usually "wins" and only the random number is read out, not the full paragraph that provides useful context. I [made a CodePen](https://codepen.io/timbrock/pen/RweaPOR) with several variations on this theme and, after the initial populating of the random numbers, VoiceOver only reads out the full paragraph for option C in Chrome and options C and E in Firefox. (That E doesn't work in Chrome seems like a browser bug.) That _does_ mean I can get the desired behaviour in Firefox by adding: ``` r tags$script( '$("#random").attr("aria-live", "false")' ) ``` but it would be simpler (for me, at least) and more cross-browser/cross-AT friendly if there was an extra argument to the `textOutput` function that prevented the `aria-live` attribute being added in the first place.
