title: grouped selectInput of length 1 doesn't work correctly.
description: This issue has been reported [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57248427/grouped-select-input-with-only-one-item) and [here](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3706) The issue happens when we pass a grouped `selectInput` of length 1. I will copy the example from the earlier github issue. ``` library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel( selectInput( "value", label = "Select Value", choices = list( "Group A" = c("a", "b"), "Group B" = c("x"), "Group C" = c("1", "2") ) ) ), mainPanel( h3("Selected Value:"), textOutput("selected") ) ) ) server <- function(input, output) { output$selected <- renderText({input$value}) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` As you can see "Group B" loses its "group" status here. This can be fixed by changing `c("x")` to `list("x")` but I feel this is still a bug. The documentation at `?selectInput` mentions > choices - List of values to select from. If elements of the list are named, then that name — rather than the value — is displayed to the user. It's also possible to group related inputs by providing a named list whose elements are (either named or unnamed) lists, vectors, or factors. In this case, the outermost names will be used as the group labels (leveraging the ⁠⁠ HTML tag) for the elements in the respective sublist. See the example section for a small demo of this feature. So named and unnamed vectors are allowed so the original example should work.

title: downloadHandler's filename not updating reactively
description:
### What I did

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(
    inputId = "filename",
    label = "Filename",
    choices = c("iris", "mtcars")
  ),
  downloadButton(outputId = "dnld")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$dnld <- downloadHandler(
    filename = paste0(input$filename, ".csv"),
    content = function(file) {
      write.csv(x = get(input$filename), file = file)
    },
    contentType = "text/csv"
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### What happened

When I change the selectInput value to 'mtcars' and click on the download button, the downloaded file is named 'iris.csv' but the content is that of 'mtcars'.

### What I expected to happen

I expected the name of the downloaded file to correspond to the value of the selectInput. eg. If the selected value is 'mtcars', the name of the file should be 'mtcars.csv'

I expected `downloadHandler()` to pick the filename reactively as it does with the content (Note that I've used `input$filename` in both the filename and the content)

### A "hack" to solve the issue

Putting `downloadHandler()` inside an observer works well:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(
    inputId = "filename",
    label = "Filename",
    choices = c("iris", "mtcars")
  ),
  downloadButton(outputId = "dnld")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$filename, {
    output$dnld <- downloadHandler(
      filename = paste0(input$filename, ".csv"),
      content = function(file) {
        write.csv(x = get(input$filename), file = file)
      },
      contentType = "text/csv"
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Final remarks

Is this a bug or is an observer required for the `downloadHandler()`'s filename to pick up (subsequent) values of an input?

  * dygraphs: Can't install dependency xts (>= 0.9-7)

```
This seems to be caused by this recent update to `xts`: https://github.com/joshuaulrich/xts/commit/1ea13d4b787abb97a03e6741d6ea9c02e483706f

Therefore, any workflow runs (including the current master) fail.

title: req(cancelOutput=TRUE) does not trigger the JavaScript event 'shiny:error'
description:
Looking through the JS events that get triggered on output elements https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/js-events.html , it seems that `shiny:error` should be called when an output errors.

Quote from the docs:

> The last event to be fired for x is shiny:value (or shiny:error if the recalculation resulted in an error)

This is not the case when `cancelOutput` is used inside a failing `req()`.

Example:

```r
library(shiny)

js <- "
$(document).on('shiny:outputinvalidated', function(event) {
  console.log('outputinvalidated ' + event.target.id)
})
$(document).on('shiny:error', function(event) {
  console.log('error ' + event.target.id)
})
$(document).on('shiny:value', function(event) {
  console.log('value ' + event.target.id)
})
"

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script(js),
  actionButton("go", "go"),
  textOutput("text1"),
  textOutput("text2"),
  textOutput("text3")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$text1 <- renderText({
    input$go
    req(TRUE)
    "test"
  })
  output$text2 <- renderText({
    input$go
    req(FALSE, cancelOutput = FALSE)
    "test"
  })
  output$text3 <- renderText({
    input$go
    req(FALSE, cancelOutput = TRUE)
    "test"
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Every time you click the button to refresh the outputs, the javascript console will show the following output. You can see that the output with the canceled output does not trigger a value or an error.

```
outputinvalidated text1
outputinvalidated text2
outputinvalidated text3
value text1
error text2
```

There are a few paragraphs above the full list that talk about some of the common events, but there is no clear definition for each one of the events. It would be useful to clearly explain under what condition each of the different events is triggered.

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(car)

empty_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_text(aes(x=0, y=0, label="Please load data"))

ui <- fluidPage(# Application title
  titlePanel("Test BoxCox"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput("datafile", "Data table",
                accept = ".csv"),
      textInput("model", "Model formula", placeholder="Y~A*B*C"),

      tabsetPanel(
        tabPanel("Box-Cox",
                 h2("Box-Cox plot"),
                 plotOutput("boxcox")
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  data <- reactive({
    if (!is_null(input$datafile$datapath)) {
      read_csv2(input$datafile$datapath)
    }
  })
  
  model <- reactive({
    if (!is_null(data())) {
      tryCatch(
        {
          lm(formula=input$model, data=data())
        },
        error = \(e) {NULL}
      )
    }
  })
  
  output$boxcox <- renderPlot({
    if (is_null(model())) return(empty_plot)
    model() %>% boxCox()
  })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The plot fails rendering with `Error in stats::model.frame: object 'input' not found`. Looks like the lazy evaluation of `model()` is the problem.

title: JS error: `i.stopPropagation is not a function` in ion.rangeSlider
description: To reproduce, run this app and open it in the browser: ```R runExample('01_hello', launch.browser=FALSE, display.mode = "normal") ``` To trigger the error, click on a blank space in the app, then press Tab. (I think it is triggered when a hidden element gets focus.) This is happening in the `pointerClick` method here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/0c177d30dc11cb2aed1612db456158b31306af9a/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/js/ion.rangeSlider.js#L864-L866 It in turn is being called from `pointerFocus` -- but that function, instead of passing in a real Event object, passes in an object that has two properties: `preventDefault` and `pageX`: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/0c177d30dc11cb2aed1612db456158b31306af9a/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/js/ion.rangeSlider.js#L742-L757 The call to `e.stopPropagation` that is raising the error is something we added in this patch: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/0c177d30dc11cb2aed1612db456158b31306af9a/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/js/ion.rangeSlider.js So we can simply update the patch to contain an empty function for `stopPropagation.`

title: Documentation: how to create action buttons in UI built entirely with HTML?
description:
As far as I can tell, there is only one page documenting how to build a shiny app's UI entirely using HTML : https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/html-ui.html

In this article, it says that "HTML form elements" are bound using the "name" attribute, and that outputs are bound using an "id". 

This made me believe that action buttons should use a "name" because they behave the same way as inputs, not outputs. However, from trial and error, it seems like buttons need to use an "id" rather than a "name".

title: Documentation: session$close() is not documented as a function on the session object
description: I was looking for a way to kill the current session. The documentation of the `session` object provides many functions that we can call, but it does not mention `close()`. I had to dig out a Google Groups message from Joe from 2015 to know that it's possible :) https://groups.google.com/g/shiny-discuss/c/7i5GLrybPwk?pli=1

title: Cannot test export values if any of them fail a `req()`
description:
This is possibly a {shiny} issue rather than a {shinytest2} issue. If it is, feel free to transfer it to that repo.

I discovered this when trying to test a shiny module that returns several reactives, and some of them may not pass a `req()` test. Here is a simpler example:

```r
library(shiny)

app <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(actionButton("go", "go")), 
  function(input, output, session) {
    num <- reactive({
      req(input$go)
      input$go
    })
    exportTestValues(
      num = num()
    )
  }
)

driver <- shinytest2::AppDriver$new(app)
driver$get_values(export = TRUE)
```

Results in an error:

```
Error in `app_httr_get()`:
! Unable request data from server
```

I understand why this happens, because `req()` is technically an error. But it's meant to be a silent error that we can work with, so I think some special value should be used instead of failing.

title: `onStop()` issues
description:
* `onStop()` should return invisibly.
* The documentation description should be more clear that it's called either on app exit or session end _depending on where_ you put it.

title: Add `session$click()` to `testServer()`
description:
Currently, it's very awkward to test action buttons using `testServer()`, because there is no dedicated function to clicking on them. They are treated as regular inputs, so if I want to simulate a click, I need to manually set its input value to the right integer with `session$setInputs()`.

It would be very useful to have a `session$click()` that would work for buttons

title: Inputs are not restored to original state after reload in firefox
description:
Shiny (latest CRAN version) inputs are restored after pressing the reload button in firefox 108.0.1 (64-bit) on Windows 10.

[Expected behaviour](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reconnecting.html):

> If you reload a shiny application by clicking on your browser’s Reload button, it will start a new session on both the client and the server, losing the state on both sides.

This is the case in chrome.

Example coming from [here](https://stackoverflow.com/q/75006966/9841389):

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("select", "Values", LETTERS[1:5], selected='A'),
  radioButtons("radio", "Radio", LETTERS[1:5], selected='A'),
  checkboxGroupInput("check", "Checkbox", LETTERS[1:5], selected='A'),
  textOutput("serverout")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$serverout <- renderText({
    print(reactiveValuesToList(input))
    paste(input$select, input$radio, paste(input$check, collapse = ", "), sep = " | ")
    })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Code that displays correctly when run on my local machine, but fails when run on shinyapps.io or from a docker container
```R
library(shiny)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

print(sessionInfo())
ui<-fluidPage(plotOutput("plot"),
              plotOutput("plot2"))
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  df<-data.frame(x=0:10,

  output$plot<-renderPlot({

      ggplot()+

      scale_shape_manual(values="\U0001F37C")+

  })
  # plot using built in ggplot shapes
  output$plot2<-renderPlot({
    df%>%
      ggplot()+
      geom_text(aes(x=x,y=y),label="\U0001F37C",size=20,
                family = "Lucida Sans Unicode")+

shinyApp(ui, server)

Example dockerfile for building the app that's also failing:
```

The code example above runs and displays fine when I run the shinyapp on my local machine, but the unicode shapes do not display in the plot either when I deploy the app to shinyapps.io, or when I build the app into a docker container and run it from the container.

library(shiny)

If `multiple = F`, spurious empty strings will be sent instead. [shinylive reprex](https://shinylive.io/r/editor/#h=0&-UGw1G43q70+P3+gNw8WBeNB5HBSg23x2YD2pSmRxOqPO6Jaegg8hgTAJDyeJLePlw-lwAGY6StGZs2Rzsgc+KhagYOrYCNwLt0AG44opi43dJSpYxwXoAFSwUPSsisapy9KOAC84ABJCBa0gWdVWfn4vCcqL0PFxe4emzexBBTn6oi0AhwcaQmHJBFWYkvTNKOicQOoKLp7hEagmArOVwAWSgAGsHFAlnGXhgu7sQm6lEZaEagwclCbGGYbDA7XAAB6kADytQDjTy8m08M5SJeKLOjQI9hYBO+B4K7XX7N7CO4jHYff1oKb9CIM4A4owiNc-cvXPqm0fuA+T4zkob4fqgShfrUvR8HQEAOM4DpOn2zADkQO4kJwjQoQSWBQKhSjoWMvQpmmGYxmA0GiHw8FKIhzpZLIIjNIwY6qBooTyBA3LnJqtS4EMS58e2nCGCQAhKCAIREFIFrpCaZDsLxpAACQYu0XSMPxknBko1xGFA5ADEqtDepBgbNCJLz8aGxGVqRhb2HU3ScMAPiIHKAC6-EgmC5H0L0zGsc4SmqRajAGDaLoHHpBlwN8AEEI+z6gZ+-q1FwGaiRA1mENwf54EoJHpg5LTkIwLluZ53lxmsfk9jpMXkLhqGEZhFlZTl2EFUVZHOI5ZUVe5XntkqtV1mA-kXuqAC+jHqtJgVwHJFCBiFGJYt0Wmco1cBGQyJm+ml5mZVZfTLLZqbFXEyTpHadrpFgqSuYgACsw2LbWShrWFEUmFFVg7fFgHJe+qXLu1p0-nlF32ddt33Y9z1vf9umoPpTV4ccrUZZZJCdXhMNXc4N13Q9T1ucjISzSIUkySxS3yatR2hVcNzhcsW0NWjsV7V6h3gydeNnXihO9UoJMI+TiAAGzvTVTKuN8AVhXE330+zkXbdz5BA4lQEpagZk4x1fS-qLhYS2Tz2y9Vo0K2AStTSOO3NVjpwYcbkNgF1--He7ACDiO4FvMRewlDCMjl-IYP8b7-zvjXIoQCDiiNfhI7RmFZFaBLII2MlciiJgKmrMctdP4KMvnmQSKlVzaDYvvCgNY3CMD4IGbSI4D4AEdJHSNfp-ZMBlAkv30dVcCg8aaryjtw6OPA+CsESOgdgig4iKGqpXZwH1ZB4DAKQVg2IqDkDnGAaaHkgA)

### Describe the problem in detail

This issue occurs when trying to work around the bug described in #3732 and other similar tickets. When the server runs `updateSelectizeInput()` with a list of choices and a non-empty selection, the client will completely clear the selectize and send a spurious empty input to the server before it actually sets the new value. In this repro, you can see the spurious empty input both in the shiny trace log as `RECV {"method":"update","data":{"sel":[]}}` and in the application as the NULL input detector is triggered. This is an issue in my actual application code since I have observers that listen for a NULL value on the selectize, and clear other parts of the page assuming that the user has intentionally emptied the selection.

The behavior I expected was for updateSelectizeInput(..., selected = 7) to cause the next input sent to the server to be a 7.

`freezeReactiveValue` does not solve this issue.

It contains 4 files/functions:

demoGlobals <- function()
{

  my_global_value <- TRUE
  
  message("Completed demoGlobals..")
  
}

    server  = demoServer()

### Describe the problem in detail

It looks like 'force(ui)' is happening before `onStart` is being executed.

title: Session ID/token exposed with downloadHandler
description:
Hello

When creating a link to download files using downloadHandler, the session ID/token is exposed in the link. This seems to be generally regarded as a serious security issue - see details at the link below:

https://owasp.org/www-project-web-security-testing-guide/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/06-Session_Management_Testing/04-Testing_for_Exposed_Session_Variables

Is it possible to use a different token/ID for links using downloadHandler? Or could you provide more information about how this might not be a serious security issue?

```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(img(src = "test.png"))

server <- function(session, input, output) {}

print(shinyApp(ui, server))
```

With the following working directory:

```
.
├── app.r
└── www
    └── test.png
```

### Describe the problem in detail

Running this Shiny app results in a page that shows only a placeholder icon. The image URL returns a 404 HTTP status. The image is a valid PNG file with read permissions, and Shiny *can* successfully serve this file by adding an explicit resource handler via `addResourcePath('prefix', file.path(getwd(), 'www'))`.

*How* the Shiny app is run does not matter; none of the following options works:

* Inside RStudio via “Run App” button
* Inside RStudio by executing the source file `app.r`
* In an interactive R terminal (manually executing the code of the `app.r` file)
* In a shell terminal via `Rscript app.r`

The issue exists across operating systems (Linux, Windows) and R versions, and at least with both Shiny 1.7.2 and Shiny 1.7.3.

**Some (but not all!) other people *can* see the file when running the minimal example above.** This indicates some machine-specific configuration, but I’m at a loss how to find it.

When intercepting `shiny:::staticHandler` calls I can see that the function is called once while constructing the Shiny app object and then repeatedly when loading the app:

* for the `sys.www.root` (i.e. `system_file('www', package='shiny')`)
* repeatedly (!) for the shared root, `LIBPATH/shiny/www/shared`
* for the bootstrap resource path (`LIBPATH/shiny/www/shared/bootstrap`)

… but never for the app’s `www` directory. Based on this I believe that there is fundamentally no chance that the resource `/test.png` could ever be served by my minimal Shiny app, despite the fact that it works for other people on their systems. And [the documentation](https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/1.4.0/resourcePaths.html) states that

> Static files under the `www/` directory are automatically made available under a request path that begins with `/`.

So this *should* work.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/20cc8e26b5e366286caf47f65d9670fbe45412dd/srcts/src/shiny/init.ts#L281

- but has **non-zero** `offsetHeight`, so is sending `hidden: false` from:

```
  $(".shiny-bound-output").each(function () {
    const id = getIdFromEl(this);

    if (isHidden(this)) {
      initialValues[".clientdata_output_" + id + "_hidden"] = true;
    } else {
      lastKnownVisibleOutputs[id] = true;
      initialValues[".clientdata_output_" + id + "_hidden"] = false;
    }
  });
 ```
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/20cc8e26b5e366286caf47f65d9670fbe45412dd/srcts/src/shiny/init.ts#L326

This is causing NULL to be returned in 

```
  getDimsDefault <- function() {
    width <- widthWrapper()
    height <- heightWrapper()

    # Note that these are reactive calls. A change to the width and height
    # will inherently cause a reactive plot to redraw (unless width and
    # height were explicitly specified).
    if (width == 'auto')
      width <- session$clientData[[paste0('output_', outputName, '_width')]]
    if (height == 'auto')
      height <- session$clientData[[paste0('output_', outputName, '_height')]]

    list(width = width, height = height)
  }
```
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/20cc8e26b5e366286caf47f65d9670fbe45412dd/R/render-plot.R#L109

When these null get passed into C++ code inside [drawPlot](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/20cc8e26b5e366286caf47f65d9670fbe45412dd/R/render-plot.R#L226) then the R.exe process crash follows - giving me very little detail about what happened.

I'd like to propose this as two separate issues:

1 I'd love for the code should protect against these NULLs - as tracking down R crashes in Shiny is time consuming unpleasant
2 I'm not entirely about this - but it might be nice to see if the shiny javascript should be consistent in its use of `offsetHeight` and `getBoundingClientRect().height` - I guess there is a reason to use one over the other in each case... and I'm not entirely sure about this... I suspect some investigation and/or expert input might be needed!

title: Bug: On Firefox, modalDialog with `easyClose = TRUE` gets dismissed prematurely when a click is made on a dropdown option that is outside the modal boundary
description:
When a modal is shown with `easyClose=TRUE`, then clicking outside the modal should dismiss it.

However, if part of the contents of the modal are overflowing outside of the modal -- such as a dropdown menu of a `selectInput()` -- then clicking on those parts should not be considered dismissing the modal. 

It seems that on Firefox (tested on windows and ubuntu), clicking on a dropdown option that is outside the modal results in the modal closing.

Example:  click on letters that are within the modal's boundary, and then click on a letter that is below the modal

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage()

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    easyClose = TRUE,
    selectInput("test", "test", letters)
  ))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Shiny.setInputValue() not worked with event.preventDefault() set when shiny:inputchanged catched with shiny 1.7.3
Bug: updateSelectizeInput(selected = X) does not work if X is not currently rendered on the client side
description:
I think this might be a duplicate of #3698 and #3578 , but the description in those issues is a bit too long and didn't exactly isolate the issue clearly, so I wanted to open another issue and explain it concisely.

When using server-side selectize, a certain number of items are rendered on the client side. When using `updateSelectizeInput()` to programatically select a new value, the new value only gets selected if it's already rendered in the browser. If the value is in the list  of available choices but is not rendered in the browser, the input just gets cleared instead.

Example: in the following code I explicitly set the selectize to only show 20 choices, so the user can select the letter "Z" using the UI but not using `updateSelectizeInput()`.

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectizeInput("test", "test", choices = NULL, options = list(maxOptions = 20)),
  actionButton("go", "select Z")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, "test", choices = LETTERS, server = TRUE)
  observeEvent(input$go, {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "test", selected = "Z")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Documentation clarification: can updateSelectizeInput be used with selectInput?
description:
I want to create a server-side select input. Only `updateSelectizeInput()` has that ability. I've always had to match the input to the update function - so naturally I wanted to use `selectizeInput()` in the UI. However, because of #3727, I tried using `selectInput()` in the UI.

The result seems to work. I don't know if there are any potentially hidden bugs by using `selectInput()` + `updateSelectizeInput()`. If not, it would be good to document that they can be mixed together so that people like me wouldn't be afraid to use it when necessary.

title: dialogViewer: allow dimensions to go right up until the perimeter of the IDE instead of forcing ~150px margin
description:
When building shiny gadgets, it's common to use `dialogViewer()` to run them inside the IDE. However, one frustrating feature of `dialogViewer()` is that it seems to not allow the viewer to come within ~70-80 pixels of the IDE (from my own testing).

For example, the following code

```r
shiny::runGadget(shiny::shinyApp("test", function(input, output) {}), viewer = shiny::dialogViewer("test", 3000, 3000))
```

Results in this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/952340/199340875-9d00d8d6-c616-4733-b91d-af6ed7ae5c61.png)

In a desktop IDE it's not too bad, but often when running a gadget inside an RStudio Server (inside a browser), those extra pixels make a difference. I often end up making a gadget run in a separate browser window instead of in the IDE just because of this. If `dialogViewer()` allowed me to get right up until the edges of the IDE, it would be much more useable.

title: Bug with bindEvent with multiple events
description:
<!--

If you're having trouble with shinyapps.io, and you have a paid account (Starter, Basic, Standard, or Pro), please file a support ticket via https://support.rstudio.com. If you have a Free account, please post to the RStudio Community with the shinyappsio tag: https://community.rstudio.com/tags/shinyappsio.

Finally, if you are an RStudio customer and are having trouble with one of our Pro products, get in touch with our support team at support@rstudio.com.

Before you file an issue, please upgrade to the latest version of Shiny from CRAN and confirm that the problem persists.

# First, restart R.
# To install latest shiny from CRAN:
install.packages("shiny")

See our guide to writing good bug reports for further guidance: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports. The better your report is, the likelier we are to be able to reproduce and ultimately solve it.
-->

### System details

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 4.2.1 (2022-06-23)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)
```
### Explanation

The documentation for `bindEvent` states that "If there are multiple expressions in the `...`, then [the object] will take a dependency on all of them." To me, this suggests that the following is true.

For any two events `event1` and `event2`, and an object `x`:
`bindEvent(x, event1, event2)`
should be the same as:
```
bindEvent(x, event1)
bindEvent(x, event2)
```

This fails in the following two examples.
In the first example, a number of events are defined that depend on two `actionButton`s.

```R
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("button1", label = "Button 1"),
  actionButton("button2", label = "Button 2")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  text1 <- reactive({
    "Text 1"
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(input$button1)
  
  text2 <- reactive({
    "Text 2"
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(input$button2)
  
  observe(label = "first", {
    print("First observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(text1())
  
  observe(label = "second", {
    print("Second observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(text2())
  
  observe(label = "both", {
    print("Third observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(text1(), text2())
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

In this example, I expected that when the first button is clicked on, the first and third observers are run. Similarly, when the second button is clicked, I expected the second and third observers to run. In reality, the first and second observers run as expected, but the third observer only runs after both the buttons have been clicked at least 1. This is due to the silent error that the reactive expressions return when the buttons have not been clicked. The expressions passed into `...` are turned into quosures and evaluated using:
`lapply(qs, rlang::eval_tidy)` (in `shiny::quoToFunction()`)
Hence, if one event returns an error, this entire expression results in an error, and the observer is not run.

This behaviour is discussed (in slightly different scenarios) in issues #1572 and #1125.

I think that two events should be treated as independent from one another.

The second issue is a little simpler, with no UI necessary.

```R
ui <- fluidPage()

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  thing1 <- reactive(NULL)
  
  thing2 <- reactive(NULL)
  
  observe(label = "first", {
    print("First observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(thing1())
  
  observe(label = "second", {
    print("Second observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(thing2())
  
  observe(label = "both", {
    print("Third observer run")
  }) %>%
    bindEvent(thing1(), thing2())
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

I expected none of the observers to execute, since all events are `NULL` and `ignoreNULL` is `TRUE` (by default) for all observers. However, the third observer is run. This stems from the same code as the last one; since the values of all the events are stored in a list, the initial value for the event of the third observer is `list(NULL, NULL)`, which is not considered a 'NULL event' by shiny (therefore the observer runs initially). I think that if both all events that an observer depends on are `NULL`, and `ignoreNULL` is `TRUE`, then the observer should not run.

Both of these situations are pretty easily to avoid/circumvent (in the worst case, you can just define multiple of the same observer). However, I created a function to demonstrate that these issues wouldn't be incredibly difficult to solve:

```R
combine_events <- function(...) {
  qs <- rlang::enquos0(...)
  vals <- lapply(qs, exec_event_safely)
  if(all(sapply(vals, event_is_invalid))) {
    # Return NULL if all other events are NULL
    NULL
  } else {
    vals
  }
}

exec_event_safely <- function(x) {
  try(rlang::eval_tidy(x), silent = TRUE)
}

event_is_invalid <- function(x) {
  inherits(x, "try-error") || is.null(x)
}
```

This fixes both the identified issues when used in the following way:
`bindEvent(x, combine_events(event1, event2))`

Not sure if the benefits of fixing this will be as great as the potential breakage for people who rely on this behaviour, but fixing this might be something to consider.

title: Get a list of current tabs in `navbarPage` or `tabsetPanel`
description:
Shiny provides an excellent API to manipulate tabs inside navbar or tabset. You can insert a new tab or remove one, but you have to keep track of your tabs in an app. If there was a function returning a character vector of all current tabs in a navbar of tabset, the tab management would be way easier. Maybe it could even return a list of shown and hidden tabs.

For instance, let's assume that we are creating and appending tabs for packages that are installed on the machine on the fly. You check periodically what packages are available and then try to append a new tab, but you really don't want to create multiple tabs for the same package. If there was a function returning already present tabs, you can easily check them and decide not to append the same tab twice. (Please ignore the technical details of package recognition etc.)

The only solution ATM that comes to my mind is to keep a list of appended tabs separately or to use some JS to check for current tabs, but I am afraid that my implementation would not be as smooth.

server <- function(input, output, session) {

[25] sass_0.4.2

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
library(shiny)
options(shiny.trace = TRUE) # confirm that input message is being sent

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectizeInput("sel", label = "Selectize:", choices = NULL),
  actionButton("set", "set to 123456"),
  textOutput("out")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, "sel", choices = 1:1e6, server = T)
  output$out <- renderText(paste("Selected value:", input$sel))
  
  observeEvent(input$set, {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "sel", selected = 123456)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

If you click on the "set to 123456" button, which should update the selectize to the value 123456, it instead clears the selectize.

However, if you first type "1234" into the selectize (enough for its search tree to load "123456" as a possible option), then subsequent presses of the button *will* set the selectize as intended.

### Describe the problem in detail

When using a selectize with more than a thousand or so options, server-side selectize is a must for any reasonable performance. As described in [this article](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html) and implemented above, you initialize a server-side selectize by setting `choices = NULL` in the UI, and running `updateSelectizeInput(server = TRUE, choices = [list of choices])` in the server.

However, for certain applications you may need the server to later force a certain selected value, without necessarily changing the list of options; for instance, if you have a button that loads a preset value. If the value you want to set is within the first 1000 in the list, then this will work as intended. But for the 1001st value and higher, this will instead clear the selection (as if you had passed `selected = character(0)`) unless the user has previously searched for that value (or something close to it that gets it to display in the dropdown).

For a multiple-select input, a similar bug occurs. If you pass a list of items to select (e.g. `selected = c(999, 1000, 1001, 1002)`), then the input will be updated with the subset of that list that is either within the first thousand or has previously been searched for (just 999 and 1000 here).

### Workaround
If you re-pass the choices when you update the selection, it works as intended. Like such:
```R
observeEvent(input$set, {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, "sel", choices = 1:1e6, server = T, selected = 123456)
})
```
This however requires storing a copy of the choices, and is probably not terribly efficient.

Confusing object name in Modularization Documentation
description:
My apologies if documentation issues are not meant to be submitted here, but I have not seen any better location.

When looking through the documentation concerning modularizing code I noticed the name of the object passed to NS() in examples is potentially confusing with the reference description on the function itself.
From [Modularizing Shiny app code](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html):
>counterButton <- function(id, label = "Counter") {
>   ns <- NS(id)
> ...
> }

This is the first use on that page, but all are similar on it.

From [NS Reference - Namespaced IDs for inputs/outputs](https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/1.7.0/NS.html)

> NS(namespace,  id = NULL)
> ...
> **namespace**   The character vector to use for the namespace. This can have any length, though a single element is most common. Length 0 will cause the id to be returned without a namespace, and length 2 will be interpreted as multiple namespaces, in increasing order of specificity (i.e. starting with the top-level namespace).
> **id**   The id string to be namespaced (optional).

The object name used in the example is **id** which is also an argument name, but the other argument for NS. 

While a careful reading of the documentation will reveal this inconsistency, anyone who might only be skimming or is less familiar with the topic (admittedly me on both counts for some time) may assume the **id** in the examples refer to the **id** of the argument names. As these are two very different objects, namespace ID versus object ID, the confusion here can hamper an understanding of the NS function and namespaces within Shiny. 

Tangentially, it wouldn't hurt if the documentation could also include an explanation of how to reference some objects within a namespace while outside of it. Only happened on this by accident but it solved an issue that otherwise the modularized code (with the form of modularizing described in the article linked to earlier) could not solve.

title: Shiny Progress freezes
description:
### Describe the problem in detail

I'm building an interactive dashboard that performs some time-consuming computations, and I am trying to add progress bars to show the user that the app is making progress. Ironically, in the process, I've created some kind of lock condition where the app gets stuck. The point where it gets stuck seems to be variable; on my last run, it stalled on iteration 485063.

I've reduced the app to a minimal reprex, below, and deployed it here: https://ezra-morrison.shinyapps.io/stuck-progress/

I'd be grateful for any debugging suggestions!

Thanks,
Ezra


### Example application

``` r
library(shiny)
library(glue)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("n iterations", inputId = "n.iter", value = 10^6, min = 0, step = 1),
  actionButton("Start", inputId = "goButton", class = "btn-success"),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

loop_function = function(session, nmax = 10^5)
{
  message("here")
  progress <- Progress$new(session, min=1, max=nmax)
  on.exit(progress$close())

  progress$set(message = 'Calculation in progress',
               detail = 'This may take a while...')

  step_function = function(i)
  {
    progress$inc(amount = 1, detail = glue::glue("On iteration {i} out of {nmax}"))
    NA
  }

  dataset =
    tibble(id = 1:nmax) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    summarize(
      .groups = "drop",
      temp = step_function(id[1])
      # in my motivating application, real computation steps would occur here
    )

  plot(cars)
}

server <- function(input, output, session)
{

  plot1 =
    loop_function(session = session, nmax = input$n.iter) |>
    eventReactive(eventExpr = input$goButton)

  output$plot = plot1() |> renderPlot()

}

shinyApp(ui, server)
#> 
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7587
```

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Reset Slider Value"),
  fluidRow(column(4,
                  sliderInput("var1", "", min = -100, max = 100, value = 0),
                  actionButton('submit', 'Submit'),
                  actionButton("reset", "Reset")),
           column(6,
                  verbatimTextOutput("text1"),
                  verbatimTextOutput("text2")))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  rv_text1 <- reactiveVal()
  rv_text2 <- reactiveVal()

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    message("Going to update")
    updateSliderInput(session, 'var1', value = 0)
    message("Is updated")

    rv_text2(paste("on reset var1 =", input$var1))
    message(paste("reset: var1 =", input$var1))
  })

  observeEvent(input$submit, {
    rv_text1(paste("on submit var1 =", input$var1))
    print(paste0("submit: var1 =", input$var1))
  })

  output$text1 <- renderText({rv_text1()})
  output$text2 <- renderText({rv_text2()})
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

In a Shiny app, I want to reset a slider to its initial value with `updateSliderInput()` and immediately process its content further. Now this happens only graphical instead as also in the actual value (`input$var1`): after setting the slider to any other than its intitial position and pressing "reset", the slider shifts back to its initial position as expected, while the printed value of `input$var1` still shows the adjusted value.
Pressing "reset" a second time, then resets the actual value of `input$var1`.

According to the help, this is intended and expected: "The input updater functions send a message to the client, telling it to change the settings of an input object. The messages are collected and sent **after all the observers (including outputs) have finished running**."

I strongly would have expected that the content of `input$var1` would change along with its graphical representation, especially if one further relies on and processes the content of the slider. Although it seems to be known behaviour, I suspect this is not that obvious (admittedly, it would be, if you would attentively read this one sentence in the help) and I would not be surprised if this behavior was a source of (unnoticed) errors.

So, it would be great if you could either fix this so that the value changes along with its graphical interpretation (if possible) or at least highlight this behavior somewhat more in the help. 

Many thanks in advance! :)

Best,
Bathyscapher

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    numericInput("number", "Insert a number from 5 to 10",
                 min = 5, max = 10, value = 7),
    htmlOutput("display")
  ), 
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$display <- renderUI(input$number)
  })
```

### Describe the problem in detail

`numericInput()` documents `min` and `max` as the minimum and maximum allowed values.  I interpret this to mean that `numericInput(min = 5, max = 10)` will return a value in the range 5–10. Whilst this is guaranteed to be the case for a `sliderInput`, it is not for `numericInput`.  Clearing the contents of the box and pressing 'enter' results in an `NA` value; manually typing a number larger than 10 results that number.  As such, it is necessary to manually validate the contents before using them – I have encountered app crashes when a user supplies out-of-range values.

```r
server = function(input, output) {
  ValidatedNumber <- reactive({
    min(10, max(5, as.numeric(input$plottedChar), na.rm = TRUE))
  })
  output$display <- renderUI(ValidatedNumber())
})
```

### Proposed solutions

1. Could this validation be performed by shiny before returning `input$number`?
2. If not, could the documentation be updated to make clear that `min` and `max` only apply to the javascript control, and are not guaranteed?

### Further note

Perhaps a similar argument applies to the `step` parameter, though the current documentation does make clear that this is only applied "when stepping between min and max".

title: `shiny::reactlog()` output doesn't contain srcref attribute for objects inside `shiny::bindEvent()`
description:
#### Brief description
`reactive`s and `render*` functions (output) always contained srcref attribute in output returned by `shiny::reactlog()` - filename and line in source code and only `observer`s didn't had srcref. However, if any of the mentioned objects are used in `shiny::bindEvent()`, they have no srcref attribute.

#### MRE
Run the app and click "Go" button.
```
library(shiny)
library(magrittr)

options(shiny.reactlog = TRUE)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("go", "Go"),
  textOutput("show")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  some_reactive <- reactive({
    2 + 2
  }) %>% 
    bindEvent(input$go, label = "labelled reactive")
  
  output$show <- renderPrint({
    data_reactlog <<- reactlog()
    "Button clicked"
  }) %>% 
    bindEvent(input$go, label = "labelled output", ignoreInit = TRUE)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
Now, stop the app, go back to the IDE to inspect `data_reactlog` object in global environment. Functons below can be used:

```
library(rlang)

extract_ids_data_to_df <- function(reactlog_data) {
  if (reactlog_data$action == "define") {
    data.frame(react_id = reactlog_data$reactId,
               label_full = reactlog_data$label,
               filename = attr(reactlog_data$label, "srcfile") %||% NA,
               location = attr(reactlog_data$label, "srcref")[[1]] %||% NA)
  }
}

dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(data_reactlog, extract_ids_data_to_df))
```
Result:
```
| react_id | label_full        | filename                 | location |
|----------|-------------------|--------------------------|----------|
| r3       | Theme Counter     | <NA>                     | NA       |
| r4       | some_reactive     | reactlog_bindEvent_app.R | 14       |
| r5       | labelled reactive | <NA>                     | NA       |
| r6       | output$show       | <NA>                     | NA       |
| r1$go    | input$go          | <NA>                     | NA       |
```
#### Importance

Having srcref attr is useful for debugging. I'm currently working on the Shiny module which can be use to set breakpoint in Shiny app. I'm using reactlog to find dependencies for chosen Id. User can choose Id (by moving mouse around the e.g. output) and then find all dependencies for this Id, i.e. see all source code relevant for this Id.

#### Expected behavior

It would be great if `reactlog` could return srcref attribute for objects used inside `bindEvent`, especially if srcref attribute is now reported for these objects if they are not used inside `bindEvent`.

I know I could try to read source code to find the objects, currently for `observer`s I'm looking for the `label` parameter in data from `utils::getParseData()`, but this is not convenient and I'm not sure how reliable this is. So I would like to avoid having to do this now for `reactive`s and `render*` functions as well, especially for `render*`s it would be more complicated as `reactlog()` do not return labels for these objects, but Id (which is good for me, because otherwise I couldn't let user to choose the Id in the app as these Ids won't be present in `shiny::reactlog()` output). However, that would mean that searching for `output$` or `output[` in the source code would be needed, i.e. more complicated text (code) searching.

#### `Shiny` or `reactlog` problem?

Please, let me know if this is something which should be posted as issue in rstudio/shiny, I understand that this may be a problem with `bindEvent` implementation.

                    "Plotly" = "plotly"),
        inline = FALSE,
        selected = "simple"
      )
    ),
    mainPanel(fluidRow(
      tabPanel(
        6,
        conditionalPanel("input.radioTest == 'simple'", plotOutput("plot2")),
        conditionalPanel("input.radioTest == 'plotly'", plotlyOutput("plot1"))
      )
    )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  iris_dt <- reactive({
    subset(x = iris, Species == input$inp_species)
  })
  
  output$plot1 <-  output$plot1x <- renderPlotly({
    Sys.sleep(2L)
    plot_ly(
      req(iris_dt()),
      x = ~ Petal.Width,
      y = ~ Sepal.Length,
      type = "scatter",
      mode = "markers"
    )
  })
  
  output$plot2 <- output$plot2x <- renderPlot({
    Sys.sleep(2L)
    ggplot(req(iris_dt()), aes(x = Petal.Width, y = Sepal.Length)) +
      geom_point()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
I created a Shiny app, in which I am drawing a scatter plot on iris dataset using libraries highchart, ggplot and plotly. When I dynamically render the UI using a graphical library (such as highchart), then for the first time rendering works as expected. But when I select a different graphical library, then the cache of older graphical library renders (for a while) before the newly selected graphical library can draw.

Here is the complete list of steps to reproduce this problem. Example code is shared.
I am selecting the library to draw the chart dynamically using a selectInput box.

Here is the problem -

1. I select a species in selectInput box and the highchart library draws a scatter plot
2. Then I select plotly in the radio button section and the rendering is done using plotly.
3. I change the species in selectInput and plotly re-renders the plot
4. Now, when I click on highchart radio button, the plot of the earlier species (from cache) is drawn for a few seconds and then the chart of the selected species is drawn.

title: How to log shiny::devmode() output ?
description:
I would like to understand a best practice way to log a shiny app, so as to track the console, which will also include shiny error traces from shiny::devmode. If this is not currently possible, I would request this as a feature.

Here is a reprex to illustrate the issue:
```
library(shiny)
shiny::devmode()
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("simple", "Just to add something normal to the log"),
  actionButton("force_error_button", "Force an Error")
)
close_sink_and_quit <- function(){
  sink(file = NULL,type = "message") 
  sink(file = NULL,type = "output") 
  close(con = flog)
  stopApp()
}

options(error = close_sink_and_quit)
options(shiny.error = close_sink_and_quit)


flog <- file("my_shiny_log", open = "wt")
sink(file = flog, split = TRUE)
sink(file = flog, type = "message")

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  onStop(function() {cat("Session stopped\n") ;close_sink_and_quit()})
  

  observeEvent(input$simple,
               cat("\npressed for",input$simple))

  
  observeEvent(input$force_error_button, {
    stop(paste("Error Forced at ", Sys.time()))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
if I refrain from pressing my force error button, but hit the simple button a few times,
I happily get the corresponding message in my console, as well as in "my_shiny_log" file .

if I force an error, although I see a useful stack trace in the console, this is _not_ represented in the "my_shiny_log" file. 
I've been pulling my hair out on this point :D

example of trace that shows in console but not in the sink log file : 
```
Warning: Error in <observer:observeEvent(input$force_error_button)>: Error Forced at  2022-07-26 12:43:12
  76: h
  75: .handleSimpleError
  74: stop
  73: <observer:observeEvent(input$force_error_button)> [#11]
  72: valueFunc
  71: ..stacktraceon..
  70: contextFunc
```

so to summarise, is it possible to duplicate the full console *including devmode's stacktrace* in a `sink`ed logging file?, or would this require a new devmode feature/bugfix to achieve ?

I had it suggested to me that a combination of wrapping the app inside a callr/processx might be a way to go, though this seemed rather heavyweight to me... thoughts ?

title: [Accessibility] `shiny::icons()` are not accessible to screen readers
description:
In the following example (retrieved from example(checkboxGroupInput, package = "shiny")), icons are used for informative purpose. However, the checkbox
is not accessible for screen readers until explicit aria-label is used by content creator because this does not provide any icon alt text by default. It
would be more desirable and safer if the aria-label is provided by default equal to font name and allow content creators to override that value if necessary.

``` r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  checkboxGroupInput("icons", "Choose icons:",
    choiceNames =
      list(icon("calendar"), icon("bed"),
           icon("cog"), icon("bug")),
    choiceValues =
      list("calendar", "bed", "cog", "bug")
  ),
  textOutput("txt")
)


server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$txt <- renderText({
    icons <- paste(input$icons, collapse = ", ")
    paste("You chose", icons)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

CC @rich-iannone 

Related discussion: [quarto-ext/fontawesome#8](https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome/issues/8)

title: req() not silent inside functions
description:
This is a pretty contrived reprex, but the moral of the story is I'd expect `text_1` and `text_2` to be identical in the app below. They are identical until one clears the numeric input, which then sends Shiny `NULL` as the reactive val: ```r library(tidyverse) library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( numericInput("row_ix", label = "row ix", value = 1), tags$h4("msg 1"), verbatimTextOutput("text_1"), tags$h4("msg 2"), verbatimTextOutput("text_2"), ) server <- function(input, output, session) { ## renders the error message: output$text_1 <- renderPrint({ mtcars %>% slice(req(input$row_ix)) }) ## swallows the error message: output$text_2 <- renderPrint({ row_ix <- req(input$row_ix) mtcars %>% slice(row_ix) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` When `input$row_ix` is `NULL`, `text_1` displays the error (unexpected) while `text_2` silently swallows the error and displays nothing (expected). (I briefly thought this could be due to magrittr's lazy evaluation, so I also tried with the new(ish) `%!>%` operator, but found the same behavior.)

title: Allow to manually call output render functions
description:
Dear devs,

I was wondering if shiny can provide functions to call output renderers manually without knowing the expressions inside of the render calls. For example, something like `shiny::renderOutput` as follows:

```r
# server:
function(input, output, session) {

  output$plot1 <- shiny::renderPlot({ ... })

  output$download <- shiny::downloadHandler(
    ...,
    content = function(con) {
        # Re-render plot1 without knowing the expression
        pdf(...)
        shiny::renderOutput(output, "download")
        dev.off()
    }
  )

}
```

Also it would be nice if `shiny::outputOptions` can add arbitrary (customized) key-value pairs, so we can store additional information needed (for example the arguments needed by `pdf()` function.

I understand that there could be lots of things to consider (such as potential side effects). However, it would be neat if there is such function, as we can programmatically write widget functions for outputs. For example, 

* downloading graphs, saving HTML widgets (without writing handlers), 
* embed an output in another session/output zoomed in or as a sub-plot,
* allow a third person to add additional processing/extract information from output results (from ggplot2 object, or htmlwidget)

#### My attempts

1. For some outputs, I am able to extract the expression from `cacheHint` attribute of `shiny.render.function` objects. However, if `cacheHint` is set to false in `markRenderFunction` (such as `DT::renderDT`), I couldn't obtain any expressions.

2. Another attempt is to directly call `shiny.render.function` with a given session and output. However, that only gives me processed results instead of what's generated from `expr`. For example, `renderPlot` returns the base64-encoded image, and I cannot set the width nor height.

title: Add `shiny:flush` and `shiny:flushed` JS events
description:
Currently it's not possible to detect in the browser when shiny flush cycle is finished.

Implementing a custom solution is not hard (can be achieved by usage of `session$sendCustomMessage` and `shiny::onFlush(ed)`), but can become inconvenient when trying to implement a feature basing on the event operating on browser only (in external package), e.g.:
```
shinyApp(
  ui =  fluidPage(doSthWhenFlushed(selectInput("val", "Val", letters))), 
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    # the below line could be skipped if event exists
    shiny::onFlushed(function() "trigger what `doSthWhenFlushed` wants do to when flushed", once = FALSE)
  }
)
```

Could that be possible to attach the events by default in shiny? E.g. by extending the default onFlush and onFlushed registered callbacks.

The event could be then also used for solving #3668

title: createBookmarkObservers in shiny.R doesn't respect shiny.sanitize.errors setting
description:
We have observed that if you manage to invoke an error while bookmark state is being restored, effectively when the address bar is being parsed, clients accessing the site within a browser will see un-sanitized errors from the server in a red bubble onscreen. This occurs even with `options(shiny.sanitize.errors = TRUE)` set.

You can create this by visiting `/?_inputs_&page=%22page-with-null-character-%00%22` in a shiny app.

My simple example only show relatively innocuous errors about parsing the url itself, so I can understand this might not really be considered a problem. I have not fully explored how many touch points this happens across.

We had hoped to be a bit zealous about hiding even the most inane workings of the server-side application if that is within reach.

[21] compiler_4.2.0   htmltools_0.5.2  sass_0.4.1      
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = basicPage(
    textOutput("date_out"),
    dateInput("date_in", "Date input", "2000-01-01")
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$date_out <- renderText(as.character(input$date_in))
  }
)
```

Click into the text field of the date input and press backspace; the date displayed will be 1999-12-31. Press backspace again; it will be today's date. Continue pressing backspace; it will be null when the field is empty.

### Describe the problem in detail
`dateInput` (and `dateRangeInput`) eagerly try to parse incomplete date strings as they are being typed, and then send off the results to the server. This can have the effect of the server trying to process a date completely different from the one that the user intended to enter. In the case of a range, this can result in a min and max in the wrong order; and with a cleared-out field that the user intends to start typing a new date in, the server sees a null value. The server will then take actions with the bogus date before the user is even finished typing (some of which may prevent the user from completing their typing, e.g. updating the input to be in the "correct" order or throwing an error for a null date).

This might stem from JavaScripts officially undefined behavior when parsing nonstandard datestrings; I'd recommend ignoring typed input in this field until the user presses enter or unfocuses the field; or only updating when the current string matches the set format.

description:
Hello,

I have a few Shiny apps hosted on shinyapps.io that allow users to download 
files. When using the apps, users run into a disconnect issue when 
downloading files on mobile devices -- both smartphones and tablets, and using 
different browsers. This issue does not seem to occur when the apps are run 
online on computers.

When downloading a file (e.g., a CSV file) from an app, the app **disconnects** 
from the server, and a window appears asking the user whether they want to 
download the file (along with a download button). The file does download if the 
user chooses that, but the problem is the disconnecting. Users who want to 
continue using the app after downloading, without any loss of progress made in 
the app, are unable to do so. I believe an app should continue to run without 
any loss of user progress even after downloading files.

Below is a reproducible example. If the app is deployed on shinyapps.io and then 
run on a mobile device, the issue above is encountered. For instance, I 
encountered it on an iPhone (with iOS 15.5) when using both Safari (version 15) 
and Chrome (version 103.0.5060.63).

Thank you for your help!

```r
library(shiny)

# ui
ui <- fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Test Downloading the iris Dataset"),

  downloadButton("download", "Download")
)

# server
server <- function(input, output) {

  output$download <- downloadHandler(
    
    filename = function() {
      "iris.csv"
    },
    
    content = function(file) {
      write.csv(iris, file, row.names = FALSE)
    }
  )
}

# create app
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
# Adapted from example in plotOutput documentation
library(shiny)
options(shiny.trace=TRUE)
shinyApp(
  ui = basicPage(
    plotOutput("plot", height=300,
               hover = hoverOpts(id = "plot_hover", delayType = "throttle"),
    ),
    verbatimTextOutput("plot_hoverinfo")
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      d <- cars
      plot(d$speed, d$dist)
    })
    output$plot_hoverinfo <- renderPrint({
      cat("Hover (throttled):\n")
      str(input$plot_hover)
    })
  }
)
```

To have a permanently unresponsive hover, click outside the plot first.
To have a hover permanently stuck in the first location you hovered over, that spams the server with the same
update every 300 ms, click on the plot first.

### Describe the problem in detail

This is due to a major bug in `throttle.ts` in which normalCall() sets a timer which, when it ends, calls normalCall() again with the *same inputs as the first call*, rather than the most recent arguments. It seems that commit 0fb154c revealed this bug by fixing a coding error in which the function was trying to unpack the arguments twice (and thus erroring out and avoiding the infinite loop).

I'm currently working on a solution to this, along with a number of other brush-related issues, on my fork at https://github.com/dvg-p4/shiny -- any input is appreciated!

title: Progress not hidden before Progress$set is called with style = "notification"
description:
### Expected behavior

In the documentation it says that Progress$new() should create the new panel, but **not** display it. This is only true for `style = "old"`. 
Additionally, the documentation for Progress$set() says that `value = NULL` hides the panel.

### Actual behaviour 

With the default (`style = "notification"`) it will display the notification panel with "message" directly when Progress$new() is called. 
`value = NULL` keeps the current values of Progress. 


### Backgroud

My use case is the following: I want the user to start a long-running background process using callr::r_bg() which prints regular outputs that shall be used to update a Progress indicator. The user needs to be able to cancel the long running function.

  observeEvent(input$start, {
    o$resume()
  }, priority = 1)
  
 o <- observe({

    if(long_run()$is_alive()) {
      status <- long_run()$read_output_lines(n = 1)
      if (length(status)>0){
        cycle <- strsplit(status, split = " ")[[1]][2]
        progress$set(value = as.numeric(cycle), detail = cycle, message = "Processing cycle") # Updating the progress
      }
    } 
   invalidateLater(2000)
  }, suspended = TRUE)
  
  observeEvent(input$cancel, {
    progress$set(value = NULL) # hide progress notification
    long_run()$kill()
    o$suspend()

  })
  progress <- shiny::Progress$new(min = 0, max = 20) # create progress notification without showing it
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Bindings can't be registered asynchronously
Add additional hooks for Websocket and HTTP traffic inspection
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file a feature request! Please take the time to search for an existing feature request, to avoid creating duplicate requests. If you find an existing feature request, please give it a thumbs-up reaction, as we'll use these reactions to help prioritize the implementation of these features in the future.

If the feature has not yet been filed, then please describe the feature you'd like to see become a part of Shiny. See:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Writing-Good-Feature-Requests

for a guide on how to write good feature requests.

-->

Shiny exposes various "hooks" to run user code when various events occur -- `onFlush()`, `onSessionEnded()`, and so on. One notable omission from the existing hooks is the ability to capture individual Websocket messages and HTTP requests. These are available in other packages that use `httpuv`, notably [Plumber](https://www.rplumber.io/articles/programmatic-usage.html?q=hook#router-hooks).

The main reason I'm interested in this is to improve the Prometheus metrics we can expose for Shiny in the [`openmetrics`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=openmetrics) package. Websocket and HTTP traffic is one of the main ways to measure load on a Shiny app, and without a way to hook into these events I don't have a way to effectively monitor them.

Ideally, I'd like to see a Websocket hook expose the same `binary` and `message` parameters used in the Websocket message handler: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b52b9e4520ad8d1e976299d5dec5e4ba3096bd04/R/server.R#L294-L297

so that we could measure binary vs. JSON traffic and the number of bytes sent/received. In order to capture messages sent, a hook would also have to be added for Websocket writes on the `ShinySession` object: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/b52b9e4520ad8d1e976299d5dec5e4ba3096bd04/R/shiny.R#L393-L402

For HTTP requests, we'd need hooks for before and after the request was handled, ideally exposing the Rook/`httpuv` `req` and `res` objects.

Although I'm primarily interested in metrics, other uses for these hooks that come to mind for these hooks include ad-hoc debugging (say, stick a `browser()` in a hook) or custom logging. It's possible that there are scenarios where users might actually want to modify the incoming/outgoing messages, too, though I doubt that would be effective for Websockets without additional changes on the Javascript side.

title: shiny app does not connect when `uiPattern` is long path.
description:
I am trying to utilize `shinyApp(uiPattern = ".*")` so that I could run an app and then grab the session$request$PATH_INFO later. In my testing, I am seeing some unexpected results whenever the path has more than a single delimiter.

Below is a minimal reproducible example of the issue.

```R
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  wellPanel(
    textInput("text", "Input"),
    verbatimTextOutput("out")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  #for debugging
  print(session$request$PATH_INFO)
  output$out <- renderPrint({
    input$text
  })
}

app <- shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*")

runApp(app, port = 1234, launch.browser = F)
```

If you point your browser to `http://127.0.0.1:1234/`, you will see the app as intended as well if you point to `http://127.0.0.1:1234/foo/`

If you try to make a path like `http://127.0.0.1:1234/foo/bar`, then the html is rendered improperly and the shiny server session is never initiated. 

Does anyone know what the issue is and if it is fixable?

I would assume that `uiPattern = ".*"` would sufficiently capture a path like `/foo/bar`. I assume it is being handled properly because the html is rendered and the status by the handler is 200, which makes me believe the error is somewhere else.

title: Unable to retrieve variables in Shiny's Server and UI environments from another function using formulas
description:
## My Issue

I'm using `stm::estimateEffect` ([source](https://github.com/bstewart/stm/blob/master/R/estimateEffect.R)) to estimate how a topic's prevalence has changed over time. The first argument passed into that function is the regression [formula](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/stats/versions/3.6.2/topics/formula).

When formulas for used as arguments in a function, any variables referenced in the formula are essentially passed in as a string. Within the function, that string is parsed and the values of those variables are retrieved from the global environment. This is different from the common way variables are passed as arguments, a new local variable is created that is equal to the variable referenced in the argument.

This is problematic when using a Shiny app. Shiny applications have a more complex set of environments than generic R scripts. For a detailed explanation, see [Scoping rules for Shiny apps](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html). In addition to the global environment, Shiny has an environment for its UI and server code.

**This is the core of the issue.** Functions called within these two environments only have access to their function-level environment and the global environment. When those functions use formulas, they're unable to retrieve the variables created outside of the global environment.

## Reproducible Examples

In this first example, I define the function and variables all within the global environment, as is the default when working with an R script.

```
linear_equation <- function(formula){
  return(eval(parse(text=as.character(formula)[3])))
}

m <- 3
x <- 10 
b <- 2

result <- linear_equation(y~m*x+b) 
```

This code runs as expected and the `result` has a value of 32.

In this next example, I build a Shiny app that allows the user to define `m`, `x`, and `b`. With those variables, it essentially does that same thing, except it doesn't use the `linear_equation` function defined above. Instead, I calculate `y` by simply running the calculation `y <- m*x+b` within the `server` function. The result is then rendered.

```
ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
  sidebarPanel(
    shiny::numericInput('m', 'Slope', value = 3),
    shiny::numericInput('x', 'X Value', value = 10),
    shiny::numericInput('b', 'Intercept', value = 2),
    h5('Y'),
    shiny::textOutput('text_output')
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  result <- reactive({input$m * input$x + input$b})
  output$text_output <- renderText({result()})
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This runs as expected; `result` has a value of 32 and it is properly rendered.
<kbd>![Screen Shot 2022-04-27 at 9 29 37 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17058405/165529823-d3a7a923-c42a-41ca-9afe-c58c0073d352.png)</kbd>

In the next example, I use the same Shiny code, except I utilize the `linear_equation` defined in the first example.

```
linear_equation <- function(formula){
  return(eval(parse(text=as.character(formula)[3])))
}

ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
  sidebarPanel(
    shiny::numericInput('m', 'Slope', value = 3),
    shiny::numericInput('x', 'X Value', value = 10),
    shiny::numericInput('b', 'Intercept', value = 2),
    h5('Y'),
    shiny::textOutput('text_output')
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  result <- reactive({linear_equation(y~input$m*input$x+input$b)})
  output$text_output <- renderText({result()})
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This returns the following error

```
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5642
Warning: Error in eval: object 'input' not found
  [No stack trace available]
```

To confirm it's not the `reactive` causing the error, I explicitly defined `m`, `x`, and `b`, and removed the `reactive` function.

```
ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
  sidebarPanel(
    h5('Y'),
    shiny::textOutput('text_output')
  )
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  m <- 3
  x <- 10 
  b <- 2
  
  result <- m*x+b
  
  output$text_output <- shiny::renderText({result})
}

shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This works as expected. `result` is created and has a value of 32 and it is properly rendered.

<kbd>![Screen Shot 2022-04-27 at 9 41 35 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17058405/165535342-6b5bab88-434e-40db-9237-c553d51838f0.png)</kbd>

Next, I try to use those explicitly defined variables in `linear_equation`
```
linear_equation <- function(formula){
  return(eval(parse(text=as.character(formula)[3])))
}

ui <- shiny::fluidPage(
  shiny::textOutput('text_output')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  m <- 3
  x <- 10 
  b <- 2
  
  result <- linear_equation(y~m*x+b)
  
  output$text_output <- shiny::renderText({result})
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

This returns the following error:

```
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5642
Warning: Error in eval: object 'm' not found
  52: eval [<text>#1]
  51: eval
  50: linear_equation [#2]
  49: server [#6]
Error in eval(parse(text = as.character(formula)[3])) : 
  object 'm' not found
```

I'm confident this error is being thrown because `linear_equation` does not have access to the variables created within the environment created within `server`. 

## Potential Solutions

### Create global variables

I could try to assign these variables to the global environment using the `<<-` operator. Although, I expect that will cause some issues with Shiny's reactivity as `input` is updated. 

### Precompute values

I could try to precompute the data I need. While this seems like a sufficient workaround and could be a good stopgap, it doesn't build a solution for the core issue.

```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput('value', 'Some value', value=2),
  radioButtons('radios', label=NULL,
               choices=c('pass', 'fail'),
               selected='pass', inline=TRUE),
  actionButton('reset_fail', 'Reset fail'),
  actionButton('reset_works', 'Reset OK'),
  p('Clicking "Reset fail" does nothing; it does not reset either input.\n',
    br(),
    'Clicking "Reset OK" resets both inputs to empty.')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$reset_fail, {
    # The incorrect call to updateRadioButtons does nothing and breaks
    # the call to updateNumericInput
    updateRadioButtons(session, 'radios', selected=NA)
    updateNumericInput(session, 'value', value=NA_integer_, max=100)
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset_works, {
    # With the correct `selected` parameter, both controls are reset
    updateRadioButtons(session, 'radios', selected=character(0))
    updateNumericInput(session, 'value', value=NA_integer_, max=100)
  })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

Calling `updateRadioButtons` with the (incorrect) argument `selected=NA` fails silently and also causes following update requests to fail. In the sample code above, the `reset_fail` observer makes the incorrect call to `updateRadioButtons` followed by `updateNumericInput`. Neither call has any effect. The `reset_works` handler has a correct call to reset the radio buttons and both update calls are handled, resulting in both inputs being reset.

FWIW, I ran across this when trying to convert an `NA` value to `character(0)` with code similar to this:

```
radio_selection = ifelse(is.na(new_value), character(0), new_value)
updateRadioButtons(session, 'radios', selection=radio_selection)
```
Unfortunately, when `new_value` is `NA`,  the `ifelse` returns `NA`, not `character(0)`, resulting in the described failure.

Thanks for all your good work!

title: An updateSelectizeInput inside a server's renderUI
description:
Hi,

My basic `shiny` app example has a `data.frame` of 20,000 genes, each with an effect and p.value numerical values:
```
set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(gene = paste0("g",1:20000), effect = rnorm(20000), p.value = runif(20000,1,0), stringsAsFactors = F)
```

And my `app` has two output options to display:
1. A volcano plot, which is a scatter plot of `-log10(df$p.value)` vs. `df$effect`
2. The same as option 1, but allowing the user to select multiple genes to be highlighted in red in the volcano plot

And I'd like the list of genes to select from only to appear if option 1 was selected by the user.

A `renderUI` within in the `server` where in the `selectInput` the `choices` argument has all 20,000 genes is too slow, therefore I followed [this tutorial](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html) using `selectizeInput` and `updateSelectizeInput`.

Below is my `app` code, where I'm defining the `selectizeInput` within the `ui` and the `updateSelectizeInput` within the `server`.

It doesn't do what I want:
1. If the `label` variable isn't defined in `selectizeInput` it throws the error `Error in dots_list(...) : argument "label" is missing, with no default`. But if I do define it, that box appears by default rather than conditioned on the user selecting option 2.
2. The list that appears does not allow selecting from it.
3.  Of lower importance, my `app` doesn't display the rendered plot, and I don't know why


```
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shiny))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shinyjs))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DT))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(readr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(plotly))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rmarkdown))

volcanoPlot <- function(df,selected.gene.set=NULL)
{
  plot.df <- df %>%  dplyr::mutate(log10.p.value = -log10(p.value))
  plot.df <- cbind(plot.df,purrr::imap(plot.df, ~ paste(.y, .x, sep=": ")) %>%
                     dplyr::as_tibble() %>%
                     tidyr::unite(text, sep="\n"))
  if(!is.null(selected.gene.set)){
    plot.df$group <- "unselected"
    plot.df$group[which(plot.df$gene %in% selected.gene.set)] <- "selected"
    plot.df$group <- factor(plot.df$group,levels=c("unselected","selected"))
    volcano.plot <- plotly::plot_ly(type='scatter',mode="markers",marker=list(size=5),color=plot.df$group,colors=c("lightgray","darkred"),x=plot.df$effect,y=plot.df$log10.p.value,text=plot.df$text,hoverinfo="text",showlegend=F) %>%
      plotly::layout(xaxis=list(title="Effect",zeroline=F),yaxis=list(title="-log10(P-value)",zeroline=F))
  } else{
    volcano.plot <- plotly::plot_ly(type='scatter',mode="markers",marker=list(size=5,color="gray"),x=plot.df$effect,y=plot.df$log10.p.value,text=plot.df$text,hoverinfo="text",showlegend=F) %>%
      plotly::layout(xaxis=list(title="Effect",zeroline=F),yaxis=list(title="-log10(P-value)",zeroline=F))
  }
  return(volcano.plot)
}

output.choices <- c("","Volcano Plot","Highlighted Gene Set Volcano Plot")
set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(gene = paste0("g",1:20000), effect = rnorm(20000), p.value = runif(20000,0,1), stringsAsFactors = F)

server <- function(input, output, session)
{
  output$selected.gene.set <- renderUI({
    req(input$outputType == "Highlighted Gene Set Volcano Plot")
    updateSelectizeInput(session,"selected.gene.set","Select Genes to Highlight",choices=unique(df$gene),multiple=T)
  })

  volcano.plot <- reactive({
    req(input$outputType)
    if(input$outputType == "Volcano Plot"){
      volcano.plot <- volcanoPlot(df=df)
    } else{
      req(input$selected.gene.set)
      volcano.plot <- volcanoPlot(df=df,selected.gene.set=input$selected.gene.set)
    }
    return(volcano.plot)
  })

  output$out.plotly <- plotly::renderPlotly({
    volcano.plot()$volcano.plot
  })
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      tags$head(
        tags$style(HTML(".multicol {-webkit-column-count: 3; /* Chrome, Safari, Opera */-moz-column-count: 3; /* Firefox */column-count: 3;}")),
        tags$style(type="text/css", "#loadmessage {position: fixed;top: 0px;left: 0px;width: 100%;padding: 5px 0px 5px 0px;text-align: center;font-weight: bold;font-size: 100%;color: #000000;background-color: #CCFF66;z-index: 105;}"),
        tags$style(type="text/css",".shiny-output-error { visibility: hidden; }",".shiny-output-error:before { visibility: hidden; }")),
      conditionalPanel(condition="$('html').hasClass('shiny-busy')",tags$div("In Progress...",id="loadmessage")),
      selectInput("outputType", "Output Type", choices = output.choices),
      selectizeInput(inputId='selected.gene.set',label="Select Genes to Highlight",choices=NULL)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotly::plotlyOutput("out.plotly")
    )
  )
)

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```
