title: Allow enabling/disabling widgets via xyzInput and updateXyz commands
description:
There are situations in which disabling input/output widgets is the best way to keep the user informed about possible actions, effective/applicable settings and possible outputs. This includes "graying out" the widget and making it non-reactive to events such as clicks or drag-drop.

One could argue that the need for this indicates bad UI design. Often that may be true, but it's still easier and shiny apps typically don't justify a month's worth of UX work. Disabled state is a simple and easy to understand way to convey that an input or output is in principle present, but at the current time not possible or not applicable.

Implementing this in third party extensions such as `shinyjs` is limited and difficult. Firstly, TypeScript widgets such as `fileInput` require deep meddling to turn off e.g. drag and drop features when they are disabled. Secondly, it's essential to have a universal visual for the disabled state (not so easy with things that are gray to start with).

It would be great to have this as a core feature, accessible via standard interfaces. E.g. `fileInput(..., disabled=TRUE)` and `updateSelectize(..., disabled=TRUE)`.

title: More informative error message for `debounce` when accidentally assigned to an observer
description:
Hi Shiny devs,
I'm still experimenting with effective use of the very useful `debounce` and accidentally applied it to an `observeEvent`. It was a relatively large app in which I did this, and the error message was quite vague:

`Error in r: could not find function "r"`

After some hours of searching my code for an `r` function thinking I might have accidentally deleted part of a function call, further debugging, and finally setting the `options(shiny.error = utils::recover)` and exploring the massive stack track I figured out what was happening.

I think this time-consuming experience could be averted for other shiny users if `debounce` had a more informative error message when the input is not what was expected. Something along the lines of:

"`r` argument passed to `debounce` is not a reactive. `debounce` must be called on a reactive expression and not an `observe`."

Reprex:
```

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

    #
    actionButton("test", "test")
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output) {

  observeEvent(input$test, input$test) |>
    shiny::debounce(1000)

}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: Shiny disconnects automatically when running locally
description:
Dear Shiny wizards,

I have a shiny app that guide people through data preprocessing. It worked for more than four years, and the code has been actively maintained and updated. We recently found a "weird" issue: if the user does not interact with "shiny", the browser automatically disconnects itself and greys out.

Here are some highlights I think they might be helpful

* The app runs on local computer and the bash script uses `Rscript -e` command.
* One of the algorithms takes extremely long time to run (~2-4 hours) and uses large RAM (~16GB). During this procedure, the main session will be blocked (by the time when the script was written, `promises` wasn't a package yet)
* There is an onSessionEnded hook, but the hook does not turn off the app, it simply releases some resources and is properly try-catched. So disconnecting from client side won't trigger server shutdown
* The app ran properly for 3.5 years, this issue occurred pretty recently, and the script runs well without shiny
* The sleep has been turned off and the computer runs 24/7


### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

Unluckily, the issue occurs pretty periodically. Please provide some suggestions/hints to help me locate the bug. I haven't checked if the server was died last time. It said "session ended". I will update this issue once I encounter the same issue again.

One can say that it is forbidden to deploy the application to RSConnect from the session that has already set this option. But it is still possible to deploy the app code that _sets_ this option. Therefore that cannot be considered as a solution.

title: Errors in throttled/debounced reactive expressions cause session to exit
description:
Launch this app and press "Cause error". It should just cause red errors to appear in the two outputs, but instead, the session exits. This is because internally, observers are used to implement the throttle/debounce behavior, and they are being exposed to the error in the reactive.

See #3580, thanks @mmuurr for pointing this out!

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("err", "Cause error"),
  textOutput("output1"),
  textOutput("output2"),
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  r <- eventReactive(input$err, {
    stop("Error at ", Sys.time())
  })
  
  r_throttle <- r |> throttle(1000)
  r_debounce <- r |> debounce(1000)
  
  output$output1 <- renderText({ r_throttle() })
  output$output2 <- renderText({ r_debounce() })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: catching registerInputHandler errors in application observers
Accessing currently selected `navbarMenu` item
description:
Hi,

Thank you for developing `shiny`.  I was not sure whether this should be filed under bugs or features, so went with the latter.

According to the documentation of `navbarMenu`, an `id` attribute should allow access to `navbarMenu` items

>If provided, you can use input$id in your server logic to determine which of the current tabs is active. The value will correspond to the value argument that is passed to tabPanel().

However, if one provides an `id` inside `navbarMenu`, this will create a named tab instead as follows, leading to the UI not rendering and also lack of access to the currently active item. 

```
navbarMenu( title = "menu", id= "test")
```

Taking a look at the source code for `bslib::nav_menu` which builds `navbarMenu` suggests that `...` should presumably support `id`s but these work for `navbarPage` only. 


```
function (title, ..., value = title, icon = NULL, align = c("left", 
  "right")) 
{
  align <- match.arg(align)
  navbarMenu_(title, ..., menuName = value, icon = icon, align = align)
}

```

I would like to know if it could be possible to support access to the currently selected item and use this in the server.

Thank you and apologies if this already exists (I could not find it after much searching. I see mention of this in https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/595#issuecomment-77254670 but this goes back to `navbarPage`) 

NelsonGon

title: Dynamic tabPanel title prevents tabPanel bookmarking
description:
Restoring a bookmarked `tabsetPanel()` Shiny app state works by looking up the `tabsetPanel` `id` and titles of the `tabPanel()`s. This causes problems when there's anything else than plain text in the `tabPanel()` title, eg. a dynamic title text with `textOutput()`, because then the saved value will have a div in it, thus the opened tab can't be restored and in fact no tab will be opened on restore.

I think the fix would be to instead use a `tabPanel()` id. It seems an automatically generated `id` value exists but instead `data-value` is used.

### System details

[19] fastmap_1.1.0    compiler_4.1.0   htmltools_0.5.2  sass_0.4.0      
```

### Example application 

This is a slightly modified script from the [multiple bookmark buttons example](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/bookmarking-state.html).

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- function(request) {
  fluidPage(
    tabsetPanel(id = "tabs",
                tabPanel(title = textOutput("title1"),
                         textInput("change1", "Change title", "Title 1"),
                         checkboxInput("chk1", "Checkbox 1"),
                         bookmarkButton(id = "bookmark1")
                ),
                tabPanel("Two",
                         checkboxInput("chk2", "Checkbox 2"),
                         bookmarkButton(id = "bookmark2")
                )
    )
  )
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  output$title1 <- renderText(input$change1)

title: Deep stack trace collection causes slow promise chaining in `renderPlot`
description:
@schloerke and I looked into an issue today where an app that calls `promises::then` (or `finally` or whatever) a few hundred times inside of a `renderPlot` was taking seconds. To be clear, it is the creation of the promise chains that takes seconds, _not_ the actual execution of the actual logic inside the chain.

In my profvis of the example below, all the time is being spent in `sys.calls()` calls, atop several layers of `wrapOnRejected`/`Fulfilled`. This implicates [deep stack collection](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Stack-traces-in-R#promises-deep-stack-traces), and indeed, `options(shiny.deepstacktrace=FALSE)` makes the performance problem mostly go away. (Oddly, @schloerke ran profvis as well, and his stacks did not show `sys.calls()`--the stack trace always ended at `wrapOnRejected`/`Fulfilled`, which doesn't make any sense to me.)

It's curious that `renderPlot` exhibits this problem but `renderText` does not. I suspect it is because `renderPlot` happens to be pretty complicated and nests a bunch of `hybridChain` calls, which each install a promise domain that each wants to capture deep stacks.

Thinking about how we could fix this, I'd want to look carefully at how deep stack collection works, and see if we can get away with deduping instances of StackTracePromiseDomain (like, if one is already installed, don't install another one). Or having multiple instances, but they detect each other somehow and only one instance does the work.

title: `"shiny.silent.error"` conditions are intercepted by user handlers
description:
Originally reported in https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/5552.

Shiny silent errors thrown within dplyr verbs no longer work as expected since dplyr 1.0. That's because starting from this version, dplyr catches all conditions of class `"error"` and wraps them in a new dplyr-specific error.

```r
class(rlang::catch_cnd(dplyr::mutate(mtcars, stop("foo"))))
#> [1] "dplyr:::mutate_error" "rlang_error"
#> [3] "error"                "condition"

# Same with `req()`
class(rlang::catch_cnd(dplyr::mutate(mtcars, shiny::req(NULL))))
#> [1] "dplyr:::mutate_error" "rlang_error"
#> [3] "error"                "condition"
```

Here are two common ways of wrapping errors.

```r
# Chained wrapping
chain <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, error = function(cnd) {
    rlang::abort(
      "Chained.",
      parent = cnd,
      call = rlang::env_parent()
    )
  })
}
chain(1 + "")
#> Error in `chain()`:
#> ! Chained.
#> Caused by error in `1 + ""`:
#> ! non-numeric argument to binary operator

# Non-chained wrapping
wrap <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, error = function(cnd) {
    rlang::abort(
      "Wrapped.",
      body = c(x = conditionMessage(cnd)),
      call = rlang::env_parent()
    )
  })
}
wrap(1 + "")
#> Error in `wrap()`:
#> ! Wrapped.
#> ✖ non-numeric argument to binary operator
```

Another possible pattern is to intercept errors and demote them to a warning. This would also interfere with operators like `req()`, causing strang warning outputs.

In principle Shiny shouldn't use `"error"` conditions to communicate or transfer control between end points since these conditions may be intercepted and handled by user code. Ideally it would use bare conditions that don't inherit from `"error"`. However this is currently hard to implement because of promises which only support `"error"` handling.

As a partial fix we could handle the chained error case by using `cnd_inherits()` instead of `inherits()` to detect silent errors. dplyr versions 1.0.0 up to current 1.0.7 use both sorts of wrapping but the next release of dplyr will exclusively use chained errors though, AFAIK.

  ), server = function(input, output, session) {

    output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
      filename = function() { input$filename }, content = content_fun
    )
	output$downloadData_1 <- downloadHandler(
      filename = "à/.csv",content = content_fun
    )
    output$downloadData_2 <- downloadHandler(
      filename = "a/.csv",content = content_fun
    )
    output$downloadData_3 <- downloadHandler(
      filename = "à.csv",content = content_fun
    )
  })
)

```

### Describe the problem in detail
The download simply fails, with no error messages on browser/server side, if there are special characters (such as à) AND a slash "/". The browser starts to download (get the filename, with / converted to _) but then fails ("Failed - No File").

If there is only one of the characters, the download works -- with the / being automatically replaced with _ .

My guess is that the code that is doing this "automatic" conversion is failing, but I couldn't identify the code in the repository to have a look.

My current workaround will be to replace the / into _ before hand. If someone point me to the right direction, I'm willing to fix and do the pull request.

title: Improve status-styling of `shiny::actionButton()`
description:
Currently, the official way to theme `shiny::actionButton()` is by adding the corresponding class (e.g. ´class = "btn-danger"`)

This, however, produces sub-optimal HTML output, because the code adds the default class regardless of this, resulting in

    <button class="btn btn-default action-button btn-light shiny-bound-input">

on the HTML side instead of

    <button class="btn btn-light action-button shiny-bound-input">

as it should be per the [bootstrap docs](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/4.0/components/buttons/#examples).

Two options provide a solution:

 1. Inspired by `shinyWidgets`, add a `status = c("default", "primary", "secondary", "success", "danger", "warning", "info", "light", "dark")` argument matched via `match.arg()`.
 2. Be smart about the `class` argument in `...`: If it contains `btn-*`, remove `btn-default` from the button classes and replace it with the provided style.

The first has better usability, but would make the assumption, that bootstrap will always have these styles.
The second wouldn't require any changes to the docs but inhibits discoverability of this theming functionality.

I would be happy to create a PR for either of those solutions, although I personally favor 1.
Please let me know if a PR is welcome and, if so, which alternative is preferred.

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- function(request){
  fluidPage(
    selectizeInput(
      "num_sel",
      label = "Select a number",
      choices = 1:3,
      selected = 1,
      multiple = TRUE
    ),
    textOutput("txt_out"),
    actionButton("useless_button", label="Useless button")
  )
}

server <- function(input, output, session){
  
  observeEvent(
    input[["useless_button"]],
    {
      updateSelectizeInput(
        inputId = "num_sel",
        choices = 1:3,
        selected = NULL
      )
    }
  )
  
  output[["txt_out"]] <- renderText(input[["num_sel"]])
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

According to shiny documentation in the updateSelectize function:
> Any arguments with NULL values will be ignored; they will not result in any changes to the input object on the client.

This is not the case as in the above application pressing the button removes the selected values and leave the selectize empty.

This only happens when the updateSelectize includes a choice updates. Therefore, it works fine when replacing the above observeEvent with:

```R
  observeEvent(
    input[["useless_button"]],
    {
      updateSelectizeInput(
        inputId = "num_sel",
        selected = NULL
      )
    }
  )
```

Although usually when the choices are updated, it is also common to update the selected values it is not always the case.

There are ways to solve this problem by for example doing something akin to:

```R
  observeEvent(
    input[["useless_button"]],
    {
      updateSelectizeInput(
       choices = 1:3,
        inputId = "num_sel",
        selected = input[["num_sel"]]
      )
    }
  )
```

Nonetheless the documentation as it is written now is confusing and can be misunderstood as it was my case.

Thanks for your help.

title: [Feature Request] Allow to pass URL parameters to runApp() and/or shinyApp()
description:
## Context 

I have a shiny app that behaves differently based on url parameters passed to it

## Pain point

When building this app, every time I relaunch the app, I need to refresh the browser with the url parameters included (either manually, or via a development widget built just for that purpose). 

## Feature Request

I'd love to be able to do something like: 

```r
runApp( urlParams = c(x = "xyz", a = "abcd") )
```

From reading the source code, it seems that this can be done here in runApp: 

```r
appUrl <- paste("http://", browseHost, ":", port, sep = "")
```

with something like

```r
appUrl <- paste("http://", browseHost, ":", port, sep = "")
if (!is.null(urlParams){
appUrl <- paste(
  appUrl, 
  "?",
	paste(
      names(urlParams),
      urlParams, 
      sep = "=", 
      collapse = "&"
    )
}
```

Let me know what you think, happy to do a PR!

Edit: this might be better to have it inside shinyApp() instead of runApp()

title: Fire js event when bind/unbind inputs
description:
I'm thinking about applying js globally to the shiny elements. One thing I notice is that some elements from `shiny` are added on demand. If the js script is initialized before these elements, then the modification cannot be fulfilled. 

Right now I wrote a loop to actively monitor the DOM changes. However, this approach is quite heavy. It would be great if shiny can fire events when bind/unbind actions occur. This will allow us to passively listen to the changes.

Thanks : )

```

### Example application

I have a parameterized RMarkdown PDF report that I am running from a Shiny flexdashboard. Shiny flexdashboard code:

```R
    ---
    title: "Company Report Frontend"
    output: 
      flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
        orientation: columns
        vertical_layout: fill
    runtime: shiny
    ---
    
    ```{r global, include=FALSE}
    library(flexdashboard)
    library(shiny)
    ```
    
    ### Select Company
    
    ```{r}
    textInput('name', label ='Firm')
    ```
   
    ### Report
    
    ```{r}
      uiOutput("downloadUI")
      
      # Create the actual downloadButton
      output$downloadUI <- renderUI( {
          downloadButton("downBtn", "Download Report")
      })
      
      # Add download handling
      output$downBtn <- downloadHandler(
            filename = "full_report.pdf",
            content = function(file) {
              rmarkdown::render("test_report.Rmd", output_file = file,
                params = list(input=input),
                envir = new.env(parent = globalenv()), clean = FALSE,
                intermediates_dir = '.',
                output_dir = '.',
                knit_root_dir = '.'
              )
            }
      )
    ```
```

And the parameterized RMarkdown doc `test_report.Rmd`:

```R
    ---
    title: "Report"
    header-includes: 
       \usepackage{graphicx}
       \usepackage{grffile}
       \usepackage{booktabs}
    params:
      input: NA
    output:
      pdf_document:
        latex_engine: xelatex
        keep_tex: true
    ---
    
    
    ```{r}
    input <- params$input 
    
    data(mtcars)
    plot(mtcars$hp, mtcars$mpg)
    title(input$name)
    ```
```

### Describe the problem in detail

When I run the dashboard, enter a name, and hit Download on Windows, it successfully produces the `.tex` file but then can't compile it. When I try to compile the `.tex` file directly in a LaTeX editor, I get `undefined control sequence` and `Missing endcsname defined` errors on any `\includegraphics` lines like this one:

```tex
\includegraphics{C:/User/LONGUS~1/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmpk1o7Q3/file1ec05b50167a_files/figure-latex/unnamed-chunk-1-1.pdf}
```

where `LONGUS~1` is a shortened folder name from the actual Windows username LONGUSERNAME.

The error goes away, and the PDF compiles, if I replace `LONGUS~1` with `LONGUSERNAME`, or just point it to the relative filepath. LaTeX does tend to get finicky about filepaths sometimes. 

Notes from lots of troubleshooting (and from helpful tips that turned out not to work from Google or from asking this on Twitter, StackExchange, and RStudio Community):

- The full absolute filepath in the `LONGUS~1` is in the knitted MD file before it's translated into `.tex`, so it's unlikely to be a Pandoc issue
- The problem does *not* appear if I run `render('test_report.Rmd')` from RStudio directly, or if I set a default `input` value and knit `test_report.Rmd` in Rstudio with the Knit button suggesting it is unlikely to be an RMarkdown issue either, but rather specifically a Shiny (or download button in Shiny) issue.
- The problem does not occur on Macs, just Windows (haven't tested *nix).
- Specifying a temporary directory filepath using a `tempdir()` or `normalizePath(tempdir())` does not solve the problem, nor does any number of configurations of setting the `_dir` options in `render()` that I tried. Even feeding it a full, un-shortened path with `normalizePath()` produces the shortened version in the `.md` output and thus the `.tex` output

I think this counts as a bug (although if someone wants to point out an option I'm missing that could get around this I'd be very happy with that). Thank you!

title: Allow updating of input values from JS
Bookmark via localStorage
description:
Currently `shiny` bookmark stores data on either URL or server. I was wondering if there is any way to store inputs in user browsers' `window.localStorage` and only export the storage keys? A use-case could be

* There are lots of inputs and URL query is too long to be usable. 
* The server might not support bookmark, or the server-side bookmark could potentially give away sensitive information of the users' (or privacy policies that require the server to store all the data on the client side).
* The users simply want to stage the inputs and resume the analysis on next login (no need to share the url with other people)

My proposal is that we can serialize inputs in javascript as string and store it in `window.localStorage` with the key to be the digested hash like `shinybookmark-20211101-070159-<hash>`. You can cap the number of bookmarks to be 1000. The date is stored in the key so you can quickly query the bookmarks to remove old ones.

In the case such that the url query string hits the hash, `Shiny` updates the date information, loads the stored inputs, and updates the input directly from js.

-----------------
PS: I also have a small extra question about how to update the shiny input widgets. I saw the current implementation in R uses `session$sendInputMessage(inputId, message)`. Is there any `js`-equivalent function that does the same thing? I was trying to implement my own version, but I found it quite inconsistent about the argname that refers to `value`. For example:

* `updateTextInput(..., value = xxx)` uses `value`
* `updateSelectInput(..., selected = xxx)` uses `selected`

It would be pretty hard to program code that automatically "guess" if `value` or `select` or some other arguments to use to update an input. I would be great if at `JS` level that we can use something like `Shiny.updateInput(id, value)` to update most (at least built-in) widgets.

title: Add a dots (...) argument to checkboxInput
description:
In working with DataTables in the `DT` package, I've learned how to implement working action buttons with the help of resources such as 

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51831190/actionbutton-within-datatable-doesnt-work-shiny-dt

(and my apologies to @yihui, as he had a really good example of this somewhere and I can't find it at the moment)

This happens to be possible for `actionButton` and `actionLink` because they have dots arguments.

I'd like to be able to do something similar with checkboxes, but can't do so "out of the box" with `shiny`.  because there is no dots argument. Implementation would look something like the following (with an example of usage following).  

I would be happy to create a pull request, but did not want to proceed with that as there may be good reasons not to do this that I'm not aware of.  Theoretically, I think this could also apply to `numericInput` and `textInput`.

What reasons might there be against doing this?

```
checkboxInput <- function(inputId, label, value = FALSE, width = NULL, ...) 
{
  value <- restoreInput(id = inputId, default = value)
  inputTag <- tags$input(id = inputId, type = "checkbox", ...) ########### dots added here!
  if (!is.null(value) && value) 
    inputTag$attribs$checked <- "checked"
  div(class = "form-group shiny-input-container", style = css(width = validateCssUnit(width)), 
      div(class = "checkbox", tags$label(inputTag, tags$span(label))))
}
```

## EXAMPLE

```
library(shiny)
library(htmltools)
library(DT)

shinyInput <- function(FUN, len, id, label, ...) {
  inputs <- character(len)
  
  for (i in seq_len(len)) {
    inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id, i),label=label, ...))
  }
  inputs
}

checkboxInputWithDots <- function(inputId, label, value = FALSE, width = NULL, ...) 
{
  value <- restoreInput(id = inputId, default = value)
  inputTag <- tags$input(id = inputId, type = "checkbox", ...)
  if (!is.null(value) && value) 
    inputTag$attribs$checked <- "checked"
  div(class = "form-group shiny-input-container", style = css(width = validateCssUnit(width)), 
      div(class = "checkbox", tags$label(inputTag, tags$span(label))))
}

EXAMPLE <- 
  data.frame(
    a = 1:2, 
    b = 3:4, 
    chk = shinyInput(checkboxInputDots, 
                     len = 2, 
                     id = "dt_chk_",
                     label = "",
                     onclick = paste0('Shiny.onInputChange( \"select_chk\" , this.id)')), 
    btn = shinyInput(shiny::actionButton, 
                     len = 2,
                     id = "dt_btn_",
                     label = "A Button",
                     onclick = paste0('Shiny.onInputChange( \"select_btn\" , this.id)'))
  )

runApp(
  shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
      verbatimTextOutput("value_check"),
      DT::dataTableOutput('table')
    ),
    
    server = function(input, output, session) {
      
      output$value_check <- 
        renderPrint({
          print(input$select_btn)
          print(input$select_chk)
        })
      
      output$table <- 
        DT::renderDataTable({
          datatable(EXAMPLE, 
                    rownames = FALSE, 
                    escape = FALSE,
                    selection = 'none'
          )}
        )
    }
  )
)
```

title: Automatically `freezeReactiveValue()` in `update*()`?
description:
I have a question related to #2946:

Wouldn't it make sense to automatically call `freezeReactiveValue()` in the `update*()` functions (e.g., in `updateSelectInput()`)? Currently, I can't think of a situation where an `update*()` function would make sense without `freezeReactiveValue()`. I may be wrong, though. But then, wouldn't it still make sense to automatically freeze in the `update*()` functions at least by default, e.g., by introducing an argument called something like `freeze` defaulting to `TRUE` (and then only freeze if `freeze` is `TRUE`)? If freezing always or by default are both too strong of a change (because they could be breaking existing apps), would it make sense to add such an argument `freeze` with default `FALSE`?

title: Idea: withReactiveConsole
description:
When building an app, I have the need to test for functions that are based on reactive elements.

```r
# dummy function
rv_ten <- function(val) {
  val(val() * 10)
  val
}
```

My current workflow is 

```r
test_that("reactive stuff works", {
  shiny::reactiveConsole(TRUE)
  x <- reactiveVal(2)
  x_modified <- rv_ten(x)
  expect_equal(x_modified(), 20)
  shiny::reactiveConsole(FALSE)
})
```

But that's quite repetitive to do this if I have to test multiple functions.

Other solutions are: 

```r
test_that("reactive stuff works", {
  withr::with_options(
    c("shiny.suppressMissingContextError" = TRUE),
    {
      x <- reactiveVal(2)
      x_modified <- rv_ten(x)
      expect_equal(x_modified(), 20)
    }
  )
})
```

But that's also a bit repetitive to do that several times.

Another option is 

```r 
shiny::testServer(
  app_server,
  {
    x <- reactiveVal(2)
    x_modified <- rv_ten(x)
    expect_equal(x_modified(), 20)
  }
)

```

But I'm not really testing the app_server here. 

So my idea would be `withReactiveConsole()`, that would mimic the "on/off" of the reactiveConsole. 

```r

withReactiveConsole <- function(expr) {
  shiny::reactiveConsole(TRUE)
  on.exit(
    shiny::reactiveConsole(FALSE)
  )
  force(expr)
}
```

So I can write:

```r
test_that("reactive stuff works", {
  withReactiveConsole({
    x <- reactiveVal(2)
    expect_equal(x(), 2)
  })
})
```

Let me know what you think, happy to send a PR. 

Colin

  tags$h1("Click the button to open the alert"),
  actionButton(
    inputId = "button",
    label = "Button"
  ),
  textOutput("out")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  shiny::observe({
    input$button
    cur_sys_call <- as.character(sys.call())
    print(cur_sys_call)

    output$out <- renderText(cur_sys_call)
  })


}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```
</details>


### Problem
In the current shiny Version 1.7.1 as well as in the most recent dev version 1.7.1.9000, `sys.call()` inside of `shiny::observe()` is different to its output in shiny 1.6.0. This has negative implications for logging behavior, in my case with the {lgr}-package.

```R
sys.call()
#>  "<observer>" "..."

# logging result
[2021-10-12 15:15:00] INFO :<observer> My Logging Message
```

```R

#> ::\nshiny\nobserve

# logging result
[2021-10-12 15:16:00] INFO :::
shiny
observe My Logging Message
```

I am am aware that this is not directly an issue for shiny itself and due to the new structure of the `observe()` function. However, it might be beneficial to users if `sys.call()`, when called inside of `x` in `shiny::observe()`, would actually return `"shiny::observe"`.
Any hints how to fix this outside of shiny would be appreciated, as well.

title: Support client side rendering for real time analytics
description:
I was recently demoed a commercial solution for real time streaming analytics visualization.
I was impressed by how smoothly the dashboard handled very many updates per second (financial market data).
I remarked that this would take 20 seconds between each update if I tried to do this in R Shiny.
The presenter responded with something along the lines "yes, especially because shiny uses server side rendering".

Unfortunately, as a data scientist, I have very limited knowledge of this aspect of the technology so I don't know how reasonable a feature request this is.

But it would be nice if I could get this kind of performance out of R Shiny, presumably using client side rendering.

title: Backwards incompatible behaviour change of isRunning() in v1.6.0
description:
### System details

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 4.0.3 (2020-10-10)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS

Matrix products: default
BLAS/LAPACK: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/openblas-pthread/libopenblasp-r0.3.8.so

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C
 [3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
 [5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=C
 [7] LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NAME=C
 [9] LC_ADDRESS=C               LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] compiler_4.0.3
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

#### `app/app.r`

```r
message('isRunning() = ', isRunning())
```

#### `run.r`

```r
shiny::runApp('app')
```

#### Run via

```sh
Rscript run.r 2>&1 | grep isRunning
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The example above yields a different result on Shiny v1.5.0 *vs* Shiny v1.6.0. Shiny v1.5.0 prints, as expected:

```
isRunning() = TRUE
```

whereas Shiny v1.6.0 prints

```
isRunning() = FALSE
```

(Both `RScript` commands fail with an error since no actual Shiny application has been defined, but that’s not relevant for this issue: I’m concerned with the behaviour *at file scope*.)

The change of behaviour of `isRunning` is unintentional as far as I can tell: its documentation didn’t change, and the changelog doesn’t mention this change. Furtthermore, `runApp` actually initialises the app state, which, in my understanding, should cause `isRunning()` to return `TRUE`:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/29b574bf94c56e69e621be8fd6d3b7eb0ae42a18/R/runapp.R#L124-L135

The issue, as far as I can tell, is that the code at file level inside the Shiny app is actually evaluated inside `as.shiny.appobj`, rather than later down the line, and thus *before* the Shiny options are set.

Unfortunately this behaviour breaks one of my packages, which relies on the value of `isRunning` to be set for the *entire* Shiny application code (klmr/box#237).

```{r}

  Sys.sleep(5)
  tf = tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
  cat(c(y,'\n'), sep='\n', file = tf)
  d = readBin(con = tf, what = "raw", n = file.size(tf))
  return(list(fn = basename(tf), d = d))
  }

writeFile = function (fut, f){
    x = fut[['d']]
    con = file(description = f, open = "wb")

    close(con)
}

renderUI({

  fileName = reactive({

      }
    )
  
  shiny::downloadButton(outputId = "button", label="Download")
})
```
````

Run the shiny app, then click the download button. Watch the R console.

### Describe the problem in detail

I am attempting to implement a `downloadHandler` so that if the file to be downloaded takes a while to create, it doesn't block everything. I'm using `future_promise` for this. When the `filename` function argument returns a promise, I get this error in the console:

```
Warning: Error in enc2utf8: argument is not a character vector
  [No stack trace available]
```

...and no download.

When I replace the `filename` argument with a character vector, it works. However, this means that doing things like making the filename depend on the file content is impossible.

Is there a way to make the `filename` argument of `downloadHandler` compatible with promises?

title: ion.rangeSlider.css doesn't get updated for users when shiny package is updated
description:
When updating from shiny 1.4.0.2 to 1.6.0 the ion.rangeSlider.css has been updated with a new version.
Web browsers that used the app before the upgrade has the old ion.rangeSlider.css file cached in the browser, and since the name is identical it's still used which causes graphical errors.

One possible solution could be to add version numbers to the css file so that in the future the web browsers cache won't block the download of the latest css.

title: Better ways to check visibility of render events
description:
I know that if a dynamic render element is not displayed at first, then it will not be rendered at all. I understand this and it saves resources. The problem is when it becomes visible, we need more than just change the `display` CSS, we also need to trigger the `shown` event.  Here is a simple example of `renderUI`

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("show", "show", onclick ="$('#div').css('display', 'block');"),
  div(id = "div", style = "display: none;", 
      actionButton("renderui", "renderui"), 
      uiOutput("ui")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
    observeEvent(input$renderui, {
       output$ui <- renderUI("aaa")
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
This will not work because I only change the display not firing the event, unless I do this `onclick ="$('#div').css('display', 'block'); $('#ui').trigger('shown')")`. 

1. This is unfriendly to most Shiny users. They just get started and begin to learn some CSS and they don't even know what is a listener. 
2. From a developer view: People nowadays are using newer frameworks like react, vue. I am not saying we should not use jquery, but we can see the trend that more apps will not include jquery in the future. Current shiny javascript for the `shown` event relies on jquery, and it checks some props that only belongs to jquery. 

For example, if I want to use native js to trigger the `shown` event

```js
document.getElementById('ui').dispatchEvent(new Event('shown', {bubbles: true}))
```
This will not work, because first I need to set up the `bubbles` and second shiny.js requires the `namespace` prop. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35240440/129992268-e891870e-9a54-4086-9252-2b09c40ad54e.png)

There is no good way I can think of to fix it in vanilla js. The additional data is provided in the `detail` property, and I can't find a way to attach the `namespace`. 

 As a developer myself feel it is not convenient to write app in this way. I need to spend hours to find out the reason is I missed the `namespace` property. I need to remember all of this next time and who knows if there are some other special requirements that are specifically relying on jquery in other cases.  

I don't really have some good solutions but just some thoughts: 1. Have a better user-friendly way to check for dynamic UI visibility problem; 2. Maybe it is time to think about the compatibility of shiny in newer frameworks without jquery.

title: tags$img not refreshing to display in the UI
description:
I have created an app that uploads an image and displays it but noticed that it wasn't working properly anymore. When a second image is uploaded the UI doesn't refresh and only the original image is shown. It seems that `tags$img` is behaving different than it did before. 

I noticed that when I use `tags$iframe` it works as expected, which is that when a 2nd image is uploaded the 2nd image is displayed in the app. Then I also noticed if I use `tags$iframe` and `tags$img` to display the same item it works as expected where the 2nd item uploaded is displayed. 

This example only uses `tags$img`, if you upload an image then it displays it but when you upload a 2nd image the first image is still displayed. The UI doesn't seem to update to display the 2nd image. 
```
library(shiny)

options(shiny.maxRequestSize=12*1024^2)

ui <- fluidPage(  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      uiOutput("ui_file_input")
    ),
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput("ui_upload")
    )
  )
)


server <- function(input, output) {
  
  rv <- reactiveValues(
    upload_state = NULL,
    img = NULL
  )
  
  output$ui_file_input <- renderUI({
    fileInput("upload",
              label = NULL,
              accept = c(".jpg", ".jpeg")
    )
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$upload, {
    rv$upload_state <- "upload"
  })

  observe({
    req(rv$upload_state)
    test_file <- readBin(con = input$upload$datapath, what = "raw", n = input$upload$size)
    writeBin(test_file, "www/fieldphoto.jpeg")
    addResourcePath("www", "www")
  })
  
  output$ui_upload <- renderUI({
    req(input$upload)
    tags$img(src = "www/fieldphoto.jpeg", width = "300px")
  })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```


When I add a 2nd output that is linked to `tags$iframe` it behaves as expected. An image is uploaded and displays as normal and when a 2nd image is upload it updates to display the 2nd image in both the `tags$img` and `tags$iframe` outputs. 
```
library(shiny)

options(shiny.maxRequestSize=12*1024^2)

ui <- fluidPage(
  
  sidebarLayout(
    
    sidebarPanel(
      uiOutput("ui_file_input")
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput("ui_upload"),
      uiOutput("ui_upload2")
    )
  )
)


server <- function(input, output) {
  
  rv <- reactiveValues(
    upload_state = NULL,
    img = NULL
  )
  
  output$ui_file_input <- renderUI({
    fileInput("upload",
              label = NULL,
              accept = c(".jpg", ".jpeg")
    )
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$upload, {
    rv$upload_state <- "upload"
  })

  observe({
    req(rv$upload_state)
    test_file <- readBin(
      con = input$upload$datapath, what = "raw", n = input$upload$size
    )
    writeBin(test_file, "www/fieldphoto.jpeg")
    addResourcePath("www", "www")
  })
  
  
  # this displays the uploaded card
  output$ui_upload <- renderUI({
    req(input$upload)
    tags$img(src = "www/fieldphoto.jpeg", width = "300px")
  })
  
  
  output$ui_upload2 <- renderUI({
    req(input$upload)
    tags$iframe(src = "www/fieldphoto.jpeg", width = "300px")
  })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

This was working as expected in the past, not sure the exact timeline but sometime with the last few months I think. The examples above are a simple reprex as the issue is part of a much larger Shiny app.  I don't understand why `iframe` causes the UI to update but not `img`. The correct files are appearing in the `www` folder. It seems to be a problem with what is being displayed.

title: Enable `fileInput` to set the `capture` attribute
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file a feature request! Please take the time to search for an existing feature request, to avoid creating duplicate requests. If you find an existing feature request, please give it a thumbs-up reaction, as we'll use these reactions to help prioritize the implementation of these features in the future.

If the feature has not yet been filed, then please describe the feature you'd like to see become a part of Shiny. See:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Writing-Good-Feature-Requests

for a guide on how to write good feature requests.

-->

Currently, the `fileInput` component in the Shiny framework does not support the [`capture`](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-media-capture/) HTML5 attribute. This feature will be of great help to any developer who is going to integrate image recognition functionality in their deep learning mobile application using a direct feed from the camera/microphone instead of select an image/audio file to upload.

Please help me up vote [this pull request](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3481) that resolves this issue to find its way into the main RStudio/Shiny framework repository.

Meanwhile, you can use the following code to work around this limitation in the current version of the Shiny framework:

```r
addCaptureAtt <- function(x, id, camera){
  if (is.list(x)) {
    if ('id' %in% names(x) && x$id == id) {
      x$capture = camera
    } else {
      if (length(x) > 0) for(i in 1:length(x)) x[[i]] <- addCaptureAtt(x[[i]], id, camera)
    }
  }
  return(x)
}

capturePhoto <- function(id, ..., camera = 'environment'){
  fileInput.tags <- fileInput(id, ...)
  fileInput.tags <- addCaptureAtt(fileInput.tags, id, camera)
  
  return(fileInput.tags)
}

ui <- fluidPage(
  capturePhoto('photo', NULL, buttonLabel = 'Capture', accept = 'image/*')
)
```

title: fileInput creates errors with with other drag and drop actions
description:
```r
library(shiny)
library(sortable)
ui <- fluidPage(
    fileInput("abc", "abc"),
    rank_list(
        text = "Drag the items in any desired order",
        labels = 1:10,
        input_id = "rank_list_basic"
    )
)
server <- function(input, output) {}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```
When you start to drag, this happens: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35240440/128115820-da1fe4eb-a91d-48cd-91b8-d5b1810c61b9.png)

The reason is when fileInput is used `input_binding_fileinput.js` adds listeners to all HTML tags to watch for DnD actions. This creates conflicts with other DnD actions either from custom scripts or other js libs. It is good that fileInput supports DnD but adding listeners to the whole HTML is a quick solution but should be avoided.

```
</details>

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```r
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    tags$head(
      HTML(
        '<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.13.13/dist/katex.min.css" integrity="sha384-RZU/ijkSsFbcmivfdRBQDtwuwVqK7GMOw6IMvKyeWL2K5UAlyp6WonmB8m7Jd0Hn" crossorigin="anonymous">
        <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.13.13/dist/katex.min.js" integrity="sha384-pK1WpvzWVBQiP0/GjnvRxV4mOb0oxFuyRxJlk6vVw146n3egcN5C925NCP7a7BY8" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
        <script defer src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/katex@0.13.13/dist/contrib/auto-render.min.js" integrity="sha384-vZTG03m+2yp6N6BNi5iM4rW4oIwk5DfcNdFfxkk9ZWpDriOkXX8voJBFrAO7MpVl" crossorigin="anonymous" onload="renderMathInElement(document.body);"></script>'
      ),
      tags$script(
        HTML(
          "$(document).on('shiny:value', (event) => {renderMathInElement(event.target);});"
        )
      )
    ),
    fluidRow(
      column(
        3,
        h4("KaTeX", strong("static"), "math:"),
        p("$$\\alpha$$"),
        hr(),
        h4("KaTeX", strong("dynamic"), "math:"),
        textInput("dynamic_input", NULL, "$$\\beta$$"),
        p(uiOutput("beta"))
      )
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$beta <- renderUI({
      input$dynamic_input
    })
  }
)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

I try to replace MathJax in my apps with KaTeX, as it is waaay faster and its [Auto-render extension](https://katex.org/docs/autorender.html) can reach `tableOutput`s and even HTML Widgets, such as `DT`, pretty well. However, it fails, of course, when the target output is updated (from `R` or elsewhere, doesn't matter), as the Auto-render extension of KaTeX is run when `DOMContentLoaded` event is fired.

So I wrote a little "appendix" that observes any `shiny:value` event and rerun the math rendering only on the `event.target`:

```js
$(document).on('shiny:value', (event) => {renderMathInElement(event.target);});
```

Here we come to the issue I think pertains the `shiny` package - according to the article on [JavaScript events in Shiny](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/js-events.html), the `shiny:value` should be used _"if you want to do something when the output value is rendered"_ (section _Output Events_, paragraph 4). **One would assume that after this event is fired, nothing additional happens** and the output (`.shiny-html-output`) is open to another bussinesses. **Yet it turns out that's not the case: bunch of stuff happens afterwards - the math is first correctly rendered, but then the output is rewritten by `shiny` JS.** If I wrap the KaTeX render call into `setTimeout(() => {renderMathInElement(event.target);}, 1);`, it works like a charm (even with such a ridiculous time like 1 milisecond), but the solution isn't any appealing to me.

I have been playing with some breakpoints in Chrome DevTools, so I discovered the timeline outlined above (because from a user perspective, the math simply _never renders_), but the proper solution is far beyond my paygrade. Maybe you can add another `shiny` JS event that would fire _after_ output is fully shown, maybe I'm missing something.

title: Showcase Mode doesn't trace files in R/ directory

[Showcase Mode](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/debugging.html) appears only to trace code in the top-level `ui` and `server` components of a Shiny app, and not in the app's R/ directory (where you would find `global.R` and modules). Minimal example of an app that tracks a button being clicked, but Showcase Mode does not trace the module itself:

module_ui <- function(id) {
    ns <- NS(id)
    tagList(

        textOutput(ns("txt"))

    moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
        txt <- eventReactive(input$btn, input$btn)
        output$txt <- renderPrint(txt()[[1]])
    })
}

library(shiny)

title: Regression with session$setCurrentTheme() not refreshing stylesheets
description:
After #3333, I've noticed some situations where `session$setCurrentTheme()` won't always disable old stylesheets. For example, note that with this example, sometimes when changing the theme, the `transitionend` event won't fire and in that case you'll see slate's border styles "leak" into the flatly theme:

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
slate <- bs_theme(bootswatch = "slate")
flatly <- bs_theme(bootswatch = "flatly")
ui <- navbarPage(
  theme = slate,
  title = "Navbar title",
  tabPanel("A", "a"),
  tabPanel("B", "b"),
  header = selectInput("theme", "Choose theme", selected = "slate", c("slate", "flatly"))
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$theme, {
    theme <- if (identical(input$theme, "flatly")) flatly else slate
    session$setCurrentTheme(theme)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

(This can also be reproduced by changing Bootswatch themes in `bs_theme_preview()` -- you'll be able to see similar "leaking" of one theme into another)

title: detect recursive runApp calls
description:
Given an `app.R` that accidentally calls `shiny::runApp`:

```R
# app.R
shiny::runApp("sub")
```

That `sub` directory is any other valid Shiny application; it may exist on the local filesystem or made available through some other R package.

It is enough to have a trivial Shiny application to demonstrate this problem:

```R
# sub/app.R
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage("hello, shiny")
server <- function(input, output) {}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

When that top-level Shiny application is launched, `runApp` is run beneath another `runApp` invocation. As a result, the requested port is not used.

```console
R -s -e 'shiny::runApp(getwd(), port = 3939)'
# => Loading required package: shiny
# => 
# => Listening on http://127.0.0.1:3288
```

Note how Shiny reports that it is listening on a different port than the requested one.

Shiny should detect that `runApp` is running beneath another `runApp` and react to this situation (with an error?).

title: updateSelectizeInput Triggers Reactive Chain Twice if server = TRUE
description:
### Bug Description
`updateSelectizeInput()` does change its updated value twice if `server = TRUE`. First, it sets the selected value to `""` and **afterwards** updates the value. This causes the reactive chain to trigger twice.

You can see this behavior by changing "Input 1" and checking the difference in the print-result whether the checkbox is ticked or not. There should not be an empty Input 2 in my opinion.


### Example application


```R


library(shiny)
set.seed(123)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("updateSelectizeInput triggers twice"),


  # main UI
  mainPanel(
    checkboxInput(inputId = "use_server",
                  label = "Use server side Processing in updateSelectizeInput()",
                  value = TRUE),
    selectizeInput(inputId = "in1",
                   label = "Input 1",
                   choices = 1:3,
                   selected = 1),
    selectizeInput(inputId = "in2",
                   label = "Input 2",
                   choices = letters,
                   selected = NULL)
  )

)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # show server checkbox value
  observeEvent(input$use_server, ignoreInit = FALSE, ignoreNULL = FALSE, {
    print(paste("server:", input$use_server))
    })

  # show input 1 value
  observeEvent(input$in1, ignoreInit = FALSE, ignoreNULL = FALSE, {
    print(paste("Input 1:", input$in1))
    })

  # show input 2 value
  observeEvent(input$in2, ignoreInit = FALSE, ignoreNULL = FALSE, {
    print(paste("Input 2:", input$in2))
    })

  # trigger update if input 2
  observeEvent(input$in1, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = FALSE, {
    choices <- sample(LETTERS, size = 5)
    updateSelectizeInput(session = session,
                         inputId = "in2",
                         choices = choices,
                         selected = choices[1],
                         server = input$use_server)
  })
}

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Downloading / uploading large files: md5 checksum does not always match
description:
Hi there !

We need to import / export large files for a Shiny offline app: users need to be able to backup and re-import all their data. It could be huge. Spatial application with a lot of layers.

We got something weird. Sometimes while uploading a large file the md5 checksum is off. The data appears to be corrupted.

I created a minimal reproducible app in a docker image to isolate everything.

title: fileInput <label> element not directly linked to <input>
description:
Is this a bug in input-file.R? https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/bcb7cde44bc3655b35257fd3cde5c2ee56028148/R/input-file.R#L116

There was a [question on stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/67939403/wcag-2-1-compatibility-with-shinydashboard-app-form-label) where someone was trying to make their fileInput control meet WCAG accessibility requirements. On reading the code in input-file.R I noticed that the tags$label element doesn't seem to be linked to the tags$input element.

The easiest way to link them would be to put the input _inside_ the label (move that closing parenthesis down three lines), or failing that use a [for attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/label#attr-for).

The full definition in input-file.R looks like this:

```R
    div(class = "input-group",
      # input-group-prepend is for bootstrap 4 compat
      tags$label(class = "input-group-btn input-group-prepend",
        span(class = "btn btn-default btn-file", buttonLabel, inputTag)
      ), # this is line 116 (tags$input could be moved above this line)
      tags$input(type = "text", class = "form-control",
        placeholder = placeholder, readonly = "readonly"
      )
    ),
```

title: Should all TypeScript config files be moved from `./srcts` to `./`
description:
Pros for keeping all configs at `./srcts`
* Does not clutter the top level repo. The configs only pertain to `./srcts`

Pros for moving all configs to `./`
* When working on TypeScript code, no need to open the `./srcts` subfolder as a new VS Code project
* Able to install Shiny package from GitHub.
	* Not able to install a NodeJS package from a GitHub subdirectory: (Denied) https://github.com/npm/npm/issues/2974
* husky (pre-commit) hooks work out of the box
	* (Can work in a custom directory like `./srcts` - https://typicode.github.io/husky/#/?id=custom-directory)

---------------

Other approach:

Keep all TS files in `./srcts`, but add an _additional_ `package.json` in the root folder that contains husky (pre-commit) hooks and points to type declarations within `./srcts`.  
* Pro: 
	* This may not be a bad approach as developer usage and Shiny application execution are different goals.
	* Top level folder only gains `package.json` 
		* Allows external developers to install the Shiny type definitions
* Con: 
	* It will lead to confusion as to why there are two package.json files.
	* Still requires internal developers to open the project on the `./srcts` folder to have the VS Code IDE work as expected.

---------------

Not having a `package.json` in the top level is a deal breaker. This prevents developers from being able to install nodejs packages from a subdirectory.  Once type definitions are exported, having the `package.json` in a subdirectory prevents users from being able to import the Shiny TypeScript type definitions.

title: Sending NULL to custom message handler drops the message altogether
description:
## Problem

You cannot send `NULL` via `session$sendCustomMessage` as this will drop the message altogether. Looking into the code https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/2360bde13efac1fe501efee447a8f3dde0136722/R/shiny.R#L1388-L1392 
it is apparent that setting the message to `NULL` will simply delete the slot in the message resulting in an empty message.

I stumbled upon this, b/c `session$sendModal` on the other hand can deal with `NULL` messages
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/2360bde13efac1fe501efee447a8f3dde0136722/R/shiny.R#L1300-L1304

Thus, you should be either clear in the documentation that sending `NULL` is not supported or change the code to something like this:

```r
sendCustomMessage = function(type, message) {
  data <- list()
  if (is.null(message)) {
    data[type] <- list(NULL)
  } else {
    data[[type]] <- message
  }
  private$sendMessage(custom = data)
}
```

## Reprex

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
   tags$head(
      tags$script(
         paste("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('callback', function(msg) {",
               "   if (msg === null) {",
               "      console.log('null passed');",
               "   } else {",
               "      console.log('non null passed');",
               "   }",
               "})", sep = "\n")
      )
   ),
   actionButton("send_null", "Send NULL"),
   actionButton("send_one", "Send 1")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
   observeEvent(input$send_null, session$sendCustomMessage('callback', NULL))
   observeEvent(input$send_one, session$sendCustomMessage('callback', 1))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: processDeps() doesn't correctly resolve tags
description:
All of dynamic UI (i.e., `insertUI()`, `uiOutput()`, etc) runs through the internal `processDeps()` function, and at the moment, it doesn't `htmltools:::tagify()` ui before sending it to the client. As a result, passing a tag-like object with an `as.tags()` method (i.e., htmlwidgets, `tagAddRenderHook()`, etc) through dynamic UI doesn't work the way you'd expect it to, for example:

```r
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
ui <- fluidPage(uiOutput("m"))
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$m <- renderUI(leaflet() %>% addTiles())
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
Error in if: argument is of length zero
```

I don't think we've noticed this subtle issue before since, if you wrap the UI in a `list()` or `tagList()`, things just happen to work because `htmltools:::flattenTags()` winds up calling `as.tags()` on the contents of the list. However, this doesn't negate the fact `processDeps()` should be processing the top-level UI object with `htmltools::tagify()` (it already does this to `findDependencies()` but the `tagify()`-ing should be done up-front and passed along to `doRenderTags()`)

title: Make exprToFunction()/nstallExprFunction() work with quosures
description:
shiny 1.6.0 started the deprecation of the `env` and `quoted` parameters in reactive consumers (e.g., reactive(), `renderText()`, etc) in favor of using `rlang::inject()` with quosures (as explained in depth here https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3108), for example:

```r
a <- 1
quo <- rlang::quo(1 + !!a)
rlang::inject(shiny::renderText(!!quo))()
```

This works because shiny 1.6's reactive consumers switch from using `installExprFunction()`  to `quoToFunction()`. However, since other packages that implement their own render functions (e.g., `htmlwidgets::shinyRenderWidget()`) still use `installExprFunction()` (or `exprToFunction()`), they don't work with the `inject()` approach to supplying quoted expressions

title: updateRadioButtons(inline=FALSE) does not remove the `shiny-input-container-inline` class from the parent div
description:
Related to https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3350 but separate issue.

Defining a `radioButtons()` as inline causes the radio button parent div (the div that has the input's ID) to get a class of `shiny-input-container-inline` and each of the labels have a class of `radio-inline`. If a `radioButtons()` is defined with the default `inline=FALSE` then none of these classes are added to the DOM. 

When `updateRadioButtons(inline=FALSE)` is called on on radio buttons that were previously `inline=TRUE`, the `shiny-input-container-inline` is not removed from the parent div, which can cause visual issues because now there's an inconsistency between the parent thinking it's inline and the options not being inline.

I haven't checked but this might be the case for checkboxgroup as well.

title: updateRadioButtons bug: always reverts to `inline=FALSE` unless explicitly told not to
description:
For most inputs, their corresponding `update*()` function has a default value of `NULL` to all the parameters, and only parameters that are explicitly used get updated.

This is not the case with the `inline` parameter of `updateRadioButtons` and `updateCheckboxGroupInput`. The `inline` argument has a default value of `FALSE`, which means that if I initialize a radio button with `inline=TRUE` and later update the choices, I get the undesired side effect of removing the inline.

Example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("test", "test", letters[1:2], inline = TRUE),
  actionButton("go", "go")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$go, {
    updateRadioButtons(session, "test", choices = LETTERS[1:2])
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The only way around this right now is to explicitly keep adding `inline=TRUE` to every update call. Fixing this will be technically a breaking change, and I'm generally conservative about breaking changes but this seems to be the right thing to do.

I checked all other input functions and other than `inline` for radio buttons and checkboxes, the only other non-NULL arguments seem to be in `updateSelectizeInput()` (and `updateVarSelectizeInput()`) with the `options` and `server` arguments.

title: runGitHub looks for the "master" branch by default, but GitHub is changing to "main"
description:
In October of 2020, GitHub changed its terminology so that what used to be the `master` branch is now the `main` branch. 

`runGitHub()` has a default where it looks for the app on the `master` branch. So, if you make a new repo, `runGitHub` will be looking for a branch that does not exist. If you know this is the issue, you can just use the `ref="main` argument to fix this, but if you don't know that is the problem it is not obvious what is going on.

title: htmlDependency used in dynamic UI breaks when `script` is provided as a named list instead of a string
description:
Not sure if this should be filed under {htmltools} or {shiny} - I filed it here because the interaction with shiny is what's broken from what I can tell.

To use `htmlDependency` to load a javascript module, we need to use `script = list(src = "test.js", type = "module")`. This works fine when the dependency is resolved from the UI, but it seems to parse incorrectly when done dynamically. Example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  htmltools::attachDependencies(
    "test",
    htmltools::htmlDependency(
      name = "test",
      version = "1.0.0",
      src = c(href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/daattali/htmldependencybug"),
      script = list(src = "test.js", type = "module")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The above code works - you'll see a javascript alert.

But if the content is loaded dynamically -- either using insertUI or using a uiOutput/renderUI -- then it breaks. Example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  uiOutput("test")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$test <- renderUI({
    htmltools::attachDependencies(
      "test",
      htmltools::htmlDependency(
        name = "test",
        version = "1.0.0",
        src = c(href = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/daattali/htmldependencybug"),
        script = list(src = "test.js", type = "module")
      )
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The page loads but the javascript module isn't loaded. Looking at the page source, I can see that it's trying to load a script with src of `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/daattali/htmldependencybug/%5Bobject%20Object%5D` - this is what's causing this bug. It seems that shiny does not know how to deal with the `script` argument being a named list, even though a named list is  allowed according to the documentation.

title: Allow option for nested directories in R/ folder to be sourced automatically with runApp()
description:
As described in the documentation [here](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/app-formats.html):

> As of Shiny version 1.3.2.9001, any .R files found in an R/ directory adjacent to your app will be automatically loaded when your app starts. Just like R packages, only the files at the top level of R/ are considered; nested directories are ignored. Files in this directory are sourced in alphabetical order and any variables, functions, or modules they create are available to be used in your app.R, ui.R, or server.R files.

It would be useful to have an option to allow nested directories to be sourced, rather than ignored. I often have a layout like this in my app's R/ directory:

```
R/
|---- global.R
|---- modules
        |---- module1.R
        |---- module2.R
        |---- module3.R
        |---- particularlyLargeTopic/
                |---- module4.R
                |---- module5.R
```

Currently, calling `runApp` (or clicking Run App in RStudio) will only source `global.R`, ignoring all the nested files.

(Note that the documentation linked above has a warning that this automatic sourcing of scripts in R/ is only available in the development version of Shiny, which is outdated advice now.)

My current workaround is just to read in all data, which isn't too annoying but would be nice to avoid:

```
invisible(sapply(list.files('./R', full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE), function(i) {
    source(paste0(i))
}))
```

Perhaps adding the following option that defaults to FALSE but can be set TRUE, in the style of `shiny.autoload.r`:

`options(shiny.autoload.r.nested = FALSE)`

title: fileInput
description:
The issue tracker is not for questions. If you have a question, please feel free to ask it on our community site, at https://community.rstudio.com/c/shiny.

After having upgraded which shiny version I am using, I am experiencing a new issue with the fileInput.
specifically the _input_ element with attributes:
- class="shiny-bound-input shinyjs-resettable"
- type="file"
- **style="position: absolute !important; top: -99999px !important; left: -99999px !important;"**

which is a child of the _span_ element with attributes:
- class="btn btn-default btn-file"

The issue is that which is in bold, the inline style for the _input_ element

ref lines 94, 95 at https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/input-file.R
```
    # Don't use "display: none;" style, which causes keyboard accessibility issue; instead use the following workaround: https://css-tricks.com/places-its-tempting-to-use-display-none-but-dont/
    style = "position: absolute !important; top: -99999px !important; left: -99999px !important;"
```

The issue is that when clicking the span element that acts as the interface, it will scroll the window to the very top left of the page no matter where the span and label elements appear on screen
This is probably not an issue with the style of the file input element itself, but rather the event handling for the span element onclick which should reference the position of the span element itself, not of its child input element

title: Misleading documentation regarding global.R
description:
I've just spent a few hours wandering around on the internet trying to understand the difference between putting things in `global.R` vs `app.R`  The discussion linked in #1063 finally cleared things up.  I understand that issue is still outstanding, but perhaps some misleading docs could be updated?

In particular
* Most importantly, the documentation for `shinyApp()` argument `onStart`
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/d582e53f73ff61953ee209c870eabb3bc7124288/R/shinyapp.R#L23-L25 This is incorrect (at least for an `app.R`), as if I understand things correctly, `shinyAppDir()` ignores `global.R` if using an `app.R`.

title: navbarPage() doesn't allow for right aligned nav
description:
We should at least support it with BS4+ with an API like

```r
navbarPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(),
  tabPanel("left1", "Left 1"),
  tabPanel("left2", "Left 2"),
  rightNav = list(
    tabPanel("right1", "Right 1"),

  )

```

title: Make it easier to include header/footer content in tabsetPanel()/navlistPanel()
description:
`navbarPage()` has `header`/`footer` arguments for including content that should appear on every 'page'. This is a quite useful feature that is missing from `tabsetPanel()` and `navlistPanel()`. For example, if I wanted to add a link break bewteen the nav and content, I currently have to do that on every tab:

```r
tabsetPanel(
  tabPanel("a", br(), "a"),
  tabPanel("b", br(), "b")
)
```

It'd be much easier to do:

```r
tabsetPanel(
  header = br(),
  tabPanel("a",  "a"),
  tabPanel("b", "b")
)
```

This would also open the possibility of including inputs/outputs that should appear on every tab:

```r
tabsetPanel(
  header = textInput("foo", "bar"),
  tabPanel("a",  "a"),
  tabPanel("b", "b")
)
```

title: Tab panel behavior when shiny tags are supplied
description:
It's strange that providing HTML tags to `...` inside `navbarPage()` 'works' in the sense that it creates an empty nav item that doesn't control anything, and also includes the tag on every tab. We should throw a warning in this case, and point to `header`/`footer` as a more official/better way to include content on each tab

```r
shinyApp(
  navbarPage(
    "Title",
    div("other stuff 1"),
    tabPanel("a", "tab a"),
    div("other stuff 2"),
    tabPanel("b", "tab b"),
    div("other stuff 3")
  ),
  function(input, output) { }
)
```

title: Tab panel functions don't produce Bootstrap 4 compatible markup
description:
And as a result, `tabsetPanel()` et al. don't work well with Bootstrap 4 "plugin" frameworks like Bootswatch 4 or AdminLTE 3, which make strong assumptions about nav (as well as other) markup. In addition to working better with these frameworks, if `tabPanel()` markup produced the right markup when it's aware that Bootstrap 4 is relevant (via it's `{bslib}` integration), then folks can also use tabs without the compatibility layer that comes by default with `bs_theme()`

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bs_theme() %>% bs_remove("bs3compat"),
  tabsetPanel(
    id = "tabset", type = "pills",
    tabPanel("A", "a"),
    tabPanel("B", "b"),
    navbarMenu(
      "More letters", 
      tabPanel("C", "c"),
      tabPanel("D", "d")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  observe(print(input$tabset))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: 1.6.0 change to runApp working directory behavior
description:
### System details
```
R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS
```

### Example application
I'm in a project directory called `repro`, and in it I have a folder `subdir`, that contains a shiny app file.

The contents of `repro/subdir/sample.R` are as follows:
```
library(shiny)

setwd('..')

UI <- fluidPage()

Server <- function(input, output, session){
  print(getwd())
}

shinyApp(UI, Server)
```
OUTPUT:
```
Restarting R session...

> packageVersion("shiny")
[1] ‘1.5.0’
> getwd()
[1] "/home/ajp1/workspaces/dashboard/repro"
> shiny::runApp('subdir/sample.R')
Loading required package: shiny

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:6030
[1] "/home/ajp1/workspaces/dashboard/repro"
```
And after upgrading to 1.6.0:
```
> packageVersion("shiny")
[1] ‘1.6.0’
> getwd()
[1] "/home/ajp1/workspaces/dashboard/repro"
> shiny::runApp('subdir/sample.R')
Loading required package: shiny

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:4599
[1] "/home/ajp1/workspaces/dashboard/repro/subdir"
```

In 1.5.0, the call to `setwd('..')` is reflected in the working directory inside the running app, whereas in 1.6.0, the app's working directory is the file's parent folder. If this behavior is intentional, I would expect to see it in the changelog.
The same behavior is observed if `shinyAppFile` is called instead of `runApp`.

description:

Download example app & profile specification: wget \ 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/master/021-selectize-plot/server.R' \ 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/master/021-selectize-plot/ui.R' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/.guix-channels.scm?inline=false' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/.guix-manifest.scm?inline=false' # Build profile. guix time-machine --channels=.guix-channels.scm \ package --profile=.guix-profile --manifest=.guix-manifest # Load profile. GUIX_PROFILE=.guix-profile source $GUIX_PROFILE/etc/profile # Launch app: Rscript -e 'shiny::runApp(launch.browser = FALSE)' ``` ### Describe the problem in detail #### Background I am developing an app under Gentoo Linux that runs just fine locally. It is meant to be deployed on a ShinyServer running on a remote (CentOS) machine where I do *not* have root access. I can install software on the remote machine without elevated priviliges (and ensure a (bit-wise!) reproducible environment) thougj using the [GNU Guix](https://guix.gnu.org) package manager. Thus, before deploying, I can setup the *exact* same environment that will be available on the target remote CentOS system on my local Gentoo system (where I have installed Guix from [this overlay](https://github.com/trofi/nix-guix-gentoo), #### Problem I experienced issues in my app (running locally using the Guix environment) that I managed to trace back to an input being empty that I had setup following the server-side example in [this article](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html) by @yihui. Unfortunately, I am not at liberty to share the full code but basically I am using a `selectizeInput` to convinently pick one out of many features to generate a specific plot for. Since 'many' means tens of thousands, client-side `selectize` is infeasible. It is my understanding that the only way to specify server-side `selectize` is by using `updateSelectizeInput` in the `server` function of the Shiny app. Trying to trouble-shoot this issue, I happened to notice that the exact same code works just fine using my local systems R installation. However, both environments use the exact same version of the `shiny` package. #### Detailed reproducible example Since I cannot share my code (and even if I could, it would be anything but a minimal example), I decided to start with [a basic public example app utilizing server-side `selectize`](https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/selectize-rendering-methods.html) and narrow it down from there. Due to the nature of Guix, reproducing my exact environment should be very easy. If you are unfamiliar with Guix, for this purpose you can think of it as an alternative to `conda`, though unlike `conda` (as far as I know) it guarantees bit-wise identity of the installed binaries and *all* their dependencies *as well as* the relevant environment. I uploaded the required files to [this snippet](https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787) for your convenience. What follows is a detailed transcript of the steps I have taken to reproduce the issue on any system providing the GNU Guix package manager: ##### Setup First, I downloaded the [server-side selectize example app](https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/selectize-rendering-methods.html) scripts as well [the files I created for easy reproduction of this issue](https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787): ```sh wget \ 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/master/021-selectize-plot/server.R' \ 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/master/021-selectize-plot/ui.R' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/.guix-channels.scm?inline=false' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/.guix-manifest.scm?inline=false' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/01.server.drop_maps.switch-to-client-side.patch' \ 'https://gitlab.com/-/snippets/2086787/raw/master/02.server.switch-back-to-server-side.patch' ``` ##### Confirm example works in Gentoo environment Next, I ensured I was running the host system's (in my case: Gentoo Linux) R installation by default: ```sh which R ``` ``` /usr/bin/R ``` Then I started an R session: ```sh R ``` From there, I ran the example app: ```R shiny::runApp() ``` The app opened in my browser and all was well. Next, I stopped the app from the R console by pressing `Ctrl+C` and finished by taking note of the session parameters: ```R sessionInfo() ``` ``` R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22) Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: Gentoo/Linux Matrix products: default BLAS: /usr/lib64/libblas.so.3.9.0 LAPACK: /usr/lib64/R/lib/libRlapack.so locale: [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.utf8 LC_NUMERIC=C LC_TIME=en_US.utf8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.utf8 LC_MONETARY=en_US.utf8 [6] LC_MESSAGES=en_US.utf8 LC_PAPER=en_US.utf8 LC_NAME=C LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.utf8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C withr_2.4.1 digest_0.6.27 later_1.1.0.1 mime_0.10 R6_2.5.0 jsonlite_1.7.2 lifecycle_1.0.0 [9] xtable_1.8-4 magrittr_2.0.1 rlang_0.4.10 cachem_1.0.4 promises_1.2.0.1 jquerylib_0.1.3 DT_0.17 bslib_0.2.4 = "no") ``` ##### Confirm example app does not work in Guix environment Next, I setup a new Guix profile with the required packages and loaded it in a new shell session: ```sh guix time-machine --channels=.guix-channels.scm \ package --profile=.guix-profile --manifest=.guix-manifest $SHELL GUIX_PROFILE=.guix-profile source $GUIX_PROFILE/etc/profile ``` To be sure, I double-checked that my
