example app. Since I did not configure a browser in that new environment, I disabled the auto-launch: ```R shiny::runApp(launch.browser = FALSE) ``` ``` Listening on http://127.0.0.1: ``` Now I switched back to my browser still running the (crashed) old instance of the app and manually modified the port to match ``. The app loaded, but the `selectize` dropdown remained empty and the `plot` output errored with ``` Error: argument is of length zero ``` Again, I killed the app via `Ctrl+C` and, for comparison, printed the sesssion information just as for the previous one: ```R sessionInfo() ``` ``` R version 4.0.4 (2021-02-15) Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: Gentoo/Linux Matrix products: default BLAS/LAPACK: /gnu/store/bs9pl1f805ins80xaf4s3n35a0x2lyq3-openblas-0.3.9/lib/libopenblasp-r0.3.9.so locale: [1] C attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base other attached packages: [1] maps_3.3.0 shiny_1.6.0 loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] Rcpp_1.0.6 magrittr_2.0.1 xtable_1.8-4 R6_2.5.0 rlang_0.4.10 fastmap_1.1.0 tools_4.0.4 DT_0.17 [9] jquerylib_0.1.3 withr_2.4.1 htmltools_0.5.1.1 crosstalk_1.1.1 ellipsis_0.3.1 yaml_2.2.1 digest_0.6.27 lifecycle_0.2.0 [17] crayon_1.4.1 later_1.1.0.1 sass_0.3.1 htmlwidgets_1.5.3 promises_1.1.1 cachem_1.0.3 mime_0.9 compiler_4.0.4 [25] bslib_0.2.4 jsonlite_1.7.2 httpuv_1.5.5 ``` I closed the R session to return to my shell: ```R q(save = "no") ``` ##### Change example to make it work in Guix environment To prove that this is related to the server-side `selectize`, I modified the app to not show any maps in the dropdown, such that is should work with both server-side and client-side `selectize`: ```sh patch server.R 01.server.drop_maps.switch-to-client-side.patch ``` For the record, this is the content of the above patch: ```diff 35,47c35,36 < session, 'state', server = TRUE, < # sorry, Alaska and Hawaii, I do not have maps for you < choices = setdiff(rownames(USArrests), c('Alaska', 'Hawaii')), < options = list(render = I(sprintf( < "{ < option: function(item, escape) { < return '
' + < escape(item.value) + '
'; < } < }", < mapurl < ))) --- > session, 'state', server = FALSE, > choices = rownames(USArrests) ``` Next, I repeated the steps described above to re-launch the modified app. As expected, this time around the patched app loaded just fine. I could even select Hawaii from the list. ##### Prove `server = TRUE` to be the culprit To further minizime the changes between working and non-working version, I switched back to server-side `selectize` without adding back the map support: ```sh patch server.R 02.server.switch-back-to-server-side.patch ``` The entire patch looks like this: ```diff 35c35 < session, 'state', server = FALSE, --- > session, 'state', server = TRUE, ``` Re-launching the app once more, I could reproduce the broken behaviour once again. ##### Verify `server = TRUE` works in Gentoo environment As a final piece of evidence, I made sure this adjusted server-side version indeed still worked under my host system's R installation. Therefore, I left the shell session I attached the Guix profile to: ```sh exit ``` Back in my main shell, I double checked the default R binary once again: ```sh which R ``` ``` /usr/bin/R ``` I launched an R session and frome there the Shiny app just as before and the app launched just fine, behaving as expected (5 entries at a time, others provided upon search, Hawaii selectable). ##### Verdict So I boiled the issue down to `server = TRUE` vs. `server = FALSE` determining whether `updateSelectizeInput` does its job or not, while using the same versions `shiny` and `jquerylib` under very similar R versions. From here, I simply have no clue how to continue trouble-shooting this as my code seems fine but I cannot figure out which packge might require up- or downgrading based on my (very) superficial understanding of Shiny's internals and (JavaScript in general). Any pointers would be highly appreciated. Best, Marcel

```R
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(DT)

ui <- function() {
  dashboardPage(
    dashboardHeader(title = "abc"),
    dashboardSidebar(uiOutput("sidebarpanel")), 
    dashboardBody(uiOutput("body")))
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$sidebarpanel <- renderUI({
    tags$div(
      sidebarMenu(id = "tabs",
                  menuItem("Data", tabName = "data"))
    )
  })
  
  output$body <- renderUI({ 
    tabItems(ui_data1("data1", tabName = "data"))
  })
  
  input_data1 <- new.env()
  input_data1$a <- reactive(1)
  input_data1$b <- reactive(2)
  
  input_data2 <- server_data1("data1", input_data1)
}

ui_data1 <- function(id, tabName){ 
  ns <- NS(id)
  tabItem(tabName = tabName,
          uiOutput(ns("body")))
}

server_data1 <- function(id, input_data1) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    output$body <- renderUI({
      tabsetPanel(
        ui_data2(ns("info1"), "Info1")
      )
    })
    
    data2 <- new.env()
    data2$input_data2 <- server_data2("info1", input_data1)
    
    return(data2)
  })
}

ui_data2 <- function(id, title) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  tabPanel(title = title,
           uiOutput(ns("body")))
}

server_data2 <- function(id, input_data1) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    c <- eventReactive(input_data1$a(), {
      2
    })
    
    sampledata <- reactive(mtcars)
    
    output$body <- renderUI({
      all_cyl <- unique(sampledata()$cyl)
      tbl_by_cyl <- lapply(seq_along(all_cyl), function(i) {
        tabPanel(all_cyl[i],
                     column(12, br(),
                            box(width = "auto",

                                                    width = "100%"))))
      })
      do.call(tabsetPanel, tbl_by_cyl)
    })
    
    observe({
      sampledata <- sampledata()
      all_cyl <- unique(sampledata$cyl)
      
      lapply(seq_along(all_cyl), function(i) {

        })
      })
    })
    
    return(sampledata)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

### Describe the problem in detail
I and my colleagues have been using shiny for building company dashboard, as we found our apps growing more & more complex, and we decided to go [modularization](https://mastering-shiny.org/scaling-modules.html).

I follow the [modularization](https://mastering-shiny.org/scaling-modules.html) chapter in mastering shiny book, but I have issue to dynamically display multiple DT in nested modules, as in the sample code above. The `sampledata` should be uploaded by users in real scenario.

We expect the `DT`s should displayed under each `tabPanel`s

title: let text(Area)Input set maxlength
description:
I like to make sure that character inputs in `textInputArea()` aren't excessively long (maliciously so?) to protect my compute.
I currently do this with https://github.com/rstudio/shinyvalidate/, which is amazing, but this is *already* bringing the overlong string into R, which somewhat defeats the purpose.

It seems that the idiomatic / better way would be to set these limits in HTML so that they are enforced by the client browser.
HTML provides the [`maxlength`](https://www.w3schools.com/tags/att_input_maxlength.asp) attribute for this purpose.

In this [S-O](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27181420/how-to-limit-the-number-of-characters-accepted-by-textinput-in-shiny-app) people are already using `shinyjs::runjs()` to set this attribute, though that seems a minor, if needless modification of the DOM.

It might also be worthwhile to expose other attributes, or maybe just a `...`?

If there's interest, I'd be happy to draft a PR.

title: Embedded non-bslib shiny apps inherit styles from rmarkdown's bslib theme
description: For example, notice how, in this document, the embedded app's sliders reflects the documents primary color ```r remotes::install_github("rstudio/rmarkdown") ``` ````yaml --- title: "Real-time theming" runtime: shiny output: html_document: theme: bg: "#121212" fg: "#E4E4E4" primary: "#EA80FC" secondary: "#00DAC6" base_font: !expr bslib::font_google("Open Sans") heading_font: !expr bslib::font_google("Proza Libre") code_font: !expr bslib::font_google("Fira Code") code-color: "#00DAC6" --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} bslib::bs_themer() thematic::thematic_shiny(font = "auto") ``` This R Markdown document is made interactive using Shiny. Unlike the more traditional workflow of creating static reports, you can now create documents that allow your readers to change the assumptions underlying your analysis and see the results immediately. To learn more, see [Interactive Documents](http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html). ## Inputs and Outputs You can embed Shiny inputs and outputs in your document. Outputs are automatically updated whenever inputs change. This demonstrates how a standard R plot can be made interactive by wrapping it in the Shiny `renderPlot` function. The `selectInput` and `sliderInput` functions create the input widgets used to drive the plot. ```{r eruptions, echo=FALSE} inputPanel( selectInput("n_breaks", label = "Number of bins:", choices = c(10, 20, 35, 50), selected = 20), sliderInput("bw_adjust", label = "Bandwidth adjustment:", min = 0.2, max = 2, value = 1, step = 0.2) ) renderPlot({ hist(faithful$eruptions, probability = TRUE, breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks), xlab = "Duration (minutes)", main = "Geyser eruption duration") dens <- density(faithful$eruptions, adjust = input$bw_adjust) lines(dens, col = "blue") }) ``` ## Embedded Application It's also possible to embed an entire Shiny application within an R Markdown document using the `shinyAppDir` function. This example embeds a Shiny application located in another directory: ```{r tabsets, echo=FALSE} shinyAppDir( system.file("examples/06_tabsets", package = "shiny"), options = list( width = "100%", height = 550 ) ) ``` Note the use of the `height` parameter to determine how much vertical space the embedded application should occupy. You can also use the `shinyApp` function to define an application inline rather then in an external directory. In all of R code chunks above the `echo = FALSE` attribute is used. This is to prevent the R code within the chunk from rendering in the document alongside the Shiny components. ````

title: When reactiveConsole() is enabled, observeEvent() doesn't work in knitted Rmd or source() scripts
description:
Hey, 

Just wanted to first say that the reactiveConsole() is an absolutely awesome new feature 💪, and as it is flagged as experimental in the doc, I wanted to share this (possibly) bug. 

Given the following code: 

```r
library(shiny)

reactiveConsole(TRUE)

z <- reactiveValues(
  n = 1:10
)

z$n

input <- reactiveValues(
  select = "this"
)

observeEvent( input$select , {
  z$n <- sample(1:1000, 10)
})

input$select <- "that"

z$n
```

```R

### Describe the problem in detail

When a user clicks inside a pickerInput dropdown, a box opens with a list of choices.  After a user makes a selection, or left clicks outside the box,  the box with the choices remains open.  Only several left clicks, a right click, or the escape key will close the box. 
It appears that the issue is that the bootstrap-select shiny-bound-input gets stuck open, and the aria-expanded property is stuck on true.  When a user left clicks, the box briefly disappears, shiny-bound-input closes and area-expanded=false, but then then quickly return to open and true.

title: Wrong Predictions in Shiny App
description:
<!--
I fitted a model using tidymodels and recipes. The model was an elastic net and I used the preprocessor in recipes with natural splines. I saved the model and reload it in shiny app. The model in the app did not consider the splines and makes wrong predictions.

I appreciated any assistance. This is a COVID-19 severity model

### System details

```R
# Predict Model
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(themis)
library(haven)

covid <- read_spss(file = 'COVID_preditor_Dez_2020_2.sav')

set.seed(123)
split <- initial_split(covid_predictor, strata = 'death')
covid_train <- training(split)
covid_test <- testing(split)

rec_simple_model <- recipe(death ~ dyspnoea + egf_baseline + age + MPA_or_AZA_iss +
                             hypertension + diabetes_ESRD + cardiovascular_disease + smoking + Steroids_iss + BMI +
                             MTOR_iss + diarrhea + time_symptoms + anosmia + headache,
                           data = covid_train) %>% 
  step_medianimpute(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_ns(age, egf_baseline,deg_free = 4) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_nzv(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_smote(death)

model_lasso <- logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine('glmnet')

work_lasso_reduced <- workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(rec_simple_model) %>% 
  add_model(model_lasso)


## folds
set.seed(123)
folds <- vfold_cv(covid_train, strata = 'death')


tune_lasso_reduced <- tune_grid(
  work_lasso_reduced,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = 30,
  metrics = metric_set(mn_log_loss, roc_auc, accuracy),
  control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE, parallel_over = 'resamples')
)

best_lasso <- select_best(tune_lasso, metric = 'mn_log_loss')

final_lasso <- work_lasso_smote %>%

title: dplyr errors in Shiny should show line numbers
description:
(This was originally posted as an issue in tidyverse/dplyr#5636)

**Summary**
Compared to the default behaviour for error messages, `dplyr` error messages are incredible difficult to debug. In multifile Shiny apps, normal error messages (from `[`) will often print the exact file and line where the issue is. `dplyr` doesn't tell you where the error is. In apps with large server files or even multiple sourced server files, this can be a problem and make it very difficult to debug Shiny as you have to go hunting to find the error.

@romainfrancois [mentioned ](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/5636#issuecomment-737294344)that it is the way `vctrs::abort()` is used because when using `base::stop()` the errors are more informative. @hadley said that Shiny needs to make better use of the error handling features in `rlang` and [recommended ](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/5636#issuecomment-758056739)I raise this issue here in the Shiny repo.

Is there any way to change this behaviour in vctrs/dplyr/Shiny so that it prints out some kind of context (file and line) for errors in Shiny? I would be happy to make these changes myself given some guidance - I've never contributed a technical change on a project before but maybe if someone points me in the right direction it could help.

-----

When using dplyr in Shiny, it is quite difficult to debug due to rather opaque messages as compared to `base` and other packages.

Here is an error message in Shiny.
```r
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)

options(shiny.error = NULL)

ui <- fluidPage(
  verbatimTextOutput("example")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$example <- renderPrint({
    mtcars[,"wrong_col"]
    
    # mtcars %>% 
    #   select(wrong_col)
    
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
# Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7436
# Warning: Error in [.data.frame: undefined columns selected
#  102: stop
#  101: [.data.frame
#   99: renderPrint [C:/Users/<My_Name>/Desktop/testShiny.R#12]
#   98: func
#   82: origRenderFunc
#   81: output$example
#    1: runApp
```

The name of the reactive is printed with the line item in the exact file where the error occured.

Here is the error message when dplyr is used instead.

```r
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)

options(shiny.error = NULL)

ui <- fluidPage(
  verbatimTextOutput("example")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$example <- renderPrint({
    #mtcars[,"wrong_col"]
    
     mtcars %>% 
       select(wrong_col)
    
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
# Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7436
# Warning: Error in : Can't subset columns that don't exist.
# x Column `wrong_col` doesn't exist.
#   120: <Anonymous>
```

Normally you have to use `rlang::last_error` and look through the summarised trace to find the error. This doesn't work in Shiny because you first have to stop the app and all context disappears so `rlang::last_error()` doesn't work. You might then think to use `options(shiny.error = browser)` and call `rlang::last_error()` from there but that still doesn't work. Instead, if you set the option you have to call the object `e` which contains a `vctrs` object containing the error. The output below is the error above with `options(shiny.error = browser)` set and includes commands called from the console session exploring the `browser()` environment. The `rlang` functions don't work, so you have to call `e`.

title: Extract the id location of Shiny input functions (like dateInput()) in a consistent manner
description:
Perhaps this exists internally in the package, but I couldn't find it.

I'm templating some Shiny modules that lets users pass in input Shiny functions like `dateInput()` or `selectInput()` to create a Shiny module on the fly.

Its all working but at the moment only for `dateInput()` as I can add the module namespace via `NS::` to the known id attibute:

```r
library(shiny)
library(assertthat)

inputShiny <- dateInput("my_id","Input Date")

# this only works with dateInput()
input_id <- inputShiny$attribs$id
  
ui <- function(id, ...){
    ns <- shiny::NS(id)
    if(!is.null(input_id)){
      inputShiny$attribs$id <- ns(input_id)
    } 
    shiny::tagList(
      inputShiny,
      outputShiny(outputId = ns("ui_out"), ...)
    )
  }

#...server code makes reactive inputs via input[[input_id]]
```

This works as I can find the `id` attribute in the object via `inputShiny$attribs$id`:

```r
str(shiny::dateInput("my_id","date"))
#List of 3
# $ name    : chr "div"
# $ attribs :List of 2
 # ..$ id   : chr "my_id"
#  ..$ class: chr "shiny-date-input form-group shiny-input-container"
 #$ children:List of 3
#...etc...
```

But the same code doesn't work with say `selectInput()` or `checkboxInput()` as its `id` is in a different location:

```r
str(shiny::checkboxInput("my_id","label"))
#List of 3
# $ name    : chr "div"
# $ attribs :List of 1
#  ..$ class: chr "form-group shiny-input-container"
# $ children:List of 1
 # ..$ :List of 3
#  .. ..$ name    : chr "div"
#  .. ..$ attribs :List of 1
#  .. .. ..$ class: chr "checkbox"
#  .. ..$ children:List of 1
#  .. .. ..$ :List of 3
#  .. .. .. ..$ name    : chr "label"
#  .. .. .. ..$ attribs : Named list()
#  .. .. .. ..$ children:List of 2
#  .. .. .. .. ..$ :List of 3
#  .. .. .. .. .. ..$ name    : chr "input"
#  .. .. .. .. .. ..$ attribs :List of 2
 # .. .. .. .. .. .. ..$ id  : chr "my_id"
 ...etc..
```
e.g. the id to change is now at `x$children[[1]]$children[[1]]$children[[1]]$attribs$id` 

I could make some kind of recursive search tool but I thought it likely or would be nice to have a function in `shiny` that would do it.  

It could be something like `extract_id(checkboxInput("my_id","my_label")` which would extract `"my_id"`. 

Or perhaps there is another way to do it?

Documentation: difference between top-level session and a module session object
description:
It seems that the `session` object that exists in a plain shiny app is a different type than what we get inside a module.

Top-level session: has a class of `c("ShinySession","R6")`, easy to see all the values we can access (`names(session)` returns a list of objects in its environment (similar to the list that is documented in `?shiny::session`).

Module-level session: has a class of `"session_proxy"`, when inquiring about what's inside of it all we can see is 

```
names(session)
[1] "parent"    "overrides"
```

Which isn't clear because both of those are `NULL`. However, it seems that the two types of sessions have the same objects, but they're not always identical. For example, from testing I can see that they share the same `session$userData` - if I set some userData in the global app, then any modules will have access to it. But of course, `names(session$input)` will be different between the two.

The distinction between the the session objects is not something I was able to find any information about online, and it would be useful to document it somewhere. Knowing that `session$userData` is shared between them is not intuitive, and understanding what functions we're expected to call on each of them would be useful. Right now there is no information on how to deal with the `session` object of a module.

    as.character(my_reactive_val())
  })

  my_reactive_val <- reactiveVal(0)

  observeEvent(input$button, {
    isolate(my_reactive_val(runif(1)))
  })

  observeEvent(my_reactive_val(), {
    if (my_reactive_val() > 0) {
      showNotification("This message sould not appaear!")
    }
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
In this application when we trigger the button, a reactive value (`my_reactive_val`) is updated with a random value. _**But**_ the update is made using the `isolate` function, so I expect that when I trigger the button, all the elements that depend on `my_reactive_val` won't change, but this is not the case : `output$out` is updated and the notification is appearing.

I thought that the isolate function allow to change a reactive value without triggering the dependent elements... Maybe I wrong or this a bug?

Best regards,
Dom

title: Notification's "X" usability issue
The return value of bootstrapPage() has changed in an unfortunate way
description:
With the current CRAN version of shiny (1.5.0):

```r
> str(bootstrapPage())
List of 3
 $ : NULL
 $ : NULL
 $ : list()
 - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "shiny.tag.list" "list"
 - attr(*, "html_dependencies")=List of 1
  ..$ :List of 10
  .. ..$ name      : chr "bootstrap"
...
```

With the development version (> 1.5.0):

```r
> str(bootstrapPage())
List of 4
 $ :function ()  
  ..- attr(*, "srcref")= 'srcref' int [1:8] 83 15 126 3 15 3 83 126
  .. ..- attr(*, "srcfile")=Classes 'srcfilecopy', 'srcfile' <environment: 0x7fbefe65d950> 
  ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "shiny.tag.function"
 $ : NULL
 $ : NULL
 $ : list()
 - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "shiny.tag.list" "list"
```

This means, user code that does something like this will now break:

```r
x <- bootstrapPage()
tagAppendAttribute(x[[3]], class = "navbar")
```

We can do better to not break this code if `{bslib}` isn't being used, but the structure will likely have to change if `{bslib}` is being used.

Some relevant discussion/use-case https://github.com/radiant-rstats/radiant.data/pull/26#issuecomment-754259304

title: Suggestion: Explicitly discourage use of `includeScript()` and `includeCSS()`
description:
These functions come from {htmltools} but they are commonly used in shiny so I think posting in this repo is appropriate.

The problem I see with these functions is that they don't use the conventional system of including static resources, which can lead to confusion to anyone who isn't intimately familiar with the differences of `includeCSS` to `link(rel = "stylesheet")`. Using include functions simply looks for the given file in the file system, completely ignoring any resource paths that may have been set. I've seen people be very confused about why these functions need to be given a `www/` prefix while images and any scripts or CSS loaded with the script and link tags don't need it. Similarly, it also means that it cannot load files under a resourcePath that's been added. And another small issue is that these functions result in inline css/js instead of linking to a file, but that's a minor issue.

title: Feature request: allow either `class` or `...` in all inputs and outputs that will get appeneded to the tag's HTML node
description:
It's a very common operation to want to add an attribute, such as `class`, to an input or output. This comes up a lot because some inputs and outputs support a `class` parameter, but not all, so having consistency there would be good. 

For example, if I wanted to add a class to a `textOutput()`, the current best way to get around this is using `tagAppendAttributes(textOutput("foo"), class = "bar")`.

The same issue comes up with other attributes that you sometimes want to add, where some inputs/output support a general `...` parameter that will add these attributes to the node, but most don't support it. This is perhaps harder to implement because there might be some input or output that is already making use of the ellipsis argument.

title: Running tools/updateSelectize.R causes scss changes to be lost
Add devmode checks and warnings for un-isolated reactives in cached expressions
description:
It is easy when using caching to accidentally leave some reactive value (either that's being modified or is an input) that is not in the cache key. 

Devmode could look at the reactive dependencies and notice that this has happened and give the user a warning/suggestion to move into the key function. E.g. 


> Warning: The reactive object `forgotten_reactive` is in the body of the cached reactive `my_reactive` but is not part of the key expression. You may want to include `forgotten_reactive` in the key statement or wrap it in an `isolate()` call to remove the dependency.

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)
get_key <- function(key) {
  print("get")
  return(1)
}

# diskCache
disk <- shiny::diskCache(dir = NULL, max_age = 5, missing = get_key, exec_missing = T)
disk$set("test",disk$get("test"))
# output: [1] "get"
disk$get("test")
# output: [1] 1
Sys.sleep(10)
disk$get("test")
# output: [1] 1
# diskCache does not evict "test" even if max_age has been reached

# memoryCache
mem <- shiny::memoryCache(max_age = 5, missing = get_key, exec_missing = T)
mem$set("test",mem$get("test"))
# output: [1] "get"
mem$get("test")
# output: [1] 1
Sys.sleep(10)
mem$get("test")
# output: [1] "get"
# output: [1] 1
# memoryCache evicts "test" and executes get_key again
```

### Describe the problem in detail

It seems that diskCache does not consider max_age (at least not in the same way as memoryCache does), although the description of the parameter in the documentation is identical:

**max_age**: Maximum age of files in cache before they are evicted, in seconds. Use Inf for no age limit.

In my understanding, diskCache should execute the `get_key` function in the example above after `Sys.sleep(10)`. 
Moreover, the documentation of memoryCache seems to be copied largely from the documentation of diskCache and even refers to diskCache in some places instead of memoryCache (e.g. in the example of the section *Missing keys*)

This might also be related to #2705

title: Feature request: `reactive()` capable of "ignoring" its queue of states
description:
### The problem:

When a reactive takes a long time to calculate and its value changes too often, the UI needs to "catch up" with the reactive values one-by-one. Here is an example code:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("num", "num", 5),
  textOutput("square")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  square <- reactive({
    Sys.sleep(1)
    input$num ^ 2
  })
  output$square <- renderText({ square() })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

If you change the input too fast but not fast enough, you end up with this issue:

![shiny](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/952340/102427463-68984a80-3fdf-11eb-98ad-1d6f049a2661.gif)

### Existing solutions

The `debounce()` and `throttle()` functions were added as a way to combat this problem. In many cases they do work, but I've often felt it's not always an ideal solution. With debounce, it can cause the user to have to wait too long to see a change, and with throttle the problem is just reduced to happen less frequently.

### Proposal

The root of the issue is that there is a queue of values that get accessed one by one. If could be useful to have something such as `reactive(.., cancelPrevious = TRUE)` which would cause any values in the invalidation loop that haven't yet been looked at to be removed. I only thought about it in a very narrow simple context and my naive thinking is that because reactive values do not require to keep their history (which makes them so well suited for bookmarking) maybe this would be possible. It's also entirely possible that this is not achievable and would break a lot of things that I haven't considered.

title: numericInput sends logical value (which breaks things with vctrs)
description:
This isn't a bug per se, but I'm raising a flag regarding empty Shiny inputs and much of the rest of the Tidyverse transitioning to vcrts as an underlying dependency. When a `numericInput` is initialized with NA (**even** `NA_real_`), the corresponding received value by the server is `NA` (logical). This can cause sneaky failures like so:
```r
observe({
  input$num %|% 0  ## using rlang's %|%, but would also manifest in other places, like dplyr operations
})
```
This causes an error (`Replacement values must have type logical, not type double`), I believe because of vctrs's type-safety strictness. Another example that does rely on rlang's coalesce operator would be if one wanted to 'insert' that input value into some location in an existing tibble col.

Normally I applaud type-safety, but I fear vctrs's strict handling will cause difficult-to-resolve headaches for lots of introductory users, _especially_ when it comes to NA values, this being just one example.

In any case, I wonder if its worth adding explicit casts to most existing Shiny inputs to help safe-guard against sneaky type issues? (I think asking a new user to `as.numeric(input$num)` is a not-so-great experience as it pulls their focus into a low-level operation while trying to teach them about reactivity in general.)

title: selectInput: when item is selected by pressing Enter, dropdown does not go away
session$setCurrentTheme should throw an error when trying to dynamically update to a different bootstrap version.
description:
### Issue
If you're using `session$setCurrentTheme()` and `bslib::bs_theme()` together to do dynamic theming, if there is a version mismatch between the original theme and the newly updated dynamic one (such as forgetting to set `version` in the update code) the theme change will silently change. 

### Proposed fix
Check to make sure that a dynamic update does not try and change the bootstrap version and throw an error if it does.

### Demo app

The following demonstrates the problem. Switching the theme won't work when the version is set to 4 because the initial chosen version was 3. Once you switch the version to 3, then the bootswatch changing starts working. 

__Steps to reproduce:__

- Change theme radio button to "flatly"
  - Nothing will happen
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6764693/101956249-406aaf00-3bcd-11eb-864b-e4d413ed1080.png)

- Change the version radio button to '3' 
  - Theme changes now respected
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6764693/101956281-4e203480-3bcd-11eb-91ce-e7afccc3abe6.png)

`app.R`
```R
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Setting version to 3 here
my_theme <- bs_theme(bootswatch = "darkly", version = "3")
ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = my_theme,
  radioButtons("current_theme", "Choose a theme for bslib",
               choices = c("darkly", "flatly")),
  radioButtons("bs_version", "Bootstrap version", choices = c("4", "3")),
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    session$setCurrentTheme(
      bs_theme(bootswatch = input$current_theme, version = input$bs_version)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Thematic styling can inherit error colors
description:
Test app:

```R
library(thematic)
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
  plotOutput("ggplot"),
  checkboxInput("err", "Throw an error", value = TRUE)
)

  output$ggplot <- renderPlot({

      geom_point()
  })
}

thematic_shiny()
shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Allow `shinyApp()` to pass `headers` to `uiHttpHandler`
description:
By default, `uiHttpHandler()` returns an `httpResponse` with only a status code and a content, unless `uiValue` is an `"httpResponse"`. 

I would be great to be able to pass headers from `shinyApp()` to this `httpResponse()`, through `uiHttpHandler()`.

Suggested change: 

-> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/shinyapp.R#L75
```
shinyApp <- function(ui, server, onStart=NULL, options=list(),
                     uiPattern="/", enableBookmarking=NULL,
                     headers = list()) {
  if (!is.function(server)) {
    stop("`server` must be a function", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Ensure that the entire path is a match
  uiPattern <- sprintf("^%s$", uiPattern)

  httpHandler <- uiHttpHandler(ui, uiPattern, headers)
```

-> https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/shinyui.R#L139

```r
uiHttpHandler <- function(ui, uiPattern = "^/$", headers = list()) {
```

```r
return(httpResponse(200, content=html, headers = headers))
```

title: Consistent printing  and labeling of reactives, observers, and render functions
description:
This is related to #3160. Currently, printing of reactives, observers, and render functions is not very consistent. There are also three kinds of labels:

1) The output from `print`/`format`
2) The `$.label` of reactives and observers, used for reactlog (I think?)
3) The function label added by `wrapFunctionLabel()`

Note that there are tests for `reactive()` for the first two types of labels here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/tests/testthat/test-reactivity.r#L1579-L1607

Here are examples of (1) and (2) from each of these types of objects:

```R
r <- reactive({a + 1 })
print(r)
#> reactive({
#>     a + 1
#> })
attr(r, "observable")$.label
#> [1] "r"

o <- observe({ a+ 1 })
print(o)
#> <Observer>
#>   Public:
#>     .autoDestroy: TRUE
#>     .autoDestroyHandle: NULL
#>     .createContext: function () 
#>     .ctx: NULL
#>     .destroyed: FALSE
#>     .domain: NULL
#>     .execCount: 0
#>     .func: function (...) 
#>     .invalidateCallbacks: list
#>     .label: observe({
#>         a + 1
#>     })
#>     .onDomainEnded: function () 
#>  ....
o$.label
#> [1] "observe({\n    a + 1\n})"

rt <- renderText({a + 1})
print(rt)
#> <shiny.render.function>
# No need for reactive label, since render function is not inherently reactive.
```

We also want to make sure that the output after passing these to `bindEvent()` and `bindCache()` is informative. For example, here's one possibility of printed output:

```R
r <- reactive({ a + b + 1 }) %>% bindEvent(a, b}
r
#> bindEvent(reactive(), a, b)
```

We also should make sure that `eventReactive()`, `observeEvent()` have good labels.

Populate the app environment # Update inputs shiny::updateSelectInput( session = session, inputId = 'assay', choices = sort(x = Seurat::Assays(object = app.env$object)), selected = Seurat::DefaultAssay(object = app.env$object) ) shiny::updateSelectInput( session = session, inputId = 'reduction', choices = sort(x = Seurat::Reductions(object = app.env$object)), selected = DefaultDimReduc(object = app.env$object) ) } ) observeEvent( eventExpr = input$assay, handlerExpr = { if (nchar(x = input$assay)) { app.env$assay <- input$assay } } ) observeEvent( eventExpr = input$reduction, handlerExpr = { if (nchar(x = app.env$reduction <- input$reduction)) { app.env$reduction <- input$reduction } } ) # Update tabs observeEvent( eventExpr = input$marinertab, handlerExpr = { switch( EXPR = input$marinertab, 'cellexplorer' = { output$label <- shiny::renderUI(expr = { shiny::h4('Cell Explorer') }) CellControls(id = 'app') CellTab(id = 'app') }, 'featureexplorer' = { output$label <- shiny::renderUI(expr = { shiny::h4('Feature Explorer') }) } ) } ) # Update servers observeEvent( eventExpr = c(app.env$object, app.env$assay, app.env$reduction), handlerExpr = { update <- all(vapply( X = c('assay', 'object', 'reduction'), FUN = function(x) { return(!is.null(x = app.env[[x]])) }, FUN.VALUE = logical(length = 1L) )) if (update) { CellServer( id = 'app', object = shiny::reactive(x = app.env$object), assay = shiny::reactive(x = app.env$assay), reduction = shiny::reactive(x = app.env$reduction) ) } } ) } viewer <- shiny::dialogViewer( dialogName = 'Seurat Object Explorer', width = 1500L, height = 900L ) shiny::runGadget(app = ui, server = server, viewer = viewer) return(invisible(x = NULL)) } # Build spaces for the UI compontents TabUI <- function(id) { ns <- NS(namespace = id) return(tagList(uiOutput(outputId = ns(id = 'marinertab')))) } ControlUI <- function(id) { ns <- NS(namespace = id) return(tagList(uiOutput(outputId = ns(id = 'controls')))) } # Add the controls CellControls <- function(id) { moduleServer( id = id, module = function(input, output, session) { output$controls <- shiny::renderUI(expr = htmltools::tagList( shiny::selectInput( inputId = 'xdim', label = 'X Dimension', choices = '', width = '90%' ), shiny::selectInput( inputId = 'ydim', label = 'Y Dimension', choices = '', width = '90%' ), shiny::selectizeInput( inputId = 'metadata', label = 'Metadata', choices = '', width = '90%', options = selectize.options ), shiny::selectizeInput( inputId = 'split', label = 'Metadata Split', choices = '', width = '90%', options = selectize.options ), shiny::checkboxInput(inputId = 'label', label = 'Label Clusters'), shiny::checkboxInput( inputId = 'legend', label = 'Show Legends', value = TRUE ), shiny::radioButtons( inputId = 'percentage', label = NULL, choices = c('Percentage', 'Frequency'), inline = FALSE ) )) } ) } # Add the outputs CellTab <- function(id) { moduleServer( id = id, module = function(input, output, session) { output$marinertab <- shiny::renderUI(expr = htmltools::tagList( shiny::plotOutput(outputId = 'dimplot'), shiny::tableOutput(outputId = 'metadata') )) } ) } # Add the logic CellServer <- function(id, object, assay = NULL, reduction = NULL, ...) { moduleServer( id = id, module = function(input, output, session) { observeEvent( eventExpr = reduction(), handlerExpr = { if (nchar(x = reduction())) { reduction() dims <- seq_len( length.out = ncol(x = object()[[reduction()]]) ) print(input$xdim) print(input$ydim) for (x in c('xdim', 'ydim')) { print(x) shiny::updateSelectInput( session = session, inputId = x, choices = dims, selected = c(xdim = 1L, ydim = 2L)[x] ) } print(input$xdim) print(input$ydim) } } ) } ) } ```
### Describe the problem in detail Input elements created by a call to `renderUI` are unable to be updated with `update*Input` in a later part of the app. In the example I posted, I'm building an app that uses a sidebar to hold controls and tabs to render different outputs. Some controls are common to all outputs, so they're rendered directly by the UI. However, other controls are tab-specific, so they're rendered only when a given tab is active. The bit of code that creates the controls ```R output$controls <- shiny::renderUI(expr = htmltools::tagList( shiny::selectInput( inputId = 'xdim', label = 'X Dimension', choices = '', width = '90%' ), shiny::selectInput( inputId = 'ydim', label = 'Y Dimension', choices = '', width = '90%' ), shiny::selectizeInput( inputId = 'metadata', label = 'Metadata', choices = '', width = '90%', options = selectize.options ), shiny::selectizeInput( inputId = 'split', label = 'Metadata Split', choices = '', width = '90%', options = selectize.options ), shiny::checkboxInput(inputId = 'label', label = 'Label Clusters'), shiny::checkboxInput( inputId = 'legend', label = 'Show Legends', value = TRUE ), shiny::radioButtons( inputId = 'percentage', label = NULL, choices = c('Percentage', 'Frequency'), inline = FALSE ) )) ``` A dataset isn't always provided, so I have logic in another part of the app that tests if we have data, and attempts to populate the inputs with allowed values The bit of code that updates the inputs ```R observeEvent( eventExpr = reduction(), handlerExpr = { if (nchar(x = reduction())) { reduction() dims <- seq_len( length.out = ncol(x = object()[[reduction()]]) ) print(input$xdim) print(input$ydim) for (x in c('xdim', 'ydim')) { print(x) shiny::updateSelectInput( session = session, inputId = x, choices = dims, selected = c(xdim = 1L, ydim = 2L)[x] ) } print(input$xdim) print(input$ydim) } } ) ``` I know that the reactivity is happening, as the `print` calls show their results in the R console, but the app's UI doesn't change. I'm using Shiny modules to group the tab-specific controls together, but the bug happens regardless of whether or not I use modules.

title: Add the .noWS argument to icons
description:
All HTML tags created with the `htmltools::tags` list can take an optional `.noWS` parameter that's used to suppress whitespace. There is no way to achieve this whitespace suppression using the `icon()` function that creates an `i` tag. The only way currently is to manually create an `i` tag without the use of `icon()`. Example: Using `icon()` inside a div, I can get the following: ``` > htmltools::tags$div("foo", shiny::icon("bar"))
foo
``` I would like to be able to achieve the following: ``` > htmltools::tags$div("foo", shiny::icon("bar", .noWS = "before"))
foo
``` I can do that if I use `tags$i()` instead of `icon()`.

title: Un-suspend elements in hidden part in Shiny
description:
### Disclaimer

I posted this issue already on [SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64682245/un-suspend-elements-in-hidden-part-in-shiny) but I guess you need to know more about the internals of Shiny to be able to answer this question, hence a re-post here.

### Problem

When I use standard Shiny, a change in the `tabPanel` somehow tells the output elements to un-suspend and show their value:
```R
library(shiny)

ui1 <- fluidPage(
   tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Start", p("Nothing to see here, really")),
      tabPanel("Calc", actionButton("do", "Calc"), verbatimTextOutput("out"))
   )
)

server1 <- function(input, output, session) {
   output$out <- renderPrint({
      input$do
   })
}
shinyApp(ui1, server1)
```

However, when using another framework (`bulma` in this case), the elements stay suspended. In order to make them work I have to explicitly switch off the suspendWhenHidden flag.
```R
library(shiny)
library(shinybulma)

ui2 <- bulmaPage(
   bulmaTabs(
      c("Start", "Calc"),
      center = FALSE,
      bulmaTab("Start", p("Nothing to see here, really")),
      bulmaTab("Calc", bulmaActionButton("do", "Calc"), verbatimTextOutput("out"))
   )
)

server2 <- function(input, output, session) {
   ## Need to comment out to make it run
   # session$onFlushed(function() {
   #    outputOptions(output, 
   #                  "out",
   #                  suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
   # })
   output$out <- renderPrint({
      input$do
   })
}

shinyApp(ui2, server2)
```

Setting the `suspendWhenHiddenFlag` seems to me like a dirty workaround. Ideally, `shiny` would realize that these controls are now shown.

Granted, `shiny` cannot take care of all frameworks and there are a myriad of ways to hide an element. `shiny` simply cannot foresee all of these. However, there should be somewhere some documentation of how to un-suspend these elements *by hand*, such that package authors can take care about that.

### Question

Is there a `JavaScript` event or an `R` command through which I can explicitly un-suspend the elements in the hidden part? In this way I could submit a `PR` to `shinybulma` such that the proper code is fired upon tab changes.

title: Add flush cycle pseudocode to Shiny documentation/articles
description:
One of the great things about Shiny is the abundance of documentation, and in particular the reactive programming docs are quite well-written. A detail that I can't find mention of in those articles, however, is that during a reactive flush, while reactive expressions and then observers are running, inputs (from the socket) _cannot_ change values and thus cause new invalidations mid-cycle. The only concrete mention of this I've been able to find is in the `promises` docs [here](https://rstudio.github.io/promises/articles/shiny.html#the-flush-cycle-1) (which are also super-well-written and very useful, BTW). Specifically, this statement:

> Only one of the four steps—receiving, updating, reacting, and sending—can be executing a time. (Remember, R is single threaded.) In particular, it’s not possible for inputs to be updated while outputs/observers are running. This is important in order to avoid race conditions that would be all but impossible to defend against.

It'd be helpful if that section of the `promises` documentation ("The flush cycle") was replicated in the Shiny docs somewhere, else folks not using `promises` may try to engineer complicated solutions to prevent race conditions, despite not needing to :-)

title: Specify HTTP response headers for static assets
description:
I've noticed that for some types of direct HTTP request handlers (e.g. to download data in an app), Shiny attaches a `cache-control` header to the response. In other cases, there's no such header attached, most notably in the case of serving static assets (like JavaScript files) via the canonical `www` path or via paths added through `addResourcePath()`.

In some testing of an application of mine that requires JavaScript files to power parts of the front-end (FE), I've found that my browser(s) will at times cache the static assets, leading to out-of-sync FE and server-side Shiny code, typically breaking the application. Clearing cache fixes this, but asking my users to manage their local cache won't work too well :-).

I wonder if it'd be possible to register additional HTTP headers to be sent back with assets served via non-socket requests. One way to do this (that I can imagine) would be to register such headers at the `resourcePath`-level during the call to `addResourcePath()`. Then any file served through a matching `resourcePath` would inherit those headers and have them served up by Shiny on the response.

This might be useful for lots of potential reasons, but my use case is very specifically for the `cache-control` header, and I'd generally be fine setting a pretty short TTL (e.g. 1 hour) for _any_ file served by my application, and thus setting this as a 'global' Shiny `option()` would work, too.

title: Suggestion: 'onStop()' should be called *after* all sessions 'onEnded()' have been called
description:
The `onStop()` function registers a callback to be called when the app is stopped/killed/dies. The `session$onSessionEnded()` (or `session$onEnded()` or `onStop(session != NULL)`) function registers a callback to be called when a specific session is stopped.

I haven't tested in other environments, but on my Windows RStudio IDE, when an app dies, the app stop callback is called before the session callbacks. 

For example:

```
library(shiny)
onStop(function() message("app stopped"))
ui <- fluidPage()
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  session$onSessionEnded(function() message("session ended"))
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

When you kill the app, you'll see the order of callbacks printed to the console.

I consider the sessions to be "children" of the "parent" app, and IMO the children should have a chance to cleanup before the parent does.

One example where this could become an issue is when you have a database connection that gets closed in `onStop()`. The individual sessions may want to record something when they end, but if the app callback happens before, then they cannot.

title: `hashReactiveVal` (or `checkReactiveVal`)
description:
I'm curious if there's ever been discussion for a general-purpose version of a reactive value (i.e. `reactiveVal`) where the [`identical()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/reactives.R#L99) check here is overriden/replaceable. The `identical()` check is extremely useful to prevent unneeded reactive invalidations, but I've found a handful of use cases where `identical()` is simply too strict.

One practical use case is when working with external data (e.g. JSON from some public API) where it's useful to keep the reactive value as the entire object, but only a subset of fields determine a true semantic change (and one is willing to discard any other changes that don't trigger a semantic change). For example, one might have a constantly-updating timestamp as part of a web-API-returned object, yet the other parts of the object remain unchanged and are the determining factors for downstream reactive code. Again, one could already do a few things: (a) strip out the timestamp or (b) create an intermediate object as part of the app, but those require 'reinventing the wheel' each time, so to speak.

In a more esoteric case (for which I'm certainly not advocating, but find it worth discussing), one might want a single reactive value, for example, where the value itself is replaceable, but _doesn't_ trigger in the invalidation cascade. An example might be a type of accumulator where you'd always want to store the new value upon `set()`-ting, but only invalidate when some _sufficiently large or 'different'_ change in the underlying value has occurred (up to the developer to then define that change). In such a case, one could create an observer that updates a second reactive value on the condition, but this again adds lot of additional objects/structures in what otherwise might be a clean single object.

In lots of other OO languages, like Java, there's the opportunity to override some form of `equals`, which may or may not correspond to also overriding the concept of an object's `hashCode`. In R I'm not aware of any way to override `identical()` (indeed it's defined in a way that suggests it'd be more-or-less impossible), so I wonder if there's appetite for a version of a `reactiveVal` that takes in a user-defined 'equivalence' function, the return value of which would then be passed on to `identical()`. (The default such function would just be `identity`.)

In spirit, this is very similar to the already-present `reactivePoll` and `reactiveFileReader` constructs, only without a timing element ... where the 'equivalence' function for those two are the user-defined `checkFunc` and the last-modified-timestamp, respectively.

A naïve implementation of such a `reactiveVal` might have a signature like so:
```R
checkReactiveVal <- function(value = NULL, label = NULL, checkFun = identity) { ... }
```
... and usage like:
```R
rv <- checkReactiveVal(NULL, "my_label", function(x) {
  ## function to compute effectively a hash value or string to be passed to `identity()`
})
rv(1)  ## conditionally set, depending on result of checkFun
rv() ## retrieve and take dependency, just like any other reactive value
```
In the above usage, the `checkFun` wouldn't have a reference to the _existing_ value (outside of referencing `rv` itself, which seem risky), but I can imagine a `checkReactiveVal` variant where the `checkFun` is evaluated in an environment where the current _value_ of the `reactiveVal` is accessible, exactly like [`private$value`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/reactives.R#L99) is in ReactiveVal (the R6 class).

title: Reactive functions should accept quosures and deprecate `env` and `quoted`
description:
**tl;dr**: In some unusual cases, it can be useful to pass a quoted expression or a quosure to `reactive()`, `observe()`, or a `render()` function. Prior to Shiny 1.6.0, you do this by passing `quoted=TRUE` to the function. As of Shiny 1.6.0 and above, we suggest using quosures and the `inject()` function from the rlang package.

Here's a simple example of the old way of doing things:

```R
a <- 1
expr <- quote({ 
  print(a + 2)
})

observe(expr, quoted = TRUE)
```


The equivalent new way of doing things:

```R
a <- 1
expr <- quote({ 
  print(a + 2)
})

inject(observe(!!expr))
```


The example above used `quote()` to create an expression object. This captures an unevaluated expression, but it does not capture the environment. If you also want to capture the environment, use a quosure. Here's the old way:

```R
e <- new.env()
e$a <- 1
expr <- quote({ 
  print(a + 2)
})

observe(expr, env = e, quoted = TRUE)
```

And the equivalent new way:

```R
e <- new.env()
e$a <- 2
# Create a quosure that captures both the expression and environment.
myquo <- quo({ print(a+2) })
myquo <- quo_set_env(myquo, e)
inject(observe(!!myquo))
```

Note that the example here uses `new_quosure()`, but there are many different ways to create quosures.



## In depth

This section contains an in-depth explanation of _why_ you need use `inject()` to use quosures. The short version is that this allows normal users to use quosures in the code they pass to `observe()`/`reactive()`/`render*()` functions.

Here's an example of the normal way of using an observer. It simply prints the value of `a() * 10` to the console. (To be concise, instead of a full Shiny app, I'll just show the reactive code and use the internal function `shiny:::flushReact()` to trigger reactive stuff to happen.)

```R
a <- reactiveVal(1)
observe({ message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })

# Trigger reactivity
shiny:::flushReact()
#> a*10 is: 10

# Udpate `a` and trigger reactivity
a(2)
shiny:::flushReact()
#> a*10 is: 20
```


There are cases where you want to create the expression in one place and then pass it to `observe()`. I won't go into detail about when this is useful; if you're reading this, you likely already have reasons for doing this. In these cases, you'd use `quoted=TRUE`:

```R
a <- reactiveVal(1)

# Create the quoted expression and pass it to `observe()`
expr <- quote({  message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })
observe(expr, quoted = TRUE)

shiny:::flushReact()
#> a*10 is: 10

a(2)
shiny:::flushReact()
#> a*10 is: 20
```

Prior to Shiny 1.6.0, this was the recommended (and only) way to pass quoted expressions to reactive functions. As of Shiny 1.6.0, we decided to start moving away from this, in part because the syntax is a bit clumsy, involving three arguments, `expr`, `quoted`, and `env` (which we didn't use in the example above). We decided to start using _quosures_, which come from the {rlang} package, and are widely used in tidyverse packages.

If you are familiar with quosures and rlang, you may expect it to simply work when you use the `!!` operator in a call to a reactive function like `observe()`. For example:

```R
library(rlang)
a <- reactiveVal(1)

# Create the quoted expression and pass it to `observe()`
x <- quo({ message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })
observe(!!x)

shiny:::flushReact()
#> Warning: Error in : Quosures can only be unquoted within a quasiquotation context.
#> 
#>   # Bad:
#>   list(!!myquosure)
#> 
#>   # Good:
#>   dplyr::mutate(data, !!myquosure)
#>   41: <Anonymous>
```

Two important things to notice: First, this throws an error, and second, it throws the error not immediately when `observe()` is called, but when `flushReact()` is called.

If you are familiar with using quosures with tidyverse functions like those from dplyr, this behavior may come as a surprise. If we are encouraging the use of quosures, shouldn't `observe(!!x)` behave the same as `observe(expr, quoted=TRUE)` from the previous example?

The thing to keep in mind is that `observe()` does not unwrap quosures. This means that the observer executes the literal code `!!x` when `flushReact()` is called. If you run `!!x` at the consle, you will see the same error message.

```R
!!x
#> Error: Quosures can only be unquoted within a quasiquotation context.
#>  # Bad:
#>  ...
```

In order to make it work as you might expect, you must wrap the code with `rlang::inject()`:

```R
library(rlang)
a <- reactiveVal(1)

# Create the quoted expression and inject it in `observe()`
x <- quo({ message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })
inject(observe(!!x))

shiny:::flushReact()
#> a*10 is: 10
```

What `inject()` does take the expression passed to it -- `observe(!!x)` in this case -- unwrap the quosures, and then evaluate it. The following are equivalent:

```R
x <- quo({ message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })

inject(observe(!!x))
# Equivalent to:
eval_tidy(expr(observe(!!x)))
# Also equivalent to this literal code:
observe({ message("a*10 is: ", a() * 10) })
```

So, `inject()` essentially looks at the expression, does some substitution of quosures, and then evaluates the resulting expression. It works for any R expression passed to it, not just `observe()`, `reactive()`, and so on.

You may be wondering, why did we make it necessary to use `inject()`? Why not have `observe()` and friends do the quosure unwrapping automatically?

It's because we the common case to continue to work, where someone uses quosures in a reactive call. Here's an example, where a quosure is passed to `dplyr::select()` is used on the `cars` dataset to get one column, either `speed` or `dist`. Code like this has worked in Shiny for as long as rlang's quosures have existed.

```R
library(dplyr)

# The name of the colum to selectt:
col <- reactiveVal("speed")
observe({
  colname <- col()
  res <- cars %>% select(!!colname)
  print(res)
})

shiny:::flushReact()
#>    speed
#> 1      4
#> 2      4
#> 3      7
#> ...

col("dist")
shiny:::flushReact()
#>    dist
#> 1     2
#> 2    10
#> 3     4
#> ...
```

The quosure unwrapping happens each time the user code inside the `observe()` is executed (which happens when `flushReact()` is called). If the quosure unwrapping had happened when the `observe` function was called (instead of when the user's code inside the `observe()` was called), then it would have thrown an error immediately. It would try to replace `colname` with the value of `colname` in the global scope -- but since `colname` isn't even defined at this time, it would throw an error. (Technical note: the unwrapping in this case involves substituting the value of `colspan`, even though `colspan` isn't actually a quosure, the substitution works the same way as if it were a quosure.)

If someone wants the quosure unwrapping to happen immediately, that's a much less common case, and that's what `inject()` is for.

title: textAreaInput: `width` parameter does not work, possibly because the attribute is applied to the inner instead of outer div
description:
When supplying a `width` to most inputs, the input actually takes on the specified width. Here is the output from 3 different inputs using widths: ``` > textInput("test", "test", "test", width = "500px")
> selectInput("test", "test", "test", width = "500px")
> checkboxInput("test", "test", TRUE, width = "500px")
``` Note that the width is being applied to the top level element in all cases. The issue is that with `textAreaInput()`, the width is applied to the input tag itself instead of the top level element. This results in the input not actually taking the proper width, unless you add a custom CSS rule or modify the parent element: ``` > textAreaInput("test", "test", TRUE, width = "500px")
``` Is this done on purpose for any reason? Will moving the width to the outer div cause other issues, or is it simply a bug?

title: Bug in date picker when using dateInput/dateRangeInput with daylight savings time for Australia/Melbourne for "min" and "max" settings.
description:
Hi Shiny Community,

I've got a very similar problem to #2204 where the date picker behaves oddly on the day Australia/Melbourne changes to/from daylight savings time. #2212 fixes problem #2204 where the value of the date picker cannot be set to the day that daylight savings changes. My issue is setting the "min" and "max" values of the date picker using dateInput() and dateRangeInput() as well as updateDateInput() and updateDateRangeInput().

**Reproducible Examples**
First set your system clock time zone to Australia/Melbourne (AEDT currently for daylight savings time or AEST for standard time). The date in question for these examples is 4th October, 2020 which is the date that Australia/Melbourne changed from standard time to daylight savings time.

**Case 1 - Blank End Date**
The case below leaves the end date blank as it can't set the value of "end" to be a "max" that doesn't exist.
```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dateRangeInput(inputId = "selectedDateRange", 
                             label = "",
                             start = "2020-01-19", 
                             end = "2020-10-04",
                             min = "2020-01-19",
                             max = "2020-10-04")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

**Case 2 - Works Fine**
The case below works fine when the "max" date is not "2020-10-04".
```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dateRangeInput(inputId = "selectedDateRange", 
                             label = "",
                             start = "2020-01-19", 
                             end = "2020-10-04",
                             min = "2020-01-19",
                             max = "2020-10-05")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

**Case 3 - Max Date Incorrect**
The case below will load "2020-10-03" as the end date, but in the date picker "2020-10-04" cannot be selected. The maximum that can be selected is "2020-10-03".
```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dateRangeInput(inputId = "selectedDateRange", 
                             label = "",
                             start = "2020-01-19", 
                             end = "2020-10-03",
                             min = "2020-01-19",
                             max = "2020-10-04")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

**Case 4 - Min Date Incorrect**
When the same date is applied to "min", the start date can begin on "2020-10-04" correctly, however the minimum date allowed in the date picker is set to "2020-10-03".
```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dateRangeInput(inputId = "selectedDateRange", 
                             label = "",
                             start = "2020-10-04", 
                             end = "2020-10-19",
                             min = "2020-10-04",
                             max = "2020-10-19")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) { }

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The same issue holds true for dateInput(), updateDateInput() and updateDateRangeInput(). Many thanks for the support.

title: Version of getDefaultReactiveDomain() that errors
description:
Currently many functions use `session = getDefaultReactiveDomain()` and then don't verify that `session` is non-NULL. This leads to confusing error messages if you call a function outside of a shiny app (the root cause of #2785 :

``` r
library(shiny)
onBookmark("foo")
#> Error in session$onBookmark(fun): attempt to apply non-function
```

<sup>Created on 2020-10-19 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

I'd suggest something like:

```R
getCurrentSession <- function(x)  {
  .globals$domain %||% rlang::abort("No active Shiny session")
}
```

And then use this function in user facing functions.

description:
When trying to send multiple values as `selected` in `updateRadioButtons()`, `{shiny}` doesn't throw an error, as opposed to `radioButtons()` alone:

Error:

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("radio", "Radios", letters, selected = letters[10:11]),
  actionButton("changes", "Changes")
)

server <- function(
  input, 
  output, 
  session
){
  observeEvent(input$changes, {
    updateRadioButtons(session, "radio", selected = letters[2])
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7085
Warning: Error in radioButtons: The 'selected' argument must be of length 1
  79: stop
  78: radioButtons
  70: ui [#2]
```

With `updateRadioButtons()`, no error:

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("radio", "Radios", letters, selected = letters[10]),
  actionButton("changes", "Changes")
)

server <- function(
  input, 
  output, 
  session
){
  observeEvent(input$changes, {
    updateRadioButtons(session, "radio", selected = letters[2:3])
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Deprecate freezeReactiveVal, and freezeReactiveValue for non-inputs
description:
Consider getting rid of `freezeReactiveVal`, and `freezeReactiveValue` for non-`input` objects. **If you're using these functions and seeing a deprecation message, please add a comment to this issue--we want to know what you're doing!**

The need for `freezeReactiveValue(input, "x")` is clear. When `server` calls for changes to an input on the client side, via `renderUI` with inputs inside, or `updateXXXInput`, or `insertUI`, it's likely that the input's current value is, temporarily, no longer useful or even dangerous (in that it might be inconsistent with other input state that has already been updated). `freezeReactiveValue` prevents outputs from rendering an error during this window of time.

The need to use `freezeReactiveVal`, or `freezeReactiveValue` with a generic `reactiveValues` object, is far less clear. I think we implemented it for "consistency" but there's nothing consistent about these use cases, and it's not clear to me that you could effectively use them today if you wanted to (especially, the "automatically thaw on `onFlushed`" seems wrong to me now).

We could fix the semantics of these functions so they can actually be used, but I'm inclined to proceed cautiously because 1) I'm still not sure what scenario exists where you'd actually want to use it, and 2) in case someone has somehow figured out a way to use the current implementation to do something useful, we'd be breaking them.

I propose we soft-deprecate these uses, and have the deprecation warning message include a link to this issue. If people are actually using these functions then we can consider un-deprecating.

title: Add format.reactivevalues
description:
Calling `format` on `reactivevalues` warns that `as.list.reactivevalues` is deprecated:
```r
library(shiny)
isolate(format(reactiveValues(x = 1)))
# 'as.list.reactivevalues' is deprecated. Use reactiveValuesToList instead.
# Please see ?reactiveValuesToList for more information.
```

Since there is no `format.reactivevalues` method, `base::format.default` is called, which calls `lapply` on the reactive values object (because it is a list, internally), which triggers `as.list`, so we get to `as.list.reactivevalues`. 

What about adding an S3 method, something like:
```r
format.reactivevalues <- function(x, all.names = FALSE, ...) {
  format(reactiveValuesToList(x = x, all.names = all.names), ...)
}
```

I can create a PR if you wish.

title: DiskCache may not prune enough items if max_n and max_size are both used
description:
In the example below, just the last item, `"f"`, should not be pruned; the rest of the objects exceed the max size of 200 bytes when serialized.

```R
d <- diskCache(max_n = 3, max_size = 200)
# Set some values. Use rnorm so that object size is large; a simple vector
# like 1:100 will be stored very efficiently by R's ALTREP, and won't exceed
# the max_size. We want each of these objects to exceed max_size so that they'll be
# pruned.
d$set("a", rnorm(100))
d$set("b", rnorm(100))
d$set("c", rnorm(100))
d$set("d", rnorm(100))
d$set("e", rnorm(100))
Sys.sleep(0.1)  # For systems that have low mtime resolution.
d$set("f", 1)   # This object is small and shouldn't be pruned.
d$prune()
d$keys()
#> [1] "d" "e" "f"
```

title: eventReactive ignoreInit clarification in docs and/or possible ignoreInit bug
description:
The documentation for `ignoreNULL` and `ignoreInit` within `observeEvent()` is quite clear. Likewise, the docs for `ignoreNULL` within `eventReactive()` is also clear. But, I believe the description of `ignoreInit` within `eventReactive()` is either misleading **or** the current behavior of `ignoreInit` is off somehow. Here's a simple Shiny app demonstrating my confusion or a possible bug (take note of the `ignoreInit` values for `re1` and `re2`):
```R
library(tidyverse)
library(shiny)

rv <- reactiveVal(lubridate::origin)

f1 <- function() {
  print("in f1")
  print(sprintf("current rv() = %s", isolate(rv())))
  rv(lubridate::now())
  print(sprintf("new rv() = %s", isolate(rv())))
  re1()
  re2()
}

re1 <- eventReactive(rv(), {
  print("in re1")
}, ignoreNULL = TRUE, ignoreInit = TRUE)

re2 <- eventReactive(rv(), {
  print("in re2")
}, ignoreNULL = TRUE, ignoreInit = FALSE)

ui <- fluidPage(actionButton("action_button_1", label = "click me"))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input[["action_button_1"]], {
    f1()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
When the app starts, `rv` is created (and is set immediately to a non-`NULL` value), as are two `eventReactive()`s, `re1` and `re2`, both of which take in their `eventExpr` a reactive dependency on `rv`. Both are also set to `ignoreNULL`, but this should not come into play here since `rv` will never be set to `NULL`.

In my interpretation of the documentation, `re1` and `re2` are both now "created", and my (apparently) naïve assumption is that they've both been "initialized", too. The documentation line for `observeEvent/eventReactive` is:

> By default, both of these will run right when they are created (except if, at that moment, eventExpr evaluates to NULL and ignoreNULL is TRUE).

"both of these", according to the docs, implies `observeEvent()` and `eventReactive()`.

When clicking the app's action button the first time, here's the (console) output:
```
 [1] "in f1"
 [1] "current rv() = 1970-01-01"
 [1] "new rv() = 2020-08-31 19:31:54"
```
 `f1()` runs, which sets `rv` and should thus invalidate both `re1` and `re2`. `f1()` then explicitly calls both `re1()` and `re2()`, however neither run. The `eventExpr` evaluates to non-`NULL` (since it's just been set to the current time), and so my only guess is that the `ignoreInit` argument is blocking both from running.

When clicking the app's action button the second time, we finally get some `re1` and `re2` action:
```
 [1] "in f1"
 [1] "current rv() = 2020-08-31 19:31:54"
 [1] "new rv() = 2020-08-31 19:31:57"
 [1] "in re1"
 [1] "in re2"
```

This confuses me, for two reasons.

The first reason is that the documentation isn't very clear about what "initialized" means in the context of a `eventReactive()`. Does `ignoreInit = TRUE` really just block the first _execution_ attempt of the reactive function? Is that first attempted execution count as the "initialization"? That feels different than `observeEvent()`, which, being a reactive _endpoint_, can logically be blocked on the app initialization procedure (i.e. the documentation and behavior make perfect sense for `observeEvent()`).

The second reason I'm confused is when `ignoreInit = FALSE`, `re2()` _still_ doesn't run on the first button-click, despite being created with `ignoreInit = FALSE`. So even if the first attempted execution of an `eventReactive()` counts as the "initialization", then `re2()` should run on that first button-click, since the `eventExpr` evaluates to non-`NULL` both during app startup (where `rv` is initialized to `lubridate::origin`) and after the button-click.

The behavior I first expected was that _both_ `rv1()` and `rv2()` would run on the first button-click. Then, after updating by beliefs and guessing a bit at what "initialization" means for an `eventReactive()`, I expected that `rv2()` would run on the first button-click. But neither reactive functions run, and that is surprising behavior to me (and perhaps some other Shiny users out there?).

BTW, this is using Shiny v1.5.0.

title: Source does not work anymore in server.R since shiny 1.5
description:
Thanks for creating shiny. You do a great job guys. 

Since updating to plotly 1.5 sourcing of external code via source does not work anymore. 
Minimal Example:

ui.R:
```R
library(shiny)
ui <- pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Example"),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(selectInput("abc", "Dum", c("A", "B")),
            uiOutput("test_me"),
            uiOutput("test_me_too"))
)
```

server.R:
```R
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$test_me <- renderUI({selectInput("BeispielUI", "Dum", c("2", "3"))})
  source("./R/helper.R", local = TRUE)
}
```
In the folder R in the file helper.R:
```R
output$test_me_too <- renderUI({selectInput("sourceBeispielUI", "Dum", c("Ich", "Du"))})
```

Error:
```R
Error in output$test_me_too <- renderUI({ : 
  object 'output' not found
```
Seems like "output" (and "input") cannot be found in the file.

In shiny 1.4 this works, in shiny 1.5 it doesn't. I could also write it in modules, but this would make things more complicated and more code would be necessary? Is there another solution?

title: Idea: define shiny options in an external (YAML?) file
description:
Deploying apps often require setting `{shiny}` options, with the most common being `shiny.host`
 and `shiny.port`.

So far, I've been doing it either by setting the options manually before the call launching the application, or by setting the options in the rprofile. 

Yet, I think it would be nice to have a way for `{shiny}` to set the options via a specific file, for example in a `shiny-options.yaml`.
I know this is doable manually right now, either by implementing my own YAML parser or by `source()`ing an .R script, yet that would be nice if `{shiny}` could automatically read this file it it exists. 

For example, we'd have a YAML file that looks like this: 

```
shiny:
	host: 0.0.0.0
	port: 2811
```

title: Allow ... in the *Output function to add attributes
description:

```r 
plotOutput(
  "plot"
) %>% tagAppendAttributes(
  onclick = "alert('hello world')"
)
```

I wonder if this could be solved by allowing `...` to the `*Output` functions, passing the named arguments which do no match the parameters to `tagAppendAttributes()`?

title: Make `update*Input` doc inherit from their classical `*Input` counterpart
description:
I've noticed that the `update*Input` functions do not automatically inherit the documentation from the parameters from their `*Input`. 

For example, the doc for `sliderInput(step = )` is rather precise:

```
#' @param step Specifies the interval between each selectable value on the
#'   slider (if `NULL`, a heuristic is used to determine the step size). If
#'   the values are dates, `step` is in days; if the values are times
#'   (POSIXt), `step` is in seconds.
```

Whereas `updateSliderInput(step = )` is

```
#' @param step Step size.
```

I think having an `@inheritParams` would be better for the doc here.

```
#' @inheritParams sliderInput
```

title: Conditional Debounce
Automatically minify CSS & JS files that are used in a shiny app
description:
(NB: This follows a discussion with @wch) 

In order to gain performance when `{shiny}` apps are deployed, it would be effective to be able to minify "on the fly" the CSS and JS files that are served with `{shiny}`, _i.e_ when they are either in the `www/` folder or when they come from other packages.

That could be done today with an R package like [{minifyr}](https://github.com/ColinFay/minifyr) __but__ this one needs NodeJS to run, which would make NodeJS necessary for running a `{shiny}` app, which might not be a good strategy :) 

One other way to do this could be by wrapping an external C or C++ library inside a package. 

I'm happy to explore this myself.

title: updatePickerInput will not work with delays/long processing time in server
description:

The code works as expected if the user e.g. deselects slowly inputs from `vs` in the example below. However, if the user is very quick in deselecting, the app will start jumping forth and back between different inputs. This problem increases, if processing time is increased in the ` server `, which I do artificially in the example below with `sleep.time`. I really cannot figure out what the problem is and if this is more general problem that might affect other applications as well. Any help would be much appreciated.

### Example application

library(rstan)

  real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // standard error of effect estimates

  real<lower=0> tau;      // standard deviation in treatment effects
  vector[J] eta;          // unscaled deviation from mu by school
}

  vector[J] theta = mu + tau * eta;        // school treatment effects
}
model {

  target += normal_lpdf(y | theta, sigma); // log-likelihood
}

I can't tell if this issue already existed with rstan 2.21.1, but it did not exist for rstan 2.19.3. Since the problem does not occur outside of a Shiny app, I opened the issue here on Shiny's issue tracker. But if you think it's not related to Shiny, then I can also open an issue on rstan's issue tracker. In that case, it might be helpful if you could sketch out what the difference is between running a Shiny app in the "In R console" mode, running it in the "In Background job" mode, and running the content of the Shiny app outside of the Shiny app. This way, it might be possible to track the problem down.
