library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
    navlistPanel(
        tabPanel("A",
                 fluidPage(
                     tabsetPanel(
                         tabPanel("B",
                                  fluidRow(
                                      column(3,
                                             sliderInput("projempWindow", "C", 1, 100, c(1, 100), 1)
                                      ),
                                      column(3,
                                             radioButtons("projempFuture", "D", c("E", "G")),
                                             conditionalPanel("input.projempFuture=='G'",
                                                              numericInput("projempDeltar", "H", 0, -2, 2, 0.01)
                                             )
                                      )
                                  )
                         ),
                         tabPanel("I",
                                  fluidRow(
                                      column(3,
                                             dateInput("projcompEnd", "J", "2020-07-01", as.Date("2020-07-16"),
                                                       as.Date("2020-09-16"))
                                      )
                                  )
                         )
                     )
                 )
        )
    ),
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    
    output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
        hist(rnorm(100))
    })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

There are two, very likely related issues here:

- `C` should be a slider, yet, it is displayed as an editbox.
- `projempDeltar` should only appear if `projempFuture` is set to `G`, but it appears even if it is set to `E`.

To make things even more mysterious (and the reason while I think these are related): removing the `dateInput` on tabPanel `H` solves *both* problems! (It is also quite strange that it has any effect whatsoever, as they are  on a *different* tabpanel...)

title: addResourcePath should allow resources that starts with a dot
description:
It's pretty common to have on a website a folder called `/.well-known`, notably for adding a `security.txt`: https://securitytxt.org/

It would be doable by doing `addResourcePath(".well-known", "inst/.well-known")`, but `addResourcePath()` regex for prefix name excludes prefixes that starts with dot. 

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/6ad2125ee74a0a6cab723fefc25449c50a4568fa/R/server.R#L74

Could this regex be turned to `"^[a-z0-9\\-_\\.][a-z0-9\\-_\\.]*$"` instead?

Happy to make a PR in that sense.

Avoid browser timeouts for slow initializing apps.
description:
If I do long calculations in global.R my chrome browser runs into [a hard 30 second timeout](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39751124/increase-timeout-limit-in-google-chrome) because Shiny does not respond.
Some time after chrome disconnects Shiny will stop the (still initializing) App because it runs into ``app_idle_timeout``. Next time I try to access the page it starts from the beginning and runs into a timeout again. The app appears to be not working.

There are various workarounds for this problem:

## The progressive lazy
[Lazy load the data (in server.R) and show a progress bar](http://www.mazsoft.com/blog/post/2018/01/01/show-progress-bar-when-pre-loading-data-in-shiny-app).
This is inconvenient to develop though. And the user still has to wait.

## The fast
Cache the data somewhere and let the app load the data from cache.
But you have to maintain the cache and that is always a hard problem.

## The manual
Increase ``app_idle_timeout`` to make sure your app has enough time to start. Then just click reload in your browser after some minutes. It will connect to the now running app. 
However, if you wait too long, shiny will kill the app after ``app_idle_timeout``.

## The ugly 
Create an html page, that contains an iframe pointing to your app. After n seconds (typical start time < n <  ``app_idle_timeout``)  forward the browser to the real app using a meta refresh tag. 
That way, if the browser is left alone, it will eventually open the app and keep it running.

## The default <- This is the feature request
If an app is initializing and the browser has been waiting for more than 20s, create an info page that shows "app initializing since 123s" and refresh this page every 20s. 
Show an error if initializing takes longer than ``app_init_timeout``
Probably the 20s wait should be configurable. 

This solution would work reasonably out of the box. If you want it fast, you got to cache.

Improvements to shiny options
description:
The documentation on `?shinyOptions` is currently wrong (introduced in #2575):

> There are a number of global options that affect Shiny's behavior. These can be set globally with `options()` or locally (for a single app) with `shinyOptions()`.

This isn't actually true for the `shiny.*` options, which currently only work when set globally (i.e., shiny reads them with `getOption()`, not `getShinyOption()`). We should either fix the docs, or make the necessary changes so that the documentation is actually true (ideally the latter). In addition, maybe it makes sense for `shinyOptions()` to add the `shiny.` prefix (it none already exists) so that `shinyOptions(host = ...)` would work for setting `shiny.host`.

title: `shinyOptions()` and `options()` not working as expected
description:
### Describe the problem in detail

I am trying to call a custom function defined in my server function when an error occurs at anytime in any part of my app so I'm trying to set the `shiny.error` option to a custom function.

The documentation in `?getShinyOption` the following about setting options: 
>  If options are set from global.R, app.R, ui.R, or server.R, or if they are set from inside the server function, then the options will be scoped to the application. When the application exits, the new option set is discarded and the global option set is restored.

But I am facing the following issues (let's say we want to call `recover()`) 

* `shinyOptions(shiny.error = recover)` seems not to work. No matter I place it within my server function or outside it, the app closes when an error occurs and `recover()` is not called.
* `options(shiny.error  = recover)` works both when set from outside or inside the server function. But the option persists after the application exits, which I didn't expect when setting from within server.

My ultimate goal is to call a function that shows a notification and restarts the application by calling to `session$reload()`.  But in this case, I found the following issues:

* If I place `options(shiny.error = session$reload)` within my server function, it has no effect.
* I tried to wrap it in a function `options(shiny.error = function() session$reload())` , but it didn't work either.
* And I finally  tried with `options(shiny.error = session$reload())` from inside the server function. But since I am making the call, the application gets reloaded all the time (I'm not sure if this is the continuous reloading is the expected behavior).




### Examples

1. Placing `shinyOptions(shiny.error=recover)` within server function. Does not work.

```R
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    actionButton("btn", "Throw error!")
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    shinyOptions(shiny.error=recover)
    observeEvent(input$btn, {
      stop("Error!")
    })
  }
)

shinyOptions(shiny.error=recover)

)

title: freezeReactiveValue() and indirect dependencies
description:
In my opinion, `freezeReactiveValue()` has a crucial drawback (and I guess this also applies to `freezeReactiveVal()` though I haven't tested it yet):
Only reactive expressions depending *directly* on the object being freezed will quit with a silent error as done with `req(FALSE)`. Reactive expressions depending *indirectly* on the object being freezed won't realize that they should also quit with a silent error. Consider the following reproducible example which is a slightly modified version of the example from `?freezeReactiveValue`:

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("data", "Data Set", c("mtcars", "pressure")),
  checkboxGroupInput("cols", "Columns (select 2)", character(0)),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    data <- get(input$data)
    # Sets a flag on input$cols to essentially do req(FALSE) if input$cols
    # is accessed. Without this, an error will momentarily show whenever a
    # new data set is selected.
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "cols")
    updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "cols", choices = names(data))
  }, priority = 1)
  
  ### Additional code not from ?freezeReactiveValue:
  cols_reactive <- reactive({
    input$cols
  })
  ### 
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    # When a new data set is selected, input$cols will have been invalidated
    # above, and this will essentially do the same as req(FALSE), causing
    # this observer to stop and raise a silent exception.
    ### Modified code:
    cols <- cols_reactive() # Original code: cols <- input$cols
    ### 
    data <- get(input$data)
    
    if (length(cols) == 2) {
      plot(data[[ cols[1] ]], data[[ cols[2] ]])
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```

The difference to the original example from `?freezeReactiveValue` is that `output$plot` does not depend *directly* on `input$cols`, but only *indirectly* via `cols_reactive()`. Thus, after having selected two columns from `mtcars` and then switching to `pressure`, `freezeReactiveValue()` does not help in avoiding the (temporary) error. This temporary error might not be a problem in this simple example, but I have an app where I need to avoid it. Of course it would be possible to manually notify all indirect dependencies to quit with a silent error, but this is a tedious and error-prone task and in my opinion, it breaks the concept of reactivity.

I guess this drawback is already known, so I'm posting this as a feature request. I guess it will be quite complicated to fix this (so that also reactive expressions depending *indirectly* on the object being freezed will quit with a silent error), but it would be great if it could be managed somehow.

_**Edit 2020-09-16 by @jcheng5:** I added `priority = 1` to the example to make it clear that even with the observers executing in the most desirable order, this is still a problem._

title: Remove (or add) choose prompt using updateSelectInput()
description:
It would be great if it was possible to create a `selectInput(..., selectize = TRUE)` *with* a choose prompt and later (under certain circumstances) *remove* the choose prompt using `updateSelectInput()`. The aim is that the input field may be cleared before running `updateSelectInput()` (i.e. before removing the choose prompt) and that it may not be cleared afterwards (i.e. after removing the choose prompt). 

The "reverse" feature would be nice, too: Creating a `selectInput(..., selectize = TRUE)` *without* a choose prompt and *adding* a choose prompt using `updateSelectInput()`.

I already posted this as a question (together with a reprex) in [this RStudio Community thread](https://community.rstudio.com/t/remove-or-add-choose-prompt-using-updateselectinput/69192), but as there have been no answers, it seems like a feature request makes sense.

title: FR: let selectizeInput choose same choice repeatedly.
description:
<!--

Thanks for taking the time to file a feature request! Please take the time to search for an existing feature request, to avoid creating duplicate requests. If you find an existing feature request, please give it a thumbs-up reaction, as we'll use these reactions to help prioritize the implementation of these features in the future.

If the feature has not yet been filed, then please describe the feature you'd like to see become a part of Shiny. See:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Writing-Good-Feature-Requests

for a guide on how to write good feature requests.

-->

I wanted to make a formula editor to assist users while writing formulas with variable names. The aim is to let users calculate new variables for a data frame based on existing variables. If there are many variable names, users won't be able to keep those in mind, hence the assist. selectizeInput is almost perfect for this case. It allows predefined items (e.g. VAR1, VAR2, ...., +, /, -, *, sqrt(, log(, lag(, first(, ),....) but it also allows users to add new items, on the go. e.g. user may want to mutliply a variable with an arbitrary number e.g. 12231232.3. This formula can be converted into a string, parsed and evaluated. Only problem is that users can't add same item twice. sqrt(x^2 + y^2) doesn't work since, **^** and **2** appear twice.

I wonder if this makes sense for other users? There maybe other scenarios, where this can be useful (some ordered selection of items for probabilities? e.g. picking multiple identical items from a collection)

title: Setting argument "selected" of updateSelectInput() to nonexisting value
tabsetPanel() doesn't work with list of panels
description:
It would be nice if `tabsetPanel()` could work more easily with a list of panels, so you can program with it without needing to know `do.call()`:

```R
panels <- list(
  tabPanel("Plot", "plot"),
  tabPanel("Summary", "summary"),
  tabPanel("Table", "table")
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tabsetPanel(panels)
)
shinyApp(ui, function(...) {})

ui <- fluidPage(
  do.call(tabsetPanel, panels)
)
shinyApp(ui, function(...) {})
```

This is somewhat related to #1928 (in the sense that if you fix issue you should also fix this one)

I think you have two main options to fix:

* Automatically splice list inputs (like htmltools)
* Use `list2()` instead of list to get explicit `!!!` splicing

title: Provide an official function to find out if an app is running locally or in a server (shinyapps/shiny server/connect/etc)
description:
This has been a question on StackOverflow for 5 years, and @yihui 's answer was to look at the SHINY_PORT envvar:

```
is_local <- Sys.getenv('SHINY_PORT') == ""
```

I see this method used very often, I myself use it a lot too, but it feels a bit dirty to do something like that when there's no official word on whether this is the correct method. I think by now it's become the unofficial correct answer, but it would be useful if shiny exported a fucntion like this.

Set the range of the axes scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0), limits=xlims) + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0, 0), limits=c(0, max(zdata$assocSig)+1)) + # Customize the theme theme_bw() + theme(axis.line=element_blank(), axis.text.x=element_blank(), axis.title.x=element_blank(), plot.margin=margin(0, 0, 0, 0), panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size=14), axis.title.y = element_text(size=18), plot.title = element_text(size=24, hjust=0.5, face="bold", margin=margin(10, 0, 10, 0))) # Grab the Gviz plot with the gene models track gzp <- grid::grid.grabExpr(plt <- Gviz::plotTracks(Gviz::GenomeAxisTrack(labelPos="above"), collapseTranscripts="meta", shape="arrow", transcriptAnnotation="symbol", title.width=0, add=T, from=xlims[1], to=xlims[2], margin=0, innerMargin=0)) # Get the variant which is nearest to the cursor point <- nearPoints(zdata, hover, xvar="x", yvar="y", threshold=1000000, maxpoints=nrow(zdata), addDist=FALSE) if (nrow(point) == 0) {return(NULL)} point$dist <- sqrt((point$x-hover$x)^2 + (point$y-hover$y)^2) #point <- point[point$dist <= 0.025, ] if (nrow(point) == 0) {return(NULL)} point <- as.data.frame(data.table::setorder(data.table::as.data.table(point), dist)) point <- point[1,] # Calculate distance from left and bottom side of the plot, in pixels left_px <- hover$range$left + hover$x * (hover$range$right - hover$range$left) top_px <- hover$range$top + (1.0 - hover$y) * (hover$range$bottom - hover$range$top) # On offset is required to ensure that the tooltip does not overlap the # mouse. See https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2239 offset <- 5 # Style the tooltip: # background color is set so tooltip is a bit transparent # z-index is set to ensure tooltip will be on top style <- paste0("position:absolute; z-index:100; color: rgb(50, 50, 50); background-color: rgba(245, 245, 245, 0.85); ", "left:", left_px + offset, "px; top:", top_px + offset, "px;") # Render the tooltip as a wellPanel wellPanel( style = style, p(HTML(paste0(" SNP: ", point$live.rsid, "
", " Pos: ", point$pos, "
", " MAF: ", round(point$MAF, digits=3), "
", " R: ", signif(point$r, digits=3), "
", " PPA: ", signif(point$ppa, digits=3), "
"))) ) }) } shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server) ``` ### Steps to Reproduce To reproduce the problem, please follow these steps: 1.) In the function get_x_y_values, please uncomment the line "#from_top <- sum(to_mm(gt$heights[seq(panel_pos$t - 1)]))" But note that the bug caused by this line may require you to restart your computer to fix it (i.e., comment out the line, restart the OS, then re-run the app) 2.) Run the shiny app. (I do this in RStudio.) 3.) Choose "b1" (or "b2", it doesn't matter) from the dropdown menu. 4.) Click the Plot button. The plot will be empty. This is the first sign of trouble. Maximize the window and the plot will become visible. 5.) Remove the "b1" selection and click the Plot button again. This will clear the plot correctly. 6.) Select "b1" and plot again. The plot will be empty. If you follow these steps with the troublesome line commented out--assuming the bad code has not run without restarting the OS--this is the expected behavior: 4.) Click the Plot button. The plot will render regardless of the initial window size. Maximize/minimize the window; the plot remains visible and is correctly resized. 6.) Select "b1" and plot again. The plot should appear just as it did the first time. ### App and Bug Description The Plot button, when clicked, generates a ggplot and a Gviz plot, tied together by cowplot::plot_grid. The tricky part is that I've implemented functionality to report information about the points in the ggplot whenever the user hovers the mouse over the plot. Since the plot is actually a composite of the ggplot and another object from the Gviz package, this functionality requires some transformations from the coordinates reported by the hover info to the coordinates of the points in the underlying plot object. To compute that transformation, I make calls to grid::convertUnit in the callback function that gets invoked on mouseover events. Even a single call to grid::convertUnit in this context causes the sporadic rendering described above. Interestingly, the problem persists after I comment out the offending line of code. It persists even when I close the RStudio session and restart!! I have to actually restart my OS (I'm running Ubuntu 16.04) to get back to the original behavior.

title: Strange behaviour setting the selected attribute of updateSelectizeInput with server=T
description:
It seems to be a strange behaviour in updateSelectizeInput with server=T when setting the selected value to the same value that it previously has. Thus, not allowing to syncronize the selected values between different tab panels.

To share the selected value between different tab panels, I use the following piece of code:

```R
Selected<-reactiveValues(GENE=NULL)
observeEvent(input$S1_GENE, Selected$GENE<-(input$S1_GENE))
observeEvent(input$S2_GENE, Selected$GENE<-(input$S2_GENE))

observeEvent(Selected$GENE, {
    updateSelectInput(session, "S1_GENE", selected=Selected$GENE)
    updateSelectInput(session, "S2_GENE", selected=Selected$GENE)
})
```

This works flawless with SelectInput and SelectizeInput with server=F. However to maintain a good response in the app with large vectors, SelectizeInput with server=T must be used. In this case, the selectizeinput enters in a loop. It seems that updating the selected attribute with the same value that it has produces an empty vector, entering into an infinite loop.

```R
Selected<-reactiveValues(GENE=NULL)
observeEvent(input$S1_GENE, Selected$GENE<-(input$S1_GENE))
observeEvent(input$S2_GENE, Selected$GENE<-(input$S2_GENE))

observeEvent(Selected$GENE, {
     updateSelectizeInput(session, "S1_GENE", selected=Selected$GENE, choices=GENE_SET, server=TRUE)
     updateSelectizeInput(session, "S2_GENE", selected=Selected$GENE, choices=GENE_SET, server=TRUE)
})
```

I tried the stable version of CRAN and the latest development with the same outcome.

title: Documentation: difference between placing several shiny tags inside a `list()` vs `tagList()`
description:
Related to https://github.com/hadley/mastering-shiny/issues/204

It's not clear whether mutltiple tags should be grouped inside a `list()` or a `tagList()`. It would be useful to document the difference and which one is recommened.

Historically, I've always used `tagList()` because there are some functions from third-party packages that expect a `shiny.tag.list` object, and also there are some advanced usecases where a generic list fails. But I'm not sure what's the official shiny position on whether tagList should always be used or not.

  })
  
  # Table Output
  output$data <- renderTable({
    location_filter() %>%
      .[date >= input$date_range[1] & date <= input$date_range[2]] %>%
      .[, date := as.character(date)]
  })
  
}

# Run the app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
I have asked the question on [stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/q/62171194/10823893) and ismirsehregal suggested to create an issue to check if this is an expected behavior. I'll just copy and paste the question below.

> I have a set of data with different date ranges for different locations. I would like my date range widget to update the minimum and maximum dates after selecting a location with the select box widget.
> 
> I have tried the steps mentioned in https://mastering-shiny.org/action-dynamic.html#hierarchical-select and have modified it for the date range widget but it does not seem to be working. I have included a reprex below where the start doesn't seem to update after selecting locations B or C but not A.

The answer given by Limey is as follows:

> The problem seems to be with setting min/start or max/end at the same time. You have to ensure that start and end both lie within the range [min and max] at all times. The easiest way to do this was to split the update into stages:
> 
>     Set min and max to the earlest and latest dates in the whole dataset
>     Set start and min to earliest and latest dates at the current location
>     Set min and max to the earliest and latest dates at the current location
> 
> I combined 1 and 2 in a single call to updateDateRangeInput.
> 
> It's messy, but it seems to work.
> 
> I changed the structure of your reactives slightly whilst investigating whether there was priority issue with their updates. Here's the whole server function.
> 
> ```
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   locationData <- reactive({
>     if (input$location == "All") {
>       dummy_data
>     } else {
>       dummy_data[location == input$location]
>     }
> 
>   })
> 
>   filteredData <- reactive({
>     locationData() %>%
>       .[date >= input$date_range[1] & date <= input$date_range[2]] %>%
>       .[, date := as.character(date)]
>   })
> 
>   # Filter location
>   observeEvent(input$location, {
>     updateDateRangeInput(session,
>                          "date_range",
>                          min = min(dummy_data$date),
>                          max = max(dummy_data$date),
>                          start = min(locationData()$date),
>                          end = max(locationData()$date))
>     updateDateRangeInput(session,
>                          "date_range",
>                          min = min(locationData()$date),
>                          max = max(locationData()$date))
>   })
>   # Table Output
>   output$data <- renderTable({
>     filteredData()
>   })
> }
> ```

title: graceful error handling in place of shutting down
description:
The current behavior of Shiny is ([intentionally](https://community.rstudio.com/t/prevent-observer-crashes/25169/3) if I understand right) to completely shut down in a lot of situations where it runs into an error. 

For both development and the "classic" use case of interactive visualizations this isn't terrible since nothing's really lost. Especially if it's primarily being used by people already familiar with R.

But imho Shiny (and r for that matter) have grown far beyond that niche and with packages like shinydashboard, the myriad of [excel-alikes](https://appsilon.com/forget-about-excel-use-r-shiny-packages-instead/), and more creating a viable platform for internal tools that democratize access to R's functionality.

I think Shiny's grown enough that it's warranted to consider baking in a more graceful means of error handling, either as a new default or as a global option of "production" vs "developent" mode. At minimum I think an app set to production mode should notify the user of an error with a copy/pasteable log output and at least stay open so they can save their work or continue using any functionality not affected by the error.

title: Print error messages from R console instead of force closing shiny app
description:
I have a shiny app that runs a monte carlo simulation with 500 replications. To do this, I use a for loop and call a function from another package to run the simulation, and then I save the data. The shiny app then produces the results using renderTable.

It is possible that the user could mistakenly enter something that would cause one or more of the simulation replications to fail to converge, triggering a `stop` in the function I'm calling. If this happens, there is nothing to render in a table. In R, I get a nice error message from the package telling me that the model failed to converge. However, in Shiny, the app just force closes.

I've tried using `tryCatch` and `showNotification`.  It does show the error briefly, but the app still force closes.  I've tried using a validate statement in renderTable to tell it to only render a table if the object exists, but it fails before it gets to the renderTable part of the code.  Essentially, the `stop` function in the function I'm calling will crash the entire app if the user inputs something that triggers the `stop` function.

Is it possible for Shiny to simply print the fatal error message from the R console instead of defaulting to closing the app?

title: conditionalPanel: allow option to not create an extra div element, to not interfere with DOM structure
description:
When using `conditionalPanel()` to conditionally show something in the UI, it inserts a new div tag. Usually it's ok, but sometimes the DOM structure is important and needs to be consistent, and having a conditionalPanel div breaks the UI. I've run into this many times in the past, but here is my latest example: inside a shinydashboard `sidebarMenu()`, it expects to only see `menuItem()` children. If I wrap one of the menuItem inside a conditional Panel, which is something that should be doable, the UI breaks (for this particular case there is a workaround, but the general problem persists)

Example

```
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenu(
      checkboxInput("show", "show item 2"),
      menuItem("item 1"),
      conditionalPanel(
        "input.show",
        menuItem("item 2")
      )
    )
  ),
  dashboardBody()
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Force output renderers to be after certain observers
description:
Hi, 

A notice before the feature request: `outputOption` doesn't work in this case.

How hard it'll be to force output renderers to be always after some observers? 

For instance, if I write an interface to users allowing them to customize `renderPlot`, the users might use reactive values such as but not limited to `input`. What's difficult is I cannot control or limit the variables getting used. This might result in a race condition with other observers.

Here's an minimal example that can reproduce the issue

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput('a', 'A'),
  textInput('b', 'B'),
  plotOutput('plot')
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- shiny::renderPlot({
    #  --- Some code you cannot control ---
    cat('Rendering plot...\n')
    plot(1:10, main = paste(input$a, input$b))
    # --- End of customized block --- 
  })
  
  # An observer that might race with the plot
  obsver <- observeEvent(input$a, {
    # update input$b
    updateTextInput(session, 'b', value = Sys.time())
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

*Every time when I update `A`, the plot gets rendered twice, but I want the renderer to wait until the observer gets finished.

I want to explicitly specify the order of `renderPlot` and `observeEvent`, so that whenever certain `observeEvent` is in the queue, `renderPlot` gets moved towards the back of queue?

```
shiny::render_after(reactives = obsver, outputId = 'plot')
```

title: Session$resetBrush Does Not Work For Shiny Modules
description:
Hello there. 

Just letting you know that if you're using shiny modules to compose a `Shiny` app the call `session$resetBrush` won't work with the default input name, and you will have to compose your id by yourself.

### UI Component
```
markerDensityPlotOutput <- function(id) {
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # REQUIRED
    ns <- NS(id)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    plot_output_to_return <- shiny::plotOutput(
        brush = ns("plot_brush"),
        outputId = ns("marker_density"),
    )
    return(plot_output_to_return)
}
```

### Server Component
```
markerDensity <- function(input, output, session) {
    observeEvent(input$plot_brush, {
           # THIS DOES NOT WORK
            session$resetBrush("plot_brush")
           # THIS DOES WORK
           ns <- NS(marker_density_plot_output_module_name)
           plot_brush_namespace_id <- ns("plot_brush")
           session$resetBrush(plot_brush_namespace_id)
    })
}
```

What's interesting is the `input$plot_brush` is detected correctly, so not sure why this is a problem

title: showtext text sizes are wrong when png(type='cairo')
description:
(Related to https://github.com/yixuan/showtext/issues/33)

Minimal reprex (must be run on a machine without aqua capabilities and viewed on a high-resolution display): 

```r
library(shiny)
library(showtext)
font_add_google("Gochi Hand", "gochi")
showtext_auto()

# showtext's dpi option currently doesn't work with CairoPNG (see issue above for more details)
opts <- options(shiny.usecairo = FALSE)
onStop(function() { options(ops) })

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    numericInput("n", "n", 1),
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      plot(head(cars, input$n), family = "gochi")
      title("Hello world")
    })
  }
)
```

Notice how the text is much smaller than it should be because showtext is unaware of the device resolution. Shiny needs to set `showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = ...)` with the resolution it passes to the graphics device for this to work properly.

title: Consider deprecating ShinySession$close
description:
Currently, the `close` field of the `ShinySession` class is public. We should consider making the field private because there are more robust public interfaces for interacting with the session lifecycle.

This issue was filed after @wch and I started to audit the set of public fields and methods that existed in `ShinySession` but not `MockShinySession`.

title: Suggestion: Auto-loading R files in R/ subdirectory should be recursive
description:
The new shiny feature of auto-loading R files in an `R/` subdir is great. 

Often in complex apps, placing all the R files in one directory is too messy and results in too many files, and a further division into subfolders is required. It's not at all uncommon to have over 50 R files, responsible for different modules, different components, different helpers, etc. I see it a lot. I would not advise anyone with over 10 files to use shiny's new auto loading feature because it only loads the top-level. I see a lot of added benefit if it were to support loading all R files under `R/` or its subdirs.

- Create a simple Shiny App following tutorials or use the default template created in the RStudio IDE (New Project / Shiny Web Application)
- Run the app and load into browser (I'm using Chrome on macOS)
- Examine the HTML or run an accessibility validation tool such as Axe (https://www.deque.com/axe/axe-for-web/)

### Problem
The HTML element has no `lang` attribute. This is a WCAG 2.1 A violation: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#language-of-page

### Expected
Pages should be accessible by default. Thus, there should be a reasonable default, and the ability to specify a different language. For English:

`<html lang="en">`

This is critical for screen readers, otherwise you can have (for example) a Spanish user's screen reader trying to pronounce English words using Spanish language rules.

There was a community question on this:
https://community.rstudio.com/t/how-to-specify-the-language-to-a-shiny-app/26472

title: UI does not render when defined as a function in a specific case
renderPrint() width option doesn't seem to work
Bookmarking (bug?): `onRestored()` is called even when no bookmark was done
description:
The docs for `onRestored` say:

> onRestored registers a function that will be called after a session is restored.

My understanding of that sentence, and also what I would intuitively think, is that `onRestored` is only called after a session is restored. If not session is restored, this shouldn't get called.

However that doesn't seem to be the case. It seems like whenever there is ANYTHING in the URL query string, `onRestored` gets called. 

Example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- function(req) fluidPage(
  bookmarkButton()
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  onRestored(function(state){
    message("restored")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server,enableBookmarking = "server", options = list(port=5555))
```

Navigating to `http://127.0.0.1:5555/` doesn't produce any output, but going to `http://127.0.0.1:5555/?foo` does.

title: "Run App" button should honour the port specified in in `shinyApp()`
description:
It's very handy to specify a port when developing and restarting your R session frequently for testing. The following code will always run the app on the given port if the code is run explicitly:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage()
server <- function(input, output, session) {}
shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port=5555))
```

But if I click on the "Run App" button (and by extension, the `runApp()` function) then the port is ignored and it will randomize a port every session. This makes testing less streamlined.

It looks like `runApp()` does know how to honour some other parameters of `shinyApp`, for example the `enableBookmarking` parameter.

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  numericInput("year", "year", value = 2020),
  dateInput("date", "Date")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$year, {
    req(isTruthy(input$year)) # stop if year is blank
    daterange <- range(as.Date(paste0(input$year, "-01-01")),as.Date(paste0(input$year, "-12-31")))

          updateDateInput(session,"date",
                          value = daterange[1]
          ))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_AU.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C               LC_TIME=en_AU.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_AU.UTF-8     LC_MONETARY=en_AU.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=en_AU.UTF-8    LC_PAPER=en_AU.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] shinyjs_1.0.1.9004 shiny_1.4.0.2     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] compiler_3.6.1  fastmap_1.0.0   magrittr_1.5    R6_2.2.2        promises_1.1.0  later_1.0.0     htmltools_0.4.0 tools_3.6.1     Rcpp_1.0.0      digest_0.6.21   xtable_1.8-2    httpuv_1.5.2   
[13] mime_0.5        rlang_0.4.4   
```

### Example application

```R
shinyApp(
    ui = shiny::basicPage(
        shiny::basicPage(
            shinyjs::useShinyjs(),
            actionButton("button", "click me"),
            textOutput("outsideModal")
        )
    ),
    server = function(input, output) {
        x <- reactiveVal(0)
        getX <- reactive({
            Sys.sleep(4)
            x()
        })
        
        observeEvent(input$button, {
            x(x() + 1)
            showModal(modalDialog(textOutput("insideModal")))
        })
        
        output$insideModal <- renderText({
            getX()
        })
        output$outsideModal <- renderText({
            getX()
        })
        
        shinyjs::runjs("
                   $(document).on('shiny:outputinvalidated', function(event) {console.log(new Date().getSeconds() + 's shiny:outputinvalidated ' + event.target.id);});
                   $(document).on('shiny:recalculating', function(event) {console.log(new Date().getSeconds() + 's shiny:recalculating ' + event.target.id);});
                   $(document).on('shiny:recalculated', function(event) {console.log(new Date().getSeconds() + 's shiny:recalculated ' + event.target.id);});
                   $(document).on('shiny:value', function(event) {console.log(new Date().getSeconds() + 's shiny:value ' + event.target.id);});
                   ")
    }
)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
There's an issue where certain shiny events are not called on outputs within modals. If you run the above app, you'll see that when you open the modal, the output outside the modal is processed correctly, but the for output inside the module a `shiny:outputinvalidated` never occurs. Additionally, the `shiny:recalculating` and `shiny:recalculated` events for the output inside the modal don't seem to be called at the correct time, and the div corresponding to the output inside the modal never has the `recalculating` class added, and hence is never greyed out.

After clicking the button, the javascript console output looks something like this:
```
3s shiny:outputinvalidated outsideModal
3s shiny:recalculating outsideModal
7s shiny:recalculated outsideModal
7s shiny:value outsideModal
7s shiny:recalculating insideModal
7s shiny:recalculated insideModal
7s shiny:value insideModal
```

I would expect the events for the output inside the modal to look like those for the output outside the modal. When you open a modal it displays the old value (not greyed out) and then instantly replaces it with the new value when it's ready, which can create problems when the UI is more complex.  In this example, I would expect the modal to open immediately, and the insideModal output to be greyed out while the new value is calculated. Additionally, packages like `shinycssloaders` don't work correctly inside modals, as they rely on the `shiny:outputinvalidated` event.

I'm not actually sure how to deal with the problem, as the modal content (and hence the html for the output inside the modal) are not in the DOM when the modal is not open. If there's a workaround that would be helpful.

title: We should be able to overwrite the bootstrap stylesheet
description:
Quite often when using a bootstrap theme css and reading it into shiny with `theme = boostrap.css`, I find styles being overwritten by the default bootstrap stylesheet. It would be great if we could avoid conflicts between the stylesheets altogether by allowing an option to replace the default stylesheet with the stylesheet set in `theme`. 

It might go something like:
```
ui <- fluidPage(class='p-0',  theme = "cosmo-bootstrap.min.css",
                           replace = TRUE
```

title: 'shiny-bound-input' class automatically added to custom Shiny input html improperly
description:
Hi, I first asked this in this RStudio community forum [post](https://community.rstudio.com/t/prevent-shiny-bound-input-class-from-being-automatically-added-to-custom-input-tag/54831) since I do not think it is necessarily a bug but rather by design- but it does have problematic unanticipated consequences. It doesn't feel like a feature request either. But it was suggested that I file an issue here. For web accessibility reasons the custom Shiny input widgets I create need to meet certain requirements. Specifically, I have cases where I need to have unique `id` attributes for `` tags within a larger Shiny input HTML block. For example, ```
mylabel
``` The `inputId` of the Shiny widget is `myid` in the `fieldset` tag. Notice each individual checkbox within has an id. The problem seems to be that as soon as I give an input tag an id attribute, Shiny appends the `shiny-bound-input` class to it. So when the above widget is rendered in the browser by Shiny, it not only adds that class to the top level alongside `myid`, but also to each individual checkbox within. So a custom Shiny input like above with five options will end up with `class="shiny-bound-input"` appended in six places. I need a way to prevent these additional class additions. It doesn't happen if I remove their id attributes, but I need to have the ids. Is there a recommended way I can prevent or override this class appending behavior? The explicit and unambiguous id pairing is critical.

title: remember state option for inputs
description:
When I create shiny apps, I frequently have inputs that show up in modals or conditional panels. They work just fine, except that if the user reopens the modal multiple times, the inputs "forget" the value that was chosen for them the previous time. Sometimes this is advantageous, but other times it's annoying. Can someone add an argument for the various input types that would allow them to "remember" the value of the previous time they were selected? Take this example where the user presses a button to select a species by which to filter the `iris` dataset. 

```
# server code
# deploy modal after UI input "selectspeciesbutton" is pushed
observeEvent(input$selectspeciesbutton, {
    showModal(
      modalDialog(
        title = "Pick a species",
        selectInput("species", 
                           "Select a species", 
                           c("Pick one..." = "", unique(iris$Species)),
        footer = tagList(
          modalButton("Cancel"),
          actionButton("speciesok","Ok")
        )
      )
    )
  })

  #Check data after ok button is pushed.
  observeEvent(input$speciesok, {
    if (isTruthy(input$species) {
        showNotification(type = "message", HTML("Species chosen correctly"))
        removeModal()
    } else {
        showNotification(type = "warning", HTML("No species chosen, try again"))
    }
  })

  irisfiltered <- reactive({
      filter(iris, Species == input$species)
  })
```
This is problematic because if the user presses the button a second time, the `selectInput` overwrites the user's previous choice, and forces a warning if the user just hits "Ok" a second time.

This could be fixed by adding the following argument to `selectInput`.
```
selected = if (isTruthy(input$species)) input$species else NULL
```
However, this gets pretty tedious when you have a lot of inputs. 

Ideally, there would be an argument called "remember" or "save.state" or whatever, that would look something like this
```
selectInput("species", 
                   "Select a species", 
                   c("Pick one..." = "", unique(iris$Species),
                   remember = TRUE)
```
This would pre-select the server-stored value for this input, if there is one. In the case where `remember = TRUE` and `selected` is not `NULL`, `selected` would be used if there is not a value for the input, but otherwise, the previously-chosen value would override the value of `selected`. In other words, something like:
```
if (remember) {
    selected <- if (isTruthy(input[[inputId]])) input[[inputId]] else selected
}
```

For backwards compatibility, `remember` should default to `FALSE`.

title: bidirectional synchronization triggers back and forth fight between transactions
description:
### System details

Browser Version: Chrome 80.0.3987.116 on macOS.

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 3.5.3 (2019-03-11)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS Mojave 10.14.6

Matrix products: default
BLAS: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/lib/libRblas.0.dylib
LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib

locale:
[1] en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8/C/en_GB.UTF-8/en_GB.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] compiler_3.5.3
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
AppModel <- function() {
  self <- reactiveValues(
      name = NULL
    )

  return(self)
}

AppModel_checkCompleteness <- function(self) {
    incomplete <- list(
      name = NULL
    )

    if (is.null(self$name) || stringr::str_length(stringr::str_trim(self$name)) == 0) {
      incomplete$name <- "You have not specified your name"
    }

    return(incomplete)
}


ui <- function() {
  view <- wellPanel(
    textInput(
      "nameText",
      "Your name and surname"),
    uiOutput("checklistUi"),
  )
  return(view)
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {                                              
  app_model <- AppModel()                                                                 
                                                                                          
  output$checklistUi <- renderUI({                                                        
    # Important. must be slow.
    Sys.sleep(2)                                                                          
                                                                                          
    completion_widget <- "Hello"                                                          
                                                                                          
    completed <- AppModel_checkCompleteness(app_model)                                    
                                                                                          
    return(completion_widget)                                                             
  })                                                                                      
                                                                                          
  observeEvent({input$nameText},                                                          
  {                                                                                       
    app_model$name <- input$nameText                                                      
  })                                                                                      
                                                                                          
  observeEvent({app_model$name},                                                          
  {                                                                                       
    updateTextInput(session, "nameText", value = app_model$name)                          
  })                                                                                      
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

The problem occurs when bidirectional synchronization between a model and a UI element is needed (e.g. one has to reload model data from the disk, but also allow the user to modify it) _and_ the transaction is slow. More details can be found [on this post on the Shiny help forum](https://community.rstudio.com/t/bi-directional-synchronization-without-triggering-a-loop/54195).

The problem happens when the textinput ui is modified by the user, then modified again _before_ the transaction to update the UI is completed. Taking a look at the websocket traffic, it's evident that during the second modification, a new request is sent to the server.

Later, the server replies to the first request, but this reply also contains, in the inputMessages field, the old value for the textinput. This sets the textinput to the old value, which generates a new request before the server has replied to now the second. This starts a cycle of bouncing back and forth between the two requests.

In my opinion, this is a bug that occurs because the frontend is sending a second request before the first transaction is completed. The UI should not accept any input until the current in-progress transaction goes back from busy to idle.

title: Allow Shiny modules to surface .Deprecate more gracefully
description:
I had a function for Shiny modules that migrated to a new version, and used `.Deprecate` as usual for other functions to point at the new version - however when the function is called in a Shiny module the usual surfacing of the deprecation method is not seen by the user, and the text of the deprecation message is attempted to be used by Shiny as a function which causes confusion. 

e.g.

In `googleAuthR` version > 1.0.0 , `googleAuth_js` was deprecated for `gar_auth_js`, but when calling the older function the error was a confusing one, and didn't point to the new function:

title: Updating selection of server-side selectize input with >1000 choices fails
description:
I have a shiny app containing a server-side selectize input with a long list (>10k) of choices. I would like to update the selection upon clicking a button. Here is a reproducible example

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton('buttonid','Button'),

  selectizeInput("listid", "A long list", choices = NULL)
  )

server <- function(input, output, session) 
  {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, "listid", choices = paste("Item", 1:10000), server = T)
  observeEvent(input$buttonid,
               {
               updateSelectizeInput(session, "listid", selected = "Item 1234")
               })
  }

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

The above code results in a blank selection when I press the button. However, if I search for "Item 1234", then change the selection, and press the button, now the item gets selected.

Also, trying to select an item between Item 1 and 1000 does not give problems, presumably because 1000 items get loaded at the beginning.

This seems akin to this old bug https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1018

title: fileUpload.R -> uploaded files don't have a unique filename
description:
I'm having trouble with the bookmark option, when multiple files are uploaded.

When files are uploaded they all get the same name assigned to them:
filename <- file.path(.dir, paste0(as.character(length(.files$name)), maybeGetExtension(fileBasename)))

When using the bookmark option in shiny, it will overwrite those files, because they have been assigned the same name on upload. This can be avoided by giving uploaded files a unique name (id):
filename <- file.path(.dir, paste0(as.character(createUniqueId(10)), maybeGetExtension(fileBasename)))

I used this fix myself and it solves the problem, but it would be nice to have it implemented into the real shiny package!

title: runTests() doesn't source app.R before running tests
description:
I noticed while working on https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/pull/2 that `shiny::runTests()` doesn't source `app.R` before sourcing files in `tests/`.

It only sources files in `R/` (if there are any), `globals.R` and `server.R`, depending on the value of `shiny.autoload.r`.

This is problematic if your app consists only of an `app.R`, but your `app.R` contains functions (or module functions) that you wish to test.

I think we should source `app.R` after any files in `R/`, but I'm open to suggestions about how we should handle the presence of `app.R` combined with the presence of `server.R`/`globals.R`. I figure at a minimum we should signal a warning.

title: Add `$click()` method to MockSession
description:
`MockSession` exposes a `setInputs()` method that can be used to programmatically set inputs, but we don't offer an easy way to click an action button programmatically without an understanding of the way button inputs transition from NULL to 0 first click and increase monotonically thereafter.

I propose a new`$click()` method on MockSession that accepts a character vector of actionButton input names and "clicks" them, internally handling value transitions.

title: onSessionEnded callback can be executed by next running app
description:
The following app displays the value of `x` and has a button that will stop the app.  The value of `x` gets initialized by the `onStart` function. There's an `onSessionEnded` callback which increments `x`.

We'd expect the app to display `x: 1` each time it runs.

```R
library(shiny)

x <- NULL
app <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(
    textOutput("txt"),
    actionButton("close", "Close app")
  ),
  function(input, output) {
    output$txt <- renderText({
      paste0("x: ", x)
    })
    
    observeEvent(input$close, {
      message("close button was clicked")
      stopApp("close button")
    })

    onSessionEnded(function() {
      message("Executing onSessionEnded callback.")
      x <<- x + 1
    })
  },
  onStart = function() {
    x <<- 1
  }
)
```

When you run it like this, with one `runApp` after the other -- without letting control go to the console -- the app displays `x: 1` on the first run, and then `x: 2` on the second. Also note the strange order that the diagnostic messages are printed out:

```R
{
  runApp(app)
  runApp(app)
}
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7789
#> close button was clicked
#> 
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7789
#> Executing onSessionEnded callback.
#> close button was clicked
#> [1] "close button"
#> Executing onSessionEnded callback.
```


Adding some `run_now()` calls in between makes it display `x: 1` both times.

```R
{
  runApp(app)
  for (i in 1:10) later::run_now()
  runApp(app)
}
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7789
#> close button was clicked
#> Executing onSessionEnded callback.
#> 
#> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7789
#> close button was clicked
#> [1] "close button"
#> Executing onSessionEnded callback.
```


The problem seems to be that, without the `run_now()` calls after the first app, the `onSessionEnded` callback can bleed into the next app.

cc @schloerke

title: snapshotPreprocessOutput: improve error handling?
description:
Shiny offers the `snapshotPreprocessOutput` function to preprocess the output of render functions. This works fine if the render function outputs as intended. If the render function returns an error (such as when `shiny::req()` is used), package authors may not realize this value gets passed directly to the preprocessOutput function.

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/c332c051f33fe325f6c2e75426daaabb6366d50a/R/snapshot.R#L10-L19
I suggest to simply adapt the documentation to say
```
#' @param fun A function that takes the output value from the render function
#' (either the intended output or an error) as an input and returns a
#'   modified value. The returned value will be used for the test snapshot.
```

Even within shiny itself, code does not consider the possibility that `output` may be a silent error instead of the intended value: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/5828ea74263d2b374d5284810e342e80d3470cf4/R/shinywrappers.R#L663-L670
See also https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/issues/1685



Furthermore, an error in a single `preprocessOutput` should probably not result in a cryptic 500 error when requesting `shinytest` output.
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/89be4bdce9dce6f8042087ce6ece0763eb8bb10c/R/shiny.R#L519-L526

# Examples
Gist app.R file: https://gist.github.com/rfaelens/a37898ec1614a0751fbd0a763d25dc59

Shinytest file
```
library(shinytest)

app <- ShinyDriver$new(path="myApp/")
cat(app$.__enclos_env__$private$getTestSnapshotUrl() )
app$getAllValues()

app$setInputs(`go_plot`=FALSE) #this fails...
app$getAllValues()

app$setInputs(`go_plot`=TRUE) # aaand we are back
app$getAllValues()

app$setInputs(`go_table`=FALSE) # this fails...
app$getAllValues()

app$setInputs(`go_table`=TRUE) #aaand we are back
app$getAllValues()
```

title: Path for js resources not recognized when serving Rmd file in a sub-directory
description:
I'm having difficulty serving Rmd files when the file is placed in a subdirectory rather than the main directory of the server.  The problem seems to be that the javascript and other resources (e.g., `shiny.min.js`) are not being loaded (returning 404 errors) and thus the page won't run.

Thus:
https://pluto.coe.fsu.edu/rdemos/NormalCalculator.Rmd
works fine, but
https://pluto.coe.fsu.edu/IntroStats/Correlation.Rmd does not.


### System details
RHEL 7.5, Apache 2.4.6
I'm redirecting the rdemos URL to shiny with Apache.
R version 3.6.0, Shiny version 1.4.0
Browser Version: <!-- If applicable -->

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
Error in sessioninfo() : could not find function "sessioninfo"
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

See the two URLs above.  These are publicly available.

The steps would be to create a subdirectory under the shiny-server directory on the host machine, and then copy a Rmd file (e.g., index.Rmd) into that subdirectory.  The Rmd file renders correctly at the top level, but not in a lower level.

### Describe the problem in detail

The problem is that when loading shared resource files, e.g., `shiny.min.js`, the sever returns a 404 error instead of the file.  In particular, if the Rmd file is in the XXX subdirectory, then the browser expands "shared/shiny.min.js" as ".../XXX/shared/shiny.min.js".  This then returns a not-found.

I'm calling this an error under shiny not shiny-server as I've tracked the issue down into the shiny package and not the server code.  

I think the issue is in resourcePathHandler(), as I think that "XXX/shared/shiny.min.js" needs to be remapped to "shared/shiny.min.js", but this is not happening for some reason.

I'm kind of stuck as I'm not sure how to debug further than I've gotten.

title: brushedPoints includes points not shown on plot
description:
Points returned by `brushedPoints` can include some that are not shown on the plot, e.g., if they are excluded by `xlim` (which leaves some blank space at the edges of the plot where there could be "invisible points"). This could be counterintuitive, and might mean that the `clip` option in `brushOpts` is not working.

[Brief discussion on RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/brushedpoints-includes-points-not-shown-in-plot/47985)

R 3.6.1
Shiny 1.4.0
RStudio 1.2.5019
Windows

Example code. To reproduce the problem, use the slider to change the `xlim` such that a point is just excluded, then brush displayed points and note the average. Finally, extend the brushed range outside the `xlim` range such that it covers one of the excluded points and note that the average value changes.

```
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

df <- mtcars

ui <- fluidPage(
  plotOutput('plot',brush=brushOpts(id="plot_brush",direction="x")),
  fluidRow(
    column(6,
           sliderInput("range", label="Range", min = 0, 
                       max = max(df$wt), value = c(0, max(df$wt)))
    ),
    column(6,
           tableOutput("brush_info")
    )  
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(df,aes(x=wt,y=mpg)) +
      geom_point() +
      xlim(input$range)
  })
  output$brush_info <- renderTable({
    brushedPoints(df,input$plot_brush) %>% summarize_at(vars(mpg),mean)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

description:
It's possible to support inline markdown in a limited sense: https://tailrecursion.com/wondr/posts/shiny-inline-markdown.html

@hadley suggested adding something like it to Shiny on Twitter: https://twitter.com/hadleywickham/status/1208110661533876258

It's definitely nice to be able to write prose in markdown in an app without needing a separate markdown file, but there are a few things we'd need to address before adding to Shiny:

1. Indentation
    - R doesn't have multiline string syntax
    - Markdown is sensitive to leading whitespace (code blocks)
    - The proof-of-concept on my blog works by removing leading whitespace by regex, so code blocks are impossible to write unless every line of the string starts at the beginning of every line, but that looks really weird if the string is nested in other tags.
    - Maybe there's some trick to making a multiline string operator in R that I just don't know?
        - __Hadley pointed out [glue::trim()](https://glue.tidyverse.org/reference/trim.html) in comments__
    - On Windows newlines are `\r\n`, so if we go the regex route, the replacement behavior would have to be based on the format of the source file. Considering files on Windows being edited in RStudio might have Unix line endings, this doesn't seem like it would be as straightforward as checking the current platform.
1. Need to promote`markdown` from `Suggests` to `Imports`
    - __Maybe use [commonmark](https://github.com/jeroen/commonmark) instead of markdown per Hadley in comments__

title: throttle and debounce are broken on master (ok on CRAN)
description:
I think `debounce()` and `throttle()` are broken as of https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/e84beffee39d540d3e891faafb9f333af32deca4.

Here's a reprex, taken from the [docs](https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/1.4.0/debounce.html):

```
library(shiny)
library(magrittr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  plotOutput("plot", click = clickOpts("hover")),
  helpText("Quickly click on the plot above, while watching the result table below:"),
  tableOutput("result")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  hover <- reactive({
    if (is.null(input$hover))
      list(x = NA, y = NA)
    else
      input$hover
  })
  hover_d <- hover %>% debounce(1000)
  hover_t <- hover %>% throttle(1000)

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    plot(cars)
  })

  output$result <- renderTable({
    data.frame(
      mode = c("raw", "throttle", "debounce"),
      x = c(hover()$x, hover_t()$x, hover_d()$x),
      y = c(hover()$y, hover_t()$y, hover_d()$y)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
}

```

With CRAN (1.4.0) (`install.packages('shiny)`), the throttled/debounced coordinates "lag behind", as expected.

With `master` (`remotes::install_github('rstudio/shiny'), the throttled/debounced coordinates are in near-perfect sync with the unthrottled coordinates. 
The remaining lag is probably just shiny at work, and in any case, does not change when `millis` is changed.

In my usage outside of the reprex, it seemed that for the *first* invalidation, the throttle/debounce is respected, but not for any later ones.
Can't reproduce that behavior in the reprex, probably because the first click is so fast.
Perhaps this helpful in debugging.

  NULL

  moduleUI('test')
)

  callModule(moduleServer, 'test')

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```r

shiny::runApp()

Editing the "changeLabel" in `selectInput()` does refresh the Shiny application but "changeLabel" does not change at all.

description:
### System details

Browser Version: <!-- If applicable -->

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 3.6.0 (2019-04-26)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS Mojave 10.14.6

Matrix products: default
BLAS:   /System/Library/Frameworks/Accelerate.framework/Versions/A/Frameworks/vecLib.framework/Versions/A/libBLAS.dylib
LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.6/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] shiny_1.3.2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] compiler_3.6.0  magrittr_1.5    R6_2.4.1        promises_1.1.0  later_0.8.0     htmltools_0.3.6 tools_3.6.0    
 [8] rstudioapi_0.10 crayon_1.3.4    Rcpp_1.0.3      jsonlite_1.6    digest_0.6.20   xtable_1.8-4    httpuv_1.5.2   
[15] mime_0.7        rlang_0.4.0 
```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("set_cache", "set cache"),
  actionButton("get_cache", "get cache"),
  p("The content of the cache"),
  verbatimTextOutput("the_cache_content"),
  p("The modified time ($mtime) of the cache"),
  verbatimTextOutput("modified_time"),
  p("Age of the cache in seconds"),
  verbatimTextOutput("age_of_cache")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  cache <- diskCache(dir = ".", max_age = 30)
  
  observeEvent(input$set_cache, {
    cache$set(key = "dttm", value = Sys.time())
  })
  
  retrieved_cache <- eventReactive(input$get_cache, {
    cache$prune()
    cache$get(key = "dttm")
  })
  
  output$the_cache_content <- renderText({
    retrieved_cache()
    as.character(retrieved_cache())
  })
  
  output$modified_time <- renderText({
    retrieved_cache()
    as.character(file.info("dttm.rds")$mtime)
  })
  
  output$age_of_cache <- renderText({
    retrieved_cache()
    invalidateLater(1000, session)
    difftime(Sys.time(), as.POSIXct(file.info("dttm.rds")$mtime))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail

Using `shiny::diskCache()` I was very confused to see that the cache updated erratically. 
In the example above, the cache is supposedly invalidated every 30 seconds, but this doesn't happen unless neither the "set cache" and "get cache" buttons are touched during 30 seconds. 

When "get cache" is pressed, the `$mtime` of the file is reset, thus the pruning only works in reference to the last time the `rds` object is retrieved, not when the `rds` object was set. 

Checking https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/cache-disk.R it seems obvious that this is caused by the lines
```
  if (private$evict == "lru"){
            Sys.setFileTime(filename, Sys.time())
          }
```
Indeed, if in the example above the cache is defined as 
```
cache <- diskCache(dir = ".", max_age = 30, evict = "fifo")
```
It works as expected. 

As seen, `max_age` and the default `evict` do not work well with each other, and this is detrimental for user cases where `max_age` is more important than `max_size`. Perhaps the solution is as simple as making the default evict policy as `fifo`?

title: Feature request: Allow insertTab() to insert at first/last position without specifying `target`
description:
Currently `insertTab()` requires specifying whether the new tab should be added before or after a specific `target` tab. There are two issues with this approach:

1. If I simply want to add a new tab at the beginning or end, it makes it harder to do this when dealing with dynamic tabs that are added/deleted because I must keep track of which tabs exist and in what order. I would want to be able to just say "add this tab at the beginning or end".

2. The current approach makes it impossible to start adding tabs to an empty tabsetpanel. If I want the user to dynamically create tabs from scratch, I cannot add the first tab because there is no existing "target"

My specific question was already kindly answered by @wch in #2693. However, it raised an issue around selectize/selectize.js#129 filtering duplicate `choices` without giving the user a `warning` or `message` indicating that it's doing so. 

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
library(shiny)

carrier_choices <- list(
  `Page Plus Cellular (Verizon)` = "number@vzwpix.com",
  `Verizon Wireless` = "number@vzwpix.com"
)
ui <- function(id){
  fluidPage(
    selectInput("b1_carrier", "Carrier", choices = carrier_choices)
  )
}

server <- function(input, output, session) { }
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### Describe the problem in detail
Note that only the first item shows up because there are duplicate `values`. If there's a way to warn the developer of this behavior that would probably save them the time trying to figure out where their `choices` went in a large choice set! 😖

Updating Websocket library to follow HTTP REDIRECT
description:
Hi Shiny development team. First, thanks for the awesome work.

Shiny uses [websocket-driver](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/f85479ba11e49dc21b2f06f2e84e0a228b5639f7/tools/yarn.lock#L2369) node module for Websocket functionality. This library does not seem to support HTTP REDIRECTs (301 or 302). Is it possible to switch to a different websocket library that does support following HTTP REDIRECTs? For example https://github.com/websockets/ws recently [added support](https://github.com/websockets/ws/pull/1490/files) for this. This library seems to be more active and better maintained compared to websocket-driver. 

If maintainers think this is an option, and don't see any major blockers, we would be happy to submit a patch. Also if you have alternative suggestions, we would love to hear.

**Use case**
We are working to enabling developing and viewing Shiny applications on a remote instance that is being accessed using a Jetty HTTP proxy. The Jetty handler for websocket proxying is under a different end-point than the HTTP proxy. So the proxy will send a redirect response (302) to upgrade request that Shiny sends. We were hoping Shiny would follow the redirect.

title: Event Handler Metrics Collection
description:
When running R Shiny applications in production it would be extremely valuable if it is possible to easily collect the performance of all event handlers. When applications start using dozens (or perhaps hundreds) of observe(Events) and (event)Reactives it becomes hard to track how all these different elements perform. 

I propose that, if event handlers are assigned to a variable as below:

`
example <- observeEvent(input$trigger, {
  interestingFunction()
})
`

`example` may then be assigned performance information on every request by input$trigger. Perhaps the simplest and most interesting piece of information would be the time it takes to finish `handlerExpr`. I understand that when an event handler is triggered often that performance information collection may introduce a performance decrease, therefore we could make this feature opt-in only. 

Furthermore, the performance data does not have to be stored in the `example` variable, but might instead be written to a csv file (for example). Writing performance data to a csv would easily allow developers to write to another (persistent) data storage solution of their choice using `session$onSessionEnded()`.

If we structure this data collection well, it may be quite trivial to create a library or Shiny function that structures the collected data and shows a performance overview as you typically see when monitoring APIs. 

Perhaps this feature already exists, if not, how much work would be involved in creating such performance collection? I would be happy giving it a first shot if I could get some pointers on crucial pieces of the Shiny code base. 

Best regards,

Michael Hogers

For example, you could imagine implementing a wizard by having next and previous action buttons that adjusted the active tab.

description:
# Introduction of the issue : binding events

- My events example pasted in firefox debug console work with shiny 1.1 and shiny 1.4.
- The same events are  binded by `$(document).on('shiny:inputchanged',..)` with shiny_1.1.0
- The same events are __not__ binded by `$(document).on('shiny:inputchanged',..)` with shiny_1.4.0

I write the issue on my Windows computer at home with R 3.4, but I've discovered the initial issue on Linux Ubuntu at work with R 3.6.

# Test

## test of current reprex 

Go to every column search input and focus : the width of the current input search will grow (for shiny 1.1 and not for 1.4).

_Please modify `largeur_saisie_min` (=input width min) if your screen is too large to see the grow. Or add many columns like a real case._

## 2nd test not in this reprex but in the link which I talk below

Go to every __integer or numeric__ column search input and focus and type `$1` it will be replaced by `1...1` in the current input (for shiny 1.1 and not for 1.4)

# Expectation

To be able to bind all similar input of the __DOM document__.

# Context of recent update about `shiny:inputchanged`

I've read #1596 and #2442, #2446 the changes about `shiny:inputchanged` in News:  
> The shiny:inputchanged JavaScript event now triggers on the related input element instead of document. __Existing event listeners bound to document will still detect the event due to event bubbling__.

Except If I didn't understand the second sentence, binding events doesn't work anymore with `DOM document` (in my example of similar input in all of my application). 

Or the guidelines about binding events have changed even for `DOM document`.

_edit : (I have an 2nd example of event, [there in DT](https://github.com/rstudio/DT/issues/569#issuecomment-471767523) not written here,  and it's the same issue : it works with shiny 1.1 and not not with shiny 1.4. title: Option to start the shiny app in a separate R session with RStudio runApp, just like Knitting Rmd
description:
This is related to #2034 (which want to start shiny app in local env and don't pollute global env), but considering shiny app itself need to have its own global environment, I think the better approach is to start the shiny in a separate R session.

I often need to prepare some data for shiny app use, and it happened more than once that the app used some variable in global env thus worked normal, but failed in deployed mode because the data was not imported in the app itself yet. This kind of problem can be revealed immediately and fixed easier if the app start in a clean environment. It's simply impractical to clean up session in every test run of shiny app, because I need to continue to work with the data in global env.

I think in general a shiny app is intended to be deployed and using some independent environment, just like knitr by default knit the RMD in a clean session. Thus it make senses use similar strategy with starting shiny app in RStudio.

title: Register Shiny JavaScript methods earlier in the life-cycle
description:
Some of Shiny's JavaScript methods (e.g., `Shiny.setInputValue`) are registered when `initShiny` executes, which is scheduled here:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/89bd7e90117b5ed0c99987d81c8ec8b51a3305c1/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L511-L515

This implies that, when htmlwidget(s) are statically rendered in Shiny, `HTMLWidgets.staticRender()` executes one tick before `initShiny()`, which means those JS methods aren't available when the user-defined `renderValue()` method executes. Some widgets, like leaflet, are privy to this and schedule relevant methods (those which reference Shiny's methods) to execute one tick later, but widget authors shouldn't be expected to know this:

https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/blob/18ec9817cf3261ed3cc0aa5d0d030d6c36ba0667/javascript/src/index.js#L266-L268

In other words, instead of delaying the method registration that happens `initShiny`, it should probably happen right away (when Shiny is loaded)

title: Bookmarking: Support for for a way to not automatically save input values
description:
Right now, bookmarking works on an opt-out basis: all inputs are saved, and if there are any inputs I don't want to save then I have to use the `setBookmarkExclude()` function to specify the inputs I don't wish to save. This generally works well and is definitely the best default behaviour.

But there are cases when I want to have complete control over what gets saved/restored, and I don't want it to be all the inputs. I would prefer to have a way to work in an opt-in basis (specify which inputs to save) rather than an opt-out basis (specifying which inputs to exclude).

For instance, if I'm working with a lot of complex dynamic UI, I already have to use custom bookmark/restore code to re-create the dynamic UI. Having shiny automatically save all inputs is proving to be an annoyance, because I'm already taking care of populating the inputs on initialization, and I have to make sure exclude all the buttons so that they won't appear as pressed when initialized.

I realize this is not a great description and there is no code sample so it might not be immediately clear what I mean. I can provide more info if requested.

title: Statically rendered htmlwidgets in Shiny don't have access to Shiny methods registered in initShiny
description:
(This issue surfaced in light of research done for https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2630.)

**The problem:** If _any_ htmlwidget is statically-rendered in shiny, it doesn't have access to the Shiny methods registered when `initShiny` executes (e.g., [Shiny.setInputValue](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/02f7a4fdc9976b27e4a522c88c9d483421c46fec/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L104-L107))

```r
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

ui <- fluidPage(
  "Check your JS console...Shiny.setInputValue is undefined!",
  leaflet() %>%
    addTiles() %>%
    htmlwidgets::onRender("function(gd) { console.log(Shiny.setInputValue); }")
)

server <- function(input, output) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Long story short, this happens because [`initShiny` executes](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/02f7a4fdc9976b27e4a522c88c9d483421c46fec/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L511-L515) after [`HTMLWidgets.staticRender` executes](https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/blob/0ef5dd57237ec7bdb1afc22f9088343a2b037aa5/inst/www/htmlwidgets.js#L664-L689). Now, the input/output binding from `initShiny` should still likely happen _after_ `HTMLWidgets.staticRender` (to that elements dynamically inserted by user code has a chance to be discovered by shiny); however, the method registration that occurs in `initShiny` should occur _before_ `HTMLWidgets.staticRender`
