title: In some cases user-code may not have access to initShiny methods
description:
As of jQuery 3.0, [document-ready handlers are now asynchronous](https://jquery.com/upgrade-guide/3.0/#breaking-change-document-ready-handlers-are-now-asynchronous), which means it's possible for the methods in `initShiny` to not be available to downstream user-code because of this:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/02f7a4fdc9976b27e4a522c88c9d483421c46fec/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L511-L515

For a minimal example of where this becomes of problem:

```r
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
shinyApp(
  ui = leaflet() %>% addTiles(),
  server = function(input, output, session) {}
)
```

Before jQuery 3.0, `initShiny` would be called before leaflet's javascript executes; however, after jQuery 3.0, `initShiny` is called after leaflet's javascript, so not all of Shiny's methods (e.g., `onInputChange`) is not available to leaflet

title: reactiveValues inconsistent/unclear behaviour in regards to order of items
description:
The documentation of `reactiveValues` mentions that it functions similarly to a list. Lists, unlike sets, should preserve order based on the order in which items were added.

This does not seem to be the case with reactiveValues. There are a few interrelated issues here:

```
# initializing reactiveValues with b,a and then asking for the names, the names come back sorted
> rv <- reactiveValues(b="b", a="a")
> names(rv)
[1] "a" "b"

# initializing a reactiveValues and only adding the items afterwards has the same behaviour
> rv <- reactiveValues(); rv$b <- "b"; rv$a <- "a"
> names(rv)
[1] "a" "b"

# BUT doing the same with a list, the order is preserved
> li <- list(b="b", a="a")
> names(li)
[1] "b" "a"

# converting to a list also doesn't keep the order
> str(reactiveValuesToList(rv))
List of 2
 $ a: chr "a"
 $ b: chr "b"
```

That's one issue. But it gets worse, because (as far as I can tell) this behaviour doesn't simply sort by alphabet, I can't tell how to predict the result, so to me it seems inconsistent. If instead of "b","a" I use "foo","bar", I get different results:

```
# asking for the names still returns them in alphabetical instead of chronological order
> rv <- reactiveValues(foo="foo", bar="bar")
> names(rv)
[1] "bar" "foo"

# BUT converting to a list now does return the original order (when using b,a in the previous example, it did not)
> str(reactiveValuesToList(rv))
List of 2
 $ foo: chr "foo"
 $ bar: chr "bar"
```

I tried running more complex experiments and couldn't find a pattern - when I add multiple items, they seem to be returned in a random order.

There doesn't seem to be a way to know in what order the items will come back out of a reactiveValues object.

description:
### System details

Browser Version: Not relevant / serverside issue

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```

Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin15.6.0 (64-bit)
Running under: macOS High Sierra 10.13.6

Matrix products: default

LAPACK: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.6/Resources/lib/libRlapack.dylib

locale:
[1] en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8/C/en_US.UTF-8/en_US.UTF-8

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] shiny_1.3.2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] compiler_3.6.1  magrittr_1.5    R6_2.4.0        promises_1.0.1  later_0.8.0     htmltools_0.3.6
 [7] tools_3.6.1     yaml_2.2.0      Rcpp_1.0.2      jsonlite_1.6    digest_0.6.20   xtable_1.8-4   
[13] httpuv_1.5.1    mime_0.7        rlang_0.4.0  
```

### Example application
```R
library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    uiOutput('input')
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$input <- renderUI({numericInput("number", "Input", 10)})
    val <- reactive({req(input$number)})
    debounced <- debounce(val, 1000)
    observe({req(val()); print('val')}) # should print 'val' immidiately after rendering
    observe({req(debounced()); print('debounced')}) # should print 'debounce' 1s after rendering
  }
)

# Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7310
# [1] "val"
```

### Describe the problem in detail
`debounce` does not invalidate initial value if the reactive expression (or any of its reactive components) uses `req`.

### Workarounds
So far, I have 2 workarounds for this.

1. Replacing `req` with `is.null` checks
```r
val <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$number)) return(NULL) 
  input$number
})
```
This of course will only work if the `req` is in the reactive expression, not if it is in a reactive component. (for example `val <- reactive({req( module_output() )})`)

2. Catching the `shiny.silent.error` produced by `req` and converting it to `NULL`
```r
reactive({
  req2null <- tryCatch(module_output(), error = function(e) return(NULL))
  if (is.null(req2null())) return(NULL) 
  req2null()
})
```
Not sure if I missed anything.

title: Allow addCustomMessageHandler and session$sendCustomMessage to take no argument
description: I regularly create JS functions that do not take any argument, and right now `addCustomMessageHandler` and `session$sendCustomMessage` only allow to write function with arg. For example: ``` $( document ).ready(function() { Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('alerthis', function() { alert("this and that") }) }); ``` Throws an error: From : https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/e3c15493a2f79996314f9d60d6f4c479f2713b9e/srcjs/shinyapp.js#L479 Same goes for `session$sendCustomMessage` which requires the name of the function and an argument. Right now I'm bypassing that by adding `function(arg)` and `session$sendCustomMessage('alerthis', TRUE)`, but it feels a little bit useless to pass that. If I had to guess the rational behind this i'd say that it's because it's doing ``` sendCustomMessage = function(type, message) { data <- list() data[[type]] <- message private$sendMessage(custom = data) } ``` https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/cf330fcd58daa6c32e38387b7f82509ee75f760c/R/shiny.R#L1256 So type can't be null, as we are turning this to JSON here https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/cf330fcd58daa6c32e38387b7f82509ee75f760c/R/shiny.R#L400 I think either passing TRUE as the default, or `message = type` by default would allow to use function without argument in JS and in R. As in https://github.com/ColinFay/shiny/commit/0fd71fe144f2b4ba97bb78c873a1bdd29846c6d3 Let me know if you want me to PR this into shiny.

title: Error when updating slider value in PhantomJS
description:
When testing an app with shinytest (which uses) PhantomJS, the current master version of Shiny throws an error when setting the value of the slider. This started happening after we updated to jQuery 3 (#2557).

The error happens when ion.rangeSlider calls `.removeProp("tabindex")` here:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/ff5377da9e9c4fe904081b44a6d29e5703b43fe7/inst/www/shared/ionrangeslider/js/ion.rangeSlider.js#L1726

According to https://api.jquery.com/removeProp/ :
> With some built-in properties of a DOM element or window object, browsers may generate an error if an attempt is made to remove the property.

The `tabIndex` property is built-in, and most browsers apparently do not throw an error if you try to remove it, but PhantomJS does throw an error.

In the previous version of jQuery that we used (1.12.4), it wrapped the removal in a try-catch:
 https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/1.12.4/src/attributes/prop.js#L16-L26

However, in the current version that we're using (3.4.1), the try-catch is gone:
https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/3.4.1/src/attributes/prop.js#L18-L22


I think the solution is to modify our copy of ion.rangeSlider so that it wraps the `removeProp()` with a try-catch.

title: Bookmarking: use *only* key=value pairs in the URL
description:
Somewhat related to https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2297

Currently, when using URL-based bookmarking, the URL is of the form `url/?_inputs_&n=200` which is completely valid and legal, but it's a bit non standard to have `_inputs_` there as a standalone without an equals sign. Some applications, [such as auth0](https://github.com/curso-r/auth0/pull/38), add an equals sign when rewriting the URL (`url/?_inputs_=&n=200`). Adding that equals sign breaks bookmarking. It would be great if bookmarking didn't break from that, and even better if perhaps that would be the default URL.

  129: drawPlot
  115: <reactive:plotObj>
   99: drawReactive
   86: origRenderFunc
   85: output$plot
    5: runApp
    3: print.shiny.appobj
    1: source
```

I'd argue that this traceback is upside down, because it's easier to read "f calls g calls h" rather than "h is called by g is called by f", and I think there's some evidence that R users find the other direction easier to understand (and it's the direction we've standardised on in r-lib/tidyverse).

title: SelectInput crashes with unnamed one-dimensional chracter
description:
Commit 1a8b36f introduced a crash of `selectInput` when choices is a one-dimensional unnamed character vector. The `choicesWithNames` function in `R/input-utils.R` does not cover this case. 
`listify` recurses into lists so the check for length-1-unnamed-characters makes sense, but it does not cover the case where the original choices vector is a 1-dimensional-character.

title: [issue] reactive expression gets stuck for no apparent reason
description:
I have the following simple setup
 
    x1<-reactiveVal()
    x2<-reactiveVal()
    x3<-reactive({
       message("a")
       req(isolate(x1()))
       message("b")
       x2()
    })
    observe(x3())

The following sequence of interactions cause the `x3` expression to become stuck and not to respond to changes in `x2`.

First I flush the initialization events

    shiny:::flushReact()

This prints out "a" as expected. `x1` is `NULL` so the `req` fails silently and no "b" is printed out.

Then I change the value of `x2`

    x2(1)
    shiny:::flushReact()

This does not produce an output although I was expecting to see "a" printed out. This is very suspicious, but`x1` is `NULL` at this point, so in some sense it might be correct: besides the side effect of printing, executing `x3` will again fail silently.

Change the value of `x1`

    x1(2)
    shiny:::flushReact()

No output produced which is expected as `x3` does not depend on `x1`.

Again change the value of `x2`

    x2(3)
    shiny:::flushReact()

No output produced. At this point `x1` is not `NULL` and `x2` has changed, so I was expecting to see "a" and "b" printed out. The `x3` expression has become non-reactive.

Notice that rewriting the above to use `eventReactive` instead of `isolate`, makes the example work as intended and all output is as expected. 

It seems that the particular usage of `req` and `isolate` creates a situation in which `x3` is non-reactive. Either there is something particular about that usage that makes the example "quirky" (this has to be documented) or it seems that there is a bug.

title: ?shinyOptions should link to ?`shiny-options`
description:
Although these pages aren't really documenting the same thing, I think it's easy to land on `?shinyOptions` expecting to find documentation for shiny's various options, when what you really want is ?`shiny-options`.

Also, maybe it's worth considering merging these two into the same page

-->

### System details

Browser Version: Google Chrome Version 76.0.3809.87 (64-Bit)

Output of `sessionInfo()`:

```
R version 3.6.0 (2019-04-26)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

Matrix products: default

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] shiny_1.3.2

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] compiler_3.6.0  magrittr_1.5    R6_2.4.0        promises_1.0.1  later_0.8.0     htmltools_0.3.6 tools_3.6.0    
 [8] Rcpp_1.0.2      digest_0.6.20   xtable_1.8-4    httpuv_1.5.1    mime_0.7   
```

### Example application and steps to reproduce the problem

<!-- If you're able to create one, a reproducible example is extremely helpful to us. For instructions on how to create one, please see: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/wiki/Creating-a-Reproducible-Example --> 

```R
# Windows shell required
tempdir()
dir.exists(tempdir())

library(shiny)

shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage("Please reload to see me fail."),
    server = function(input, output) {
        shell(paste("rmdir", dQuote(
            normalizePath(tempdir(), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE), q = FALSE
        ), "/s /q"))
    }
)
```
![screen](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36849480/62448828-fcf66a00-b768-11e9-8f6a-b369cf3a723d.gif)
### Describe the problem in detail

I have already tried to get help via the [rstudio community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/shiny-app-unresponsive-after-r-sessions-tempdir-is-deleted/36507) and by reviving this [issue](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2421), where Dean Attali suggested using `tempdir(check = TRUE)`  in shiny's source code what seems reasonable to me, regarding the following:

I have a shiny app deployed locally via RScript.exe and `runApp` on a Windows machine which runs just fine. However, when the app is idling for a few days the browser displays the following:

![err](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36849480/62448755-c7ea1780-b768-11e9-98dd-b77e159ca9cd.PNG)

This is unrelated to the apps content.

I was able to generate a log file which gave me:
> Warning in file(open = "w+") :
>   cannot open file 'C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpO0mnd9\Rfdd88a66def': No such file or directory
> Warning: Error in file: cannot open the connection
>   [No stack trace available]

... and indeed the according folder generated on starting up the R session and the files generated on starting the shiny app were deleted (automatic cleaning done by Windows? - I'm not sure why).

I am able to reproduce this error when I'm intentionally deleting the R sessions `tempdir()` hosting the shiny app (as shown above).

It seems also others are affected: please see [this](https://community.rstudio.com/t/shiny-tmp-file-error/22043) and [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53152076/temp-files-automatically-deleted-in-r-shiny-app).

In my eyes it would be sufficient if the shiny application exits with an error in this situation instead of continuing to run in an unresponsive manner.

Adding an argument `tempDir` to `runApp()` (defaulting to `tempdir()`) would also be conceivable.

---

By now I've found a setting in Windows 10 (Storage Sense) concerning the deletion of temporary files, which seems to be active by default.

Navigate as follows and **uncheck**:

 1. Settings
 2. System Storage
 3. Storage Sense
 4. Change how we free up space automatically
 5. Delete temporary files that my apps aren't using

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36849480/62927285-81bf3480-bdb6-11e9-9baf-cf3e8a4afdc6.png)

Nevertheless, in my eyes this situation should be **prevented** in the shiny source code or the app creator should have the possibility to **specify where** the apps **temp files are stored** (without setting environment variables).

title: renderTable digit does not perform the same as xtable
description:
I have a table that I produced by xtable that I use in a report that has different significant digits for different row. I made use of assigning each element in the table with a digit value in a matrix. I tried using the same digit arguments in an xtable  arguement that is then sent to renderTable, but they seem to be ignored. In addition, when I out the digit arguments in the renderTable they appeared to be ignored and a default of 2 is applied everywhere

I am trying to reproduce the table interactively through R shiny but cannot because the digit option only takes a single value. Can you change the functionality in renderTable to reproduce what is used in the xtable environment?

title: Request: bookmarking with remote storage
description:
When using server-side bookmarking, the state of the app gets saved as an RDS file to the file system. There are cases where this would be almost a perfect solution, except you can't use the local file system for some reason (for example, when you're hosting on infrastructure that doesn't give you persistent local storage). For those cases, it would be great if you could specify your own place to save the RDS file to/load from.

From a very quick glance at the source code, I found that setting `shinyOptions(save.interface = mysave)` and `shinyOptions(load.interface = myload)` allows me to perform bookmarking from a custom directory. But I can only make it work with a directory on the local machine. It looks like it might be feasible to modify the bookmarking source code a little bit to also allow more flexibility to allow the user to save the file to a completely different medium as well, such as S3.

title: Dynamic includeHTML() with htmlwidgets
description: There seems to be a problem with using `includeHTML()` dynamically with htmlwidgets. Note that this non-dynamic approach works: ```r # also works with plotly::plot_ly() htmlwidgets::saveWidget(leaflet::leaflet(), "foo.html") ui <- fluidPage(includeHTML("foo.html")) srv <- function(input, output) {} shinyApp(ui, srv) ``` But the dynamic approach throws an error. I also tried this with plotly and DT and it throws the same error ```r ui <- fluidPage(htmlOutput("inc")) srv <- function(input, output) { output$inc <- renderUI(includeHTML("foo.html")) } shinyApp(ui, srv) ```

### Example application *or* steps to reproduce the problem

```R
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
    actionButton("create", "New"),
    div(id = "end")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    i <- 0
    observeEvent(input$create, {
        i <<- i + 1
        link_id <- paste0("link", i)
        observe(print(unclass(input[[link_id]])))
        insertUI("#end", ui = div(actionLink(link_id, "Link")))
    })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

#### Output

```
# App starts
# New is clicked
## NULL
## [1] 0
# New is clicked
## NULL
## [1] 0
# Link is clicked
## [1] 1
# Link is clicked
## [1] 2
```

### Describe the problem in detail

When the "New" button is clicked, an `actionLink()` is added via `insertUI()`, in addition to a new observer. This observer is fired twice -- once with `NULL` and another time with `0` in `input[[link_id]]` . (A non-dynamic app would add the `observe()` externally, I'm adding observers on the fly. When hard-coding the `observe()` outside the `observeEvent()`, the observer is triggered with `NULL` right away, and with `0` as soon as the "New" button is clicked.)

Is this behavior intended? I would expect that only the `NULL` event is triggered.

Trying to test this app using {shinytest} adds extraneous clicks.

title: Document and Allow specifying port range for random port selection
description:
It seems that Shiny chooses random ports from 3000-8000 for connections. Some possible improvements that would be desirable:

- document that this is the random port range
- allow specifying a different random port range
- some mechanism for determining if the port is available before it is selected?
- a way to exclude ports from the range

The context here is RStudio Server and users who want to be restrictive around which ports are accessible. Some documentation would be nice, and optional control over the process through a server or package-install specification would probably be ideal. 

I'm not sure what standards are for this type of thing... if an environment variable would be workable, etc.

Shiny gives error if named selectInput choices are a factor
description:
Selection inputs in Shiny allow you to provide a named vector of choices so that the names are shown to the user but the values are what are passed to input. It was designed for the choices to be a character vector, but it's easy to accidentally pass it a named factor vector. If you do you get an extremely confusing error.

It seems like selectInput should either:
* convert the vector from factor to character with as.character, or
* provide a more clear error.

Here is an example showing the issue.

Thanks!

```r

library(shiny)

choices <- letters

choices <- factor(choices) # comment this line out and the app works
# if the choices are a factor instead of character, shiny gives the error:
# Error in (function (choice, name)  : 
#   All sub-lists in "choices" must be named.

names(choices) <- LETTERS

ui <- fluidPage(selectInput("example", "Choose", choices))
server <- function(input, output) {}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: FR: add disabled argument to inputs
description:
It would be nice to be able to include a **disabled** attribute to some inputs like `numericInput`, `textInput`, `passwordInput` and `checkboxInput`.

I can set the attribute with some JavaScript or `shinyjs`, but it would be nice to have that option/argument by default.

Here's a short example using `shinyjs`:

```
library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

ui <- fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  actionButton("enab", "Enable Inputs"),
  actionButton("disa", "Disable Inputs"),
  numericInput("num", "Include a number", value = "", min = 1, 1000),
  textInput("text", "Caption", "Data Summary"),
  passwordInput("password", "Password:"),
  checkboxInput("check", "Some value", FALSE)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  isEnabled <- reactiveVal(TRUE)
  
  observeEvent(input$enab, {
    isEnabled(FALSE)
  })
  observeEvent(input$disa, {
    isEnabled(TRUE)
  })
  
  observe({
    shinyjs::runjs(HTML(paste0('document.getElementById("num").disabled = ',tolower(isEnabled()),'')))
    shinyjs::runjs(HTML(paste0('document.getElementById("text").disabled = ',tolower(isEnabled()),'')))
    shinyjs::runjs(HTML(paste0('document.getElementById("password").disabled = ',tolower(isEnabled()),'')))
    shinyjs::runjs(HTML(paste0('document.getElementById("check").disabled = ',tolower(isEnabled()),'')))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

          self$events[[name]] <- data
        }
      }
    }
  ),
  public = list(
    ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
    on = function(event, handler, input = FALSE, enabled = TRUE, init = FALSE, ...) {
      if (enabled) {
        if (is.null(private$handlers[[event]])) {
          private$handlers[[event]] <- list()
        }
        uuid <- uuid::UUIDgenerate()

            handler(self$input[[event]], self)
          }, observerName = uuid, ignoreInit = !init, ...)
        } else {
          self$createEvent(event)
          if (init) {
            #handler(NULL, self$id)
          }
          trigger <- function() {
            tryCatch({
              if (is.null(self$events[[event]])) {
                handler()
              } else {
                data <- self$events[[event]]
                handler(data$value, data$target)
              }
            }, error = function(e) {
              print(paste("MY_ERROR:  ", e))
              print(paste("throw", event, self$id))
              print(handler)
            })
          }
          observeEvent(self$events[[event]], {
            print(">> handler")
            trigger()
          })
        }

        private$handlers[[event]] <- append(private$handlers[[event]], list(
          list(
            handler = handler,
            uuid = uuid,
            observer = `if`(!is.null(observer), observer$observer)
          )
        ))
      }
    },
    ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
    broadcast = function(name, value = NULL, target = NULL, include.self = FALSE) {
      if (is.null(target)) {
        target <- self$id
      }
      if (include.self) {
        private$trigger(name, list(value = value, target = target))
      }
      lapply(self$children, function(child) {
        child$broadcast(name, value, self$id, include.self = TRUE)
      })
    },
    ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
    emit = function(name, value = NULL, target = NULL, include.self = FALSE) {
      if (is.null(target)) {
        target <- self$id
      }
      if (include.self) {
        private$trigger(name, list(value = value, target = target))
      }
      if (!is.null(self$parent)) {
        self$parent$emit(name, value, self$id, include.self = TRUE)
      }
    },
    ## ---------------------------------------------------------------
    createEvent = function(name, value = NULL) {
      if (!name %in% ls(self$events)) {
        #value <- paste0("__", name)
        #makeActiveBinding(name, env = self$events, fun = function(v) {

        ## this will not trigger handler on init because

        if (is.null(value)) {

        } else {
          data <- list(
            value = value,
            timestamp = as.numeric(Sys.time())*1000
          )
          self$events[[name]] <- data
        }
        makeReactiveBinding(name, self$events)
      }
    },
```

### Describe the problem in detail

the problem I have is this. Without any extra code I'm using this:

1. makeReactiveBinding() on self$events
2. observeEvent on self$events
3. update self$events value (by calling trigger from broadcast)

and observeEvent is not triggered. If I replace makeReactiveBinding with makeActiveBinding It works fine except I can't use `self$events$foo` to trigger update of `renderUI`.

What's wierd is that when I have:
```R
   x$broadcast("foo", include.self = TRUE)
   x$broadcast("foo", include.self = TRUE)
   x$children$y$emit("foo", include.self = TRUE)
```
emit trigger observeEvent but broadcast not, and trigger is called, the value is updated and it's changed and it's reactive.

I've asked about this here https://community.rstudio.com/t/makereactivebinding-dont-work-with-observeevent/32845 yesterday but it's more a bug then a question.

Is there any case when observeEvent is not triggered when activeValue change?
> (Note that "recalculate a value" does not generally count as performing an action--see eventReactive for that.)

from https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/1.0.3/observeEvent.html

So why observeEvent is not triggered? what is not an action and how can I force the action? Is this a bug or is there a work around on this?

title: add default (pre-reactivity) HTML content
description:
Typically, some of the dynamic-output (`uiOutput`, `htmlOutput`) elements take up zero space on instantiation and "pop out" when reactivity or requirements catch up. It may be preferred (from a UX standpoint) to have that space filled with something, both to keep the surrounding content stable as well as to (perhaps) hint at what will be coming into that spot. Obviously `shiny` cannot always know what that space looks like, but the author can easily provide a best-guess space-filler. For instance, if a module exports an icon that indicates (by color or icon, perhaps) the status of something. Typically, the setup would be: ```r shinyApp( ui = shinyUI( pageWithSidebar( headerPanel("Outputs"), sidebarPanel( "before", htmlOutput("statusicon"), "after" ), mainPanel() ) ), server = function(input, output, session) { output$statusicon <- renderUI({ Sys.sleep(1) icon("check-square") }) } ) ``` I suggest a helper-function that allows for default values: ```r #' @param func function for HTML rendering, such as htmlOutput #' @param ... arguments passed to the function defaultOutput <- function(expr, default = list()) { out <- force(expr) out$children <- htmltools::tags$div(default) out } shinyApp( ui = shinyUI( pageWithSidebar( headerPanel("Outputs"), sidebarPanel( "before", defaultOutput(htmlOutput("statusicon"), default = icon("square")), # <--- the only change "after" ), mainPanel() ) ), server = function(input, output, session) { output$statusicon <- renderUI({ Sys.sleep(1) icon("check-square") }) } ) ``` The rendered content seems straight-forward and consistent: ```r htmlOutput("statusicon") #
defaultOutput(htmlOutput, "statusicon", default = icon("square")) #
#
# #
#
``` This can be trivially extended to delayed-plots with something like ```r defaultOutput( plotOutput, "someplot", default = tags$div(style = "width:100px;height:200px") ) ``` This function is trivial and barely has any substance, and it should probably check before over-writing `$children`. But the point is to make the function intuitive and clear to hold space before reactivity introduces real content. Thoughts?

title: Observers/reactives fire in indeterminate order
description:
This is a follow-up to #2463 and https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/2429#issuecomment-497474108.

We've always told users that shouldn't rely on the reactives/observers firing in a specific order (unless `priority` is used), because the order is arbitrary. However, it's also true that we've assumed that the observers will fire in a deterministic order -- specifically, the order in which they were defined.

This assumptions turns out to not be true, either in the CRAN version of Shiny (1.3.2) or the current master version of shiny, with the fastmap PR merged (#2429).

Here's an example:

```R
library(shiny)

v <- reactiveVal(0)

observe({
  message(v(), ": observer 1")
})
observe({
  message(v(), ": observer 2")
})
observe({
  message(v(), ": observer 3")
})


v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
# and so on ...
```

The naive assumption is that it would print out something like this each time `flushReact()` is called:

```
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
1: observer 1
1: observer 2
1: observer 3
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
2: observer 1
2: observer 2
2: observer 3
```

And in the CRAN version of Shiny, it does this... for a while. But after running it a number times, it changes order:

```
d> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
6: observer 3
6: observer 1
6: observer 2

...

d> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
19: observer 2
19: observer 3
19: observer 1
```

In the current master, it does something different:

```
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
1: observer 1
1: observer 2
1: observer 3
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
2: observer 3
2: observer 2
2: observer 1
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
3: observer 1
3: observer 2
3: observer 3
> v(isolate(v()) + 1); shiny:::flushReact()
4: observer 3
4: observer 2
4: observer 1
```

It switches back and forth, reversing the order each time.

The question at this point is what to do about it. We can make the order fixed, by changing this line:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/17afce6fa1f3bc284a295b2ed16fb143692fbc79/R/reactives.R#L47

from this:

```
  .dependents$values(),
```

to something like this:

```
   .dependents$mget(as.character(sort(as.numeric(.dependents$keys())))),
```

With that change, it goes in 1-2-3 order every time.

However, another option is to just leave it as is on master. With the CRAN version of Shiny, it looks like applications will fire the observers in the defined order many times, and then switch. For app developers, if their app relies on the ordering assumption, they might not test their application enough to see that it falls down, or that when it does, it happens inconsistently enough that they don't know how to debug it.

With the master version of Shiny, the order switches every time, so if a developer relies on ordering, it's a fail-fast result, which can help them find the bug more quickly.

So in short: we can sort the dependents, in which case observers fire in the order that they're invalidated (I think), and this will allow developers to rely on at some (undocumented) assumptions about ordering. Or we can not sort them, in which case developers will quickly encounter problems if they rely on undocumented assumptions about ordering, and have to fix their code.

Keep in mind that for any existing apps that rely on the ordering assumption, with the CRAN version of Shiny, they are currently buggy, even if it is not immediately obvious to the developer.

title: Example app for freezeReactiveValues can emit error messages
description:
The purpose of the example app for `freezeReactiveValues` is to demonstrate how to suppress error messages. However, it can still emit error messages in some cases.

This is a slightly modified version of the example app (I added some `message()` calls):


```R
ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("data", "Data Set", c("mtcars", "pressure")),
  checkboxGroupInput("cols", "Columns (select 2)", character(0)),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    message("observe: ", input$data)
    data <- get(input$data)
    # Sets a flag on input$cols to essentially do req(FALSE) if input$cols
    # is accessed. Without this, an error will momentarily show whenever a
    # new data set is selected.
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "cols")
    updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "cols", choices = names(data))
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    message("renderPlot: ", input$data)
    # When a new data set is selected, input$cols will have been invalidated
    # above, and this will essentially do the same as req(FALSE), causing
    # this observer to stop and raise a silent exception.
    cols <- input$cols
    data <- get(input$data)

    if (length(cols) == 2) {
      plot(data[[ cols[1] ]], data[[ cols[2] ]])
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

If you check two of the columns so that a plot shows up, and then select the other data set, sometimes a red error message shows up briefly, and this appears in the console:

```
renderPlot: mtcars
renderPlot: mtcars
renderPlot: mtcars
renderPlot: pressure
Warning in min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
Warning in max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
Warning in min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
Warning in max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
Warning: Error in plot.window: need finite 'xlim' values
  [No stack trace available]
observe: pressure
```

The error occurs because the `renderPlot` is executing before the observer when the data set is changed. I can't get this to happen consistently, though. It happens the first time when I run the app in a new R session, but not after that. This is with Shiny 1.3.2.

However, with the fastmap PR (#2429), I can get the error message every time, not just the first time.

New command to run remote Shiny apps
description:
It all started with our second Shiny app in a gist. The first one was showing fine since it was named **app.R**:
```
runGist('https://gist.github.com/helgasoft/0353c54a3b50deceeb18afc1b0a7f460')
#  ye-ye!
```
The second one could not have the same name in Github, so when we tried to run it, that did not work.
```
runGist('https://gist.github.com/helgasoft/7d702d52d827dd20c460ca4ba664011e')
# bummer, error "App dir must contain either app.R or server.R."
```
Turns out _runGist_ is calling _runUrl_ which expects a zip file with _app.R_ inside.
So the available, but restricted R commands to run remote Shiny apps currently are:
1) runGist() - works only with Github gists named 'app.R'
2) runUrl() - accepts only zip/tar files with 'app.R' inside
3) runGitHub() - the app is in a repo

How about **executing apps directly from single remote source files**?  
With **any name**, like 'app1.R', 'my.app' or 'shiny.pride' ?
Here is a custom function to do that
```
shiny_url_run <- function(url) {
  require(shiny)
  file <- tempfile(fileext='.R')
  download.file(url, file, cacheOK=F)
  obj <- shiny:::shinyAppDir_appR(basename(file), dirname(file))
  runApp(obj, quiet=T)
}
# glitch: after termination it ends up in the debugger and needs Stop to be pressed
```
You can try it in Rstudio. That's how we did run our second (third,etc) Shiny app gist.
```
source('https://helgasoft.com/code/shrun.R')
shiny_url_run('https://gist.github.com/helgasoft/7d702d52d827dd20c460ca4ba664011e/raw/39b83d78a9d63ab609f691927ef65a60dddb4111/dygaps.R')
```
Now, wouldn't it be nice to have a **new command** called 'runShiny' or 'runNoZip' or 'runFrom' doing the same thing in the next version of Shiny ?
Any thoughts from the core team ?
Hope to get the ball rolling...

title: Input changed event fired on document
description:
This pertains to the javascript side of shiny. I had forgotten and was surprised all over again to see the `shiny:inputchanged` event is not fired on a changing input element and instead is fired on `document`. 

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/a4a49a354e1b411dbb57bd3e5a0acd5666c62655/srcjs/input_rate.js#L270-L281

So, if one wanted to handle a selection of `shiny:inputchanged` events one must listen for all `shiny:inputchanged` events. The listener must then check each event for a relevant property or properties. This came up as I was imagining a new input, which suppresses the values of its child inputs until a condition is met (think a selection of inputs inside a form updated only when the related submit button is clicked). Unfortunately, implementing such an input while all input changed events are fired on the document seems highly inefficient. 

Is there any possibility of triggering the event on the input element instead of document? If I understand correctly, the event would still bubble up, so existing listeners could still catch the event.

title: Weak references for reactive dependencies
description:
This is a follow-up to #2423. When a reactive expression has a dependency on a reactive value (or reactive expression), it will not be GC'd until it is invalidated, because the reactive value maintains a reference to it until it is invalidated. Since reactive expressions cache their last value, this can result in significant memory leakage.

The same is also true of observers, but since they don't cache their values, it results in less memory leakage.

Example code:

```R
library(shiny)
library(pryr)
rm(list=ls())

mem_used()
#> 49 MB

v <- reactiveVal(1)

r <- reactive({
  v()
  # Use sample() to avoid ALTREP optimization of 1:1e6
  sample(1:1e6)
})

o <- observe({
  r()
})

mem_used()
#> 49 MB

shiny:::flushReact()
mem_used()
#> 53 MB

rm(r, o)
mem_used()
#> 53 MB

# Alternatively, can run rm(v)
v(2)
mem_used()
#> 49 MB
```

Ideally, we could solve this by changing reactive values (and expressions) so that they have weak references to downstream objects.

title: Allow removal of value from reactiveValues list
description:
As far as I know, there is no way to remove a value from a reactiveValues list. Unlike a regular list, when setting a value to NULL, it still prints in the reactiveValues.

This has been previously discussed on the Google group https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/4XxbaHQoE3o

@wch brought up the argument of 

> deleting items is that the behavior for an item deleted from a reactiveValues object is not well-defined - what should happen if a reactive expression takes a dependency on values$x, but then values$x is removed?

I would say that's not necessarily a big issue - it's already possible to remove reactive values that have potential dependencies. We can remove UI that has inputs in it, and anything that depends on a deleted input simply never receives any future invalidations from that value. I think that would be fine.


### Super hacky workaround?

Purely out of curiousity I wanted to see how I can do this without shiny's support. I haven't tested it much and I don't know if there are any repercussions for doing this (I'm sure there may be!), but the following two lines can work. Very hacky, I do not actually recommend this. 

```
rm("name", envir = .subset2(rv, "impl")$.values)
 .subset2(rv, "impl")$.valuesDeps$invalidate()
```

**EDIT:**

The above no longer works in the newest version of shiny. You now need to use:

```
.subset2(rv, "impl")$.values$remove("name")
```

in order to remove an element from the reactiveValues list. But the second line from above, the one that causes invalidation, also doesn't work anymore and I'm not sure how to replace it.

title: Creating an observer leaks memory
description:
For example:

```R
library(shiny)
gc()
lastmem <- as.numeric(pryr::mem_used())
o <- observe({
  message("running observer")
})
shiny:::flushReact()
#> running observer

o$destroy()          # Shouldn't hurt to try this
shiny:::flushReact()

rm(o)
gc()
cat("Increase:" , as.numeric(pryr::mem_used()) - lastmem, "bytes")
#> Increase: 1864 bytes
```

Add hide/disable to InputBinding API
description:
Currently there is not an official way to hide or disable inputs in the InputBinding API.

[shinyjs](https://deanattali.com/shinyjs/) is currently the premier way to do this — via `shinyjs::disable` and `shinyjs::enable` — but it relies on the internal structure of Shiny inputs instead of building on any of our publicly available APIs.

Doing this was originally suggested by Joe in #1286, an issue in which @daattali (author of shinyjs) requested a feature that would simplify the way shinyjs determines an input's type.

title: Documentation: Mention that selectizeInput can be done server-side, but only using its update function
description:
The fact that selectizeInputs can render server-side can be useful for many, but it's a hidden feature because it isn't documented in the selectizeInput/selectInput documentation. The only way to know about it is by stumbling across it on google or by looking at the `updateSelectizeInput` function and noticing that there is an extra `server=TRUE/FALSE` argument.

It can be confusing why this `server` parameter is only available in the update function but not in the builder function. The reason for this doesn't have to be documented, but I do think it would be very helpful to at least mention in the builder function that if the user has tens of thousands of options, this can be an option. 

Related to @alandipert 's [comment](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1061#issuecomment-487666378) on another input widget that has an asymmetry between its builder and update function

title: Cannot download html_notebook reports (because shiny assumes file extension comes after the last dot)
description:
@wch has an example for [generating rmarkdown reports and downloading them with shiny](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/generating-reports.html). If you slightly modify it to use a `html_notebook` instead of an `html_document`, it breaks. Here is the code (I simplified it a bit):

```
ui <- fluidPage(
  downloadButton("report", "Generate report")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$report <- downloadHandler(
    filename = "report.nb.html",
    content = function(file) {
      tempReport <- file.path(tempdir(), "report.Rmd")
      file.copy("report.Rmd", tempReport, overwrite = TRUE)
      params <- list(n = input$slider)
      rmarkdown::render(tempReport,
                        output_file = file,
                        output_format = "html_notebook",
                        params = params,
                        envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
      )
    }
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

When you try to download the report, you keep getting hit with a failed file download.

Looking into the issue a little bit, I noticed that the problem is that the `file` parameter that shiny provides us in the `content()` function loses the `.nb` in the filename extension, and becomes `<uuid>.html`. But the `rmarkdown::render` function, given an `html_notebook` format, automatically changes the filename extension to `.nb.html`. So the two filenames don't match.

I don't know if this issue should be opened in shiny or in rmarkdown. Up until now, I would have thought that the assumption that a filename only comes after the last dot is a safe assumption to make, I've never come across another case where that doesn't hold true. I don't know what the proper solution would be, maybe providing an additional optional argument to `downloadHandler` that would let you specify the file extension, or maybe shiny can internally see if the supplied filename has `.nb.html` then don't strip out the `.nb`. I'm not sure which solution is cleaner. I generally would say the second solution is ugly and hacky, but only because html notebooks are explicitly an RStudio product, I feel that maybe it would be acceptable for shiny to make an exception for it.

### Temporary solution

After the call to render the file, add two lines

```
fileCorrected <- sub("\\.html$", ".nb.html", file)
file.copy(fileCorrected, file)
```

title: Helper function show_icons() to get valid icon()s
description:
Related: #2263 

Currently, the documentation simply refers to the FontAwesome site:

> Icons are drawn from the [Font Awesome Free](https://fontawesome.com/) (currently icons from the v5.3.1 set are supported with the v4 naming convention)...

and

>  For lists of available icons, see http://fontawesome.io/icons/ ...

Unfortunately, the website only lists icons in the _current_ version (5.8.1 as of this writing) and there doesn't appear to be any easy way to find out which icons _were_ available for a _specific_ version (e.g. `shiny`'s current supported version of 5.3.1).

That means the process of looking up icons to use is currently quite onerous -- either guess & check by running your app, or look on the website and check the version nested in a given icon's page (e.g. I learned `pepper-hot` is apparently only available since 5.7.0 [here](https://fontawesome.com/icons/pepper-hot?style=solid))

It would be ideal if FontAwesome would offer an easier UX for this. But `shiny` could include a helper-function like `show_icons`; a rinky-dink version I cooked up is:

```
library(magrittr)
icons = file.path('www', 'shared', 'fontawesome', 'css', 'all.min.css') %>% 
  system.file(package = 'shiny') %>%
  readLines(warn = FALSE) %>% tail(1L) %>%
  strsplit('.', fixed = TRUE) %>% unlist %>%
  gsub(':before\\{content:".+"\\}', '', . ) %>% 
  grep('fa-', ., fixed = TRUE, value = TRUE) %>% 
  grep('[{,]', ., value = TRUE, invert = TRUE) %>% 
  gsub('^fa-', '', .)
```

I'm sure it doesn't capture everything correctly but I think it's close.

I don't know what the glyphicon version would look like or if it's necessary.

PS this phrase is quite confusing for a new user (me) who has no idea about the whole version shift situation, and is given no further context (e.g. in Details)

> currently icons from the v5.3.1 set are supported with the v4 naming convention

PPS the glyphicon link in the documentation isn't correct (redirects to the top of the page and the HTML tag is apparently missing):

http://getbootstrap.com/components/#glyphicons

Areas=c("Russia","USA")

              sliderInput("slider_data",label = "Dates",min = initRange[1],max=initRange[2], value = initRange,dragRange = T,width = "100%")

title: [Feature Request] Adding onKeyPress event to textInput
description:
Hey, 

One feature I receive from clients when building a Shiny App is the ability to "validate" through pressing the Enter key when using a `textInput()`. 

Example: You use `textInput()` as a Search Form, with a button to validate the search just below. I've been asked several time to implement a validation of search through pressing the Enter button here, which I always do locally via jQuery but I feel like there should be a more systemic way to do it.  

I think it would be nice to have a native keypress event here, the same way we have a click event on `plotOutput()`

My suggestion: 

``` r 
pkgload::load_all()
textInput <- function(inputId, label, value = "", width = NULL,
                      placeholder = NULL) {
  
  value <- restoreInput(id = inputId, default = value)
  
  div(class = "form-group shiny-input-container",
      style = if (!is.null(width)) paste0("width: ", validateCssUnit(width), ";"),
      label %AND% tags$label(label, `for` = inputId),
      tags$input(
        id = inputId, 
        type="text", 
        class="form-control", 
        value=value,
        placeholder = placeholder, 
        onKeyPress = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('%s_keypress', event.key)", inputId)
        )
  )
}

library(shiny)
ui <- function(request){
  tagList(
    textInput("plop","plop"),
    br(),
    textOutput("text")
  )
  
}

server <- function(input, output, session){
  observeEvent( input$plop_keypress, {
    print(input$plop_keypress)
    if (input$plop_keypress == "Enter"){
      output$text <- renderText({
        "You've validated"
      })
    }
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

```

As you can see, the key is printed to the console, and we can create conditional events on pressing the 'Enter' button. 

Tested on : 
- Chrome 
- Firefox
- Safari
On a Mac OS

Things to look at : 
- Is the pressed key returned the same way on each OS /Browser? 
- The "click" events input names are defined by the user in `plotOutput()`, maybe this can be the same here. My personal preference is `inputId_keypress` though, but I also could understand the need for consistency :) 

If ever you think this is a good idea, I'll be glad to do a PR. 

Colin

title: Dynamic dateRangeInput start / end "frozen" after bookmark restore
description:
The following simple app shows that after a dynamic dateRangeInput is restored, the start / end values no longer get properly updated when the dateRangeInput is redrawn. To reproduce this issue:

1. Start the app and verify that _source_ indeed propagates to _target_
2. Bookmark the app
3. Restore the app from the bookmark and verify that the source selection no longer propagates to target.

```
library(shiny)

ui <- function() {
  fluidPage(
    
    dateRangeInput("date1",
                   "Source:",
                   min = Sys.Date()-10,
                   max = Sys.Date()),
    uiOutput("date2-ui"),
    bookmarkButton("my_bookmark")
  )
}

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output[["date2-ui"]] <- renderUI({
    req(input$date1)
    dateRangeInput("date2","Target:",min=Sys.Date()-10,max=Sys.Date(),start=input$date1[1],end=input$date1[2])
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server,enableBookmarking = "server")
```

This was not yet an issue with Shiny 1.0.1, but materialized when upgrading to 1.2.0.

title: [Feature Request] Eager versions of pollReactive and reactiveFileReader
description:
The `pollReactive` and `reactiveFileReader` functions are, well, reactive, which means the `valueFunc` and `readFunc` functions are not run unless the reactive is needed by another observer or reactive.

I have a use-case where `valueFunc`/`readFunc` are relatively expensive, but observers that are dependent on these reactives need to be relatively fast.

In this case, it would be better to have an eager, observant version of `pollReactive` and `reactiveFileReader`, so that the idle time between `input$button` clicks can be used to run `valueFunc`/`readFunc`.

```
data <- reactiveFileReader(2000, session, filePath = "data.csv", readFunc = function(filePath) {
    ...
    # Takes ~1000ms to run
})

observe({
    # This block should only be triggered by input$button
    input$button
    use_data_somehow <- isolate(data())
    # user expectation is that this block runs effectively instantaneously (i.e. <100ms)

    # as it stands now, the first time input$button is clicked after a file
    # modification is detected, this block will take >1000ms to run
    # subsequent button clicks will be very fast (as desired), until a file change is detected again
})
```

title: Double redraws for brush
Difficulties with insertUI and setting state
description:
I have some fairly complex states that need to be set after an `insertUI` call is made. I'm having trouble getting operations to run in the order that I want them to. Here is a small example:

```


library(shiny)

ui <- basicPage(
    h2('Insert'),
    actionButton("loadui","loadui")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
    i <- 1
    observeEvent(input$loadui,{
        j <- i
        print(j)
        insertUI(
            "h2",
            "afterEnd",
            tags$div(
                textInput(paste0("txt",j), paste0("txt",j), value=j),
                textInput(paste0("txtn",j), paste0("txtn",j))
            ),
            immediate =TRUE
        )
        
        observeEvent(input[[paste0("txt",j)]],{
            updateTextInput(session, paste0("txtn",j), value= input[[paste0("txt",j)]])
        })
        
        #updateTextInput(session, paste0("txt",j), value= paste("+", input[[paste0("txt",j)]]))
        #updateTextInput(session, paste0("txtn",j), value= "initial")
        onFlushed(function(){
            updateTextInput(session, paste0("txt",j), value= paste("+", isolate(input[[paste0("txt",j)]])))
            updateTextInput(session, paste0("txtn",j), value= "initial")
        })
        i <<- i + 1
    })
    
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

When they are inserted, I'd like the first text input to be "+1" and the second one to be "initial". I tried updating within onFlushed or just in the server, but not much helped. Is there a way to trigger an event after all of the input/outputs have been resolved? Or maybe a way to pause reactivity while the inputs are getting updated?

title: varSelectInput: typo in documentation, and would also help to make it clear why it's needed
description:
I just looked over the docs for the new varSelectInput and ran into trouble trying to parse this sentence: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/c79034649077f5fa6f8d615ce10c457eb33a2d2a/R/input-select.R#L240-L244

Another thing I wasn't able to pick up from the documentation is why this input is even necessary and made it into the very elite list of inputs supported by shiny. It feels very esoteric, and I'm having a hard time rationalizing why shiny added it.

The documentation didn't offer much insight other than saying it returns symbols, but it would be helpful if the docs were more explicit on why exactly this is useful. I also looked at @schloerke 's [example app from the PR](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/2091#issue-193434802) and it still seems to me that the only reason this exists is to return a symbol.

If that is the reason for this input, then would it make sense to instead offer a `symbol = TRUE/FALSE` parameter for select inputs, so that this would be more generic rather than only work for dataframes? The specificity of this input feels a bit forced to suit a very particular need that isn't a general shiny need. Adding more clear documentation about its usage would clear this up :)

title: Bookmarking bug (or documentation required): only last setBookmarkExclude() is respected
description:
I have an app with several inputs that have long names that I want to exclude from bookmarking. I didn't see anywhere in the documentation, online or in roxygen, that `setBookmarkExclude()` should only be called once, so I assumed I would be able to call the function many times in a row. It turns out that it overwrites the previous ones. So something like this

```
setBookmarkExclude("t1")
setBookmarkExclude("t2")
setBookmarkExclude("t3")
```

Will only exclude `t3` from bookmarking. Either this is a bug, or it should be mentioned in the documentation that this will not work. Maybe it is mentioned somewhere and I just didn't see it!

title: windowTitle argument needs better default
description:
In `titlePanel`, the `windowTitle` argument defaults to `title`. If the title is complicated, this can end up with arbitrary HTML, CSS, and script tags being inserted into the head, which can break shinyapps.io, Connect, and Shiny Server when they go to inject their SockJS scripts:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/129551/51622452-7a543e80-1eeb-11e9-9d1f-9aca099c268d.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/129551/51622481-8a6c1e00-1eeb-11e9-9e5b-dd49de32ecb3.png)

One possibility discussed with @aronatkins would be to only take the `title` as the default value if it's a string, or alternatively, walk the first level of the tree looking for strings (which would let you at least put a logo). We could emit a warning if the `title` is too complicated to extract a `windowTitle`, asking the user to provide one explicitly.

title: History.go(0) stopped resetting shiny app in Firefox browser
description:
**Description:**
When calling the js-function "history.go(0)" from within a Shiny app, it will not reset the widgets in a Firefox browser. 
However, in a Chromium-Browser, the reset of all widgets works as expected.

This functionality stopped working suddenly sometime during the last week. In this period, the code of my app has not changed at all so I assume, the behaviour is somehow related with a R-package update (or it may be browser-related).

**Steps to reproduce:**
I wrote a minimal reproducible example and hosted it here: [https://nonserial.shinyapps.io/ResetButton/](https://nonserial.shinyapps.io/ResetButton/)

```{r}
library(shinyjs)
library(shiny)

# Define the js method that resets the page
jsResetCode <- "shinyjs.reset = function() {history.go(0)}" 
#jsResetCode <- "shinyjs.reset = function() {location.reload()}"

ui <- fluidPage(
  shinyjs::useShinyjs(), # 
  extendShinyjs(text = jsResetCode, functions="reset"),
  div(id="mainpage",
      titlePanel("Reset Button Test"),
      fluidRow(
        sidebarPanel(
          radioButtons(inputId = "lore_i", label = h5("lore ipsum"),
                       choices = list("dummy text 1" = 1, 
                                      "dummy text 2" = 2),
                       selected = character(0)),
          tags$hr(),
          textInput("lore_a",
                    label = NULL,
                    placeholder = "textinput"),
          actionButton("reset", "Reset App via JS"), 
          actionButton("reset2", "Reset App via shinyjs"), 
          width = 3),
        
        mainPanel(
          h3("Description:"),
          h4("1) Click on a radio-button and fill in a text into the textInput."),
          h4("2) Then clicking the Reset-button in a Firefox-Browser (version 64.0), will not reset the shiny app."),
          h4("3) However, clicking the Reset-button in Chromium-Browser (version 71.0.3578.98) DOES reset the shiny app.")
        )
      )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {  
  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    js$reset()
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$reset2, {
    shinyjs::reset(id="mainpage")
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

**Instruction:**
Once started the app:
1) Click on a radio-button and fill in a text into the textInput.
2) Then clicking the Reset-button in a Firefox-Browser (version 64.0), will not reset the shiny app.
3) However, clicking the Reset-button in Chromium-Browser (version 71.0.3578.98) DOES reset the shiny app.

**Question:**
Does anyone have an idea, what could cause this problem or does anyone have a workaround?

**Edit:**
I also implemented the shinyjs::reset(id)-function, that shows the exactly same behaviour as described above.

title: hover with multi-panel plots
description:
I have a shiny app that helps a user visualize electropherograms (essentially spectra) that come from automated DNA sequencers. I would like the user to be able to hover over a peak and find out the time the peak came off the instrument. I also would like to be able to compare multiple electropherograms by plotting the spectra one above the other.

If I plot a single spectrum, I can recover the mouse x-position with the 'hover' option provided to plotOutput() in the ui. If I stack plots using base graphics and the par(mfrow=c(n,1)) where n is the number of spectra, the results are unpredictable. Basically the x-position is recoverable in part of the plot region but not throughout.

As a final piece of information, I wrote this app several years ago and it's been working as expected until I updated R and the shiny package to fairly recent versions: (R 3.4.4; shiny 1.2.0).

I've included an app.R file that reproduces this issue on a simple case using histograms and the old-faithful data and shows the approach I have been taking. I get the same behavior whether I set 'clip' in hoverOpts to TRUE or FALSE.

I asked about this on stackoverflow as well [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54099480/r-shiny-hover-with-multi-panel-plots](url), and have not received any feedback as of yet. 

Thanks for any insight in advance here.

Here is a self-contained example, though it uses histograms rather than spectra plotted with plot()

```
library(shiny)

ui = fluidPage(

titlePanel("Mulitpanel hover: Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

sidebarLayout(
  sidebarPanel(
     sliderInput("bins","Number of bins:",min = 1,max = 50,value = 30)
  ),

  mainPanel(
     textOutput("xpos"),
     plotOutput("distPlot",hover=hoverOpts(id="plot_hover",clip=TRUE))
      )
   )
 )

 server = function(input, output) {
   output$xpos = renderText({paste("x coord:",input$plot_hover$x)})
   output$distPlot = renderPlot({
   x    = faithful[, 2] 
   bins = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

   par(mfrow=c(2,1))
   hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
   hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'orange', border = 'white')
  })
 }
 shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: Bookmarking: unnecessarily unrecoverable error when query string contains more params than expected
description:
If a bookmarkable app is opened with a bookmarkable URL that contains an extra parameter that the bookmark system doesn't know about, then **none** of the inputs get set to their values and the following error message appears `Error in RestoreContext initialization: Failed to parse URL parameter "value"`.

I think Shiny should be a little more forgiving when this happens, and still set all the values that it's able to. Whether or not to notify the user about the extra values is another question as well (I think it should be quiet).

This can happen from many situations, for example if an app is updated and an input gets removed, if the app developer or end user change the URL, or if a URL is shared using a third party application that automatically adds a parameter (for example, links in marketing emails or from social media often get a parameter added). None of these cases should cause the bookmark engine to fail.

Example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- function(req) {
  fluidPage(
    bookmarkButton(),
    textInput("text", "text", "text")
  )
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server, enableBookmarking = "url", options = list(port = 3900))
```

Run this app, and navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:3900/?_inputs_&text="texttest"`. This works. Now navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:3900/?_inputs_&text="texttest"&foo=bar`. The bookmarking doesn't work and an error is shown.

Potentially related to #1650

title: Widget values persist across page reloads on Firefox ESR
description:
I'm filing this issue for future reference -- we don't plan on making a workaround for this behavior.

On most browsers, reloading a Shiny application clears all input values and gives them the default values. With Firefox ESR, the browser will restore the previous input value when the page is reloaded, which can be surprising in some cases.

References:
https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=46845
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7377301/firefox-keeps-form-data-on-reload

title: insertUI/callModule to add, removeUI/??? to remove (no mechanism to deactivate a "server" instance)
description:
This would probably also solve https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1797 https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/548 and https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2040

In short, there is capability to a) modularise application server processing (by using callModule) and there is also b) capability to add/remove UI sections via a number of mechanisms, but commonly via insertUI/removeUI.

When trying to use a combination of the above we encountered the problem that there seems to be no opposite to callModule().

For example:
- Imagine you have a data set and you wish to allow your users have a widget to select an X axis column, a Y axis column and plot it - as part of a larger application you would write a sub-module/widget that would allow them to do that which would consist of select box for X, a select box for Y and a plot output.
- Now extend that concept by allowing users to create multiple instances of the widget (ie a dashboard of graphs) - this could be achieved by using `insertUI([target], [after], [UI of widget - with ID])` and calling `callModule([ID of UI of widget], [data])`. This would produce a UI/Server pair which hangs off the session namespace via id ID (having used `ns <- NS(id)` and `ns("selectX")` etc).
- Finally, you want to provide the ability for your users to remove graphs as they want.  The UI element can be removed with removeUI(), but there is no capacity (that I know of) to remove the server functionality added with callModule()


Arguably, as long as the UI/Server pair has a unique ID every time, this is workable with the cost of non-release of memory and processing of removed widgets. However, if you take the same principle and use it to serve tabs on your site which would have the same ID each time they are instantiated/selected then currently you end up with multiple server instances reacting to a single UI instance that is regenerated each time the user moves away from and back to - all due to the fact that there is no way to do the reverse of callModule() [that I know of]

NOTE: this is specifically a problem when using `output$plot <- ....`, `observe({ input$selectX })` or `observeEvent(input$selectY, {})` in the sub-module/widget

title: Cannot install shiny (1.2.0) with R 3.3.x
description:
This issue stems from the lack of a compatible Windows binary version of `httpuv` 
being available on CRAN for R 3.3.x.

Because this is fundamentally a packaging / dependency problem for _one_ platform (Windows), and an old release of R, I don't think it's likely to get solved by the RStudio / Shiny maintainers. I'm just documenting the problem and a workaround here for posterity.

If you are using R 3.5.x, it's unlikely you'll have this exact problem, but some of the workaround steps below may be helpful in similar situations.

## Problem
The latest version of `shiny` available as of this writing (November 2018) is **1.2.0**. This requires `httpuv` version >= 1.4.4. For R versions 3.3.x, the latest binary package available on CRAN for `httpuv` for Windows is **1.4.1**.

Because the dependency on `httpuv` 1.4.4 cannot be resolved with the available binary packages on CRAN for R 3.3.x, the resulting error occurs when attempting to install `shiny`:

```
⋮
* installing *source* package 'shiny' ...
** package 'shiny' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** R
** inst
** preparing package for lazy loading
Error in loadNamespace(i, c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[i]]) : 
  namespace 'httpuv' 1.4.1 is being loaded, but >= 1.4.4 is required
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'shiny'
* removing 'C:/Users/IEUser/Documents/R/win-library/3.3/shiny'
Warning in install.packages :
  running command '"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-33~1.3/bin/x64/R" CMD INSTALL -l ↩
"C:\Users\IEUser\Documents\R\win-library\3.3" ↩
C:\Users\IEUser\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpMnGbom/downloaded_packages/shiny_1.2.0.tar.gz' ↩
had status 1
Warning in install.packages :
  installation of package ‘shiny’ had non-zero exit status
```

## Workaround

After allowing the above package installation to fail (this still fetches and installs all the other dependencies), manually install an older binary `shiny` package which doesn't require `httpuv-1.4.5`; the one I found that worked was <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/contrib/3.3/shiny_1.0.5.zip>.

### Installation within RStudio

Once you've downloaded that .zip, install it using the "Packages" tab within RStudio, then _Install from:_ → _Package Archive File_ and browse to the place where you saved it.

### Installation within R

This command will install the Windows binary for `shiny-1.0.5` from the CRAN project site from within a command-line R session:

```R
install.packages('https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/contrib/3.3/shiny_1.0.5.zip',
                 repos=NULL, type='win.binary')
```

## Possible alternative: Rtools

Repeat the installation process for the `shiny` package after installing [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) and choose `y` when asked if you want to install the available source version of any updated packages.

title: icon() can't use FontAwesome 5 font styles
description:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/5e2b40d3a92ea602d7187dafe49eba0d1e220cde/R/bootstrap.R#L1520-L1560

The new FontAwesome version has font classes `far` and `fal` (Most of them are pro-only, but [some](https://fontawesome.com/icons?d=gallery&s=regular&m=free) are free, such as `check-circle` or `address-book` in regular styling)

Using them requires a different `prefix_class`, but this can't be changed at the moment.
Adding `far` or `fal` to `class` (`icon("check-circle", class = "far")`) doesn't work either because `fa` comes first.

I would code a PR for this but I wand to know what solution you prefer?

1. Add a new argument (non-functional for glyphicon) `icon <- function(name, class = NULL, lib = "font-awesome", style = c("normal", "regular", "light"))` wich is ignored for glyphicon
2. Add new options for `lib` ("font-awesome-regular" and "font-awesome-light", maybe?)
3. Be smart about `class` containing these special classes

I kind of prefer the first option because of code clarity, but the third has the advantage of not adding a lib-specific argument to `icon()`.

title: Feature Request: sink console output to JavaScript console
description:
# Overview

Improve app debugging process by making realtime R console output available via the browser JavaScript console.

# Motivation

I help to onboard many new shiny users to a shared shiny server, and inevitably one of the major friction points is hunting down the logs on the server. The `sanitize.errors` and `fullstacktrace` options only go so far in terms of alleviating this challenge, and I've been beginning to try to think about ways to tighten the debugging loop when building a shiny app - especially for users that might not be familiar with an external server os / filesystem.

# Proof-of-concept

While iterating on this process a bit, I put together a proof-of-concept to split the console output & messages out to the JavaScript console so that the R console outputs are immediately accessible in the browser while the app is running. 

I built a new R connection that executes arbitrary R code on the message, which I then use to re-route the console output to a `console.log()` call using `shinyjs::runjs` (demo and example app in [this repo](https://github.com/dgkf/callbackConnection)). I learned just barely enough of the C interface to get this off the ground. The example is quite finicky (crashes sporadically, requires regular restarts of the R session), but it showcases the proposed functionality and one way of implementing it.

title: Async cached plots raise "Error in !: invalid argument type" error
Output widget is not turning gray
description:
#### Bug
Consider the following example, a shiny application with two tabs. Each tab is made of a shiny module. The first module consists of a slider input widget. The second tab consists of a histogram. The slider input controls the number of bins in the histogram. If the user changes the number of bins with the slider input and moves to the second tab, the histogram does not turn gray. Instead the histogram is shown with the old number of bins until the calculation for the new histogram is done. Then the histogram is updated immediately.

This behavior is not limited to histograms. It seems that it happens with all output widgets. 

#### To Reproduce
 1. Start the minimal example
 2. Go to the second tab and move the slider input to another value
 3. The histogram turns gray until the calculation is done. The histogram is shown with the new number of bins
 4. Go to first tab and move the slider input to another value and change to the second tab
 5. Histogram does not turn gray. The histogram is shown until the calculation is done. Then the histogram is updated immediately with the new number of bins. 

#### Minimal example

You can download a minimal example from https://github.com/be-marc/minimal-example-shiny

 `App.R` 
* Main application, that calls the modules `module_tab1` and `module_tab2`
* Transfers a reactive list with a value from `module_tab1` to `module_tab2`

 `module_tab1` 
* Consists of an input slider widget 
* Stores the value of the input slider widget in a reactive list

 `module_tab2`
* Consists of an input slider widget and a histogram
* Updates the number of bins in the histogram depending on the last updated slider widget



  `App.R`.

**App.R** 
```r
library(shiny)

source("module_tab1.R")
source("module_tab2.R")

ui <- tagList(
  shiny::navbarPage(
    id = "navbar",
    title = "Minimal Example",
    shiny::tabPanel(
      title = "tab1",
      tab1UI("tab1")
    ),
    shiny::tabPanel(
      title = "tab2",
      tab2UI("tab2")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  tab1Output <- shiny::callModule(tab1, "tab1")
  tab2Output <- shiny::callModule(tab2, "tab2", tab1Output)
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

**module_tab1.R** 

``` r
tab1UI <- function(id) {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)

  shiny::fluidRow(
    shiny::column(
      4,
      sliderInput(ns("bins"),
        "Number of bins:",
        min = 1,
        max = 50,
        value = 1
      )
    ),
    shiny::column(8)
  )
}

tab1 <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Reactive list for data transfer from module 1 to module 2
  tab1Output <- shiny::reactive(
    list(
      bins = input$bins
    )
  )

  return(tab1Output)
}
```

**module_tab2.R** 

``` r
tab2UI <- function(id) {
  ns <- shiny::NS(id)

  shiny::fluidRow(
    shiny::column(4, sliderInput(ns("bins"),
      "Number of bins:",
      min = 1,
      max = 50,
      value = 50
    )),
    shiny::column(
      8,
      shiny::plotOutput(ns("histogram"))
    )
  )
}

tab2 <- function(input, output, session, tab1Input) {
  slider_value <- reactiveVal(30)

  # Update slider value from tab1
  observeEvent(input$bins, {
    slider_value(input$bins)
  })

  # Update slider value from tab2
  observeEvent(tab1Input()$bins, {
    slider_value(tab1Input()$bins)
  })

  # Render histogram
  output$histogram <- renderPlot({
    print(slider_value())
    
    # Add sleep to simulate long calculation
    Sys.sleep(4)
    x <- faithful[, 2]
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = slider_value() + 1)
    hist(x, breaks = bins, col = "darkgray", border = "white")
  })
}

```

", " Days to Term Start: ", point$COLUMN, "

title: Plot brushing fails in IE11/Win10 in VMWare
description:
I noticed during release testing that the last plot in the example app [139-plot-brush-scaling](https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/content/4344/) intermittently doesn't work on IE11/Win10 in VMware.

No other team member has been able to reproduce the problem, either in their copy of VMWare or on a physical Windows box.

When I visit the application for the first time, I'm able to brush the last plot without issue.

However, if I reload the page or resize the window, I'm not able to brush the last plot. When I click on the plot, I notice a very small box appear over the corresponding "Brush: Fail" label.

The only plot that fails this way is the last plot.

@wch has theorized that this is caused by a different order of events occurring in the browser under these circumstances for some reason. The small box that appears is the brush panel, but it's not sized or positioned correctly as a result.

This screen recording demonstrates the problem: https://tailrecursion.com/~alan/tmp/ie11_win10_vmware_plot_brush_bug.mp4

title: Plots sometimes are very narrow in Firefox
Different text wrapping behavior for code (pre) output in Safari
description: The text wrapping behavior for code output is different in Safari compared to Firefox and Chrome (all tested with latest releases). A horizontal scrollbar won't appear in Safari, instead the lines of text are wrapped. In the above screenshot (from the `shiny-examples` app: `017-select-vs-selectize`), Firefox is **LEFT**, Safari is **CENTER**, and Chrome is **RIGHT**). From a little investigation between me and @wch yielded some findings (from Trello card notes): > It turns out that Safari displays text with the CSS properties white-space: pre; overflow-wrap: break-word differently from other browsers. ... JSFiddle: https://jsfiddle.net/fba61pct/2/ > > With those CSS properties, Safari wraps text but the other browsers do not. > > It seems that setting overflow-wrap: normal fixes it in Safari. However, Bootstrap specifically sets overflow-wrap: break-word for pre tags, and we would be overriding it. I'm not sure why they made that choice -- it seems to have no effect in other browsers.

title: Input event queue can stall in apps that use async
description:
If input events are received during async processing and queued, and those input events happen to not invalidate any observers, then processing of the queue can stall.

Use this example app:

https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/blob/c93174759c7c6291382d552fbd70177875005133/133-async-hold-inputs/app.R

Click Go, then change the radio value, then Go, then change the radio value, etc. Do not wait for the previous button click to be processed before hitting Go. After your third or fourth button click, wait for R to catch up. You'll see that the output has permanently fallen behind.
