title: In IE11, can't drop .csv files downloaded with Edge
description:
In the course of 1.2 testing, @shalutiwari noticed that certain files couldn't be dropped on the file input at https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/content/4036/

After much sleuthing, we determined that **only CSV files downloaded using MS Edge** failed to upload when dropped on the upload example.

CSV files downloaded using Edge have conspicuous permissions. Below is a screenshot @wch made of permissions on files downloaded using IE11, Chrome, and Edge:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26024/46972199-d7ca2b00-d072-11e8-8566-bdb3c5d39032.png)

## Additional things we know

- If the file is downloaded in a VM to a folder that's mapped to the host, like `Downloads`, the weird permissions aren't on the file and an upload will work.
- Uploading by clicking on the "Browse" button and selecting the file downloaded with Edge works fine.
- The problem seems to be specific to CSV files. Uploading an image downloaded with Edge to e.g. https://html5demos.com/dnd-upload/ works fine, and the image doesn't have the weird permissions on it.
- If the conspicuous permissions added by Edge are removed, the file uploads properly.

## Ideas to mitigate

- We might want to error on the R side if the list of uploaded files is empty. The error message could include a note about this particular error. The error that does currently happen is on the R side, "Error: invalid 'description' argument', but it's not helpful.

title: plotOutput UI options don't work with ggplot2 3.0
description:
With ggplot2 2.2.1, it was straightforward to get interactivity with a plot. nearPoints, brush, plot clicks, and other features worked quite well. With ggplot2 3.0, however, the normal functionality no longer works. There are two manifestations of this so far:

1. Shiny maps to the number of pixels on the plot, not the plot data. If I have an x and y bivariate plot ranging from 0 to 1, and I interact with the plot (say brush to zoom) in the lower left, the plot won't read 0 on the y axis, but instead will map to its maximum height (if height = 465, then the lowest point on the graph is 465, not 0 as is the case in the original data). 
2. Shiny nearPoints can't automatically fill in xvar and yvar of a ggplot. Earlier, nearPoints could automatically identify xvar and yvar in ggplots. Whatever changed in ggplot2 3.0 also broke this functionality. 

If I am missing anything let me know, but it strikes me that the changes to ggplot2 3.0 to align it within the tidyverse have broken the way shiny access its data. This manifests as failing to read xvar and yvar in nearPoints, as well as plot interactivity defaulting to the pixels of the plot instead of its data. 

Thanks for building such a fantastic package, I hope these comments are helpful in future updates to shiny.

title: Custom label and html display in server-side selectize elements
updateSelectizeInput causes double-run
description:
Hi, 
I have made a reproducible example below to show my problem.

I am using [mpg](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html) dataset which contains some fuel economy data by car manufacturers and models. 

I have two selectInput's each for manufacturer and model selection. I have defined the choices argument for `manufacturer` input in ui and I expect the list of  `model` input could be updated depending on the value of  `manufacturer`. And a subset of mpg table by selected manufacturer/model is shown as an output.

I have realised my app runs twice when I initialise the app or when I select a different value in `manufacturer` input. I insert `str(input$model)` before generating the underlying table to capture this phenomenon. When I initialise the app, `input$model` value is `""` the first time and gives a blank table and only then server runs again and `input$model` value is updated to give a table. And if you exam the `input$model` value in `observeEvent(filtered_models(), {` before and after `updateSelectizeInput`, you will see `input$model` value stays the same and this confuses me.

The double-run is not ideal especially if some big tables with intensive calculation are needed. Will be appreciated if someone could help me with this issue. 

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2) # use mpg dataset in ggplot2
library(data.table)

dt <- as.data.table(mpg)
manufacturer_list <- dt[, unique(manufacturer)]

ui <- fluidPage(
    selectInput(inputId = "manufacturer",
                label = "Manufacturer",
                choices = manufacturer_list,
                selected = manufacturer_list[1]
                ),
    selectInput(inputId = "model",
                label = "Model",
                choices = NULL
                ),
    tableOutput("table")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  filtered_models <- reactive({dt[manufacturer == input$manufacturer, unique(model)]})
  
  observeEvent(filtered_models(), {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, 'model', choices = c(filtered_models()), selected = filtered_models()[1])
  })
  
  filtered_mpg <- reactive({
    # str(input$model)
    dt[manufacturer == input$manufacturer & model == input$model]
  })
  
  output$table <- renderTable(filtered_mpg())
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: SelectInput sending changes to server when search box is empty
description:
Referencing an old issue: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/404

As @jjallaire pointed out,

> (1) By default when the user empties out the select input Shiny sends no
changes to the server.

> (2) When the select input loses focus and is empty the last selection is
re-inserted into the control (again no changes are sent to the server).

This was the exact behaviour upto and including version 1.0.5.

When I updated to version 1.1 Shiny selectInput has started sending changes to server when the user hits backspace. This is causing all the downstream reactive dependancies to reexecute when the user hits backspace to clear the search box.

Reproducible example:

```
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    selectInput("state", "Choose a state:",
                list(`East Coast` = c("NY", "NJ", "CT"),
                     `West Coast` = c("WA", "OR", "CA"),
                     `Midwest` = c("MN", "WI", "IA"))
    ),
    textOutput("result")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$result <- renderText({
      cat("Running...")
      paste("You chose", input$state)
    })
  }
)
```

When you hit backspace in shiny version < 1.1 `Running...` is not printed, however in version 1.1 it is printed everytime.

title: updateSelectInput's documentation is self-contradicting with regards to "selected"
description:
updateSelectInput's [documentation](https://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/updateSelectInput.html) claims that "Any arguments with NULL values will be ignored; they will not result in any changes to the input object on the client.", but passing "selected=NULL", or not specifying selected (as it defaults to NULL), clears the selection.

selected's param documentation _does_ say "If not specified then defaults to the first value for single-select lists and no values for multiple select lists.", even if this is odd for an "update" function.
The documentation goes on to specify that "for these inputs, the selected item can be cleared by using selected=character(0)".

Does selected really need 2 values that will clear it (character(0) and NULL), and no special values that will keep it the same? (Yes, you can pass selected=input$label to keep it the same, as mentioned in issue #1234, but it really doesn't seem like this should be necessary.)

I propose a fix where, at the very least, selected=NULL results in no change to the selection as the first line quoted above implies.
If the new default value of selected was then made to be "character(0)", the contradictions in the documentation would magically resolve with no further changes. Although I personally think that it would make more sense to keep the current selection by default.

title: Allow multiple brushes on plot
description:
Hi, a feature request:
Allow the user to select multiple regions on a plot/image and get a list of brushed rectangles.
Currently the brush on plotOutput allows only one selection, and the brush disappears when the user selects a new area.
#### Two usage alternatives:
1. By holding the control key while selecting multiple regions
2. By allowing the user to create multiple regions and delete a region by clicking on it

This would be extremely valuable for labeling/tagging purposes on images / graphs etc.

#### References:
A (simple) example of multiple brushes on d3: http://bl.ocks.org/ludwigschubert/0236fa8594c4b02711b2606a8f95f605
PR on dc.js: https://github.com/dc-js/dc.js/issues/1288

Thanks for the awesome work you're doing!

title: feature request: Support server-side file browser
description:
I'm considering migrating classes to Rstudio Cloud or using Rstudio Server Pro. The main thing that is holding me back is that shiny apps and gadgets that work in/with Rstudio don't have a good solution to load and save files to and from the server.

AFAIK the available options are:

1. Using `rstudioapi::selectFile` from an Rstudio Window. On a server this will open the file browser *behind* the app (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudioapi/issues/91). The same applies when using an external browser from Rstudio. I'm not sure if this is fixable unless, somehow the file browser could be shown in a modal.

2. Using `rstudioapi::selectFile` with Rstudio viewer works ok but tabs eat up a lot of screen real estate on a laptop screen and adjusting the viewer size resets print width which can make printed output unreadable (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1913)

`rstudioapi::selectFile` is a great feature (thanks @@kevinushey!) but still has several other [limitations](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudioapi/issues/92#issuecomment-378049112) although these will hopefully be addressed in the not too distant future after Rstudio 1.2 is out

3. The only option that works with an `external` browser is `shinyFiles`. However, this package is not actively maintained and [doesn't work with renderUI](https://github.com/thomasp85/shinyFiles/issues/25)

An additional requirement for me is access to file paths for loaded and save files. Both `selectFile` and `shinyFiles` offer this but they still have the issues above.

Is a server-side file browser that works with shiny apps something that rstudio / shiny could support?

title: rbind results from callModule to a data frame
Calling "future::resolved" inside of an observe() function occasionally causes a segfault when user interrupts R process in RStudio
description:
I discovered this while converting my package to async Shiny and trying to use the "resolved" function in futures inside an observe() function. If the user is running the app within RStudio and either interrupts the process via the console or by closing the app window, occasionally R will encounter a fatal error and have to restart.

Below is a minimal reprex. It doesn't happen every time--I believe the user has to interrupt the process when the resolved function is being checked--but I managed to cause the error to happen consistently (at least once every 10 starts and interrupts) with the below code. The high frequency of the invalidateLater call is just to make R call the "resolved" function more often to make the error occur more consistently. It occasionally occurred in my code even when the invalidateLater was set to a much more reasonable 1000.

``` r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
   titlePanel("Crash Test Shiny"),
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         actionButton("submitbutton", HTML("Submit"))
      ),
      mainPanel(
      )
   )
)
future::plan(future::multisession)
server <- function(input, output) {
  test2 = reactive({
    input$submitbutton
    future::future({
      Sys.sleep(5)
      "Future"
    })
  })
  observe({
    invalidateLater(1)
    if(future::resolved(isolate(test2()))) {
    }
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: issue with shiny modal
description:
Hi,

I have a button "launch" clicking on which opens a modal popup. In this popup I have a datatable populated, allowing users to filter records and there is a submit button.  on clicking the submit button,observeEvent(input$submit) it takes the records and populates the parent page of the modal.  I close the modal by calling removeModal().
This works fine the first time.
However if I click the "launch" button second time, it automatically calls the observeEvent of the submit button observeEvent(input$submit)  and takes the records and populates the parent page.
Is there a way to prevent this from happening.  I just want the modal to show up again for user to filter the records.

I tried putting the logic inside submit button in isolate() , but it did not resolve.

title: Firefox can’t establish a connection to the server
description:
Create a simple demo dashboard like the following:

```r
## app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "Basic dashboard"),
  dashboardSidebar(),
  dashboardBody(
    # Boxes need to be put in a row (or column)
    fluidRow(
      box(plotOutput("plot1", height = 250)),
      
      box(
        title = "Controls",
        sliderInput("slider", "Number of observations:", 1, 100, 50)
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  set.seed(122)
  histdata <- rnorm(500)
  
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    data <- histdata[seq_len(input$slider)]
    hist(data)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(host = "0.0.0.0", port = 5328))

title: Feature Request - hoverOpts - control units
description:
I would like to request that an additional parameter be added to hoverOpts and plot interaction control functions interacting with plot_output and image_output. This parameter will control the units assigned to the x y values returned by input$plot_hover, input$plot_click etc values. Currently this is assumed based on the output function plot_output or image_output. with plot_output, the units are in the same units as the data, and with image_output the units are in pixels and based on location of the mouse.

I am using treemap data and I need to associate the mouse location with one of the boxes in the treemap. treemap software will calculate the coordinates of the boxes, however, when I plot a treemap using plot_output, i receive x/y coordinates in terms of the data and this is not useful. I would like to be able to define the units as "data" or "pixel" as a parameter of the hoverOpts function. This way I can get pixel location using the plot_output function.

I then can use the pixel coordinate together with the coordinates the treemap software calculates to identify which box the user has selected. With this I can then do complex follow up calculation for the user based on the box selected in the plot.

something like 
hoverOpts(id = NULL, delay = 300, delayType = c("debounce", "throttle"),
  clip = TRUE, nullOutside = TRUE, unitsType = c("data","pixels"))

title: Clearer documentation on what types inputs return
description: Nathan used a `radioButton` with `choices = c(TRUE, FALSE)` expecting the `input$x` type to be logical, not character. We should make sure all of our input types clearly document the data types of values that will be returned.

title: IPv6 address should be bracketed within HTTP URLs
description:
When Shiny creates the HTTP URL from a running server indicating the address it is reachable on, it should bracket any IPv6 address within the URL.

For example, if binding on `::1` port `5873` (IPv6 loopback), the resulting http URL should be: `http://[::1]:5873`. Currently, Shiny will generate the URL without brackets, like `http://::1:5873` which is an invalid URL.

title: Feature request: freehand/lasso selection for brushing
description:
During a conversation at eRum2018 with @bborgesr, I managed to show a use case (out of potentially many) for this feature, which we currently (with some js flavour)  implemented in our package, iSEE (http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/iSEE.html). She suggested me to open up an issue officially for better visibility and tracking - my guess is indeed many people would fancy the freehand selection, especially when the "point cloud" is not exactly rectangular and/or the edges could play nicer if defined as a path.

A running demo for the package/app can be found here: http://shiny.imbei.uni-mainz.de:3838/iSEE_PBMC4k/ - in this case, some panels are pre-linked to each other, so you would just need to interact with the first one.

More in detail, we did implement a lasso-polygon-selection, which works by clicking point by point the edges of the polygon to be (closed once the start and end coincide). Nonetheless, it would be extremely cool to have such selection supported/streamlined in the official Shiny framework.

Thoughts from the dev team?

title: calling makeReactiveBinding on an object that already has a binding stops reactivity
description:
@jcheng5 FYI I was seeing some strange effects in my app using `makeReactiveBinding` where the data would stop being reactive at some point. Couldn't consistently reproduce. Then I added checks around all calls to `makeReactiveBinding` so the binding won't be 'created' if a binding already exists and the problem seemed to go away.

Below in screenshot and code to illustrate the issue. The code below runs in _Report > R_ in [radiant.data](https://github.com/radiant-rstats/radiant.data). Sorry, haven't had time to make an easier to reproduce example.

```r
options(width = 100)

## diamonds is reactive
bindingIsActive(as.symbol("diamonds"), env = r_data)

## making sure we don't have extra variables
diamonds <- select(diamonds, price:z)

## add a variable
diamonds <- mutate(diamonds, extra1 = 42)

## column name is added and .get_data() reactive is updated
colnames(diamonds)
colnames(.get_data())

## recreate the binding
makeReactiveBinding("diamonds", env = r_data)

## add another variable
diamonds <- mutate(diamonds, extra2 = 42)

## diamonds is still listed as reactive but ...
bindingIsActive(as.symbol("diamonds"), env = r_data)

## column name is added BUT .get_data() reactive NOT updated
colnames(diamonds)
colnames(.get_data())
```

title: inconsistent scope object passed to find method of inputs and outputs
description: On the js side of shiny, on initialization, within the [`bindOutputs()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L5-L12) function, the scope object passed to each output's find method is first transformed into a jquery object. However in [`bindInputs()`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/srcjs/init_shiny.js#L128-L135) the scope object is left as is. The articles outlining how to create custom inputs and outputs indicate the find method must transform `scope` into a jquery object. In my case I was looking to treat `scope` as a dom element, I could for custom inputs, and then could not for custom outputs. This is a small inconsistency and the fix is straightforward. Unfortunately, fixing the inconsistency would break the code of anyone who accidentally assumed `scope` was already a jquery object. Is that reason enough to leave things as they are? I would be happy to put together a tiny PR.

title: nearPoints and brushData do not work with dataframe created by splitting data frame
description:
This is an issue that arose with a shiny gadget for selecting points to label: https://github.com/AliciaSchep/gglabeller/issues/6

The goal was to be able to split a dataframe, create plots from each split, and then run the shiny app on each split.  However, this leads to an issue because when `nearPoints` (or `brushData`) is called for a ggplot made from any but the first dataframe created, it seemingly fails to recognize the points.  Below is an example adapted from the basic selection demo in the shiny documentation:

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(shiny)

#Create some data
testdata <- tibble(sample = rep(LETTERS[1:6], each = 15),
                   catvar = rep(paste0("var_",letters[1:15]), times = 6),
                   contvar = abs(rnorm(90)))

#Split data into manageable chunks for plotting by categorical variables
testlist <- testdata %>%
  mutate(catvar = as.factor(catvar),
         group = as.numeric(catvar) %>%
           cut(3) %>% #cut into how many pieces?
           as.integer()) %>% 
  split(.$group) #returns a list of dataframes

ui <- basicPage(
  plotOutput("plot1", click = "plot_click"),
  verbatimTextOutput("info")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(testlist[[2]], aes(x = catvar, y = contvar, label = sample)) +
      geom_point()
  })
  
  output$info <- renderPrint({
    nearPoints(testlist[[2]], input$plot_click, threshold = 10, maxpoints = 1,
               addDist = TRUE)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

With testlist[[2]] as the input data, nothing happens on clicking on the points.  However, with testlist[[1]] the app behaves as expected.  Similarly, if the code is adapted for brushPoints instead of nearPoints, it works okay for testlist[[1]] as a data source for the plot but not testlist[[2]].

Feature request: Argument to make shinyAppDir use a local environment
description:
Whenever I develop bigger applications in `shiny` and run them via `shinyAppDir` (or `runApp("some/path")`), my `.GlobalEnv` gets clustered with variables necessary for the app to run, which I don't like. 

My current workaround for this is to source the app object directly instead to keep the global environment clean.

```
source("path/to/app.R", local = new.env(), chdir = TRUE)$value
```

However, there are  three issues with this approach 

1. If the `server` body contains relative paths they won't be resolved as intended. 
2. The contents of `www` are not acessible.
3. If the app follows the `ui.R/server.R` interface this workaround becomes even more complicated.

I have found ways to resolve all of these issues but it is rather tiresome to do this for every app I develop and less shiny affine developers might have a hard time understanding and maintaining the code. 

It would be nice to have an optional `env` argument in `shinyAppDir` to allow launching apps in a local environment like `print(shinyApp(...))` does. This would also make it easier to pass arguments to applications although #440 and `shinyOptions` already provide good solutions. 

Following the discussion in #237, my impression was that this change should be straightforward to implement (at least back then).

title: Working with S4 data structures supplied by user - extracting data
Possible memory leak when renderPlot uses a reactiveVal from outside of session function
description:
In this example, there's a `reactiveVal` object defined outside the session function, and it it used in a `renderPlot`.

When the app is started and stopped, and then `gc()` is called, the session environment does not get garbage collected. If you start and stop the app again, and then run `gc()` again, it still does not get GC'd.


```R
data <- reactiveVal(1:10)
app <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  function(input, output, session) {
    message("Token: ", session$token)
    reg.finalizer(environment(), function(e) message("Finalizer: ", session$token))
    
    output$plot <- renderPlot({
      plot(data(), data())
    })
  }
)


app # Run app and then quit
gc() # Finalizer not run

app # Run app and then quit
gc() # Finalizer not run
```


To get the finalizer to run, you need to do:

```R
rm(data)
gc()
```


When `data` is defined inside the server function, this problem doesn't occur. Also, if `renderText` is used instead of `renderPlot`, the problem doesn't occur.

title: Memory leak with reactiveTimer and invalidateLater
Chrome opens new tab when downloadButton is clicked
description:
When a user interacts with a Shiny app in Chrome and clicks a downloadButton button, Chrome opens a new tab for the duration of the report generation. In trying to solve this problem, I came across https://community.rstudio.com/t/downloadbutton-disable-target-blank-tag/6605.

I merely redefined downloadButton, by copying/pasting code from bootstrap.R and editing it in my global.R file to be
```r
downloadButton <- function(outputId, label = "Download", class = NULL, ...) {
  aTag <-
    tags$a(
      id = outputId,
      class = paste('btn btn-default shiny-download-link', class),
      href = '',
      target = NA, #'_blank',
      download = NA,
      icon("download"),
      label,
      ...
    )
}
```
Note the only change is to make the target value be NA instead of '_blank'.

After including the redefined function in my global.R file, I have confirmed the desired behavior (i.e., no new tabs open) now exists in the latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, and Internet Explorer.

title: Implicit calls to xxxOutput not working inside modules
description:
I just answered [a question on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49721349/render-functions-dont-dispay-in-modaldialog-inside-shiny-module) regarding implicit calls to output functions (as defined by `markRenderFunction`) with shiny modules.

For some reason dynamic contents are not shown. Here is a minimal example



    ---
    runtime: shiny
    output: html_document
    ---

    This modal appears empty

    ```{r, echo = FALSE}
    secondModule <- function(input, output, sesison, trigger){
      observeEvent(
        trigger(),
        showModal(modalDialog(renderText({"Text 1"})))
      )
    }

    actionButton("btn", "show first modal")

    callModule(secondModule, "moduleId", reactive({input$btn}))
    ```

    This one does not

    ```{r, echo = FALSE}
    actionButton("btn2", "show second modal")

    observeEvent(
      input$btn2,
      showModal(modalDialog(renderText({"Text 2"})))
    )
    ```

The same behavior can be seen with `plotOutput` (See the SO link above).

The workaround I suggested was to use both `renderText`  and `textOutput` inside the module but I was wondering if this is actually a bug in the  implementation of `markRenderFunction` or if these functions are not meant to be used in such a "convoluted" way.

title: selectizeJSON should be coercing values to lowercase
description:
According to note [here](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/update-input.R#L700) data that is searched by server selectize is already in lower case, but some simple testing shows this is not the case. MRE taken from this example: https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/option-groups-for-server-side-selectize.html ```{R} library(shiny) ui <- fluidPage( selectizeInput('group', NULL, NULL, multiple = TRUE, options = list( #### ADDED THIS ONE LINE#### maxOptions = 5, placeholder = 'Select a category', # predefine all option groups optgroups = list( list(value = '1st', label = 'First Class'), list(value = '2nd', label = 'Second Class'), list(value = '3rd', label = 'Third Class'), list(value = 'Crew', label = 'Crew') ), # 'Class' is a field in Titanic2 created in server.R optgroupField = 'Class', optgroupOrder = c('1st', '2nd', '3rd', 'Crew'), # you can type and search in these fields in Titanic2 searchField = c('Sex', 'Age', 'Survived'), # how to render the options (each item is a row in Titanic2) render = I("{ option: function(item, escape) { return '
' + escape(item.Age) + ' (' + (item.Sex == 'Male' ? '♂' : '♀') + ', ' + (item.Survived == 'Yes' ? '♥' : '⊝') + ')' + '
'; } }") )), verbatimTextOutput('row'), title = 'Using options groups for server-side selectize input' ) server <- function(input, output, session) { Titanic2 <- as.data.frame(Titanic, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) Titanic2 <- cbind(Titanic2, value = seq_len(nrow(Titanic2))) Titanic2$label <- apply(Titanic2[, 2:4], 1, paste, collapse = ', ') updateSelectizeInput(session, 'group', choices = Titanic2, server = TRUE) output$row <- renderPrint({ validate(need( input$group, 'Please type and search (e.g. Female)' )) Titanic2[as.integer(input$group), -(6:7)] }) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` When I search "Adult" nothing appears because search term is coerced to lowercase "adult", but values in data.frame that are searched retain capital letters. I find that if I change code [here](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/update-input.R#L701) to `tolower(data[[v]])` everything works in this example. This issue doesn't appear when maxOptions is larger than the number of options in selectize, because I believe the server filter was simply sending all values to client and client sorting code was effectively performing filtering.

Can shinyoutput entries be removed?
description:
Can we _remove_ elements from a shinyoutput object?
Some simple testing suggests no (at least not with the first few obvious guesses):
```R
## in shinyServer(function(input, output, session)):

output$foo <- renderText("foo")

## rm(output[["foo"]]) ## doesn't work
## output[["foo"]] <- NULL ## also doesn't work
```
The reason for wanting such a function is to prevent server-side memory accumulation in long-running applications that frequently call `insertUI()` & `removeUI()`.

For example, `insertUI()` might insert a dynamically-generated `textOutput("foo", ...)` element coupled to a corresponding `output[["foo"]] <- renderText(...)` assignment to the session's `output` object. Later, when `removeUI()` removes the `textOutput("foo", ...)` element, I'd like to 'clean-up' the session's `output` object by removing the `output[["foo"]]` entry. (In this example, "foo" is a randomly-generated unique ID.)

For applications where this is a frequent procedure the UI-side of the application can be kept tidy, but I suspect the server-side `output` object simply continues to accumulate these entries.

Is there any way to _remove_ a specific entry in the `output` object by that entry's ID?
(I can't find any such function/procedure in the docs.)

title: Very slow performance with options(shiny.deepstacktrace=TRUE)
description:
Benchmarking app:

```r
#options(shiny.deepstacktrace=TRUE)

library(shiny)
library(promises)
library(future)
plan(multicore)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
  checkboxInput("deepstacktrace", "Deep stack traces enabled?", getOption("shiny.deepstacktrace", FALSE)),
  textOutput("summary"),
  actionButton("success", "Benchmark success"),
  actionButton("failure", "Benchmark failure"),
  textOutput("time")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  mode <- reactiveVal()
  elapsed <- reactiveVal()
  
  observeEvent(input$deepstacktrace, {
    options(shiny.deepstacktrace = input$deepstacktrace)
  })
  
  output$foo1 <- renderText({
    req(input$success)
    
    mode("Success")
    start_time <- Sys.time()
    promise_resolve(TRUE) %...>%
      identity %>%
      finally(~{elapsed(Sys.time() - start_time)})
  })
  outputOptions(output, "foo1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
  
  output$foo2 <- renderText({
    req(input$failure)
    
    mode("Failure")
    start_time <- Sys.time()
    promise_resolve("boom") %...>%
      stop %>%
      finally(~{elapsed(Sys.time() - start_time)}) %...!%
      {} # prevent crash
  })
  outputOptions(output, "foo2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
  
  output$time <- renderPrint({
    req(elapsed())
    isolate({
      msg <- paste(mode(), "in", format(elapsed()))
      message(msg)
      cat(msg)
    })
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

With `shiny.deepstacktrace` enabled, I'm seeing 380ms for success and 475ms for failure on average. Without it, 13ms for success and 17ms for failure (still not as fast as I would like).

title: Shiny applications on Ubuntu 16.04.3 LTS (GNU/Linux 4.4.0-97-generic x86_64) deletes its own logs
description:
I am running a simple app, which is stored in `app.R` on an Ubuntu server, which was set up according to the specifications in Dean Attali's [blog post](https://deanattali.com/2015/05/09/setup-rstudio-shiny-server-digital-ocean/) (Note: the server is not a digital ocean droplet). The code from the app is as follows:

```
library(ggradar)
library(scales)
library(tidyverse)

ui = fluidPage(
    fluidRow(
        column(width=6, offset=3,
               plotOutput('test')
        )
    )
)

server = function(input, output, server) {
    output$test = renderPlot({
        mtcars %>%
            rownames_to_column(var='group') %>%
            mutate_at(vars(-group), funs(rescale)) %>%
            tail(4) %>%
            select(1:10) -> mtcars_radar
        ggradar(mtcars_radar)
    })

    sdklfjsd
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The last line in `server()` is there to force the app to error out. If I run `ls -lah /var/log/shiny-server/` before the app crashes, I can see that the log is there. It is also there for a brief moment after the app crashes. However, after about 5 seconds of the app crashing, the log file is deleted. I don't believe this is the intended behavior, and I could not find anything online that discussed this issue.

title: renderPlot cache breaks when width/height throw
description:
Thanks to @vnijs for reporting a version of this from radiant.data.

In pre-async versions of Shiny, the following code works; click Go to make the plot appear. After the async merge, this breaks. Note that the `w`/`h` `eventReactive`s throw a `req(FALSE)` exception the first time they're called; post-async, this seems to permanently break the `drawReactive`.

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("go", "Go"),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  w <- eventReactive(input$go, { 400 })
  h <- eventReactive(input$go, { 400 })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    plot(cars)
  }, width = w, height = h)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: R shiny server + leaflet Memory leak
description:
## Background

I have to create a prototype map based dashboard for a project. I decided on R shiny, as it had the best data management for my data, and easy to use. I use Leaflet in combination with Rshiny. After creating the map, it gets updated at certain intervals and recreates the map with new data (kind off batch real time). The data will be quite a lot, but is still manageable on a leaflet application.

## Code:
```
library(shinydashboard)
library(leaflet)

ui <- fluidPage(
  dashboardBody(
    box(width = NULL, solidHeader = TRUE,
                 leafletOutput("busmap", height = 900)
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

liveish_data <- reactive({
    invalidateLater(6000)
    lat <- runif(3000, min=51, max=53.5)
    lon <- runif(3000, min=4, max=8)
    DF_Actueel <- data.frame(lat,lon)
    print("refreshed")
    DF_Actueel
  })

  output$busmap = renderLeaflet({
    DF_Actueel <- liveish_data()
    map <- leaflet(options=list())%>%
      addProviderTiles(providers$OpenStreetMap.HOT) %>%
      addMarkers(data = DF_Actueel)

    map
  })
}

title: Validation errors in futures aren't treated as errors
description:
Shiny raises errors with custom subclasses in order to trigger custom UI behavior. For example, a very common/useful feature of Shiny is the [`req` function](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html), which you use to conditionally raise a "silent" error--instead of a red error message in the UI, you get silence, which is often what you want (for example, the user hasn't selected a dataset yet, instead of `Error: No applicable method for `filter_` applied to an object of class "NULL"` you just want nothing.

```r
> library(shiny)
> te <- try(req(FALSE), silent = TRUE)
> class(attr(te, "condition"))
[1] "shiny.silent.error" "validation"         "error"              "condition"         
```

But when used with multicore/multisession futures, error subclasses don't work correctly with `value(..., signal = TRUE)`. These fail in two different ways. With multicore, `value()` returns a try-error instead of signaling:

```r
> library(shiny)
> library(future)
> plan(multicore)

> f1 <- future({ stop("boom") })
> value(f1)  # Throws error (correct)
Error: boom

> f2 <- future({ validate(need(FALSE, "Validation error")) })
> value(f2)  # Returns try-error (incorrect)
[1] "Error : \n"
attr(,"class")
[1] "try-error"
attr(,"condition")
<shiny.silent.error: >
```

And with multisession, it's signaled, but it's become a `simpleError`:

```r
> plan(multisession)
> f3 <- future({ validate(need(FALSE, "Validation error")) })
> value(f3)  # Works...?
Error : Validation error
> cond <- attr(try(value(f3), silent = TRUE), "condition")
> class(cond)  # But actually the classes are gone
[1] "FutureEvaluationError"     "FutureError"               "simpleError"              
[4] "error"                     "FutureEvaluationCondition" "condition" 
```

@HenrikBengtsson At first I thought this was a simple matter of fixing up the corresponding `value` methods for these two future types, but it occurred to me that you might've done this on purpose--like it might not be safe to serialize errors across process boundaries or something? Would love to hear your thoughts. It would be hard to ship the next version of Shiny without having a resolution to this problem.

title: [Feature request] Bookmarking: ability to initialize an app with at a bookmarked state (great for dev/testing)
description:
Related to #1874 where @bborgesr told me about `updateQueryString()`

Prior to bookmarking, when I had to do a lot of testing of things that involved many other inputs being set to particular values, I used to use a lot of `update***()` functions. Now that we have bookmarking, I've made it regular practice to always add bookmarking to apps in development, and when I need to test a specific state of the app, I bookmark, then I keep loading up the app and pasting into the URL to come back to the same state. Works great!

However, to do this I have to open up the app in the browser (as opposed to RStudio Viewer where it's faster for quick dev), and I have to paste in the URL. I would love to be able to copy a bookmarked URL, and then set it at the beginning of the app using

```
updateQueryString("?_input_&foo=bar")
```

so that every time the app starts it will automatically do it's bookmarking magic and bring me back. But bookmarking only seems to work immediately on app load, so the line above doesn't do anything useful. Maybe there could be better way to achieve that wanted behaviour rather than using updateQueryString - perhaps an `options()` flag or some function to be called prior to the app starting. It would be a nice little feature for quickly testing large apps.

title: add md() convenience function to write fragments in markdown
description:
I'm so used to writing in basic markdown (*emph*, **bold**, `pre` etc.), I can't get myself to write, say `shiny::tags$em("foo")`.
Maybe others are feeling the same.

I build myself a simple wrapper to be able to easily write markdown:

```
#' @title Convert markdown to html
#'
#' @param text A character vector to be converted to markdown.
#'
#' @param HTML A logical flag, indicating whether the result should additionally be wrapped in shiny::HTML().
#'
#' @noRd
md <- function(text, HTML = TRUE) {
  res <- markdown::renderMarkdown(
    file = NULL,
    output = NULL,
    text = text
  )
  if (HTML) {
    res <- shiny::HTML(text = res)
  }
  return(res)
}
```

which can be used wherever shiny expects HTML.

Now I can write something like:

```
fileInput(
  inputId = "rdata",
  label = md("Upload a `*.rdata` file created by *pensieve*."),
)
```
which makes life a little easier.

Is there any interest in supporting this directly in shiny? I'm guessing an `md()` function might be an alternative to / modelled on the existing `HTML()`.

If there's interest, I'd be happy to write up a PR.

---

Just to be sure, what this isn't:
- this is not about including external files, `shiny::includeMarkdown()` does that already,
- this is strictly about *Markdown*, **not** RMarkdown.

title: DOM not updated with selectInput(selective = FALSE) added with insertUI()
description:
I have a large app that implements a dynamic UI. Given the need to update only a single element at a time, I moved away from using `renderUI()` and was able to use the `insertUI()` function to successfully add/remove the UI elements needed for the project.

They work as expected with a small caveat: the DOM is not updated to reflect the selected elements as they are with renderUI(), i.e. the `selected` attribute is never added to the `option` elements. Is this by design or a bug? In short, the elements are always created and operate as expected, but my testing code is no longer able to determine the value of a selection as the DOM is left unchanged.

Please inspect the DOM in the following app after a `selectInput()` and `verbatimTextOutput()` pair has been added and some selections have been made.

```
library(shiny)

# Code license: MIT
# Using selectInput(selectize = FALSE) with insertUI()
# by Tim Thomas
# adapated from work by Bárbara Borges

ui <- fluidPage( 
  actionButton('insertBtn', 'Insert'), 
  actionButton('removeBtn', 'Remove'), 
  tags$div(id = 'placeholder') 
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  ids <- c()
  
  observeEvent(input$insertBtn, {
    id <- paste0(input$insertBtn)
    ids <<- c(id, ids)
    div_id <- paste0("div_", id)
    select_id <- paste0("select_", id)
    output_id <- paste0("output_", id)
    choices <- lapply(1:4, function(x) {paste("Choice", x)})
    insertUI(
      selector = '#placeholder',
      ui = tags$div(
        id = div_id,
        selectInput(select_id,
                    select_id,
                    choices,
                    multiple = TRUE,
                    selectize = FALSE),
        verbatimTextOutput(output_id)
      )
    )
    output[[output_id]] <- renderText(input[[select_id]])
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$removeBtn, {
    removeUI(
      selector = paste0('#div_', ids[length(ids)])
    )
    ids <<- ids[-length(ids)]
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

I first submitted this as a [topic](https://community.rstudio.com/t/dom-not-updated-with-selectinput-selective-false-added-with-insertui/4469) on community.rstudio.com. Let me know if this needs to be removed in favor of tracking it here.

title: Feature Request: buttonGrid
description:
A common feature of a Shiny app is to have a set of grouped buttons, for instance the CFL app here: https://daattali.com/shiny/cfl/

- There's a (single) column of buttons
- Clicking on a button changes the state of a variable via `Shiny.onInputChange` in `www/main.js` 

```JS
$( "#welcome_list" ).on( "click", ".welcome_row", function(x){
    Shiny.onInputChange("gamerowclick", $(this).data("gameinfo"));
  });
```
- The selected button from the group modifies the state of the app

A useful feature for `shiny` would be to group buttons together by a master input variable, and for each button in the group to have a unique id, as follows:

- Master id: input$button.master.id
- Unique button id: input$button.master.id_button.id

Please note I initially suggested this as a feature for `shinyjs` https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/issues/151 but @daattali suggested it didn't fit there but might be a reasonable thing to suggest to add to `shiny` 

# Quasi Example

```r
the_ui <- fluidPage(
  shinyjs::useShinyjs(),
  div(id = "select_game_page",
      buttonGrid(
        button.master.id = "gameid",
        button.contents = list(
          gridButton(
            button.id = "game004",
            button.text = "UK vs US"
          ),
          gridButton(
            button.id = "game006",
            button.text = "DE vs FR"
          )
        ),
        columns = 2
      )),
  
  hidden(div(id = "game_info_page",
             fluidPage(
               datatableOutput("game_info"),
               actionButton("select_another_game",
                            "Select Another Game")
             )))
  
  
)

the_server <- function(input, output){
  
  output$game_info <- renderDataTable({
    
    shinyjs::hide("select_game_page")
    shinyjs::show("game_info_page")
    
    game_data %>%
      filter(game.id == input$gameid) %>%
      datatable()
    
  })
  
  observeEvent(input$select_another_game,
               {
                 shinyjs::hide("game_info_page")
                 shinyjs::show("select_game_page")
               })
  
}

shinyApp(the_ui, the_server)
```

ggsave changed current graphic device and moved all plot in shiny out of shiny
description:
[Stackoverflow discussion](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47699956/ggplot-in-shiny-app-go-to-rstudio-plot-window/47701308)

This shiny app used `ggsave` to save a ggplot object before rendering it.

```r
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
SAVE_PLOT <- TRUE
ui <- fluidPage(fluidRow(column(12, plotOutput("plot"))))
server <- function(input, output){
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    print(dev.list())
    cat("current device:\n")
    print(dev.cur())
    g <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
    if (SAVE_PLOT) {
      ggsave("plot.png", g)
    }
    print(dev.list())
    cat("current device:\n")
    print(dev.cur())
    g
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

If user made some plot in R session,

```r
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
```

then the app will show plot in RStudio plot window instead of Shiny window.

We can see the current open graphic device changed after `ggsave`

```r
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:7766
        RStudioGD quartz_off_screen quartz_off_screen 
                2                 3                 4 
current device:
quartz_off_screen 
                4 
Saving 12.9 x 5.56 in image
        RStudioGD quartz_off_screen quartz_off_screen 
                2                 3                 4 
current device:
RStudioGD 
        2 
```

This is not limited to RStudio. R console have same problem.

Basic plot and `dev.print` don't have this problem.

We can work around the problem by saving and restoring the device before/after `ggsave`, however ideally this should not be needed for user. 


```r
      cur_dev <- dev.cur()
      ggsave("plot.png", g)
      dev.set(cur_dev)
```


I'm not sure if this is a problem in Shiny or `ggsave`, or some interaction between them.

title: Suggestion/bug: Inputs should be consistent in the type they return
description:
I think it would be a good idea to have the basic inputs try to return the same the data type whenever possible.

For example, a `numericInput()` will return `int` when the number chosen is whole, `num` when the number is not whole, and `logi NA` when the number is invalid. Perhaps it would be nicer if the same type was always returned, for example always returning `num` (or `NA_real_`, if that's the NA version of numeric)

````Rmd
---

author: "Ben Forbes"
date: "25 October 2017"
output: html_document
runtime: shiny
---

```{r}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(lubridate)
date
```

```r
library(lubridate)
##

## 
##     date
date
## function ()

title: `downloadhandler` function executed twice in RStudio Mac browser
description:
When running a Shiny app in RStudio Mac, the `content` function in `downloadhandler` will execute twice.
- click download button, a blank page and a dialog asking to confirm file name pop up.
- the `content` function run once.
- after file name was confirmed, file was saved.
- the `content` function run again.

In my app I dynamically generate some files and pack them into zip when user clicked a download button. This behavior caused the files to be generated twice.

This only apply to the RStudio builtin shiny browser(safari). The Mac Safari and Chrome don't have this problem.

There are some other random bugs, when the download process will actually start a new app instance (in Mac Safari) or download a html which is just app html (in Mac Chrome). That was not easily reproducible but should be relate to this bug.

To test the behavior, just add these two line in [the download example](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/examples/10_download/app.R):

```r
    content = function(file) {
      cat("content function started\n")
      write.csv(datasetInput(), file, row.names = FALSE)
      cat("content function ended\n")
    }
```

title: Problem passing reactive in modules
In eventReactive, ignoreNULL=TRUE prevents code from being executed even if other reactive values are being invalidated
description:
It seems to me that there are undesired side effects of setting ignoreNULL=TRUE in eventReactive():

Apparently, code will generally not be executed as long as the event equals NULL - even if other relevant events in that context occur, e.g. the change of a reactive value. As a consequence, inserting an event handler with ignoreNULL=TRUE may prevent code from beeing executed that otherwise would work fine.

Please see my example below:
```
ui <- shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("eventReactive and observeEvent"),
  sidebarPanel(
    actionButton("evReactiveButton", "Button"),
    p(),
    radioButtons("radio", "Select a value:", c("One"=1, "Two"=2, "Three"=3), selected=1)
  ),
  mainPanel(
    p("This works right from the beginning:"),
    verbatimTextOutput("myText1"),
    p("This doesn't work until the button is pressed for the first time:"),
    verbatimTextOutput("myText2"),
    p("This works right from the beginning:"),
    verbatimTextOutput("myText3")
  )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  buttonReaction1 <- eventReactive(input$evReactiveButton, ignoreNULL=FALSE, 42)

  buttonReaction2 <- eventReactive(input$evReactiveButton, ignoreNULL=TRUE, 42)

  output$myText1 <- renderText({
    b <- buttonReaction1()  # eventReactive having ignoreNULL=FALSE
    input$radio
  })

  output$myText2 <- renderText({
    b <- buttonReaction2() # eventReactive having ignoreNULL=TRUE
    input$radio
  })

  output$myText3 <- renderText({
    # No eventReactive 
    input$radio
  })
  
})

shinyApp(ui=ui,server=server) 
```

title: reactiveValues inside downloadHandler
Can't update value server selectize
Consider changing do.call(f) to do.call("f")
description:
When debugging Shiny code, the printed call stack can be absurdly large, as shown [here](https://gist.github.com/wch/d23e223437c06e3b4b46b97f7186788e). This is due to the use of `do.call(runApp, args)`. If we switch to `do.call("runApp", args)`, the call stack will be much easier to understand.

Additionally, changing the args from the form `list(a, b)` to `list(quote(a), quote(b))` will make the arguments look nicer.

I've illustrated with some examples here: https://gist.github.com/wch/2e941363ef3f6138cb6230ed0e060874

title: create a browser handler for browseURL
description:
When Shiny applications are deployed to a remote server, the `browseURL` function still attempts to use the default URL opener. On some Linux systems, this is `xdg-open`.

The `browseURL` function can be disabled by configuring the `browser` option to `"false"`:
```r
option(browser = "false")
```

Shiny should offer a handler for the `browser` option that broadcasts the URL to the client and then opens that URL in a new tab.

```r
shinyBrowseURLHandler <- function(url) { ... }
option(browser = shinyBrowseURLHandler)
```

Shiny could install this handler automatically (possibly when non-interactive?), but that might raise backwards-compatibility concerns.

title: Generalized solution to having containers/panels influence the size of their children
description:
Currently `plotOutput`, htmlwidgets, tables, etc. all have their own notion of default size. `plotOutput` defaults to 100% by 400px, htmlwidgets has a complicated scheme that depends on what kind of environment it thinks it's in. But it's currently impossible for containers like `fillRow` or `valueBox` to influence them to go to e.g. a fluid height, without resorting to JS and/or targeted solutions for specific element types.

I'd like us to think about a flexible, general solution/pattern to how containers can influence the size of their children, if they want to. I discussed this with @wch briefly and initially thought it might involve doing some clever stuff in R at tag render time, but after we explored that it seems like it makes much more sense to do something based on CSS.

title: Minor security vulnerability (user tokens in URL)
description:
This was originally reported because of a pen-test that one of our SSP customers performed ([Zendesk ticket](https://rstudioide.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/22421)). We talked about this as a team, and the point of this issue is to lay out the problem and a possible solution (and it obviously allows us to keep track of progress on this front).

### The problem
In some applications, some URLs in the page (and logs) can sometimes show a session token that preferably should either never be accessible to anyone (except the user on that particular session) or be masked to as to be useless by itself. This problem happens in apps that include downloadLink/downloadButton, but also in apps that use htmlwidgets (like DT and server-side selectInput).

To be clear, this is not a token for the SSP session (that would be really bad) but it does identify the specific Shiny session. So if two people were already connected to the same app and user A clicked a downloadButton, and user B got ahold of the URL from the logs, then user B could also download that file.

However, even though this is a valid concern, it's mostly benign, because to get ahold of the token in the URL you'd first need to get ahold of the logs. On a properly secured system (with https and the principle of least privilege applied) this shouldn't be anybody but root. That plus the fact that the session token doesn't give you the ability to auth, further narrows the usefulness of the "hole".

### Possible solution
During our team meeting, the best solution that occurred to us was to keep the raw token in the URL, but salt it with a value that is stored in the session of the Shiny app (or did I get this wrong, @jcheng5?). Only the salted token would allow you to download files, etc.

We could fix that for downloadButton by turning it from a link to a post. We couldn't do it using a cookie though, because you might have the same app open in two browser windows.

title: Get plot size from rmarkdown figure size
Allow to change the resolution of plots globally (or change the default to 96dpi)
description:
Hi,

Currently in a dynamical .rmd document, plots have a different aspect when output by regular chunks or by shiny. This is because the default resolution is different: 96dpi for regular output and 72dpi in `renderPlot`.

To make sure that plot sizes match, there are two solutions

1. either set `dpi=72` as default for regular output
2. or set `res=96` for all shiny output

Example:

````
---
title: "rmd image size"
output: html_document
runtime: shiny
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.retina=1)
library("ggplot2")
library("shiny")
```

```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=2}
ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(wt, mpg))
```

```{r  fig.width=5, fig.height=2}
# default res = 72
renderPlot({
  ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(wt, mpg))
}, width=5*72, height=2*72)
```

```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=2, dpi=72}
ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(wt, mpg))
```

```{r}
res <- 96
renderPlot({
  ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(wt, mpg))
}, width=5*res, height=2*res, res=res)
```
````

Currently solution 1 is easy to implement by setting `dpi` in `knitr::opts_chunk` but leads to poor resolution figures. It would be nicer to be able to set plot size in "in" in shiny and have `res` be read from a global option `shiny.plot.res` or something similar. In which case it would be possible to write

```
# once
options(shiny.plot.res=96)
# then
renderPlot({
  ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(wt, mpg))
}, width=5, height=2, units="in")
```

and this would match other plots.

title: using NA as an radioButtons option
description:
I am currently building an app that uses a large number of `radioButtons` for the user to input whether Yes or No was indicated on a form so the information can be added to a SQL database. However, it is not unusual for neither Yes or No to be selected on the form. Because of this, I would like a NA to be selected as a third option for the `radioButtons`. Looking at the HTML from a `radioButtons()` input with my desired values, we can see that there is no value associated with the NA option: radioButtons( inputId = "ex_legal", label = "Is over 21?", choices = list("Yes" = TRUE, "No" = FALSE, "N/A" = NA), selected = NA, inline = TRUE )
Even though there is no value associated with the "N/A" option, setting `selected = NA` still results in the correct "N/A" option being selected on the app loading. However, with no value being associated with the NA input, an empty character string is entered into the SQL database rather than an NA value. Since the columns associated with the `radioButtons` in the SQL database are booleans, the database then converts the empty strings to FALSE, which defeats the purpose of having N/A as an option. I am not sure if this behaviour is intentional or if I stumbled onto a bug. In addition to empty strings being entered into the SQL database, this issues causes the `shinyjs::reset()` function to fail when `selected = NA` in the `radioButtons` input. You can see [issue #142](https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/issues/142) in the shinyjs repo for a complete reproducible example. Thanks in advance for your help!

title: show validate(need()) errors in input widgets
description:
(Apologies if this is a completely moronic idea; I do not have the necessary big-picture view of shiny yet, just thinking about this as a naive user).

If there is an offending input (via `validate(need())`), I'd like to point users to exactly *where* they entered something bad. 
`validate()` will currently only display such an error in *place of the `renderX()` output*, which, depending on the app design, may be in a completely different place.
It seems to me that some (good) UI/UX data entry examples show you `success`/`warning`/`bad` *directly* in the input field, by, say, highlighting it in red or whatever.

I'm aware that I could (probably) build this myself with additional `renderX()` elements near *every* input element, but that just seems like a lot of cruft and duplication.

So, I was wondering, whether it might be worthwhile / possible for `validate(need())` to (optionally) "render" it's error messages to some (arbitrary) `inputID`, perhaps via an expanded `updateXInput()`.

The `validate(need())` pseudo-code in some reactive expression might read something like:

```
validate(
  need(
    expr = {input$foo != "bar"},
    message = "Bad things happen when you enter 'bar'. Be more creative.",
    label = "input$foo",  # this argument could do double duty to indicate which input label to render the error to,
    alert_input = TRUE
    # this might indicate that the error message should be rendered inside the input widget
    # would default to FALSE, in which case errors are rendered to the output objects
  )
)
```

Perhaps `updateXInput()` could then do the work of, well, updating the input widget, by, say, applying some additional "alerty" CSS, and inserting a small div with the error message.
(Though I'm not sure when in the reactive-cycle `updateXInput()` is invoked, and the whole thing would probably need to be quite fast so as not to annoy users).

Perhaps this is a way to go about https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/33.

title: Consider refactoring output/error/message queues to respect original order
description:
In the PR for dynamic tabs, I made a comment that `insertTab` and `updateTabsetInput` weren't playing together well because `insertTab` waits for flush and `updateTabsetInput` doesn't. It turns out that wasn't true, `updateTabsetInput` uses `sendInputMessage` which does wait for flush (there's a message queue). But `insertTab` uses `sendMessage` (which doesn't buffer) so it has to do it in `session$onFlush[ed]` in order to delay until the reactive flush is over.

Consider 1) adding a queue (optionally) for `sendMessage`, and 2) combining the queues so that actions take place in the order they were executed on the server. This will lead to fewer surprising ordering issues.

title: Consider tying invalidateLater and observers with session=NULL to app lifetime
description: Right now, `invalidateLater` and `observers` with `session=NULL` never get destroyed. We should consider tying them to the app lifetime like `onStop()`.

title: Complex Shiny app with many tabItems loads slowly
description:
I have a Shiny app with many (100-150) sub pages (using Shiny dashboard). All sub pages have the identical structure and just show different data (there are about 10 data tables, a few plots, and a few other controls on each page).
Starting that Shiny application from RStudio takes rather long (about 1 min).

I built a minimal example: 
```
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(DT)

# Specify number of pages
numPages <- 150
pageIds <- paste0("page", seq_len(numPages))


# Shiny module UI function (10 data tables + 5 plotly plots per page)
modTestUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    h1(id),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table1")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table2")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table3")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table4")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table5")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table6")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table7")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table8")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table9")),
    DT::dataTableOutput(ns("table10")),
    plotOutput(ns("plot1")),
    plotOutput(ns("plot2")),
    plotOutput(ns("plot3")),
    plotOutput(ns("plot4")),
    plotOutput(ns("plot5"))
  )
}

# Shiny module server function
modTest <- function(input, output, session) {
  testData <- reactive({
    mtcars
  })
  
  output$table1 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table2 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table3 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table4 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table5 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table6 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table7 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table8 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table9 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  output$table10 <- DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(testData()) })
  
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({ ggplot(testData(), aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, group = cyl)) + geom_boxplot() })
  output$plot2 <- renderPlot({ ggplot(testData(), aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, group = cyl)) + geom_boxplot() })
  output$plot3 <- renderPlot({ ggplot(testData(), aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, group = cyl)) + geom_boxplot() })
  output$plot4 <- renderPlot({ ggplot(testData(), aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, group = cyl)) + geom_boxplot() })
  output$plot5 <- renderPlot({ ggplot(testData(), aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, group = cyl)) + geom_boxplot() })
}

# UI function
ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "Test"),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenu(
      menuItem(text = "Dummy", tabName = "dummy"),
      lapply(pageIds, function(y) menuItem(text = y, tabName = y))
    )
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    do.call(
      tabItems, 
      c(
        list(tabItem(tabName = "dummy")),
        lapply(pageIds, function(x) { tabItem(tabName = x, modTestUI(x)) })
      )
    )
  )
)

# Server function
server <- function(input, output) {
  lapply(
    pageIds, 
    function(x) { callModule(modTest, id = x) }
  )
}


shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

(This loads faster than the full app, but usually still takes more than 30 seconds).

Is there a way to speed this up?
(FYI: During the useR conference I briefly discussed this with @wch)

While testing the minimal example, I also noticed that the Shiny app sometimes loads much faster (rather 10s instead of 30s). However, it is not clear to me what causes this (it seems a rather nondeterministic behavior; the code did not change at all). 
Here are two Rprofvis profiles, one from a slow and one from a fast startup: 
[profiles.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/files/1155144/profiles.zip)

Would be great if you could look into this.

Thank you very much!

title: shiny ignores nested child Rmds
description:
In brief:
What happens: The shiny app does not run because it does not have all the files in the temporary directory in which it is running, when there are nested Rmarkdown chunks included as children.
What should happen: The child files should be copied over so that the shiny application can find them

Details:

I have three markdown files, `test.Rmd`, `child1.Rmd`, and `child2.Rmd`. The file `test.Rmd` is the "main" file, and the others will be included as children: `test.Rmd` will include `child1.Rmd` as a child in a chunk, and `child2.Rmd` will in turn be included by `child1.Rmd`. 

If I use `runtime: shiny`, the nested child `child2.Rmd` is not found in the temporary folder where the application is run. Shiny reports the error "Cannot open the connection" (for `child2.Rmd`). 

`test.Rmd` content:

    ---
    output:html_document:
    runtime: shiny
    ---
    
    ## Read in child
    
    ```{r child='child1.Rmd'}
    ```

`child1.Rmd` content:


    ### Read in second child, from child
    
    ```{r child = "child2.Rmd"}
    ```

`child2.Rmd` content:

    This is a test.

The issue seems to be that the shiny runtime does not know about `child2.Rmd` and therefore doesn't copy it over. `test.Rmd` compiles just fine when `runtime: shiny` is commented out, or when the following is added to the end of `test.Rmd`:

    ```{r child='child2.Rmd', eval = FALSE}
    ```

This seems to alert the shiny runtime that `child2.Rmd` is needed so that it is copied over properly.

title: Random seed is affected by running app
description:
This should display the same result each time you run the app, but it doesn't:

```R
library(shiny)

a <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(verbatimTextOutput("txt")),
  function(input, output) {
    output$txt <- renderText(runif(1))
  }
)

set.seed(123)
runApp(a)

set.seed(123)
runApp(a)
```

Another demo app that shows that the random seed changes even though it shouldn't:

```
a <- shinyApp(
  fluidPage(verbatimTextOutput("txt")),
  function(input, output) {
    output$txt <- renderText({
      digest::digest(.GlobalEnv$.Random.seed)
    })
  }
)
runApp(a)
runApp(a)
```

title: Japanese "SO" letter causes JSON error in `renderDataTable`
description:
When I read a CSV file (by `read.csv`) generated by MS Excel, in CP932 encoding, and rendered it through `renderDataTable`, shiny app raises a JSON error.
![so](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12293919/27212289-d13cf162-5299-11e7-8498-b9bc6518eff9.PNG)

Apparently, it only occurs when the data includes Japanese "SO" letter ("\u30bd" in UTF-8) in the data.
Inspecting the JSON string generated, it seems a backslash is inserted after the "SO" letter, which makes it an invalid JSON.
```
{"draw":1,"recordsTotal":1,"recordsFiltered":1,"data":[["ソ\","so"]]}
```

The error occurs if the data frame has been read from the CSV file directly.  No error occurs if the same data frame is generated inline.

Also, the error does not occur if the letter is parsed by `gsub` function once by:
```{r}
x$jpg <- gsub("\u30bd", "\u30bd", x$jpg)
```
I am currently using this as a workaround to avoid the error.
But, if there is more fundamental solution would be appreciated.

Here is a minimal code example.
```r
library(shiny)

title: running shinyApps synchronously when multiple inline
description:
I apologize if this has already been covered, but I exhausted all the search terms I could on Shiny issues and StackOverflow and found nothing.  I am guessing this is something simple, but let's say we have more than one `shinyApp` inline, and we want each to run all with a single `CTRL+Enter`.  **Please note I am not trying to run the two Shiny apps simultaneously.  I would like to run them synchronously.**

```
app <- shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
        numericInput("n", "n", 1),
        plotOutput("plot")
    ),
    server = function(input, output) {
        output$plot <- renderPlot( plot(head(cars, input$n)) )
    }
)

runApp(app)
runApp(app)
```

`runApp` only runs once.  While this may seem dumb, if we think about Shiny gadgets, then we might want the return value from one gadget to then feed a second `gadget1() %>% gadget2()`.  For my specific use case, see https://github.com/r-spatial/mapedit/issues/24.

Is this possible, or is there a workaround?

Thanks so much!

title: output is not refreshed after (slow?) reactive is done
description:
Dear Shiny developers/community,

I have a fairly complex app processing lots of data on a big machine.

---

Specifically, I have a huge `tibble` `input.data` that is loaded with upon startup and filtered based on several criteria using drop-downs (some of the `selectInputs` are generated dynamically on the fly, depending on prior choices).
The filtered data is then used to create an interactive heatmap (`plotlyOutput`). There are several additional inputs customizing the heatmap generation incl. the number of clusters to assign the rows to.
Then, some columns of the input data are summarized across columns, and merged with the cluster information from the heatmap.
The resulting table is shown using `dataTableOutput` and downloadable through a `downloadButton`.

As many of these steps are quite slow, I make extensive use of `reactive`s, to cache the filtered data, the heatmap, the summarized data (i.e. "`annotation`") and the output table.

---

This app used to work without a problem for month and withou changing code I now encountered the following problem:

It is 'normal' that the outputs are replaced by errors in the beginning, while the slow operations still run.
I can catch this by testing for valid input and returning `NULL` otherwise, but here is actually helps to explain the issue:

---

*expected behavior*

Initially, the heatmap & the output table outputs show errors (as the filtered data does not exists yet).
After a while, they both appear.

*new behaviour*:

Initially, the heatmap & the output table outputs show errors (as the filtered data does not exists yet).
After a while, the heatmap appears, **but the output table still shows the error**.
The computation of all `reactive`s must have finished successfully, as I can download the (correct!) output table via the button.

---

Here are the corresponding code snippets:

```R
# ui.R

#...
dataTableOutput("table"),
downloadButton("table.xlsx.export.button",label="Export table")

#...
```

```R
#server.R

#...

table.object <-
  reactive(
    heatmap.object() %>%
    generate.table(annotation())
  )

output$table <-
  renderDataTable(gene.annotation())

output$table.xlsx.export.button<-
  downloadHandler(
    filename=get.table.xlsx.name,
    content=
      function(file){
        table.object() %>%
        save.table.xlsx(file)
      }
    )

#...
```

---

Attempting to cut my code down to a MWE, I ended up at a working state that is just plain puzzling:

If I rename the `outputId` of the table from `"table"` to `"test"` (and change the corresponding `server.R` line from `output$table <-` to `output$test <-`), the app works again.
As it did with the original `outputId` before.

---

I tried to further cut this down but when I remove the heatmap and the download button, minimize the `input.data` and drop all but the first filtering step, showing the input data in the table instead of the intended output, it works with both `outputId`s.

I tested many different names and besides `test` only `table.gene` happens to work.
Interestingly, these two work 100% of the cases I tried (which at least for `test` is a lot).

So I doubt that there are confounding factors and I think that the calculation of the heatmap takes a long time, somehow triggering a bug in Shiny's scheduling.

---

I will keep working on narrowing it dow but maybe you have an idea?

Could it depend on the order in which elements are refreshed?
Would this be influenced by the `outputId`?
I didn't find a pattern (`test1`,`test2`,`test3`,`test4`,`testy`,`gene.tables` and `talbe.gnee` don't work), but maybe it isn't the `outputId` itself that matters but some kind of hash of it?

---

I'm really stuck and desperate after several days of trying to figure this out.

---

I did not update shiny or R on the machine in question.
I reproduced this on three different machines with two different versions of R (3.3.3 and 3.4.0).
Unfortunately, I am not allowed to share the data used by my app.

---

Sorry for the long report but I didn't know what might be useful for you as this just doesn't appear to be logical at all.

Best,
Marcel

title: Avoid browser refresh in Shiny triggering observe() restart
description:
Suppose I have the following Shiny app (minimally-reproducible example):

**`global.R`**

    # Clear environments
    rm(foo.insert)
    rm(.test)
    if (!exists('.test')) .test <- new.env()
    
    library(shiny)
    
    ## Setup
    set.seed(1234)
    .test$foo <- data.frame(replicate(10,sample(0:100,5,rep=TRUE)))  # nrow(.test$foo) returns 5
    
    foo.insert <- function(x) {
      newRow <- sample(0:100,5,rep=TRUE)
      newDf <- rbind(x, newRow)
      assign(x = 'foo', value = newDf, envir = .test)  # Add 1 row and reassign .test environment
      cat(paste0(Sys.time(), ' Foo now has ', nrow(newDf), ' rows.\n'))
    } # foo.insert(.test$foo)

**`ui.R`**:

    shinyUI(navbarPage(title = "TestApp",
                       tabPanel("Home",
                                withTags({
                                  div(class="container", checked=NA,
                                      div(class="jumbotron", checked=NA, 
                                          h4("Testing123"),
                                          tableOutput("downloadTable")))
                                }),
                                icon = NULL),
                       footer = NULL
    ))

**`server.R`**:

    shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
        
        ## Set up observers
        updateFoo <- observe({
          invalidateLater(30*1000, session = NULL)  # Update every 30 seconds
          foo.insert(.test$foo)
        }, priority = 1)
        
        ## Reactively get the table data (to pass into the render function) every x seconds
        tableData <-reactivePoll(30*1000, session = NULL,
                                 checkFunc = function() {Sys.time()},
                                 valueFunc = function() {
                                   get('foo', .test)
                                 })
        
        
        output$downloadTable <- renderTable({
          tableData()
        }, width = '100%')
        
      })

Here's the problem:

The loads and seems to run. I call my `foo.insert()` function inside the `observe` in my server definition which gets the underlying data on some interval (here, I set it to 30 seconds). Because I added the `cat` output in the definition, I can confirm in the console within RStudio that it is indeed running correctly every 30s.

When I open the app inside my web browser (RStudio > Run App > Open in Browser), I notice that doing so re-runs the `foo.insert()` function within my `observe` as if the app was just launched. **This also happens when I do a page refresh (F5)** -- and is confirmed by the `Sys.time()` in my function's `cat` console output. In other words, every time I hit F5, it executes the function irrespective of the observer.

Obviously this is not desirable for my app (the function should run server-side every 30s regardless of what the user does). How can I fix this?

**EDIT:** Updated above with less-complex reproducible code (in case anybody else has this same question). Thanks Winston for chiming in -- I wasn't aware you could have the `observe()` function run outside of `shinyServer` and after some initial testing (moving it to my `global.R`) that seems to have done the trick.

title: Initialize radio buttons without any choices provided
description:
This is possible for `checkboxGroupInput()`, but not for `radioButtons()`. The use case is when the user wants to create the choices dynamically via `updateRadioButtons()`. This isn't trivial to implement, as it is for `checkboxGroupInput()` because (as of now, at least), `radioButtons()` always wants to select something (so there has to be something to be selected)... Maybe we could make an exception to this..?

Working code for `checkboxGroupInput()`:
```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  checkboxGroupInput("ch", "Checkboxes", choices = character(0))
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "ch", choices = 1:3)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Non-working code for `radioButtons()`:
```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("rb", "Radio buttons", choices = character(0))
) # This errors with "Error in args$choiceValues[[1]] : subscript out of bounds"
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  updateRadioButtons(session, "rb", choices = 1:3)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Note: the error is basically unchanged in Shiny > 1.0.1: `Error in choices[[1]] : subscript out of bounds`
