title: Interaction between bookmarking and existing query parsing
description:
This Shiny gallery application shows an example where the URL query string might be used to initialize application state.
https://gallery.shinyapps.io/032-client-data-and-query-string/?foo=bar&icky=scratchy

Is there documentation discussing how user query parsing might interact with Shiny URL bookmarks? I see that https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/advanced-bookmarking.html has information about custom `onBookmark` and `onRestore` callbacks.

In particular, if I add a query argument after the `_inputs_` token, like:
> http://localhost:3939/content/8/?_inputs_&caps=true&txt=%22upwhen%22&icky=scratchy

Shiny errs with:
> Error in RestoreContext initialization: Failed to parse URL parameter "icky"
This is because my `scratchy` value is not wrapped with `%22`.

If I present a non-bookmark query argument that does not encounter parsing difficulty, there is no error; the argument is silently ignored.
> http://localhost:3939/content/8/?_inputs_&caps=true&txt=%22upwhen%22&answer=42

If I visit a Shiny application using query arguments:
> http://localhost:3939/content/8/?answer=42
and then ask for a bookmark, the initial query arguments are lost:
> http://localhost:3939/content/8/?_inputs_&caps=false&txt=%22%22

Maybe just recommend against custom query parsing when using bookmarking...

Related to #1643

title: Handle bookmarks if app code has changed
description:
RSC now supports bookmarkable state and will be shipping with this support next week. In RSC it is really easy for user's to update code or rollback code. This means today it'd be easy for a user to deploy a new version of an app that breaks existing bookmarks.

There are a few ways I can think of that we could address this user story:

1. We do nothing. Bookmarkable state is something that users have to opt-in to by adding code. That means it is on them to be smart about updating apps that have bookmarks in them. 

2. We could make changes in RSC to warn the app author during a rollback or during a re-deploy if that app has bookmarks. This would require a lot of invasive changes in RSC and potentially the IDE.
 
3. We could make some changes to Shiny to try and handle an update better. For example, if there are discrepancies between the bookmark and the app, we could load the default with a warning. The changes would be picked up by SSP, RSC, and OS SS.

My vote is for #3. 


@trestletech @wch could you weigh in on this issue?

title: session can crash if doBookmark called too early
description:
Hi,

We were planning to set up an application that periodically saves the user state. Unfortunately, if doBookmark is called too early, it appears to interfere with the restore process and causes the session to crash.

The below code can be used to demonstrate the issue. If you run the application, open it in the browser and refresh a few times (approximately 5-10 times), then it will usually crash the session at least once with the error:

```
Warning: Error in getCurrentRestoreContext: No restore context found
Stack trace (innermost first):
    31: getCurrentRestoreContext
    30: observerFunc
     1: runApp
```

Below is the code for minimal reproducible example (need to refresh the browser a few times to induce error, in real life this seems to affect about 10% of page loads):

```
library(shiny)
ui <- function(request) {
  fluidPage(
    tagList()
  )
}

server <- function(input,output,session) {
  enableBookmarking("url")

  load_timer <- reactiveTimer(30e3)

  observeEvent(load_timer(), {
    session$doBookmark()
  })
}

shinyApp(ui,server)

```

Regards,

Andras

title: Feature Request: allow selectizeInput to be passed HTML
description:
In light of a recent PR (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/1521), Winston and I were talking that it may be nice to allow a similar thing for `selectizeInput()`. This would entail two things:

1. allowing users to pass two args (`choiceNames` and `choiceValues`), instead of one (`choices`). We may do this in #1521 still, so that the APIs for constructing `radioButtons`, `checkboxGroupInput` and `select(ize)Input` look similar and consistent. 

2. allowing the `choiceNames` argument to `selectizeInput` (does not apply to `selectInput`) be a list whose elements can be arbitrary HTML/tags objects.

For example, it would be nice to allow users to do something like [this](https://selectize.github.io/selectize.js/#demo-github).

title: Modules and conditional panels
description:
(Edited: there's really only one bug and the original post was misleading)

It's impossible to do the following (which I think is how everyone would go about using modules + conditional panels):

```r
conditionalPanel(
 condition = paste0("input.", ns("smooth"), " == true"),
 ...
)
```
since the namespacing that `ns` provides for modules includes a dash (i.e. `moduleID-elementID`), JS gets mad, and we need to at least do a good job of documenting that, since there's no expectation that users should know the internals of how namespacing works (but in this case, this obviously becomes relevant).  When the `condition` of a conditionalPanel involves an input or output coming from a module, you need to do this (use brackets instead of a dot):

```r
conditionalPanel(
 condition = paste0("input['", ns("smooth"), "'] == true"),
 ...
)
```

Which is not really ideal... But unless we want to change the internals of `NS` (which I don't think we do), we need to document this. I'd suggest doing it in the three places that people are probably going to check if they get in trouble:
- documentation for conditional panel
- article for dynamic UI (section on conditional panel)
- article for modules (just a note)

title: modalDialog inside a tab does not always show up
Negative click coordinates & domain with ggplot2 when combining coord_flip with scale_reverse
description:
The click object produced from a ggplot2 works correctly when using `coord_flip`, and when using `scale_x_reverse` or `scale_y_reverse`. However, when the flipped coordinates are combined with a negative scale, the `x`, `y`, and `domain` elements of the resulting list are all incorrectly negated.

This is easy to work around if one is aware of the problem, but it is confusing.

Minimal example:

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
    fluidRow(
        column(3, plotOutput("p_plain", click = clickOpts("click_plain"))),
        column(3, plotOutput("p_flip", click = clickOpts("click_flip"))),
        column(3, plotOutput("p_reverse", click = clickOpts("click_reverse"))),
        column(3, plotOutput("p_both", click = clickOpts("click_both")))
    ),

    fluidRow(
        column(3, verbatimTextOutput("info_plain")),
        column(3, verbatimTextOutput("info_flip")),
        column(3, verbatimTextOutput("info_reverse")),
        column(3, verbatimTextOutput("info_both"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    data <- data.frame(X = c(3, 5, 5), Y = c(0, 20, 5))

    p <- ggplot(data, aes(X, Y)) + geom_path()

    output$p_plain   <- renderPlot( p + ggtitle("plain"))
    output$p_flip    <- renderPlot( p + coord_flip() + ggtitle("coord_flip"))
    output$p_reverse <- renderPlot( p + scale_x_reverse() + ggtitle("scale_x_reverse"))
    output$p_both    <- renderPlot( p + scale_x_reverse() + coord_flip() + ggtitle("both"))

    output$info_plain   <- renderPrint( input$click_plain[c(1,2,4)] )
    output$info_flip    <- renderPrint( input$click_flip[c(1,2,4)] )
    output$info_reverse <- renderPrint( input$click_reverse[c(1,2,4)] )
    output$info_both    <- renderPrint( input$click_both[c(1,2,4)] )

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
````

title: validateIcon in actionLink
description:
In the current version of shiny, `actionLink` is defined in the following way
```
actionLink <- function(inputId, label, icon = NULL, ...) {
...codes...
  list(validateIcon(icon), label)
...codes...
}
```

That basically means that everything putting as the third item after `inputId` and `label` will be treated as an `icon` and will need to pass the `validateIcon` check. As a result, when users don't want an icon but forgot to define `icon = NULL`, the `...` gets his chance to be checked by `validateIcon` and in most cases, it will return an error message saying `Error in validateIcon: Invalid icon. Use Shiny's 'icon()' function to generate a valid icon`.

One example is the first issue in giphyr
 https://github.com/haozhu233/giphyr/issues/1
I fixed it by defining `icon = NULL` https://github.com/haozhu233/giphyr/commit/62662d137b1fad390391a5129ca02e5ab377ab83

title: brush on plot got wrong value with coord_fixed in ggplot2
description:
I found the zoom in with brush for my plot always miss a big chunk of area. It turned out Shiny brush didn't return correct x, y values when `coord_fixed` is used, i.e. the scale in x y is same but the x y range is different.

This is a minimal example modified from the zoom example, and turn on shiny trace to show the brush values. With `coord_cartesian` the brush value is correct. 

I guess `coord_fixed` did some transformation with the scale and that was not recognized by the brush value calculation.

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
options(shiny.trace = TRUE)
dat <- data.frame(
  xval = runif(40,-60000,60000),
  yval = runif(40,-15000,15000)
)
ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 8, class = "well",
           h4("Brush and double-click to zoom"),
           plotOutput("plot1", height = 600,
                      dblclick = "plot1_dblclick",
                      brush = brushOpts(
                        id = "plot1_brush",
                        resetOnNew = TRUE
                      )
           )
    )
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Single zoomable plot (on left)
  ranges <- reactiveValues(x = NULL, y = NULL)
  
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(dat, aes(xval, yval)) +
      geom_point() +
      coord_fixed(xlim = ranges$x, ylim = ranges$y)
    #coord_cartesian(xlim = ranges$x, ylim = ranges$y)
  })
  
  # When a double-click happens, check if there's a brush on the plot.
  # If so, zoom to the brush bounds; if not, reset the zoom.
  observeEvent(input$plot1_dblclick, {
    brush <- input$plot1_brush
    if (!is.null(brush)) {
      ranges$x <- c(brush$xmin, brush$xmax)
      ranges$y <- c(brush$ymin, brush$ymax)
      
    } else {
      ranges$x <- NULL
      ranges$y <- NULL
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Feature Request: inputTable
description:
rhandsontable is a truly wonderful R package to create spreadsheet-like inputs to shiny apps (thanks to @jrowen) but it has a couple of downsides. One is that it does not work on mobile devices, e.g., tablets, (because the underlying handsontable library doesn't). The other is that there is no strong separation between inputs and outputs (as far as I understand it, the widget serves as both) which can often be confusing during programming as it deviates a bit from regular shiny programming. It would be great if shiny had its own, dedicated inputTable widget with similar functionality as rhandsontable. 
In fact, this idea is very old, as a similar feature (called inputmatrix or matrixinput) is sitting in the shiny incubator for several years now.

title: Incorrect ggplot2 click coordinates when using fixed aspect ratio
description:
When using `coord_fixed()` with ggplot2, the coordinates returned by clicking on the plot do not take into account the fact that ggplot2 has changed the extent of its plotting window.

Minimal example:
```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
    plotOutput("mainPlot", click = clickOpts("mainPlotClick")),
    verbatimTextOutput("clickReading")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
    data <- data.frame(x = c(-10,10), y = c(-10,10))
    
    output$mainPlot <- renderPlot(
        ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + coord_fixed()
    )
    
    output$clickReading <- renderPrint( input$mainPlotClick[1:2] )
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Clicking shows that the x coordinate corresponds to where the plot is before the `coord_fixed()` is applied. Commenting out the `coord_fixed()` has everything working properly.

reactivePoll leaks the polling observer
description:
(I am going to use reactiveFileReader as an example, since it directly uses reactivePoll and is easier to use as a demonstration)

Imagine this use case:
```
reactiveReader <- reactiveFileReader(100, session, somePath, readLines)
observer <- observe({
   content <- reactiveReader()
   ## do some magic stuff with content here
   if (!is.null(observer)) {
      observer$destroy()
      observer <- NULL
      reactiveReader <- NULL
   }
})
```

After executing this code, the programmer will probably think that the reactiveReader is properly cleaned-up and the polling mechanism has been properly disposed of.

Wrong.

Thanks to the leaked observer on line [1316](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/19623694f585c8e7a8cf2c38e831a6752e5520c6/R/reactives.R#L1316), the polling function will keep getting executed and as far as I know there is no way to actually cancel it.

If you have a long lasting session, this can and will cause a lot of trouble :)

title: Do shiny/RStudio support the Selection and execCommand API's?
description:
Hi,

I am working on a small package, called rclipboard (https://github.com/sbihorel/rclipboard), which intends to provide a shiny UI button with copy-to-clipboard functionality. This is achieved by "wrapping" the button code around the HTML5-based clipboard.js (https://www.clipboardjs.com) javascript framework. Essentially, this packages will do with clipboard.js what the zeroclipr R package (https://github.com/smbache/zeroclipr/) does with the Flash-based zeroclipboard.js framework.

clipboard.js relies upon the Selection and execCommand API's, which are supported by most modern web browsers.

Interestingly, my copy-to-clipboard button works just fine when it is included in an app deployed on a Shiny server, but it does not when the same app is run locally from RStudio. While there could be many reasons why this is the case, I wanted to start by asking whether shiny/RStudio support the Selection and execCommand API's.

Thanks for you help.

PS: the same question was posted on Shiny Discuss a while ago but received no reply yet.

title: Feature: way of affecting a family of inputs all at once
description:
## Motivation

For example, let's say that you generate arbitrarily many `actionButton()`s dynamically with `insertUI()`, and these have ids like `btn1`, `btn2`, `btn3`... You, as the app author, have no way of knowing how many action buttons there are in the app at any given moment. However, you want the set a behavior in your `server` function, such that whenever one of those buttons is clicked, an identical or similar task is performed.

If you were only doing this for `btn1`, it's trivial:

``` r
observe({
  input$btn1
  # stuff
})
```

It may be nice to allow this for all buttons (or for all buttons with the same prefix or class or whatever level of specificity we decide is appropriate). E.g.:

``` r
observe({
  withInput(startsWith = "btn")
  # stuff
})
```

This may sound a little contrived, but even this basic functionality seems useful to me. To make it less contrived, but more complicated, consider the scenario in which you could access some variable about the element, while still only needing to set the behavior once. For example, let us say that you want fill a `uiOutput` slot with the picture of the person whose name is the label of each action button (assume we have a function `getPicByName()`). Then you'd need to know the label of the element inside the reactive block. Something like:

``` r
renderUI({
  btn <- withInput(startsWith = "btn")
  getPicByName(btn$label)
})
```

@jcheng5, @wch, what do you think?

title: dateRangeInput broke in 14.1
description:
Hello!

One of my apps broke when I updated to 14.1. I was able to track the the problem to down to `dateRangeInput()`. 

Here is a small reproducible example. This is the stock template shiny app that you get in Rstudio going File >> New File >> Shiny Web App, with an additional `dateRangeInput()`.

```
#
# This is a Shiny web application. You can run the application by clicking
# the 'Run App' button above.
#
# Find out more about building applications with Shiny here:
#
#    http://shiny.rstudio.com/
#

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

   # Application title
   titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),

   # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins 
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         sliderInput("bins",
                     "Number of bins:",
                     min = 1,
                     max = 50,
                     value = 30)

         # ------ comment this out and the app works again ----------
         ,dateRangeInput( "dateRange",
                          "Manually Update Visible Date Range to:",
                          label = 'Date range input: yyyy-mm-dd',
                          start = "2015-10-15", end = "2016-02-01" )
         # ----------------------------------------------------------


      ),

      # Show a plot of the generated distribution
      mainPanel(
         plotOutput("distPlot")
      )
   )
))

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  # this browser() is never evaluated if dateRangeInput() bugs out in ui.R
    browser() 
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
      # generate bins based on input$bins from ui.R
      x    <- faithful[, 2] 
      bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

      # draw the histogram with the specified number of bins
      hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
   })
})

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


```

With this, no plot output is ever produced. It actually appears that the server code is never run, (the `browser()` call is never triggered in the server). In the javascript console the error is `_UTCDataAsLocal` attempting to access a null date, and it appears to be some kind of fatal error on the javascript side that prevents any R server side code from running.

title: Brushing issue with facet_grid when scales="free",space="free"
Brush with facet_grid doesn't select correct points
description:
Hi Cheng,

Please run the reproducible code.

Here are two box plots created. The upper one is simple. The bottom one is a box plot with `facet_grid`. 

The idea is to link them together. Brushing points in one of them will highlight the points and the ones in the other box plot.

Now, selecting points in one box plot seems not to be functioning well.

And the box plot with `facet_grid` even doesn't work with itself. 

```
    library(shiny)
    library(ggplot2)


    server <- function(input, session, output) {

      mtcars$cyl = as.character(mtcars$cyl)
      mtcars$gear = as.character(mtcars$gear)

      vals <- reactiveValues( keeprows = FALSE)

      observeEvent(input$brush_1,{
        Res=brushedPoints(mtcars,input$brush_1,allRows = TRUE)
        vals$keeprows = Res$selected_
      })
      observeEvent(input$brush_2,{
        Res=brushedPoints(mtcars,input$brush_2,allRows = TRUE)
        vals$keeprows = Res$selected_
      })


      output$table1 = renderPrint({
        brushedPoints(mtcars,input$brush_1,allRows = TRUE)
      })

      output$table2 = renderPrint({
        brushedPoints(mtcars,input$brush_2,allRows = TRUE)
      })

      output$plot_1 = renderPlot({
        set.seed(123)
        ggplot(mtcars,aes(x=cyl,y=mpg)) + 
          geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
          geom_jitter(aes(color=vals$keeprows),width=0.2)+
          scale_color_manual(values = c("black","red"),guide=FALSE)    
      })
      output$plot_2 = renderPlot({
        set.seed(123)
        ggplot(mtcars,aes(x=cyl,y=mpg)) + 

          facet_grid(.~gear)+

          geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
          geom_jitter(aes(color=vals$keeprows),width=0.2)+
          scale_color_manual(values = c("black","red"),guide=FALSE)

      })


    }

    ui <- fluidPage(

      plotOutput("plot_1",brush = brushOpts("brush_1",resetOnNew = FALSE)),
      plotOutput("plot_2",brush = brushOpts("brush_2",resetOnNew = FALSE)),
      splitLayout(verbatimTextOutput("table1"),verbatimTextOutput("table2"))

    )

    shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

How can we solve this problem and make `facet_grid` work fine with `brush`.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/40102096/r-shiny-brush-with-facet-grid-doesnt-select-correct-points

Thank you.

title: Request: Brushing with grid graphics
description:
This is a feature request. My understanding is that Shiny plotOutput interaction currently supports base graphics and ggplot2. I would like to request support for grid graphics. grid graphics allows multiple named viewports to be created, and it would be useful to be able to map interaction into those named viewports.

Currently, I am using the hack below to set up base graphics to match a grid viewport.

```
output$plot <- renderPlot({

    # ... draw some grid graphics ...

    seekViewport("...someviewport...")
    par(new=T, plt=gridBase::gridPLT())
    plot(1, type="n", axes=F, 
         xlab="", ylab="", 
         xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1),
         xaxs="i", yaxs="i")
})
```

Thank you for providing this very useful library to the R community.

title: Feature request: provide a way to include code in both the UI and the server with only one call
description:
Currently, if you write a function for a package that requires some UI code (such as adding javascript to the page or adding UI elements) as well as server logic, you have to expose two functions to the user: one to call in the UI, one to call in the server. It'd be great if there was a way for the user to call one function that would both add code to the UI and to the server portion of the app.

I can provide more details or clarification if needed

title: More informative error messages when a required param is missing from the input* functions
description:
Anecdotally (at least for me and from seeing questions on SO and from seeing people's emails to me), one very common error when writing shiny code is forgetting to set one of the required parameters. Usually the label, but sometimes the id or the "min"/"max"/"value".

The error messages that get printed out are usually from downstream and are not direct enough to tell the user exactly which param is missing, and more importantly which function the error was in.  Example:

```
> sliderInput("Whoops forgot my id!", 1, 10, 5)
Error in force(default) : argument "value" is missing, with no default
> sliderInput("Whoops forgot my id!", min=1, max=10, value=5)
Error in tag("div", list(...)) : 
  argument "label" is missing, with no default
> textInput("text")
Error in label %AND% tags$label(label, `for` = inputId) : 
  argument "label" is missing, with no default
```

 It'd be helpful IMO if the error would say which function caused it (helpful for the last 2 examples) and spell out exactly the problem (helpful for the first example)

The main downside is that the source code might get cluttered with a lot of redundant checks if this is not done in a more clever generic way.

As with the last few issues I submitted, I'd be happy to help with the code since it requires no brain power :)

title: When using the `shiny.trace` option, allow specifying to only log SEND or RECV messages (or both)

It's great to have the ability to debug apps using `options(shiny.trace=TRUE)`.  But often I find the information to be overwhelming and I'm often only interested in seeing either the RECV or the SEND messages, so it'd be nice if we had a way to specify that.

I  can submit a PR if a shiny team member thinks this is acceptable.

title: shiny::brushedPoints fails to detect axis variables in dev version of ggplot2
description:
I am not sure whether this should be considered a bug in `ggplot2` or in `shiny`, so I am filing it in both places ([here is the issue at ggplot](https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/1850) )

When using the dev version of `ggplot2`, attempts to use `shiny::brushedPoints` leads to the error:

> Error in brushedPoints: brushedPoints: not able to automatically infer `xvar` from brush

I reverted to the stable version of `ggplot2`, and the same code works. I am not clear enough on the structure of the communication to track down what is going wrong. I will try to start digging tomorrow.

Here is minimal code to reproduce the error. Simply brushing on the plot causes the app to crash.

```
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    iris %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Sepal.Length
                 , y = Sepal.Width)) +
      geom_point()
  })

  observeEvent(input$point_Brush, {
    brushedPoints(iris, input$point_Brush)
  })

}

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    plotOutput("distPlot"
               , brush = "point_Brush")
  )

)

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

Pretty much all browsers these days support it, even IE8. See:

title: Request: allow selectize input to be initialized as server-side
description:
It'd be convenient if we could initialize a selectize as `selectizeInput("select", "Select one", choices = letters, server = TRUE)` rather than having to call `updateSelectizeInput(..., server = TRUE)`.

Similarly, after a selectize input gets updated to `server=TRUE` once, it would make sense to me that it would remain server-side when the choices get updated in the future. But that does not seem to be the case, it looks like every single time the `updateSelectizeInput()` is called with new `choices`, the `server=TRUE` argument has to be supplied again.

Sorry for no reproducible example, hope the report is clear and easy enough

title: Allow Customization of Reload Gray-out Screen

Either way, it'd be good if users could customize and brand this "reload" gray out screen.

title: Fix source ref tests when package is byte-compiled with R-devel
description:
This is from an email from Tomas Kalibera:
# 

I have been looking at why shiny is not working with the R byte-code compiler. Before R-71397 it could not as the byte code compiler did not support source reference tracking (obtaining lines of code), but starting with this version the support has been added. The plan is to switch the byte-code compiler on by default, soon, so this is why I am looking at why several remaining packages don't work with it.

Shiny tests are failing with R-71397 (from https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk) and the byte-code compiler on

```
env R_ENABLE_JIT=3 R_COMPILER_SUPPRESS_ALL=true ./bin/R CMD check down/shiny_0.14.tar.gz
```

The reason is that the shiny tests capture certain aspects of the source references that cannot really be made the same as with the AST interpreter. With the compiler/byte-code interpreter, source references for code in promises correspond to the file where the code is actually written (where the "spelling" is). With the AST interpreter, instead, the source references to promises correspond to the code location where promises get forced. The compiler behavior is more correct (and also implementing the AST behavior in the compiler is not possible, even though for debugging it might be nice to have access to both). Unfortunately implementing the compiler behavior in the AST interpreter is also impossible (or, infeasible, the performance overhead would be very large). Normally, stack traces are read by humans, so this is not an issue, but the shiny tests happen to capture the AST behavior.

The AST behavior is captured in test-stacks.R, "integration tests". It is easier to see what is going on with stacktraceoffset to FALSE:

```
options(shiny.stacktraceoffset=FALSE)
library(testthat); library(shiny); test_file("testthat/test-stacks.R")

   num                                     call loc
1   35                                        h
2   34                       .handleSimpleError
3   33                                     stop  5]
4   32                                        A  9]
5   31                                        B 13]
6   30                             <reactive:C>
7   29                         ..stacktraceon..
8   28                                    .func
9   27                              withVisible
10  26                      withCallingHandlers
11  25                              contextFunc
12  24                              env$runWith
13  23                       withReactiveDomain
14  22                                  ctx$run
15  21                        self$.updateValue
16  20                        ..stacktraceoff..
17  19                                        C 16]
18  18                              renderTable
19  17                                     func
20  16                           origRenderFunc
21  15 renderTable({     C() }, server = FALSE) 16] <===== HERE
22  14                         ..stacktraceon..
23  13                              contextFunc
24  12                              env$runWith
25  11                       withReactiveDomain
26  10                                  ctx$run
27   9                        ..stacktraceoff..
28   8                                  isolate 16] <===== HERE
29   7                      withCallingHandlers
30   6                       captureStackTraces 16] <===== HERE
31   5                               doTryCatch
32   4                              tryCatchOne
33   3                             tryCatchList
34   2                                 tryCatch
35   1                                      try 16]
```

The marked lines show the differences. With the AST interpreter, there is no line number info, because the interpreter would provide source reference for some library files (for which it doesn't have them because there would be a performance overhead of having them, but the tests only look at references in test-stacks.R anyway). The code for these promises is in fact at line 16 as given by the compiler.

Would it be possible to make shiny work given this? Ideally shiny should not depend on either behavior with source references for promises. In my tests for the compiler source reference tracking, I allow both variants so that they run both with the AST interpreter and the compiler.
# 

And from another email:
# 

> Tomas, thanks for letting us know about this problem and for taking the time to explain what you've found. We'll investigate it. Is it correct that this must be tested on R-devel 71397 or greater?

Yes, it is correct. Earlier versions do not support tracking of expression and of source line references in the byte-code.

> Tomas, is there a way to enable source references when compiling a file? I would like to do some small experiments with the new byte-code compiler -- I want to compile some simple code and examine the source references.

The source reference tracking  and expression tracking in the compiler is always on. This means that the ways to enable/disable tracking have not changed in 71397. Expression tracking is always on (there is no way in R to disable it). Source reference tracking is on for parts of code that have source references attached. Whenever the compiler compiles code with source references attached, it will also put the source references into bytecode. This means you do not have to do anything new about disabling/enabling source references compared to what was there prior 71397.

And the full story as I know it is that source references are kept in the parsed code in attributes. But, often, they are not, for performance reasons, because the AST interpreter runs slower on code that has the source references (e.g. it has to keep extracting references from blocks of commands, etc). This can be controlled from "keep.source" (a global option, which is false by default in non-interactive invocation and true in interactive). By default,  pre-compiled packages (and packages prepared for lazy loading) do not have source references, you can set "R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE" environment variable to "yes" when building packages to change this. I hope the defaults will change but that should not impact shiny much - people did already have these controls now.

The source references (and expressions) are stored in arrays in the byte-code constant pool, you can see they are present with the byte-code disassembler (but there should not be a need to do that - unless perhaps to verify you have the right R version). So, with 71397 and newer, you now get

```
> compiler::disassemble(compiler::cmpfun(function(x, y) { x <- x + y; x * y}))
list(.Code, list(8L, GETVAR.OP, 1L, GETVAR.OP, 3L, ADD.OP, 4L, 
    SETVAR.OP, 1L, POP.OP, GETVAR.OP, 1L, GETVAR.OP, 3L, MUL.OP, 
    7L, RETURN.OP), list({
    x <- x + y
    x * y
}, x, structure(c(1L, 57L, 1L, 66L, 57L, 66L, 1L, 1L), srcfile = <environment>, class = "srcref"), 
    y, x + y, x <- x + y, structure(c(1L, 69L, 1L, 73L, 69L, 
    73L, 1L, 1L), srcfile = <environment>, class = "srcref"), 
    x * y, structure(c(NA, 1L, 1L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 
    1L, 1L, 3L, 3L, 7L, 7L, 7L), class = "expressionsIndex"), 
    structure(c(NA, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 6L, 6L, 
    6L, 6L, 6L, 6L, 6L), class = "srcrefsIndex")))
```

With an older version, you get

```
> compiler::disassemble(compiler::cmpfun(function(x, y) { x <- x + y; x * y}))
list(.Code, list(8L, GETVAR.OP, 1L, GETVAR.OP, 2L, ADD.OP, 3L, 
    SETVAR.OP, 1L, POP.OP, GETVAR.OP, 1L, GETVAR.OP, 2L, MUL.OP, 
    4L, RETURN.OP), list({
    x <- x + y
    x * y
}, x, y, x + y, x * y))
```

You can also have a look at compiler tests for expression tracking and source reference tracking,
src/library/compiler/tests/srcref.R and src/library/compiler/tests/srcref.R and src/library/compiler/tests/curexpr.R
yet perhaps there is nothing surprising - the tests are essentially similar yet less sophisticated that source reference tracking tests in shiny

title: Feature request: ability to stop an executing function
description:
When your shiny app has some actions that can take a long time, it can often be useful to have a way to stop the function that's running. For example, clicking a "analyze" button that takes 5 minutes, and after a few seconds you realize you wanted to change some parameter, your only solution is to refresh the app.

This question has been asked many times (and got the most attention [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/37664197/stop-a-time-consuming-function-on-button-click-shiny) and [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/30587883/is-it-possible-to-stop-executing-of-r-code-inside-shiny-without-stopping-the-sh) and [here](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26600271/r-shiny-how-to-allow-users-to-stop-the-process-and-how-to-stop-the-app-from-ba)). In one of those, there was one suggested answer that offered a workaround of spawning a child process using mcparallel, and the main shiny app has control over killing that process when it wants.

The issue was also discussed on shiny-discuss a few times, and earlier this year @jcheng5 mentioned [there may be a solution to this](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/j9-NeG9v5ds) in the future.

I'm not asking for this to happen now, but I wanted there to be an official issue for this so we can track it and know when/if it gets implemented

title: updateRadioButtons: names of choices vector get lost
description:
Hi all,
I noticed a problem when updating choices of radio buttons with a named vector: The names do not appear in the user interface. The issue occurred after updating to shiny 0.14.
Example:

```
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  radioButtons("RadioButtons", "radio buttons",
               c("Item A"=1, "Item B"=2, "Item C"=3)),
  actionButton("update","update"),
  textOutput("selected")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$update, {
    updateRadioButtons(session, "RadioButtons",
                       choices = c("Item X"=1, "Item Y"=2, "Item Z"=3))
  })

  output$selected <- renderText(paste("Selected:", input$RadioButtons))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

In fix #1291 the line
`choices <- as.character(choices)`
was added. As far as I understand
`choices <- sapply(choices, as.character)`
would make a better job, since plain `as.character` strips the names.

title: Maximum update rate of reactive expressions
description:
In my program I have a multi-selectize input to select data, often between 10 and 20 datasets. I merge the selected data, do some calculations on it, and return the results. This process takes a bit of time. When I then add or remove multiple (let's say 5) items from the selectize at once, the calculations are re-done 5 times, instead of waiting for a short while for my input to finish and doing one calculation.

Is there a way to either 
a) make the selectize wait for a certain time (like a second) before submitting the change to the server, or
b) make reactives re-calculate the results only at a certain rate

I tried to implement the later by caching the results, using reactiveValues to record the time of the last call, and invalidateLater if I returned a previous result. However, it does not work yet as I expected it.

title: Let modules get at top-level session inputs
description:
@cpsievert is working on module support for Plotly's event handling, i.e. hover, click, etc. See https://github.com/ropensci/plotly/pull/700 for his previous attempt.

Plotly events are not raised on individual plots, but on groups of plots (using the "source" argument to bind plots into groups; by default all plots belong to the `"A"` group, but you can set this to whatever). These events are then sent to the server via (basically):

`Shiny.onInputChange("<eventName>-<groupName>", eventValue)`

and accessed on the server via the R function `event_data(eventName, groupName)`, which then calls `getDefaultReactiveDomain()$input[["<eventName>-<groupName>"]]`.

The group names are, rightly, not module-namespaced; it's desirable to allow plotly plots in different modules to be assigned to the same group. However, `getDefaultReactiveDomain()$input` from within a module only gives you access to namespaced input values.

It would be great if we could introduce a way (that is not too tempting for the less module-savvy, who should be sticking to arguments and return values to communicate with the outside world) to get at inputs that are at the global namespace level.

title: Github version breaks my code with dynamic UI rendering
description:
Hello,

I've just installed the fresh GitHub version (13.2.9005) of Shiny and it broke my code. I'm rendering "wrapper containers" on the fly and right after I'm filling them with plots. With the old (i.e. CRAN) version (0.13.2) everything was working well, but now it seem like the 'renderPlot' is executed before the 'wrap' output is rendered, so it fills the old one and then it's overwritten with an empty 'wrap'.
Can I trigger the "fill" renderPlot somehow else then with a reactive value (something like "onRenderComplete")?

See this simple example:

```
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
    sliderInput("size", NULL, min = 10, max = 20, value = 15),
    actionButton('print', 'print'),
    uiOutput('wrap')
)

server <- function(session, input, output){
    react_valves <- reactiveValues()

    output$wrap <- renderUI({
        input$print
        react_valves$wrap_rendered <- runif(1)
        plotOutput('fill', height = isolate(input$size) * 100, click = clickOpts(id = "fill_click"))
    })

    output$fill <- renderPlot({
        react_valves$wrap_rendered
        plot(1:10, cex = 1.2)
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Tabs aren't properly restored
brushedPoints/nearPoints not working with ggplot2 with non-cartesian coordinates
description:
Shiny does not seem to cope with non-cartesian coordinates systems in ggplot2 plots.
Below, I provide an example very similar to the plot interaction in [this](http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/plot-interaction-selecting-points.html) shiny gallery app where the brush and click events seem to be getting the wrong coordinates when using `map_coord()` instead of `coord_cartesian()`.

This doesn't seem to a be a problem when using base graphics for mapping as someone pointed out to me in this [question](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/38806503/shiny-click-brush-not-working-with-non-cartesian-coordinates) on StackOverflow. If possible, I would prefer to continue using ggplot2 with `coord_map` (and avoid the distorted maps obtained with `coord_cartesian`).
Is this something you would be looking into in the future?

Thanks!

```
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

map_world <- function(world, mapPoints, xlim, ylim){
  # function to generate ggplot world map
  ggplot() + 
    geom_polygon(data=world, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group)) +
    geom_point(data=mapPoints, aes(x=Longitude, y=Latitude), color="red") +
    # coord_map messes up the brush select
     coord_map(xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim)
    # coord_cartesian would work but distort the map
    # coord_cartesian(xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim)
}

mapPoints <- data.frame(Longitude=c(-103, -108, -130, -120),
                      Latitude=c(52, 40, 45, 54))
world <- map_data("world")

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 6, 
           plotOutput("plot1", height = 300, 
                      click = "plot1_click", brush = "plot1_brush") )
  ),
  fluidRow(
    column(width = 6, 
           h4("Near points"), verbatimTextOutput("click_info") ),
    column(width = 6, 
           h4("Brushed points"), verbatimTextOutput("brush_info") )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  # output world map
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    map_world(world = world, mapPoints = mapPoints, 
              xlim=c(-180,180), ylim=c(-90,90))
  })
  # output clicked points 
  output$click_info <- renderPrint({
    nearPoints(mapPoints, xvar="Longitude", 
                  yvar="Latitude", input$plot1_click)
  })
  # output brushed points 
  output$brush_info <- renderPrint({
    brushedPoints(mapPoints, xvar="Longitude", 
                  yvar="Latitude", input$plot1_brush)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

    ui <- fluidPage(mySampleUI('myUI'))

title: navlistPanel Should Allow Fixed Width Value
description: The navigation bar of a `navlistPanel` contains text links to tab panels, so the text is not something which should expand to take up more size when the browser window is enlarged. It creates unnecessary horizontal whitespace in the navigation list. Currently, only relative widths are acceptable to `widths` e.g. `c(3, 9)`. It should be possible to easily specify a fixed width (e.g. `200px`) for the list panel and allow the tab panels to consume the remainder of the space, which changes according to the width of the browser, since they would contain items, such as plots, more suitable to resizing.

I also wonder if it could be generalised so that each radio button could have more than one HTML element associated with it. For example, a text option next to each button and a `selectizeInput` box directly below the text.

Currently, the documentation of `choices` for `radioButtons` doesn't specify what data type it should be, although it only works when it is a character vector. This is a more general request than #1093.

title: Issue with Shiny server running two applications

description:
When a selectizeInput with a placeholder, choices = NULL, selected = NULL, and multiple = FALSE is updated to have a set of choices with length > 0, the placeholder disappears and the first element of choices becomes the selected value. I want the placeholder to remain and selected = NULL, since only the choices were updated, not the selected argument.

However, if multiple = TRUE, when choices are added the placeholder remains and selected remains NULL.

Below is a minimal example: when the UI loads, the selectizeInput has a placeholder, choices = NULL and multiple = FALSE. When you check the box, the server updates the choices to be c("var1", "var2", "var3", but does NOT update selected, yet the placeholder disappears and "var1" is selected by default. This happens even if I specify selected = NULL in the updateSelectizeInput call.

Is this a bug or intended? Is there a way to keep a placeholder and nothing selected with multiple = FALSE?

```
library(shiny)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("selectizeInput demo"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectizeInput(
        inputId = "variable",
        label = h3("Treatment variable"),
        choices = NULL,
        multiple = FALSE,
        selected = NULL,
        options = list(placeholder = "This is a placeholder")
      ),

      checkboxInput(
        inputId = "add_choices",
        label   = "Add choices",
        value   = FALSE)
    ),
    mainPanel = NULL
  )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  observe({
    if (input$add_choices) {

      updateSelectizeInput(
        session = session,
        inputId = "variable",
        choices = paste0("var", 1:3),
        selected = NULL)
    }
  })

})

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

server <- function(input, output, session) {

}

title: Adding support for inline inputs? (Very naive implementation inside)
description:
I sometimes want my inputs to be inline, usually because I want to either place some short text or a button next to an input.  I've created a very simple `inlineInput()` function that I use:

```
inlineInput <- function(tag) {
  stopifnot(inherits(tag, "shiny.tag"))
  tagAppendAttributes(tag, style = "display: inline-block;")
}
```

And then I can do something like this

```
inlineInput(textInput("username", NULL, placeholder = "Username")),
actionButton("check", "Check availability")
```

I don't think it'd be a good idea to include this wrapper function in Shiny, it's just a proof of concept that I myself use.  There are already a few functions in shiny that take a `inline` boolean flag, do you think it'd be a good idea to add such a parameter to all input functions?  I would gladly do it if you think it's a good idea

title: update*Input functions should sanitize labels
description: The `update*Input` functions currently pass `label` as raw text, and the value is assigned in the client using jQuery's `.text()` function. This means that if a tag object is passed, it doesn't display properly. For example: ``` R shinyApp( ui = fluidPage( textInput("text1", tagList("Label 1 - tagList with inline tags", tags$i("italic"))), textInput("text2", "Label 2 - raw HTML italic"), textInput("text3", "Label 3"), actionButton("updateTags", 'Update Label 3 with tagList("Label 3", tags$i("Italic"))'), actionButton("updateHTML", 'Update Label 3 with "Label 3 italic"') ), server = function(input, output, session) { observeEvent(input$updateTags, { updateTextInput(session, "text3", tagList("Label 3", tags$i("Italic"))) }) observeEvent(input$updateHTML, { updateTextInput(session, "text3", "Label 3 italic") }) } ) ``` For `textInput`s that have a label when created: - Label 1 is created with a `tagList()` and `tags$i()` and the text displays with italics. - Label 2 tries to use raw HTML text, but the `` tag gets escaped, so the text itself is not italic. Label 3 is a `textInput` that has its label updated with `updateTextInput`: - When updated with `tagList("Label 3", tags$i("Italic"))`, the result is `Label 3,[object Object]`. - When updated with raw HTML, `"Label 3 italic"`, the result is `Label 3 italic`. The behavior should be consistent for `textInput`, and `updateTextInput`, but they treat the `tagList` input differently. Additionally, for `actionButton`, the behavior is opposite that of `updateActionButton`. - `actionButton` respects tag objects, and escapes raw HTML, like `textInput`. - `updateActionButton` does not properly respect tag objects, and puts raw HTML inline without escaping. For example: ``` R shinyApp( ui = fluidPage( actionButton("button1", tagList("Button 1 - tagList with inline tags", tags$i("italic"))), br(), br(), actionButton("button2", "Button 2 - raw HTML italic"), br(), br(), actionButton("button3", "Button"), br(), br(), actionButton("updateTags", 'Update Button 3 with tagList("Button 3", tags$i("Italic"))'), actionButton("updateHTML", 'Update Button 3 with "Button 3 italic"') ), server = function(input, output, session) { observeEvent(input$updateTags, { updateTextInput(session, "button3", tagList("Button 3", tags$i("Italic"))) }) observeEvent(input$updateHTML, { updateTextInput(session, "button3", "Button 3 italic") }) } ) ``` I believe the proper solution is for the update functions to do this with the `label`: ``` R label <- as.character(htmltools::as.tags(label)) ```

title: Issue with "hidden error" when using eventReactive
description:
I'm not exactly sure how `eventReactive()` works internally so my diagnosis might not be correct.

It seems that when a reactive context tries to get the value of a reactive value that's defined with a `eventReactive()`, the first time it's called (ie. before the variable gets an initial value) a silent error is thrown with no text.

Explanation:

Here's a simple app that assigns the value of a button into the `foo` reactive using `eventReactive`, and there's also a textOutput that just displays static text

```
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("btn", "Button"),
  textOutput("text")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  foo <- eventReactive(input$btn, input$btn)

  output$text <- renderText({
    "hello"
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

As expected, the app shows a "hello" message.

Now, add a `cat(foo())` just before returning "hello".  Now when you run the app, "hello" doesn't show up until after the button gets pressed, because before that the `cat(foo())` statement results in a "silent" error.  When I put a `browser()` there to inspect the value of `foo()`, I just got `Error:` without any text for the error.

title: Suppress error messages
description:
For security reasons, have an option to prevent any raw error messages from getting to the client--make them sanitized. Raw error messages can contain file paths, internal hostnames, argument values, and sometimes even source code snippets.

(Let the user throw "trusted" exceptions and turn all other exceptions into generic exceptions?)

Currently you can work around this by throwing a generic exception in `options(shiny.error = function() { ... })` but that means even logging doesn't occur (you can't get the error from within shiny.error--seems perverse, but it's modeled on `options(error)`).

We should at least have shiny.error functions with at least one argument, be passed the error. This would allow a complete workaround.

We should also consider building our own version of this and sticking it directly into our server products, so you can opt into this behavior across an entire server (or override on a per-app basis) with a config file.

Ref: https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/shiny-discuss/FyMGa2R_Mgs/FNyusgdxBgAJ

title: Feature request: Allow tabset and navbar to have nameable ID values for hyperlinking
description:
Currently, navbars and tabsets generate a random ID number between 1,000 and 10,000 to use as the middle section of an id value (e.g. `<div ... id="tab-1234-1">`).  This allows for the links to be created in the navbar/tabs (e.g. `<a href="#tab-1234-1">`). I would guess the need for a randomly generated ID value is so that multiple navbars and tabsets can exist with unique ID names in the same HTML file.

The problem I have is that I can't create a hyperlink to a particular page or tab of the application because I can't predict the random number that will be used in the link.

There is already an `id` input for the `navbarPage` and `tabsetPanel` functions, which both pass the `id` to the `buildTabset` function.  Once it reaches `buildTabset`, `id` is only used to define the id of the `<ul>`, while randomly generated ID values are created on line 724 of bootstrap.R:

``` R
tabsetId <- p_randomInt(1000, 10000)
```

... and later pasted into the middle of the ID string on line 736 to give the "`tab-1234-1`" format:

``` R
thisId <- paste("tab", tabsetId, tabId, sep="-")
```

I would propose that the `id` value passed to `buildTabset` should also be used as the value of `tabsetId`, defaulting back to the randomly generated value if `id=NULL`.  There shouldn't be an issue with duplicate id values in the HTML because we would still need to append `tabId` to the `tabsetId`.

So my proposal for lines 724 and 736 would be:

``` R
tabsetId <- ifelse(is.null(id), paste0("tab-", p_randomInt(1000, 10000)), id)

---
thisId <- paste(tabsetId, tabId, sep="-")
```

This should allow users to create `navbarPage(..., id="myTabNameHere")`, which would produce `<div ... id="myTabNameHere-1">`, that could be linked from ui.R using `tags$a("See this page", href="#myTabNameHere-1")`.

I apologise for not trying to edit this myself, but I'm not terribly confident using Git.

title: Unify resource requests for embedded applications
description:
If a Shiny application contains embedded applications (loaded in iframes), each of those embedded applications loads a separate copy (via a distinct URL) of resources that should be shared (bootstrap, fontawesome, etc).

These resources should all map to the same top-level location, thus allowing the browser to use its cache and reduce the amount of network pressure.

title: defer loading of iframes
description:
When a Shiny application contains a number of iframes, defer loading those iframe until after the parent application starts.

If the iframe content is allowed to load, those requests may be serviced before the parent application's server connection. In some cases, this will cause timeouts.

title: Heatmap, leaflet & shiny
custom output bindings receive inconsistent JSON data
description:
When sending values to custom output bindings, the 'auto'-JSON-ifying doesn't behave consistently.
At a minimum (I haven't tested beyond simple vectors), the value appears either as an object _or_ as single value in the client's browser, which complicates using these values.

A full 3-file (`server.R`, `ui.R`, and `www/test.js`) gist to reproduce the problem is here: https://gist.github.com/mmuurr/54315e3a5d581d8e6a46

Simple examples (living inside `shinyServer(...)` in `server.R`) below:
- for `output$test_output_val <- character(0)`, the JavaScript value in `renderValue` is an `[]` `object` (i.e. an array of length zero).
- for `output$test_output_val <- "foo"`, the JS value is a `"foo"` `string`, i.e. _not_ an array (and thus doesn't have a an array length).
- for `output$test_output_val <- rep("foo", 2)`, the JS value is `["foo", "foo"]` `object`, i.e. once again an array (with length two).

When writing a single output binding that might receive variable-length outputs from the server, this complicates parsing (as otherwise, one can iterate through the length of `data` in `renderValue`, which works in the length-zero and length-two cases, but fails in the length-one case).

The default behavior for jsonlite is to convert the character vector to an array regardless of length, and I think Shiny should conform to that behavior (if using jsonlite), right?

``` R
jsonlite::toJSON(character(0)) ## returns an array
jsonlite::toJSON("foo") ## returns an array
jsonlite::toJSON(rep("foo", 2)) ## returns an array
```

Hi all!
First of all I want to thank the developers of Shiny: great job!

Now I want to describe my issue and ask for help of the community.

I am trying to create an example of a ShinyApp that allows to automatically generate UI inputs for some scalars provided in a named list. For example, I feed my App with this list:

method <- list('Method name' = "My Great Method", 
                      'Post process' = TRUE,
                      'Iterations' = 20).

The App should scan this list and create an input for each element of the list. Ids of the inputs should be set to be equal to the tranformed names of the elements in the list (e.g. lowercase and without whitespace). This part is solved programmatically and I have a reactive list which contains ids of all inputs created.

For the example above the App's UI should include three inputs: a text input with id "uiFrame_methodname", a checkboxInput with id "uiFrame_postprocess" and a numerical input with id "uiFrame_iterations". So in this case I have access to, say, a vector `vars` on the server side. It keeps ids of created input elements ("uiFrame_methodname", "uiFrame_postprocess" and "uiFrame_iterations").

User, of course, is able to change values of these inputs. And the App should keep track of it: when a user changes value of any of the inputs, I need to trigger the event handler. Usually I use observe() to do something like this, but it works only when I explicitly specify an input id which should be observed by Shiny:

```
observe({
if (input$mySliderInput1 > 200)
{print("Hello")}
})

```
observe({
if (input[[vars[1]]] == "My Great Method")
{print("Hello")}
})
```

So, in short, I need to make Shiny react to events related to programmatically generated inputs whose names are kept inside some variable.

I hope I described everything clearly and recieve an answer soon! 
Thank you in advance!

updateSliderInput doesn't update the value until the input is in view, which can cause problems
description:
When using `updateSliderInput()` on a `sliderInput` that is in a tab that isn't currently visible, the slider doesn't actually get updated until it is visible.  This is not the case with other inputs I tested and causing problems if another input/output depends on that slider.

Example: this app has two tabs, each with a slider input. There is an output specifying what the value of the slider in tab2 is. Whenever the slider in tab1 is changed, the slider in tab2 is updated to match it. Note that the output _should_ change whenever tab1 slider is moved, but it only gets updated after seeing tab2 slider.

```
library(shiny)
runApp(shinyApp(
  ui = 
    navbarPage(
      "title",
      tabPanel(
        "tab1",
        sliderInput("num1", "Set slider in tab2 to:", 1, 10, 1),
        textOutput("foo")
      ),
      tabPanel(
        "tab2",
        sliderInput("num2", "num", 1, 10, 1)
      )
    )
  ,
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    output$foo <- renderText(sprintf("Number in tab2 is: %s", input$num2))
    observe({
      updateSliderInput(session, "num2", value = input$num1)
    })
  }
))
```

Note that if you put both sliders in the same tab, things work as expected. Also, if you change the slider input to a numeric input, then again things work as expected.

title: conflict between shiny dateRangeInput and rpivotTable
description:
(re-submit at @wch request)

The problem is reproduced on the current version of shiny in dev `devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")`.

There are two versions of rpivotTable to test:

This version **does work** with the `dateRangeInput` example below, but it is the one that had issues with ggvis etc.
It uses `jquery 1.11.0` and `jquery-ui 1.10.4`.

```
devtools::install_github("smartinsightsfromdata/rpivotTable", ref='master')
```

This other version **does not work**  with the `dateRangeInput` example below, but it is the one that is aligned with the latest dev version of shiny & qgvis.
It uses `jquery 1.11.3` and `jquery-ui 1.11.4`.

```
devtools::install_github("smartinsightsfromdata/rpivotTable", ref='dev')
```

This is the testing code:

```
library(shiny)
library(rpivotTable)
library(dplyr)
ui = shinyUI(fluidPage(
  dateRangeInput('dateRange',
                 label = 'Rango de Fechas: yyyy-mm-dd',
                 start = as.Date("2015-01-01"), end = Sys.Date() -1
  )
  , rpivotTableOutput('table' )

))

server = function(input, output){
  output$table <- renderRpivotTable({
    iris %>%
      tbl_df %>%
      filter( Sepal.Width > 3 ) %>%
      rpivotTable
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

With `devtools::install_github("smartinsightsfromdata/rpivotTable", ref='dev')` I get this error at the console:

```
jquery-ui-1.11.4.js:4558    Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'empty' of undefined
```

And this is the code associated:

```
    /* Generate the date picker content. */
    _updateDatepicker: function(inst) {
        this.maxRows = 4; //Reset the max number of rows being displayed (see #7043)

title: KISS principle on the server.R | global.R side
add keyboard_step to updateSliderInput arguments
description:
Ion.RangeSlider allows one to specify the size (in percentage) of keyboard steps on a slider (see http://ionden.com/a/plugins/ion.rangeSlider/demo_advanced.html)
Currently, in Shiny, we cannot specify this programatically.  It is only possible by making an index.html file with the keyboard step hard-coded in, for example:

```
<input class="js-range-slider" id="topNDate" data-type="double"
  data-min="1385856000000" data-max="1438297200000"
  data-from="1385856000000" data-to="1438297200000"
  data-step="86400000" data-grid="true" data-grid-num="9.66666"
  data-grid-snap="false" data-prettify-separator=","
  data-keyboard="true" data-keyboard-step="1"
  data-drag-interval="true" data-data-type="date" data-time-format="%F"/>
```

Ideally this property would be exposed to both `sliderInput()` and `updateSliderInput()`, so when setting and changing the max and min of a sliderInput, the keyboard-step can be precisely controlled.

title: unicode inequalities (u2264 and u2265) not working on windows
description:
**The issue is that the options in selectInput lists with unicode characters appear to be ignored.**

This bug is specifically related to Windows (I've tested with Windows 7 and Windows 10).  The MWE below works perfectly on unix-type systems (tested on OS X 10.10.5 and Ubuntu 14.04).

The issue is related to certain unicode characters, specifically u2264 and u2265, though there probably are others.

It's not obvious if this is an R issue or a shiny issue, [though in discussion](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/3KDGxupzRRQ) with @yihui, he suggested I open an issue here.  I have tested on the latest R-devel build for Windows and the issue is still present:

```
> sessionInfo()
R Under development (unstable) (2015-09-20 r69402)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_Australia.1252  LC_CTYPE=English_Australia.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_Australia.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C                      
[5] LC_TIME=English_Australia.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] shiny_0.12.2.9003

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] R6_2.1.1         htmltools_0.2.9  tools_3.3.0      rstudioapi_0.3.1
 [5] Rcpp_0.12.1      jsonlite_0.9.17  digest_0.6.8     xtable_1.7-4    
 [9] httpuv_1.3.3     mime_0.4
```

A work around (as suggested by @yihui) is to change the locale from English (the default on my machine) to Chinese:

```
if (.Platform$OS.type != "unix") Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "Chinese")
```

Another work around is to not use windows machines - unfortunately that's not always possible.

Here's the MWE:

```
require(shiny)
app <- shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    "\u2264 and \u2265",
    uiOutput("bin_prob_k"),
    uiOutput("bin_prob_inequality"),
    uiOutput("bin_prob_out"),
    plotOutput("pmf")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$bin_prob_k = renderUI({
      numericInput("binom4_k", label = "Number of successes (k)", value = 3,
                   step = 1, min = 0, max = 10)
    })

    bin_choices = reactive({
      nms = paste("P(X",c("=","\u2264","<","\u2265",">"),input$binom4_k,")",sep="")
      return(nms)
    })

    output$bin_prob_inequality = renderUI({
      selectInput("bin_prob_type", label = "Inequality type", choices = bin_choices())
    })

    output$pmf <- renderPlot({
      n=10
      prob = 0.4
      probs = dbinom(0:n, size=n, prob=prob)
      mtext(input$bin_prob_type, side = 3, col = "red", cex = 1.2)
    })

    output$bin_prob_out = renderUI({
      withMathJax(paste0("\\(",input$bin_prob_type,"\\)",sep=""))
    })
  }
)
```

Looking closely, when the locale is English, the `\u2264 and \u2265` characters included as the first element in the ui render as equals signs.  This might suggest that in the background somewhere, the inequalities are being rendered as equals and then only the unique values are being displayed.

When the locale is changed to Chinese, the first element in the ui displays the inequalities correctly and the selectInput has all 5 entries displayed correctly.

title: Memory leak in nested render/output functions
Undefined label for selected item when updating server side selectize input element
description:
There seems to be an issue with displayed labels when updating a selectizeInput element (server=TRUE, selected != NULL, and custom JS display function based on a data frame). The selected item is marked as `undefined` in the drop-down menu. See the following code: ``` library(shiny) runApp(list( ui = bootstrapPage( selectizeInput("selectizeTest", label="Selectize Test", choices=NULL) ), server = function(input, output, session) { choices <- cbind(value = paste0(rownames(mtcars),".v"), label=paste0(rownames(mtcars),".l"), name=paste0(rownames(mtcars),".n"), html = paste0("", rownames(mtcars), ""), mtcars) updateSelectizeInput(session, "selectizeTest", choices=choices, selected="Cadillac Fleetwood.v", server = TRUE, options = list(render = I( '{ option: function(item, escape) { return "
" + item.html + "
"; } }' )) ) # also for return "
" + escape(item.name) + "
" } )) ``` This is most likely a timing problem. When updating the server-side selectize element some time after app initialization (e.g. using invalidateLater) with a new value, this item is displayed correctly according to the provided JS `option` function. In the first case, I guess, the data frame is not yet available and the `selected` parameter is interpreted as new value without label. See also [http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html](http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html). It may be helpful to update this page (the JS function name needs to be `option` instead of `options`; it should be clear that the data frame has to contain a `value` and a `label` column; the return value of the `option` function should always be wrapped in a `div` or similar tag, otherwise the items are not displayed correctly). Thanks

title: Feature request: Allow unique tags using string mangling for environments
description:
Right now, I'm trying to develop an app in Shiny that facilitates the use of modules:

```
#UI MODULE
module_env$normalization <- new.env()

eval(envir = module_env$normalization, {
  #Create the UI here
  ui_normalization <-
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel('Normalization (FPKM)',
      p("normalization"),
      actionButton("var_echo", "Echo variables")
    )
  )

  #Create your initial input/output variables here
  sum_exp <- NULL
  output_sum_exp <- NULL

  #Always register last
  register_module(
    name="Normalization (FPKM)",
    module=ui_normalization,
    env=module_env$normalization,
    inputs=c('sum_exp'),
    outputs=c('output_sum_exp')
  )
})


###SERVER MODULE
eval(envir=module_env$normalization, {

observeEvent(input$var_echo, {
  print(get("sum_exp", module_env$normalization))
})

})
```

As you can see, I'm using lots of reactive variables to make sure that modules stay separate as well as environments. It all works fine, and the input/output between modules works like a charm.

However, the main problem lies when the UI tags overlap--if UI tags from separate modules overlap, this results in events being fired for more than one module at once. This can be bad.

There are a couple of fixes for this:
1. Coral users into using prefixes for their tag names, hoping that different tags don't overlap.
2. Design a string mangling system to ensure that tag names stay unique.

I like the idea of an optional string-mangling system based on environment to enable Shiny users to make tags unique should they start to make modular apps that need encapsulation.

title: Allow `radioButtons` to start unselected
description:

The use case is one where I need to understand if a user is making an explicit choice or if they want this option to remain unspecified.

My other option is to inject an artificial choice (basically, "use default") and let that be the initial selection.

title: Support date-time input

I am aware that there are a number of examples which pull in date-time pickers into a Shiny application, but it would be great if Shiny could provide this without independent augmentation.

title: Allow `dateInput` to have an unspecified value
description:
It would be nice to allow a `dateInput` control to have an unspecified value. Right now, if you provide `value=NULL`, you get "today" by default.

The use case is one where I want to know if the user has made a explicit choice of a date value. Not choosing a date value could mean that a search is unbounded, for example.

title: Using observe vs observeEvent
description:
This is a discussion I started on the [Google Group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/attali$20observe/shiny-discuss/Ah47LxpX2wI/am3Gx-s_thQJ), but since it hasn't been resolved and I don't want to lose reference to it, I wanted to post it here so that it's not forgotten and can be further discussed in the future.

**Original post**  
Hi Joe, I didn't want to have a discussion in an unrelated github issue so I'm moving here.

(For everyone else, see https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/115#issuecomment-111581458)

First of all, I'm sorry if I've been spreading bad advice.

When I first noticed `observeEvent` it seemed useful and I couldn't find too much docs on it or usecases so I used it as I thought made sense. Here's my reasoning for using it, let me know if it's valid or not: I like to use `observeEvent` even when the expr is very simple and only includes one reactive because of two reasons:
1. it takes care of the NULL case and doesn't run when the input is NULL, which is very often the wanted behaviour and saves me from writing `if (is.null(input$x)) return()`
2. I like how it's explicit in terms of exactly what reactive needs to change in order for it to run. I don't need to look at the code inside the expression to see what reactive value is the dependency, I have it as a parameter.

If observeEvent is slower or in any way worse or there are good reasons for not using it, do let me know. Or if my two points are invalid, let me know. That was just my uneducated way of seeing the difference between the two

Thanks 

---

**Joe's response**  
I'm impressed that those are your two reasons--they are the two best reasons I could think of, and #1 didn't occur to me until today.

For #1 I was hoping validate(need(input$x, FALSE)) would be an idiom that got widely adopted not only for observers but in reactives and outputs as well. Now that I put that in writing I see how ridiculous that sounds--it's a lot of tokens for what should really be something as concise as `required(input$x)`. I need to think more about this.

For #2 this is a philosophic difference, I guess. I built reactivity into Shiny because years of both web and desktop UI programming have led me to dread callback hell and the subtle bugs it introduces, and observeEvent is really nothing more than letting you use imperative/callback-style in Shiny's reactive world. Now, there's no question that imperative/callback-style is necessary sometimes--action buttons demand them. But I always get a little squeamish about encouraging imperative idioms outside of narrow cases. The reason for this is because I really believe that thinking reactively is the key to making non-trivial Shiny apps that are robust and can be reasoned about, and observeEvent when used for non-button scenarios can be a crutch that is definitely helpful at first but can delay learning about observers.

I'm curious--both of your reasons would seem to apply to eventReactive just as much as to observeEvent. Do you find yourself often using eventReactive for the same reasons? Or is there something different about the nature of reactive expressions vs. observers that makes eventReactive less appealing?

---

**My last response**  
#1. I must admit I was never an adopter of `validate`. I knew about it since day 1 of learning shiny but I always found it a bit clunky and never seemed to like it, so if I needed to validate an input I prefered to do it myself with `if (is.null())` or whatever other check was necessary. And when observeEvent came along and I saw the `ignoreNULL` param, I thought that was meant to solve my problems :)  I do see many people using validate so it does have its place, I just personally didn't adopt it.
#2. I do see your point on the reactivity vs callback nature of functions. So again, maybe this is just personal preference. I find it simpler and easier to say "when this value changes, I want to run this code".  I realize this is not what you intended shiny to be like but it's more intuitive to me in some use cases and I find the code simpler. I use reactivity more natively when using the `renderFoo` functions - that's one place where being reactive is almost always what I find the most natural and works well. Another time I use `observeEvent` is when I have a more complex expression with many reactive values inside but I only want it to run when one reactive value changes (not necessarily a button). Instead of putting most of the code inside an isolate, it just makes more sense to me personally to say "run this code when this one value changes".  I agree that reactivity is key to shiny and very important to learn, and I'm not saying that these techniques should be necessarily encouraged, but after developing many complex apps this is what works best for me.
#3. I do indeed use eventReactive probably more than the average shiny developer (although I always forget it's not called reactiveEvent - difference naming scheme). But I don't use it as often as observeEvent, I think it's because I prefer to use `reactiveValues` which takes away the need to make reactive variables. Again, this is probably steering very far away from what shiny was meant to do, but I find it's simpler to develop larger apps.

All in all, I find reactivity very useful and a good approach to some things (such as UI rendering and outputs), but for a lot of logic stuff I prefer the callback approach. I don't really actively think of it as being callback instead of reactive - in my mind I just think "instead of being dependent on all the variables inside the expression, I want to only be dependent on the variable that I decide".  I hope that makes sense.

---

I'd love to resolve this or get some more insight at some point, to know whether or not I should continue to be using `observeEvent`/`eventReactive` or if I should use the more traditional approach that everyone else uses.

title: renderPrint() and renderPlot() capture function side-effects
description:
I'm not sure if it makes sense to try to fix these issues, but we at least should have an article about it. These functions (and `renderImage`) capture function side-effects, which can result in unexpected behavior when they access a `reactive` which is cached -- Shiny only caches the return value, and not the print or plot side-effect.

This has come up in `renderPlot` in #781, and `renderPrint` in #871.

title: Allowing inputs to be reset
description:
I've implemented a [reset](https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/R/reset.R#L56) functionality in a package I wrote, which allows users to reset any input or many inputs inside a tag to their original values.

I think this can be very easily supported by native Shiny with much cleaner code and it doesn't require a lot of code. I forked shiny and made a commit to show what it could look like.

[Here's the commit](https://github.com/daattali/shiny/commit/e97b44d2a8f70f4b0afcf30a4fe9dc3adc876b34?ws=0) (there seems to be some whitespace diffs, sorry)

My idea was to just add a `reset` method to input bindings, and call that method similarly to how `receiveMessage` works.  The actual implementation might not be the way you'd like it, but I'm wondering if you approve of this general idea.  I think it could be useful functionality and really doesn't take much code.

Using the small commit I did in less than an hour, it's possible to change the settings or values of slider inputs/selectize inputs/date ranges and textInputs, and with one simple call to revert them back to their original state.

Example (if you have the code from my commit):

```
runApp(shinyApp(
 ui = fluidPage(
 div(
 id = "form",
 dateInput("date", "Date", value = "2014-06-19", min = "2014-06-10"),
 textInput("text", "Text", "lalala"),
 selectInput("select", "Select", 1:5, selected = 3:4, multiple = TRUE)
 ),
 actionButton("btn1", "reset all"),
 actionButton("btn2", "reset only date"),
 actionButton("btn3", "change minimum data ('reset' will revert this setting)")
 ),
 server = function(input, output, session) {
 observeEvent(input$btn1, resetInput(session, "form"))
 observeEvent(input$btn2, resetInput(session, "date"))
 observeEvent(input$btn3, updateDateInput(session, "date", min = "2000-01-01"))
 }
))
```

title: How to pass arguments to a reactive function?
Outputs can not be unbound and re-bound
description:
This is a regression in Shiny 0.12.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/czXoYWnXGe8/CjO_S5swG2kJ
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/kHUI5E9ZDvE/1aZR0mdlVNUJ

``` r
library(shiny)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    verbatimTextOutput('test'),
    tags$script(
      "setTimeout(function(){Shiny.unbindAll();Shiny.bindAll();},1000)"
    )
  )
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  output$test <- renderPrint({
    invalidateLater(500, session)
    runif(1)
  })
})

runApp(list(ui=ui, server=server))
```

If the bug is present, the numbers will stop changing about a second after the app loads. If the bug is not present, then the numbers will keep changing forever.

This was introduced in v0.12 while I was fixing https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/749. The actual commit is https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/6c36ea5753b39ea1204c2ff68474c1a50c7f4424.

The problem with that commit is that in order to avoid binding an output that's currently bound, it checks `$el.data("shiny-output-binding")`. When a binding is unbound, that data was not removed (which arguably is also a bug). A better test is to check for the CSS class `shiny-bound-output`.
